en: Preface to the Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings:
For forty-nine years, the Old Barbarian [the Buddha] whispered and murmured, engaging his heart and mind with sentient beings who possess consciousness.
He spoke until he reached the point where speech can no longer reach; then, suddenly, atop the tip of the Dragon’s Tail, a clap of thunder shook the great earth.
Their emotions were suddenly overwhelmed with laughter. Turning over in their seats, each was immediately able to ride upon the wind and mount the breath, summoning rain and forming clouds;

like dragons and thunder, they were swift and agile, manifesting the marks of a Great Man. Not dependent on words and letters, they attained entry into the True Dharma through intuitive comprehension of the meaning.
Therefore, it is called the "Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings. In brief, the essential purport of this school does not go beyond this single "separate" [transmission].
With a single word, one can stir the long river into cream and curd, and transform the great earth into yellow gold.

Though a thousand-fathom tongue cannot reach it in discourse, here, naturally, every grain cast forth is diamond-king dust that pierces the entrails and dissolves the bones and flesh of men, transforming them into a single reed-pipe—the primordial Yang-energy.
Not only does that which has roots become flowers; [it also brings forth the fruit].
As for the fruit [of this teaching], even stubborn voids and strange rocks cannot fail to be imbued with warmth and moisture, thereby joining in its resonance.

The Layman Hai Changlimei, having followed the lineage of the Yellow River and Luo Valley to succeed Master Ziyu and transmit the essence of nature and destiny (*xingming*), and having attained sudden realization under the elder who "bent the branches," became the heir to the single thread of the "Plucking the Flower" (the *Huayan* transmission). He then compiled [this work] from Śākyamuni Buddha down to the golden...

Colorful is the joy! You have already arrived at the Great Mirror, where the Five Schools were revitalized. A transcendent hero beyond the boundaries of time for a thousand ages, you have compiled his words and entrusted them to the common people (*li*).
May each person manifest a thousand billion bodies, preaching the Dharma everywhere, so that everyone may realize and understand it.
Only then will you see the hands and eyes pervading the entire body of the common people, with every root and every pore emitting light and preaching the Dharma. For...
An eminent hero among the great patriarchs of the ancestral vehicle of the first awakened ones, you illuminate this degenerate age.

(I, your unworthy disciple,) have long since vowed my heart to this Way and have labored to uphold it for many years; yet, though I have called out in the heavens, there has been no one to respond in harmony.

Suddenly, your letter arrived beyond the reach of spiritual communion, and finding our hearts to be in perfect accord, I finally realized that the Buddhas and Patriarchs still have true sons remaining. The Dharma gate is indeed in deep distress.

I have provided a sudden and comprehensive explanation for this purpose, and have thus composed a preface on the "Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings. Furthermore, I have appended the symbolic expressions of the Five Houses.
Written with prostrations by He Nan of Mi Fa Zang at Tian Shou Sheng En Chan Temple in Deng Wushan, Wu Gate.
Preface to the *Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings*:
The World-Honored One, in transmitting the Dharma and entrusting the robe, exhorted Kāśyapa:

"I now entrust to you the pure Dharma-eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa, the true mark which is markless, and the subtle, wondrous, orthodox Dharma. You must protect and uphold it. He further commanded Ānanda.
The secondary transmission of the transformation must not be allowed to be interrupted.
At the end of his life, the World-Honored One earnestly cast off one shoulder of the burden weighing twelve hundred catties.

Viewed in this light, the Sūtra teachings he expounded for forty-nine years were all matters concerning the benefit of sentient beings and the reception of those who come to him; they were, in sum, not [the ultimate teaching].
Ultimate. If we discuss this according to the Chan masters, it is precisely like using a wolf’s tail to sweep away tracks—the more one sweeps, the deeper they become.
That the habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) have not been exhausted is the fault right here. This matter does not reside in many words or much talk, nor is it in remaining silent for a long time.
As long as the central tree of your mind has no root, there will come a day when the sprouts of spiritual awakening break forth.
The World-Honored One’s grandmotherly heart was far too revealing;

sentient beings, in their ignorance and folly, took it for a sweet fruit, investigating it daily and chewing on its flavor, unaware that they were being bound to death by its entangling vines. To this day, who is willing to seek it?
Liberation.

Although more than a thousand years have passed since the World-Honored One entered *nirvāṇa*, it is as if it were this very day. The spring breeze blows gently, wafting the fragrance of an auspicious destiny that endures for ten thousand ages.
Amidst the verdant mists of the twin *śāla* trees, the traces of his deeds remain vividly clear, restoring the obscurity of a thousand kalpas. At Elephant Head...

Regarding hemp and wheat: although it is shown that the golden body is neither extinguished nor born, this golden body has never failed to be filled with the wondrous nature and spirit of the eyebrows and eyes.
How could it be something obtained only after sentient beings have practiced? These ignorant and stubborn kinsmen have for many lifetimes willingly endured hardship;
dwelling in the house of birth and death, they create unrestrained calamities, yet they do not recognize their own single segment of radiance.
Clear! From antiquity until now, it has pervaded heaven and earth; it was originally this single assembly on Vulture Peak.

Śākyamuni was not before, and sentient beings were not after. It cuts off the conventional relationship between host and guest, and there is no distinction between the titles of "sentient being" and "Buddha."
The Great Perfect Mirror Wisdom: the dust-motes and lands are all clearly illuminated; though the measure of kalpas may come to an end, the radiance alone remains.

There is not a single star-path; principle has fallen to the ground of the intellect. Were one to attempt to point out a single star, a flaw would immediately arise. This is what is named the "Pure Dharma-Eye.
It is like the youth Saṃghanandin, who, holding a round mirror, went directly before the Venerable Rāhula. The Venerable asked: "How many [stars do you see]?"

“How old are you? He replied, “One hundred years. The Venerable One said, “You are still but a child; how can you say you are one hundred years old? The boy said, “I do not understand the principle [of conventional age]; I am truly one hundred years old. The Venerable One asked, “Are you skilled in the pivot? The boy said, “The Buddha said: ‘If a person lives for a hundred years without understanding the pivot of the Buddhas, it would be better to live for but a single day and attain decisive realization. The Venerable One was moved. He took him as his attendant and had him enter the order. Later, he became known as the Elder Śrīghana. He attained Arhatship and lived for one hundred and twenty years. His remains were preserved in a stūpa at the city of Śrāvastī. It is said that even today, when people offer incense and flowers there, they hear the sound of the Dharma being preached. The other said, "What does that which you hold in your hand signify? The youth replied, "The great perfect mirror of all Buddhas is without flaw or obscuration within or without;
two people may see it together, for their mind-eyes are alike. "Indeed, indeed! The patriarchs of the Western Heaven possess tongues of sharp wisdom and wondrous supernatural powers;
how could these exist apart from the minds of sentient beings? This continued until the twenty-eighth [generation].

The Patriarch Bodhidharma was the first patriarch in this eastern land. Knowing that the sentient beings of the land of Zhendan possessed the capacity for the Mahayana, he traveled alone with effortless ease.
He manifested a distinct "hand and eye," upholding the principle of the smile;

he proclaimed that there is no reliance on words and letters, a separate transmission outside the teachings, pointing directly at the human mind to see one's nature and become a Buddha. Is there, then, truly such a separate transmission outside the teachings?

Because sentient beings of the Dharma-ending age are mostly mired in words and letters, they take the spoken holy teachings to be the ultimate reality, failing to believe in that which transcends them—the innate suchness where there is neither cultivation nor realization, the Buddha-nature beyond both death and birth.

They cast their bodies and minds into the weeds and treat their six sense-faculties as discarded objects. Therefore, I have come to clear away these branches and vines and to cut off this entanglement once and for all. I require—

You must directly realize this in its entirety and suddenly clarify the ground of the mind. After nine years, four people attained it. Of the lineage of Great Master Huike, the transmission reached the Sixth Patriarch.
After the Sixth Patriarch, the robe and bowl were no longer passed on; rather, mind was sealed by mind, transmitted from patriarch to patriarch in succession.
Ultimately, words and phrases are merely means to enliven others; even a blink of an eye or a raising of an eyebrow becomes a superfluous teaching. This continued until the time of Deshan.
When Huangbo Xiyun was examined, he immediately manifested a strange reaction by changing his facial expression. However, with Dahui Zonggao, it was not so;

with a single stroke across a thousand rivers, the wild waves were suddenly stilled, and the practice of staffs and shouts was relegated to the high shelves. Following Dahui Zonggao, from the Yuan through to the Ming dynasties, the number of enlightened masters who emerged grew ever more abundant.
Although their recorded sayings (*yulu*) circulated widely, there was no one who could truly enter [the Way].
The Dragon Canon is truly lamentable. Lately, heterodox teachers have preached the Dharma, defiling and staining the ancestral gate.

The single school of "seeing one's nature" that came from the West has become like the oral transmission of a village old woman in Seven Villages. Even the Patriarchs and Buddhas can do nothing about it.

Now, this *Jiaowai biechuan* (A Separate Transmission Outside the Teachings), newly compiled by the layman Li Mei of Yanguan, has appeared; this layman has long investigated the Chan school and possesses profound [insight].

Exhausting the ultimate intent, one discerns the paths of principle through the karmic conditions of the patriarchs and Buddhas. One must thread together the origins of the ancient and modern *nian* and *song* verses.
Those of the dharma-ending age, whether monastics or laypeople, should realize their own original face;

do not seek it elsewhere. This mind is never obscured day or night and remains indestructible through kalpas. There is no Buddha outside the mind—there are only tall bamboos and verdant pines. There is no mind outside the Buddha—it is the mountain.
The great earth and the rivers are immediately and clearly understood. Do not linger in words and letters; apply yourself single-mindedly to the practice.
Suddenly open the true eye, continue the ancestral lamp, and establish new regulations. Suppress the ancient style of the Buddhas and uphold the mind-seal of the Patriarchs.
Offer a single incense stick to repay the Layman; only then will you know that the pure Dharma-eye mentioned above has been here all along.
Written by Yufeng Yuanxin of Mount Jing on the Mid-Autumn Day of the Guiyou year of the Chongzhen era of the Imperial Ming Dynasty.
Preface to the *Chuanxiao Baizhuang* (The Special Transmission Outside the Teachings).
When I, an old monk, previously read the words of Dahui, I saw his citation of the karmic conditions concerning Master Shaokang Liaobian. It is said that as soon as Liaobian raised [the matter],...
As for "playing with [the topic]," one said: "Ever since I was kicked by Master Ma, I have laughed without ceasing until this very day.

When has he ever had such talk as 'peaks layered in emerald green,' 'mountain streams murmuring,' 'willows on the banks holding mist,' 'garden flowers smiling at the sun,' 'cuckoos singing in lofty trees,' or 'butterflies dancing among fragrant thickets'?
From ancient times to the present, he has only been full of clever, flowery rhetoric."

There is no one who surpasses this old man. Observe how he presents [the teaching] in such a manner; it does not reside solely in the novelty of his words and phrases, but values only the extraction of the ultimate essence.
What is the ultimate essence? Have you not seen how, in his private quarters, he asked a monk:
"When Deshan saw a monk enter the gate, he would strike him with his staff; when Linji saw a monk enter the gate, he would shout at him; when Xuefeng saw a monk, he would simply say, 'It is...'"?
"What is it? When Muzhou saw a monk, he would say, "This is a case already resolved; I grant you thirty blows. Do these four old fellows have any way to benefit others?
A monk said, "They do. Dahui said, "Note! As the monk hesitated, Dahui shouted and sent him out.
Upon hearing this, Zunpou was suddenly liberated from his former evil knowledge and perverse understandings, and thus he attained realization.
A truly free and easy monk. Furthermore, when Dingxu entered the room, Dahui asked him, "When there is no releasing out from within and no admitting in from without—just at such a time, what is it?
As Xu was about to respond, Dahui struck him three times with his bamboo staff.
Xu suddenly attained great enlightenment. Later, when Elder Beixian entered the room, Dahui asked, "Not being joined with the myriad dharmas..."
When asked, "Who is the companion? Xian replied, "One who cannot be supported. Dahui asked, "Who is the one who cannot be supported?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As Xian was about to respond, Dahui struck him, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment.

It can be seen that there is nothing better than this for opening the true eye of man and liberating one from intellectual understanding through the urgency and secrecy of the staff and shout. Thus, the Old [Master]...
Master Sengsheng did not understand how to strike while circling; he used only a single stick, striking from head to toe.

His sole intent was for people to have their "true eye" suddenly opened at the very point where they were struck by the stick, so as to see through to their own original state—a realization that cannot be obtained from another and stands far beyond the names and phrases of both the internal and external teachings.
Only then will one know that which was compiled by Layman Limei. From...

The ultimate pivot-words of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are definitively not mere characters; only then can one "lift up and go" immediately, beyond the reach of nets and snares, and impossible to call back.
Even if one attains such a state, it is sufficient only for one's own liberation.

If we speak of the battle, however, each must exert their strength at the point of turning, without lingering in abstruse or subtle principles, but seizing the living prey with a single flavor and raising the supreme teaching in its entirety. This is the fundamental...

Dividing into one single point, he transcends Buddhas and surpasses patriarchs. He walks alone in solitary liberation; his wielding and seizing are spontaneous, his killing and giving life are sovereign.
He is able to govern all names and phrases, neither sitting in the place of death nor blinding the eyes of others. Only then is he fit to benefit both himself and others.
If this is not yet so, then for the time being, look east and west upon these written pages. Suddenly, if you catch sight of it, then come back to me, old man.
The monk asked for a blow from the master’s hand; since he had already seen it, why did he still need to receive the blow?
Is there anyone here who can distinguish the black from the white? If no one can do so, do not rashly presume to employ staff or shout.
Composed by the senior monk Yuánwù, Abbot of Āyuwáng Monastery, in the Xiṇwèi year of the Chóngzhēn era.

*Chiao-wai pieh-chuan*, Scroll One:
Śākyamuni Buddha (the Fourth Honored One of the Bhadrakalpa). The twenty-fourth year of King Zhao of the Zhou dynasty, the year of Jiayin, the fourth month.
He was born on the eighth day of the month. When he reached the age of nineteen on the eighth day of the second month in his forty-second year, he desired to seek renunciation.
He thought to himself, "What further encounter shall I have? Thereupon, he went out to observe the sights at the four gates and saw the four signs;
his heart was filled with both sorrow and joy, and he reflected: "This aging, illness, and death must ultimately be wearying and loathsome. Then, at the hour of midnight, there was one...
A deity from the Śuddhāvāsa heavens, appearing within the lattice window, joined his palms and said, "The time for your renunciation has arrived; you may now depart.
Upon hearing this, the Prince felt great joy in his heart and immediately leaped over the city wall to leave.

He went to Mount Dandaka to practice the Way, first staying with Ārāḍa Kālāma for three years to study the concentration of the sphere of nothingness (*ākiñcanyāyatana-samādhi*). Realizing it was not the ultimate path, he abandoned it. Furthermore...

He went to the abode of Udraka Rāmaputra and studied the meditative attainment of neither-perception-nor-non-perception for three years; realizing it was not the ultimate truth, he abandoned it as well.
He then went to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, where he joined with various non-Buddhist practitioners and subsisted on a diet of hemp and wheat for six years. Thus, a sutra says:

"By means of no-thought and no-mindfulness, and without the practice of sensation, he completely subdued all non-Buddhists. Having first undergone trials of heterodox methods, he thereby demonstrated various skillful means.
He eradicated all divergent views and led them to Bodhi. Thus, the *Samantaprabhā-sūtra* states:

"On the eighth day of the second month, at the time when the morning star appeared, the Bodhisattva attained enlightenment and was titled the Teacher of Gods and Humans; he was then thirty years of age.
This was the year of Guiwei, the third year of King Mu’s reign. Subsequently, in the Deer Park, he turned the Wheel of the Four [Truths] for the five men, including Kauṇḍinya.
He turned the Wheel of the Dharma and realized the fruit of the Path. He preached the Dharma for forty-nine years in this world. Later, he addressed his disciple Mahākāśyapa:
"I entrust to you the pure Dharma-eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvāṇa, and the subtle, correct Dharma of the true mark that is signless.
You must protect and uphold it. He further commanded Ānanda to serve as his deputy in the transmission and transformation of the teachings, ensuring they would not be severed.
He ceased speaking and uttered this verse: "The Dharma is originally no-dharma; no-dharma is also dharma. Now that I transmit the time of no-dharma, how has dharma ever been dharma?
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken this verse, he further addressed Kāśyapa:
"I shall entrust to you my golden-threaded *saṃghāṭī* robe. Transmit it to the one who succeeds me, until the appearance of the Buddha Maitreya in the world. Do not..."
[He] caused [them] to decay. At that time, the World-Honored One arrived at the city of Kuśinagara and addressed the great assembly:

"I now suffer from back pain and wish to enter *nirvāṇa*. He then proceeded to the banks of the Hiraṇyavatī River, beneath a pair of *śāla* trees, where he lay on his right side with his feet叠疊 (one upon the other) in profound, tranquil stillness.
One thousand and seventeen years after the World-Honored One’s parinirvāṇa, the teaching reached the Central Plains; this was [the period of] the Later...
The tenth year of the Yongping era of the Han dynasty was the wuchen year.

As soon as the World-Honored One was born, he pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, walked seven steps, looked around in the four directions, and said: "In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. Yunmen Wenyan said:

"Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow of my staff and fed him to a dog, so as to ensure peace throughout the world. Xuedou Xian said: "I would have immediately overturned the meditation seat. Fachang Yu said: "Excellent!"

"One blow! Too late, you were born! Before leaving Tuṣita, a single spike should have been driven into the space beneath his heels; how could it wait until this day? Even so, it is like drawing one's bow after the thief has fled. Yunfeng Yue said: "Although Yunmen possessed a plan to quell the chaos, he lacked the way to emerge from it himself. Baoning Yong’s verse says: "Before the primordial chaos was divided, no one was yet aware; As soon as heaven and earth were split apart, affairs manifested in secret. Heaven bestowed a skillful means capable of the marvelous; In the end, he yielded to him for a performance. Tiantong Huo said: "Although this story of Yunmen circulates, it cannot avoid falling into his trap. Gao Feng Miao said, "The World-Honored One was much like a sacred tortoise dragging its tail, thereby inviting the omen of his own death.

Although Yunmen fully upheld the orthodox command, he too was creating unnecessary conditions for ignorance. At that time, he should have simply drawn a circle on the ground, written the letter "Ding" within the circle, and then extended both hands to show them.

This would have ensured the matter dissolved like melting ice. Chushi Qi’s verse says: "The nine dragons spout water from the void; Golden lotuses spread beneath his feet. Heaven and earth cannot contain it; This time, he has no choice but to emerge."

The womb—why do you alone claim supremacy? To whom do you speak? You have mistakenly taken up the second month. But tell me, what is the first month? *Pfft!* Jin-su Wu said: "I am not like Yunmen, who made such a fuss over nothing.

Had I been there at the time, I would simply have stepped forward, placed my hand upon my forehead, and said, 'Cat! Let us see where his face will land. One day he ascended the seat. When the assembly had gathered and settled, Mañjuśrī struck the gavel and said: "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma-King; the Dharma of the Dharma-King is thus.
