Lingyin Yue said, "Master Wang, it is not that you have not emptied your heart and poured out your guts; yet I have not seen you succeed in transforming customs or changing social mores. This mountain monk has raised but a single donkey: when it goes along with the flow, it gallops eastward and westward by no less than thousands of miles in a single day;

but when it is forced against the grain, it does not move even a single step. Tell me, how far apart is this from Master Wang’s water buffalo? After a long silence, he said, "The fisherman dances his oars; the rustic old man sings his songs. Jin-su Wu said, "Nanquan sought the fundamental, but unknowingly turned it into the extraneous.
The Master asked a monk, "There was a fine breeze last night. The monk replied, "There was a fine breeze last night."
The Master said, "It has blown down a pine tree in front of the gate. He repeated, "It has blown down a pine tree in front of the gate.
Then he asked another monk, "There was a fine wind last night. The monk replied, "What kind of wind was it? The Master said, "It blew down a pine tree in front of the gate."

[The monk] asked, "What kind of pine is this? The Master said, "One gain and one loss. (Cuiyan Zhen said: "Among the assembly there was much deliberation; some said, 'Previously he answered according to the facts. )

Therefore it is said he "attained" [the Way]. Later, he was not right to ask, "What wind is this? Therefore it is said he "lost" [the Way]. Yet, they only know that the chariots and books were unified and that jade and clay are of one source; why is this so? It is because they do not know the root-source of the Way or the depth of its principle.

Do you wish to understand? When you meet a swordsman on the road, you must present your sword; if you are not a poet, do not offer your poem. The Master wrote a letter to Zhunyu, saying: "Principle changes according to phenomena."
Vastness is not external; phenomena are harmonized with principle. Silence is not internal; this was the conclusion of the letter from Sengda.
He then asked Zhunyu, "What is meant by 'vastness is not external'? Zhunyu said, "To ask one and answer a hundred is no hindrance.
[The monk] asked, "What is meant by 'silence is not internal'? Zhunyu said, "To perceive sounds and forms is not the mark of a master. The monk asked Chang again:
The monk asked Changsha. Changsha stared at him with wide-open eyes. The monk then repeated the latter part of the question. Changsha then closed his eyes to show him.
The monk then asked Zhaozhou. Zhaozhou made the gesture of eating. The monk again repeated the latter part of the question. Zhaozhou made the gesture of wiping his mouth with his hand.
Later, the monk recounted these instances to the Master (Jiangshan). The Master said, "These three men are not mistaken; they truly are my disciples. (Jiangshan)

Xiqin said: "Although Nanquan had the karmic conditions for raising these sons, alas, he loved his children so much that he failed to notice their ugliness. Little did he realize that among these three men, one has eyes but no feet, one has feet but no eyes, and one has neither feet nor eyes.
Nevertheless, all three could serve as teachers to Nanquan. Why is this so? Because principle and phenomena are clearly distinguished. Below Nanquan Mountain there was a hermitage master.
Someone said to him, "The Master Nanquan has recently appeared in the world; why do you not go to pay him a visit? The hermitage master replied, "It is not only Nanquan..."
Quán came out of his room and said, "Even if a thousand Buddhas were to appear in the world, I would not go. When the Master heard this, he ordered Zhāozhōu to go and investigate him.
Zhāozhōu went there and immediately prostrated himself. The hermitage master paid him no heed. Zhāozhōu walked from west to east, and again from east to west;
the hermitage master still paid him no heed. Zhāozhōu said, "The grass bandit has been utterly defeated," and then he pulled down the curtain and departed.
He returned and reported this to the Master. The Master said, "I have always suspected this fellow.
The next day, the Master went to the hermitage with a novice, carrying a bottle of tea and three cups. He threw them onto the ground and said, "Yesterday's! Yesterday's!"
The hermitage master said, "What was that thing yesterday? The Master struck the back of the novice with his hand and said, "You've had me fooled!

You've had me fooled! Then he shook out his sleeves and turned back. Xuedou Xian said: "How great were Nanquan and Zhaozhou! They were exposed by this fellow carrying a wooden board. Weishan Zhe said: "The hermitage master sat watching the victory and defeat.

How great were Nanquan and Zhaozhou! They met their downfall on pure ground. Zhihai He said: "It is so, yet while the hermitage master could indeed hold the boundaries, he could not share in life and death together [with them]."

When Zhaozhou prostrated himself, he simply said, "I know you, you thief! He waited for [the monk] to go from east to west and from west to east, then he grabbed his staff and chased him out of the hermitage.

Just see what other skills Zhaozhou had! [One day] he ascended the hall and said, "To speak of 'suchness' (tathatā) is already to have changed it. These days, monks must walk among the heterodox species.
Guizong said, "Though one performs the actions of an animal, one does not receive the retribution of an animal. The Master said, "Alas, Old Man Meng!"

Han: "And yet, he goes on like this. (Deshan Mi said: "Nanquan has been poisoned. Langye Jue said: "I, this mountain monk, am not so. When meeting water, I drink the water; when meeting grass, I eat the grass.

How could I know the conduct of a beast? Fahua Ju said: "Tell me, what is 'walking among different species'? A stone ox lies long in the mist of the three springs; a wooden horse neighs at times in the spring of an autumn night. Tianqi Rui said: "To wear horns and shed hair, one must personally reach this ground.

If you vainly engage in research, you will certainly be unable to do anything about it. At present, he merely thinks of water and grass, knowing nothing else. This is a man of the house who speaks the truth. But tell me, how does he transform?")

"Then they are of different categories. What about 'unchanging'? It was not said: "Alas, Old Man Ba has gone off like this again. [The Master] ascended the hall and said: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra fought each other at the third watch last night;
I gave each of them twenty blows and expelled them from the monastery.
Zhaozhou asked, "Whom will the Master’s blows be made to eat [suffer]? The Master said, "Tell me, where did Old Wang’s fault lie? Zhaozhou bowed and withdrew. (Yunmen)

Yandai said, "I have deeply received the Master’s compassion; I shall return beneath his robe and bowl to find peace and happiness. He also spoke on behalf [of Zhaozhou], saying, "To eliminate the harm for the sake of the assembly. Baoci then said, "Now tell me: did Zhaozhou’s 'stop' signify his approval of Nanquan, or his disapproval?

Jiashan Ling said, "Nanquan displayed his brilliance for a time, yet he could not help but pile up earth on level ground. Although Zhaozhou acted with direct immediacy, he was unaware that his forehead had struck the earth.

Zhaojue Qin said, "Nanquan struck the strings, and Zhaozhou played a different tune. How painful! Heaven above! If it were Chongning, it would not be so. Last night, the lanterns and pillars gave rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma; I give each of them twenty blows and order them back to their original positions."

Someone came forward and said, "Whom does the Master intend for the staff to strike? The Master replied to him, "The guest falls and the host falls. Jingshan Gaofeng’s verse says: Nanquan was without fault; his mouth could bring disaster. Zhaozhou prostrated; the grass-robber was utterly defeated. Jingshan takes no account;

he settles the case based on the facts. Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—let them pass to one side. Once, when the Master went to a manor house, the master of the estate had prepared in advance to receive and honor him.
The Master said, "I, this old monk, usually move about without letting others know. How could you have made such preparations?
The head of the manor replied, "Last night the local deity reported that the Master would come today. The Master said, "Wang Laoshi, my practice lacks power;
I have been seen by ghosts and spirits. An attendant then asked, "Since the Master is a *kalyāṇamitra* (a spiritual friend), why..."
He was spotted by the local deity (tǔdì). The Master said, “Serve another portion of rice before the local deity. (Master Shengying said:

“Nanquan, having been questioned by this monk, could not help but make his living inside a ghost cave. Yunju Xi said: “Is this a reward for him or a punishment? As for the local deity spotting him—was it Nanquan or not Nanquan? Cuiyan Zhen said:

“Many among the assembly say that ‘Sulū sulū’ is simply the portion of rice before the local deity. To theorize in such a manner is a profound insult to the ancients. Why? Because they know only how to spin out flowery words and branches, but do not understand the principle of Nanquan. Do you all wish to understand? Grasp it!”)

If one loses the proper measure, one will inevitably enter a deviant path. To let go [of all constructs] and abide in spontaneity (*ziran*), the body has neither going nor staying. Tiantong Jue said: "If I, this old monk, had seen the master of the manor speak in such a way at that time, I would have seized him and said: 'I will not let you go! Why is that?'"
"One who comes to speak of right and wrong is themselves a person of right and wrong. The Master once said, "In Jiangxi, Mazu says 'this very mind is Buddha.
I, Old Wang, do not speak thus. It is not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.
In speaking thus, is there any fault? Zhaozhou bowed and departed. At that time, a monk followed him and asked Zhaozhou, "The Master..."
After bowing while seated, he departed. [The monk] asked, "What was the meaning of that?

Zhaozhou said, "You should ask the Abbot instead. The monk then asked, "What was the meaning of the Venerable Shen's statement just now? The Master said, "He, however, understood my intention. [Huanglong Xian says:

When the ancients spoke thus, it was like peering at a leopard through a tube; one sees only a single patch. Even if one enters the forest without stirring the grass and enters the water without ruffling the waves, this is still like riding a horse across the edge of thin ice. If it were...]"

One who has mastered the art of shooting down a vulture—why not rub an itch on a snake’s head? Those who have passed through the barrier, try to discern this! After a long silence, he said: "The embroidered mandarin ducks emerge from the golden needle. Linji Yixuan said: "Those two old fellows, though skilled at moving their fingers inside boots... Jingshan Daowu said: "These two old men, though adept at moving their fingers within their boots..."

Little do they realize that the bystander is the one who appears ugly. Chushi Qi said: "Nanquan and Zhaozhou were both brought to account by this monk. ○ Huangbo served as the head seat for his teacher.
One day, Huangbo took up his almsbowl and sat upon the Master’s seat. When the Master entered the hall and saw him, he asked, “In what year did you begin practicing the Way, Elder?
Huangbo replied, “Before the time of King Bhīṣmagarjitasvararāja. The Master said, “You are still the descendant of Old Wang;
get down! Huangbo then moved to the second seat and sat there. The Master then desisted. (Miaoyan Yu said: "He who seeks to deceive the enemy perishes. — Yangshan.)

Yun said, "Not so. You must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping tigers. Wuquan said, "The extent of your realization has reached such a height. Xuedou Xian said, "It is a pity that Old Master Nanquan saw only the sharpness of the tip of the awl.

Had I been Nanquan at that time, as soon as he said 'before King Wei-yin,' I would have taken the second seat, leaving Huangbo unable to stir for the rest of his life. Nevertheless, one must still rescue Nanquan. Yunfeng Yue said, "Later, there were many discussions in the monasteries;

some said, 'Huangbo had the mechanism for trapping tigers, while Nanquan had the function of killing tigers. To speak in such a manner is truly lamentable. Little do they realize that this old thief has years but no [wisdom]."

"Virtue! Even sitting down to eat, you do not act according to your proper station. If you were under Yunfeng’s guidance, what would you say about 'before King Weyin'? Old Wang is even more straightforward—you must take a beating and be driven out! Jingshan Gaofeng said: "Why wait for him to ask in what year he began his practice?

As soon as he entered the hall and saw that he was in the seat of the presiding master, he took up his bowl and sat in the second seat. Even if Huangbo possessed the 'trap for tigers' device, where could he have applied it?
One day the Master asked Huangbo: "A world of gold, with walls and fences of silver—what kind of person is this?"
"Where does he dwell? Huangbo replied, "He dwells in the abode of the sages. The Master said, "There is yet another person; in what land does he dwell?
Huangbo then stood with his hands joined in *añjali*. The Master said, "If you cannot say it, why not ask Old Teacher Wuzhuo?
Huangbo then asked, "In what land does this other person dwell? The Master said, "What a pity! The Master then asked Huangbo, "Regarding *samādhi*..."
"Through the study of wisdom and the other perfections, one clearly sees the Buddha-nature. How is this principle to be understood?
Huangbo replied, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, do not rely upon or depend on a single thing. The Master said, "Is this your own realization, Elder? Huangbo replied, "I dare not say so.

The Master said, "Setting aside the cost of rice and water for a moment, who will pay the cost of your straw sandals? (Later, Guishan Lingyou asked Yangshan Huiji, "Is it not the case that Huangbo failed to grasp Nanquan? Yangshan replied, "It is.")

Yun said, "Not so. You must know that Huangbo possessed the mechanism for trapping tigers. Wuquan Shouzhi said, "The extent of your realization is this great. Baofu Zhuan said, "If it were not for Wuyang, Huangbo would have been buried alive. Wuzu Ji said, "Wuyang was much like painting legs on a snake.

Yunfeng Yue said, "If you do not sleep in the same bed, how will you know there is a hole in the lining of the quilt? Dayue Zhi said, "He who deceives his enemy perishes. Jingshan Guangzuo said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present one's sword;
if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. Chushi Zhi said, "This is both meeting with advantage and falling into disadvantage. △.
He then struck the wooden block three times. The monk set down his axe and returned to the Sangha Hall; the Master returned to the Dharma Hall.

After a long while, he entered the Sangha Hall again and saw the monk sitting beneath his robes and bowl. The Master said, "He has nearly ruined me! A monk asked, "When the Master returns to his quarters, what do you use as a guide?
The Master replied, "Last night at the third watch I lost the ox; when I rose at dawn, I had lost the man."
The Master of Fire (Heshang Moheyan) was once encountered by the monks of the East and West Halls while they were disputing over a cat.
The Master addressed the assembly, saying, "If you can speak the Way, I shall save the cat; if you cannot speak the Way, I shall kill it. The assembly was speechless. The Master then killed it.
When Zhaozhou returned from outside, the Master presented him with the previous account. Zhaozhou then took off his sandals, placed them on his head, and walked out. The Master [laughed].
It is said: "If you had been there, you would have saved the cat. (Xuefeng asked of Deshan regarding Nanquan’s act of beheading the cat, "What was the underlying meaning?

Deshan struck him with his staff and drove him out, then called back, "Do you understand? Xuefeng said, "I do not understand. Deshan said, "Even with such grandmotherly kindness on my part, you still do not understand. Baofu Zhan said: "Even so, it is merely a pair of worn-out straw sandals.

Cuiyan Zhi said: "The Great Zhaozhou could only save himself. Xuedou Xian composed a verse on Nanquan’s beheading of the cat: Both halls were filled with Chan practitioners; Stirring up dust and smoke, they could do nothing about it. Fortunately, Nanquan was able to issue the command.

"Cutting in two with a single stroke, regardless of bias. Regarding the verse on Zhaozhou wearing his sandals: "The public case is complete; I ask Zhaozhou: In the city of Chang’an, he wanders at leisure. No one understands him wearing his straw sandals upon his head; Returning to his home mountain, he simply stops.

Dayi Zhi said: "Nanquan acted according to the mandate; Zhaozhou acted according to the situation. Although this is so, it cannot avoid being discussed by people’s lips. Danyuan wishes to walk hand-in-hand with Nanquan," and he then took up his whisk and said, "If you can say something, I shall take it away.

The assembly was speechless. He then said: "To cry until the blood flows is useless; it is better to keep one's mouth shut for the rest of one's life. Wanfeng Wei said: "The two head monks lacked the mechanism to settle the chaos; Nanquan..."

There is the hand that can save a nation. Observe how, as soon as the true command is issued, who would dare to open their mouth on the scene? Zhaozhou saved the cat, yet arriving late does not make him a master. Songshan shook his sleeves and departed; tell me, did he save it or not?

Tianqi said, "When there is leisure, one makes preparations—patterning brocade and clustering flowers—but when the moment arrives, one is like a statue carved from clay or wood. You all have reached Nanquan; for what purpose did he hold up his rosary and ask, "What is this?

Nowadays, Zen practitioners do not look to the true command of the occasion, but instead give rise to emotional attachments and fixed views regarding whether something is cut off or not. Therefore, they miss Nanquan’s great life-force. Behold how their spiritual brilliance is naturally distinct; it does not depend on you.

[The Master] spoke idly, then revealed the matter of one’s own fundamental portion. Therefore, it was only then that he granted his approval. Had it not been thus, it would have been entirely like blind men groping for an elephant.

While the Master was in the abbot’s quarters with Xiangshan warming themselves by the fire, the Master said, "Without pointing east or west, speak directly of the matter of your own fundamental portion.
Xiangshan thrust his fire tongs into [the ashes] and stood with hands folded. The Master said, "Although it is so, you are still one thread behind Old Wang."
A monk came to inquire after his health, standing with his hands folded in a formal greeting. The Master said, "Too worldly. The monk then pressed his palms together in homage.

The Master said, "Too monastic. The monk was speechless. (Jingshan Daoyuan said: "Pressing palms together is too monastic; folding hands is yet again worldly. When it is neither of these, there is no place for your venerable body to rest. Only one who has the 'nose' [the essential core] can respond.

*Oṃ suru suru, siri siri.* He gave a shout and said: "What is this? Lately the royal decree has become strict; it does not permit encroaching on another's path or seizing another's market. (Chushih Qi said: "Folding hands is too worldly; pressing palms together is too monastic. It is neither monastic nor worldly.")

"Not vulgar. Who would dare settle upon a name? Even if one were to examine this closely, it is merely setting up a target to draw an arrow. But tell me: does this fall on the monk’s side, or does it fall on Nanquan’s side?
Once, while a monk was washing his bowl, the Master snatched the bowl away from him. The monk stood there empty-handed, and the Master said, "The bowl is in my hand;
why are you chattering with your mouth? The monk had no reply. Later, as the Master entered the vegetable garden, he saw a monk. The Master then...
The Master struck him with a tile. The monk looked back, and the Master then raised one foot. The monk was speechless. The Master then returned to his quarters.
The monk followed him in and, after making his salutation, asked, "Venerable Sir, when you just now struck me with a tile, was that not to awaken me?
The Master said, "And what about my raising my foot? The monk had no reply. (Later, there was a monk who asked Shishuang Zhu.)
Nanquan raised his feet. What was his intention? Shishuang raised his hand and said, "Is it like this? [He] ascended the hall and said, "Wang Laoshi is selling himself;
is there anyone who will buy him? A monk stepped forward and said, "I will buy him. The Master said, "Neither as something expensive nor as something cheap—how will you buy him?
The monk had no reply. (Zhaozhou Congshen spoke on his behalf: "Next year, I will sew a robe of cloth for the Master. Wolong Qiu spoke on his behalf: "It belongs to me.")

Heishan Yin said, "What kind of principle is this? Xuedou Xian said, "Although it is a masterpiece that craftsmen vie to purchase, it still does not resolve the underlying mechanism. But tell me, would Nanquan have approved? Xuedou was also about to offer a price, which would have left Nanquan with no way to advance and no path to retreat.

After a long silence, he said, "The Master cannot be accommodated elsewhere. Xiaoyan Bao said, "This talk of selling oneself has been handled by venerable masters of successive generations; there have been many who have offered their prices in response."

Yet, in the end, one could never do anything with him. Today, this mountain monk shall also present a brand-new price, such that Nanquan’s very person can no longer belong to himself, nor can it belong to another; he can neither act as a guest nor as a host.
[The Master] waited and said, "Cloud does not act as noble, nor does it act as lowly. How would you buy it? He simply said to him, "For now, please return to the Abbot’s quarters for a cup of tea.

The Master said: "The Buddhas of the three periods do not know 'there is'; the cat-servant and the white ox, however, do know 'there is. [Daimpui Zhi] said: "Since the Buddhas of the three periods do not know 'there is,' when have the cat-servant and the white ox ever even dreamed of it?

Truly, one must know that there is a person above who knows 'there is' before one can attain it. But who is this person who knows 'there is'? They drink the official wine and lie on the official street; they die where they are and are buried where they are. On the battlefield, there are infinite heroes..."

"Heroic Han! Mountains and peaks piled high, corpses exposed— Jingshan Daoyuan’s verse says: The Buddhas of the three ages do not know of his existence; Old and decrepit, he wanders abroad. His eyelids cover all five Mount Sumerus;

He performs somersaults within the great ocean. The wildcat and the white ox, however, know of his existence; The waterfall does not flow, yet the green mountains run. I laugh at the master Wuzhuo for no reason, Mistaking a winnowing basket for an ironing board.
The Master went with Guizong and Magu to pay respects to National Teacher Nanyang. On the road, the Master drew a circle and said: "Speak!"

Upon arriving, he departed immediately. Returning to Guizong, he sat within a *yuanxiang* (perfect circle). Magu performed a woman’s bow. The Master said, "If that is so, then you will not go. Guizong asked, "What kind of mental activity is this? The Master then called out to him and they returned together; he did not go on to pay his respects to the National Teacher. (Baoci then said: "As for Nanquan speaking thus, was it an expression of approval or disapproval? Yunju Xi said: 'He had originally been going to pay his respects to the National Teacher. Nanquan) Nanquan said, "I am going to pay my respects to the National Teacher. The Master said, "The National Teacher has already passed away. Nanquan said, "Even though he has passed away, I must still go to pay my respects. The Master said, "Even if you go, what will you say? Nanquan said, "I will say: 'The autumn wind blows over the yellow leaves. The Master said, "After you have spoken these words, how will you act? Nanquan said, "I will strike the ground with my staff three times. The Master said, "After you have struck the ground three times, how will you act? Nanquan said, "I will laugh loudly and depart. The Master said, "After you have laughed loudly and departed, how will you act? Nanquan said, "I will turn my head and look back. The Master said, "After you have turned your head and looked back, how will you act? Nanquan said, "I will weep bitterly and depart. The Master said, "After you have wept bitterly and departed, how will you act? Nanquan said, "I will walk straight ahead without looking back. The Master said, "You have already gone too far; you cannot return. Nanquan said, "I am already returning. The Master said, "If you come here, you will surely be struck by my staff. Nanquan said, "I am not coming here. The Master said, "If you do not come here, you will surely be struck by my staff. Nanquan said, "I am neither coming nor not coming. The Master said, "Since you are neither coming nor not coming, why are you struck by my staff? Nanquan said, "It is because I am struck by your staff that I am neither coming nor not coming. Chan Master Huahui of Zhangjing Temple in Jingzhao Prefecture. He was the son of the Xie family of Quanzhou.
When Master Baizhang sent a monk to visit him, the Master was ascending the hall; as the monk unfolded his sitting cloth and bowed, he rose and took up one of the Master’s sandals.

[He took] his sandals. Having brushed away the dust with the sleeves of his robe, he turned them upside down and placed them facing downward. The Master said, "This old monk has committed a transgression. (Huanglong Xin said:

"Baizhang displayed his spiritual powers to the full, yet it was not enough to dispel Changjing’s remark, 'This old monk has committed a transgression. Gushan Gui said: "Huanglong Meng-ba-lang still lacks one move. He only knows that Baizhang displayed his spiritual powers, but he does not realize that Baizhang’s skills were completely exhausted.

He only knows that Changjing said, 'This old monk has committed a transgression,' but he does not know that Changjing accepted the charge at once. Do you understand? A snake swallowing a shrimp is still tolerable; there is yet another centipede following behind. ○
A monk came, circumambulated the Master three times, shook his staff, and stood there. The Master said, "It is so; it is so. (Changqing Ling, speaking in his stead, said:
"Where are the body and mind of the Master’s Buddha-dharma? That same monk went to Nanquan and likewise circumambulated him three times, shook his staff, and stood there.
Nanquan said, "It is not so; it is not so. This is merely turned by the power of the wind; in the end, it will fall into ruin. The monk said, "Zhangjing said..."

"It is. Why did the Master say it was not? Nanquan said, "Zhangjing is indeed so; it is you who are not. (Changqing Ling said, "What kind of mental activity is the Master's? Yunju Xi said, "Zhangjing did not necessarily say 'it is,' nor did Nanquan necessarily say 'it is not.

He also said, 'If this monk had simply taken his staff and walked out at that moment, it would have been perfect. Jingshan Guang raised the case of Magu taking his staff to Zhangjing, circling the meditation seat three times, shaking his staff once, and standing there upright, saying, "Forged from pure steel, cast from raw iron. Zhangjing said, "It is! It is! Miaoxi said: "Is it so? Is it so? Nanquan said, "It is. Changqing Ling said, "The Master, what kind of mental activity is this?

Yunju Xi said, "Zhangjing did not necessarily say 'it is,' and Nanquan did not necessarily say 'it is not. Furthermore, he said: 'If this monk had simply taken his staff and walked away at that time, it would have been just right. "Three or five layers of flowers laid upon brocade. Again, Magu took up his staff and went to Nanquan; he circled the meditation seat three times, struck the ground once with his staff, and stood there upright. Miaoxi said, "He has already admitted defeat. Nanquan said, "It is not so, it is not so.

Miaoxi said, "To add cuffs upon willow branches. Magu asked, "Zhangjing said it was so; why does the Master say it is not? Miaoxi said, "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful. Nanquan said, "Zhangjing was right."

"This is not you; this is moved by the power of the wind and will ultimately perish. Miaoxi said, "Try holding a torch and looking at it. Nanquan asked, "How thick is the skin on his face? He then called to the assembly, saying, "Yunmen has made such a critique; tell me, does he accept him or not? Chushi Qi said:

"When Magu circled the bed and shook his staff, it was the standard ritual for paying respects. Why did Zhangjing say 'it is' and Nanquan say 'it is not'? When a bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip, a sweet melon is sweet from stem to end. Tianqi said:

'In general, when traveling to study, one must possess the correct eye of inquiry to avoid being ensnared by various quarters. It is because that monk’s application was unclear that he was subject to their judgment. Zhangjing merely went with the flow.'"

Nanquan cuts off the flow of all streams. If one acts with ease within the Middle Way, responding universally and adapting to circumstances, it is like a dragon obtaining water or a tiger relying on a mountain. If, however, one pursues fragrances and seeks out traces, becoming mired in footprints and lost in tracks, it is like a sheep butting against a fence or a monkey confined in a cage.

This monk indeed has great function overflowing his breast; yet, alas, he is well-acquainted with his own origins. thereby sparing the monk from wandering within the realm of right and wrong.
Chan Master Dazhu Huihai of Yuezhou.
Chan Master Dazhu Huihai was the son of the Zhu family of Jianzhou. He first went to visit Mazu. Mazu asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "I have come from Dayun Temple in Yuezhou. Mazu asked, "What do you intend to seek by coming here? He replied, "I have come..."
He requested the Buddha-dharma. The Patriarch said, "In my place, there is not a single thing. What Buddha-dharma do you seek? You neglect your own precious treasury;
why do you abandon your home and wander about? He asked, "Which one is the precious treasury of Huihai? The Patriarch replied:
"What you have just asked me is your own treasure-trove. It is fully complete; there is nothing lacking. You may employ it with sovereign ease—why should you seek it elsewhere?
At these words, the Master spontaneously recognized his own original mind, not through intellectual cognition. He leaped for joy and prostrated in gratitude.

He served the Master for six years and composed the *Tunwu rudao yaomen lun* (Treatise on the Essential Gate of Sudden Enlightenment for Entering the Way) in one fascicle. His Dharma-nephew was Xuanyan.
He secretly departed for the region beyond the Yangtze River and presented himself to Mazu. After Mazu had finished reading it, he addressed the assembly, saying: "In Yuezhou there is a great pearl;
it is perfectly round, bright, and penetrating, free and at ease, with no place of obstruction. A monk asked, "How can one attain Great Nirvana? The Master said:
"One does not create the karma of birth and death. [The student] asked, "What is the karma of birth and death? The Master said, "Seeking great *nirvāṇa* is the karma of birth and death.
Abandoning defilement to grasp purity is the karma of birth and death. Having attainment and realization is the karma of birth and death.

Not being free from the gate of counteractive measures (*pratipakṣa*) is the karma of birth and death. [The student] asked, "How then can one attain liberation? The Master said, "Originally, there has been no bondage."
Do not seek to understand; simply act directly. This is the Peerless One (Asamasama). A Tripiṭaka Master asked, "Does True Suchness (Tathatā) undergo change?
The Master said, "It does undergo change. The Tripiṭaka Master said, "Zen Master, you are mistaken.
The Master then asked the Tripiṭaka Master, "Does True Suchness exist? He replied, "It exists. The Master said, "If it were without change, it would certainly be nothing more than an ordinary monk."
Have you not heard? A good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) can transform the three poisons into the three clusters of pure precepts;
transform the six consciousnesses into the six supernormal powers; transform afflictions into bodhi; and transform ignorance into great wisdom.

If True Suchness were subject to change, then the Tripitaka would truly be nothing more than the teachings of external paths. The Tripitaka Master said: "If that is so, then True Suchness must possess existence."
"Transformation and change. The Master said, "If one clings to the idea that True Suchness undergoes transformation and change, one is likewise an outsider (tīrthika).
Yuan the Vinaya Master asked, "When you, Reverend, cultivate the Way, do you still apply effort? The Master replied, "I apply effort. [The Master] asked, "How do you apply effort? The Master replied:

"When hunger comes, one eats; when weariness comes, one sleeps. The monk asked, "Is it not the case that all people do exactly this? Do they apply themselves to practice in the same way as you, Master?
The Master said, "They do not. The monk asked, "Why do they not? The Master said, "When others eat, they are unwilling to eat;
they demand a hundred things. When they sleep, they are unwilling to sleep; they harbor a thousand schemes. That is why they are different. — Recorded by Vinaya Master Du.
[Oral Tradition].
Chan Master Fahui of Letan, Hongzhou.
Chan Master Fahui of Letan, Hongzhou, asked Mazu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Mazu—

The Master said, "Lower your voice and come closer; I will tell you. The Master then stepped forward. The Patriarch gave him a slap and said, "Six ears do not share a secret. Go now and return tomorrow.
On the following day, the Master entered the Dharma Hall alone and said, "I request the Abbot to speak.
The Patriarch said, "Go for now. Wait until I have ascended the hall; I shall come out and provide testimony for you. At that moment, the Master suddenly attained realization.
He paused and said, "I thank the Great Assembly for their witness," whereupon he circumambulated the Dharma Hall once and departed.
Chan Master Zhijian of Shanshan in Chizhou:
When Chan Master Zhijian of Shanshan was first traveling on pilgrimage with Guizong and Nanquan, they encountered a person on the road.
The tiger. Each passed by the side of the tiger. Nanquan asked Guizong, "Just now, what was that tiger like? Guizong said, "It was like a cat.
Guizong then asked the Master (Nanquan), and the Master said, "It was like a dog.

He then asked Nanquan, and Nanquan said, "I saw it as a great beast" (Daguang Zhi said: These three old fellows are gathered together talking in their sleep. If you wish for penetration, investigate them all at once).
"One must first capture this tiger. Once, while the Master was eating his meal, Nanquan gathered up the raw rice and said, "Is it raw?
The Master replied, "It is not raw. Nanquan said, "Even 'not raw' is still secondary. After Nanquan had walked several paces, the Master called out, "Elder!
Nanquan turned his head and asked, "What is it? The Master said, "Do not say that it is secondary. While they were working together to select edible ferns (*jue*), Nanquan...
Picking up a stalk [of greens], he said, "This is a truly excellent offering. Nanquan said, "It is not only this; he would pay no heed even to a hundred flavors of rare delicacies.
Nanquan continued, "Even so, each and every one must taste it before they can be said to have attained it.

(Cuiyan Zhi said: "As for Shan’s speaking in such a manner, is there anyone who can avoid it? If one can avoid it, one has not yet possessed the eye. If one cannot avoid it, then one contradicts the previous statement.)
Chan Master Ledu Weijian of Hongzhou.
One day, while Chan Master Ledu Weijian was sitting in meditation behind the Dharma Hall, Mazu saw him and blew twice into his ears.
The Master rose and, seeing it was Mazu, returned once more to his meditative concentration. Mazu went back to his quarters and ordered an attendant...
[The monk] took a bowl of tea and offered it to the Master. The Master did not look at it and simply returned to the hall.
Chan Master Daoheng of Mingxi in Lizhou once said: "I have a great illness that cannot be cured by the physicians of this world. (Later, a monk asked Cao...)

Shanjì said, "An ancient said, 'I have a great illness that cannot be cured by the physicians of this world. I do not know what kind of illness this is. Caoshan said, "It is the illness that cannot be gathered together. [Shanjì] asked, "Do all sentient beings also have this illness? Caoshan said, "Yes."

"Everyone has this; does the Master also have this ailment? Caoshan said, "I cannot find its point of origin even while searching. "Then why do all sentient beings not suffer from this ailment? Caoshan said, "If all sentient beings were to suffer from this ailment, they would no longer be sentient beings.
"I wonder, do the Buddhas also have this ailment? Caoshan said, "They do. "If they have it, why do they not suffer from the ailment? Caoshan said, "Because they are lucidly aware."
Chan Master Huizang of Shigong, Fuzhou.
Originally, he made his living as a hunter and held a deep aversion toward śramaṇas.
Once, while chasing a deer, he passed before Mazu’s hermitage. Mazu then went out to meet him. The Master asked, "Did you see the deer pass by? Mazu replied:
[The Master] asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am a hunter. The Master said, "Are you skilled at archery? He replied, "I am skilled at archery.
The Master said, "With one arrow, how many do you shoot? He replied, "With one arrow, I shoot one. The Master said, "Then you do not understand archery.
[The hunter] asked, "Does the Master understand archery? The Master said, "I do. [The hunter] asked, "With one arrow, how many do you shoot? The Master said, "With one arrow, I shoot a whole flock."
The monk said, "This is life and that is life. Why shoot at a flock of them? The Patriarch said, "Since you know it is thus, why do you not shoot yourself?
The monk said, "If you were to have me shoot myself, I would truly have no place to begin.

The Patriarch said, "This fellow’s ignorance and afflictions from kalpas past are today suddenly extinguished. The Master cast down his bow and arrows and entered the Patriarch’s community to leave the household life. (Xuedou Xian said:)

"Master Ma’s one arrow for a whole flock—though he shot with skillful precision, what use is there in it? It is not as good as Shigong’s one arrow for a single bird; he was truly a master of his craft. Today, Xuedou emulates the deeds of the ancients and intends to release an arrow.

He shouts out, "Watch the arrow! and then says, "It has hit the mark. Qingliang Qin said: "Tell me, what is the principle behind shooting one arrow at a flock? Truly, even the life-force of the three thousand great thousandfold world-systems would not require more than a single arrow.

Cuiyan Zhi said: "Master Ma’s one arrow for a flock is still not quite perfect. This mountain monk shoots one arrow at all moving and sentient beings, and there is none that does not hit. Even so, this only accounts for half; the other half remains for you all."

[The] Elder said: One day, while [the Master] was performing manual labor in the kitchen, the Patriarch asked, "What are you doing? He replied, "I am tending oxen. The Patriarch asked, "How do you tend them?
He replied, "Whenever they go into the grass, I pull them back by the nose. The Patriarch said, "You truly know how to tend oxen. The Master then ceased [speaking].
After the Master established his own residence, he constantly used the bow and arrow to test and engage practitioners (as recorded in the *Sanping Zhang*). The Master asked Xi...
The Master said, "West Hall, do you still understand how to seize empty space? West Hall replied, "I can seize it. The Master asked, "How do you seize it?
West Hall reached out his hand and grasped at the air. The Master said, "You do not know how to seize it. West Hall then asked, "Brother Teacher, how do you seize it?
The Master grabbed West Hall by the nostrils and pulled. West Hall let out a cry of pain and said, "You are pulling too hard!"
The man’s nostrils were as if about to fall out. The Master said, "You must grasp empty space in this very way before you will succeed. (Tianqi Rui said:

"Had he been able to perform the 'lion's backward leap' at that moment, Hui-zang would have had his bones ground to powder. It was all because he leaned against the wall and relied on the fence that he met with such a deadly blow. What a pity that although [the Master] exerted every effort to uphold the truth, it is rare to encounter one who understands it. Today, let us speak face-to-face.)

"Is there anyone who has attained universal penetration? As for this mountain monk, speaking thus with a mouth full of words—how is it? (The sword leaves its precious sheath because of injustice; the medicine comes from the golden jar to save the sick.)
Chan Master Lanrang of Jiangxi.
Elder Liang of Hutang asked, "I have heard that you, elder brother, have painted a portrait of our late master;
I would like to request permission to pay my respects. The Master opened his chest with both hands to reveal it to him. Liang then bowed. The Master said:
The Master said, "Do not prostrate; do not prostrate. Huilang said, "Brother, you are mistaken. I am not prostrating to my brother.
The Master said, "You are prostrating to your late teacher, Zhenan. Huilang asked, "Why did you tell me not to prostrate? The Master said, "How could I have been mistaken?"
Chan Master Daoming of Nanyuan in Yuanzhou.
Entering the hall, the Master said: "A swift horse needs but one lash; a swift man needs but one word.
If there is something, why not come forward? If there is nothing, each of you take care. A monk asked, "What about that one word? The Master then—
He stuck out his tongue and said, "Wait until I possess the mark of the broad and long tongue; then I shall speak to you.
Dongshan went on a pilgrimage and ascended to the Dharma Hall. The Master said, "We have already met. Dongshan then descended. The next day, he ascended again and asked:
"Yesterday, I was already graced by the Master’s compassion. I do not know where it was that we had already met.
The Master said, "Mind after mind, without interruption, flows into the ocean of nature. Dongshan said, "How could I have let this pass?"
Dongshan took his leave. The Master said, "Study the Buddha-dharma extensively and bring great benefit to others. Dongshan said, "I do not ask about studying the Buddha-dharma extensively;
what is meant by bringing great benefit? The Master said, "Do not oppose a single thing."
Chan Master Hong’en of Zhongyi in Langzhou:
Whenever a monk arrived, he would snap his fingers and make the sound "he-he.
When Yangshan came to receive the precepts, the Master likewise snapped his fingers and made the sound "he-he. As Yangshan moved from west to east, the Master snapped his fingers again.
[The Master] made the sound "he-he. Yangshan moved from east to west; the Master again clapped his mouth and made the sound "he-he.
Yangshan stood in the center, and only then did he receive the precepts. The Master asked, "Where did you obtain this samādhi? Yangshan said:
[This] was transmitted from Caoxi upon the seal. The Master asked, "You say that at Caoxi, he used this samādhi to receive what kind of person?
Yangshan said, "To receive Yixiu Jue. The Master asked, "Where did you, Reverend, obtain this samādhi?"
The Master said, "I attained this samādhi under Master Madaishi" (Langye Huijue said: "Do not speak of your sorrows to one who is already sorrowful").
Yangshan asked again, "How can one realize the meaning of seeing the Buddha-nature? The Master said, "I will give you a parable.
Suppose there is a room with six windows, and inside there is a monkey. Outside, there is another monkey. From the east side, someone calls out, 'O gibbon!'"

The gibbon immediately responded. Thus, when called from all six windows, it responded from each. Yangshan bowed in thanks and said as he rose, "I have now understood everything through the Master’s analogy.
Yet there is one further matter: if the inner monkey has fallen asleep while the outer monkey wishes to meet with him, what then?
The Master descended from his rope-platform bed, took Yangshan by the hand, and danced with him.
He said: "Once the *xingxing* (monkeys) have seen you, it is like a tiny *jiaoming* insect building a nest upon the eye-lashes of a mosquito, crying out at a crossroads:
'The land is vast and people are few; those who meet are rare. (Yunju Xi said:

"If Zhongyi had not received this single phrase from Yangshan at that time, where would there be a Zhongyi? (Chongshou Chou said: "Is there anyone who can settle this principle? If one cannot settle it, it is merely the handiwork of one playing with their own spirit. Buddha.
"Where does the meaning of 'nature' reside? Xuangjue then said, "If it were not for Yangshan, how could one have seen Zhongyi? But tell me, where is it that Yangshan saw Zhongyi?"
Chan Master Changer of Lestam, Hongzhou.
When Nanquan arrived and saw the Master sitting with his face against the wall, he patted the Master on the back.

Chan Master Wuye of Fenzhou was a native of the Du family from Shangluo in Shangzhou. He heard that the Gate of Chan under the Great Master Mazu was like the cauldron of state affairs.

Ding Sheng went specifically to pay his respects. Seeing that the Master’s appearance was extraordinary and magnificent, and that his voice resonated like a bell, Ding remarked, "This is a lofty Buddhist hall, yet there is no Buddha within it.
