"Can one turn a single breath back to obtain the entirety of the Great Canon? The Master said, "What kind of *bi-luo* (turnip cake) mold do you have? Bring it here quickly! (Jingshan Gao said:
"At the fifth watch, rising before dawn, there are still travelers on the night road. Question: "What is the teaching of the entire lifetime?
The Master said, "Shang Daren Qiu Yiji. Question: "What is Chan? The Master said, "A fierce fire frying with oil."
A monk came for an audience. The Master asked, "Are you a newly arrived monk? He replied, "I am. The Master said, "Can you let go of this entanglement? He replied, "I cannot.
The Master said, "Carrying your shackles and presenting your petition, go out by yourself. The monk then departed. The Master called out, "Come here!
I ask you truly: where have you come from? He replied, "From Jiangxi. The Master said, "The Abbot of Letan is on your back."
[Later,] fearing that you would speak recklessly, did you see it? The monk had no reply. ○ While [the Master] was reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, a monk asked, "What sūtra are you reading?
The Master said, "The Great Radiant Clouds; the Blue Radiant Clouds; the Purple Radiant Clouds.
He then pointed to what was before him and said, "What kind of cloud is that over there? [The monk] said, "It is black clouds to the south. The Master said, "Today, you must..."
A monk named Yuweng asked, "The character 'yi' (以) is not formed; the character 'ba' (八) is not correct. What chapter or phrase is this?
The Master snapped his fingers once and said, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The infinite superior causes of the lectures and praises above—look!

A frog leaps up into the sky; an earthworm dashes across the Eastern Sea. (Jingshan Gaofeng said: This monk asked only about the first character of the scripture, yet Muzhou treated it as if he were fully proficient in all the various arts.)

The *Zilun* (Wheel of Characters). Using the *Longkan Shoujian*, the *Tangyun*, and the *Yupian*, I have annotated it from beginning to end and placed it within this monk’s breast. This monk is truly extraordinary; he immediately accepts and takes responsibility for it. But tell me, where is the place of his acceptance?

Listen to these annotations: "The character 'yi' is not formed; the character 'ba' is not present. Before a finger-snap has even ended, it pervades heaven and earth. Striking open the forty-two gates of the *Prajñāpāramitā*, one penetrates the assembly at the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* where "Skill in All Arts" is taught.

Teachings internal and external are gathered at once; both mundane and supramundane matters are fully provided for. Boundless transgressions are like ice melting in fire; immeasurable supreme meanings are like a heap of Ganges sands. Furthermore, there is a final phrase: the "Secure Treasury."

Permanently preserved. Entirely for Xiong Bozhuang of Shanshan. Chushi Qi said: "What is the first character at the beginning of the sutra? Muzhou snapped his fingers once, thereby [revealing] that which the Yellow-Faced Old Man could not exhaustively explain in forty-nine years.

At one time, he revealed it all. Miaoxi added a point to what was already sharp, saying: "There is yet one final phrase; do you all understand it thoroughly? After a long silence, Shan Duanyi said, "I shall rest here, having put my doubts to rest. Feng Gaoyou then rose up. Tianqichao said:

This monk was skilled at answering but unskilled at questioning; Luzhou was skilled at questioning but unskilled at answering. One who is skilled at questioning holds a night-bright talisman in hand—how many know when the dawn breaks? One who is skilled at answering knows only that the iron spine props up the heavens, but does not realize the crown of the head touches the earth.

"If it were this mountain monk, I would have struck him on the spine as soon as he hesitated and driven him out the door. [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? He replied, "Hebei. The Master said:
"In that place there was Master Zhaozhou; have you ever been there? The monk replied, "I left that place not long ago.
The Master asked, "What words did Zhaozhou use to instruct his disciples? The monk recounted the story of the tea. The Master then laughed heartily and said:
The monk felt ashamed and asked, "What was Zhaozhou’s meaning? The Master said, "It was merely a provisional expedient for the occasion. The Master continued, "Alas!
Zhaozhou has been splashed with a ladle of filth by you! He then struck him. The Master then asked the novice, "How do you understand this?
The novice immediately prostrated himself. The Master struck him as well. Later, the monk went to the novice and asked about what had just occurred.
"The Master comes to beat you; what are you doing? The śrāmaṇera said, "If it were not for my Master, he would not have beaten me.

(Xuedou Xian said: "This monk is truly intolerable! He takes a ladle of filth and splashes two ancient Buddhas. If you, venerable seniors, can discern this, not only will you clear the injustice for the two prefectures of Zhao and Mu, but Xuedou and all the old masters under heaven will likewise be cleared of fault.

If you cannot say it, you will continue to splash people everywhere until the end of time. (Jingshan Daokai said: "Xuedou only knows that a ladle of filth was splashed upon the two prefectures of Zhao and Mu; he does not realize that this monk..."

At that time, he was splashed with a ladle of excrement by Zhaozhou; yet when he arrived at Muzhou, he suffered another ladle. It was simply that he did not know the "fragrance" (the true essence). Had he known the fragrance, where would there be two ancient Buddhas?

Chushi Qi said: "This monk did not understand the intent of drinking tea; he did not know the fragrance of the excrement. He brings misfortune upon good people by falling into a pit of filth. How many blows of the staff does he deserve? Xuedou and Miaoxi let him off with one stroke, but they ought to have escorted him into the Nirvana Hall for him.
A newly arrived monk came to pay his respects. Just as he was about to prostrate, the Master rebuked him, saying: "Disciple, why have you stolen the monastery's fruit?"
The disciple ate it. He said, "I have only just arrived; why did the Master say I was stealing fruit? The Master replied, "The stolen goods are right here.
Chan Master Qianqing Chunan (Dharma heir of Huangbo Xiyun).
Chan Master Chunan of Mount Qianqing in Hangzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Fuzhou. He first visited Rong (Furong Daokai), who looked at him and said, "I am not your teacher;
your teacher is Huangbo, who is beyond the rivers to the north. The Master bowed in farewell and subsequently went to visit Huangbo.
Huangbo asked, "How is it when you have not yet manifested the reflections of the triple world? The Master replied, "Is this not the very moment?"
"Is there? Huangbo said, "Setting aside for a moment whether there is or not, how is it right now? The Master said, "Neither present nor past.
Huangbo said, "The Dharma-eye of my lineage is already within you."
Chan Master Lingguan of Mount Wushi (Dharma Heir of Huangbo Yun).
Chan Master Lingguan of Mount Wushi in Fuzhou (commonly known as Old Guan) usually kept his door bolted, so few people saw him.
Only one lay devotee would arrive at mealtime to deliver offerings, at which point the master would open the door. One day, Xuefeng waited for an opportunity and knocked on the gate; the Master—
He opened the door. Xuefeng suddenly grabbed him by the chest and said, "Are you an ordinary man or a sage?
The Master spat at him and said, "You wild fox spirit! He then pushed him out and closed the door. Xuefeng said, "I only wanted to recognize my elder brother.
Later, because Xuefeng came to knock on the door, the Master asked, "Who is it? Xuefeng said, "The phoenix chick. The Master asked, "What are you doing here? Xuefeng said, [nothing further].
When Xuefeng came to visit Old Guan, the Master opened the door, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! Xuefeng hesitated; the Master then pushed him away and closed the door.
Later, after Xuefeng had established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "If I had been able to enter Old Guan’s gate at that time..."
"You lot, you wine-dregs eaters! Where are you searching? (The Old Master said: "Xuefeng has these words, but at that time he could not enter.")

Now, as for "entering and not being able [to enter]," Mingzhao Qian spoke on behalf of Xuefeng: As soon as he saw the door open, he said, "To move is to perish. He also spoke on behalf of Laogan, saying, "How brilliant! How brilliant! Xuedou Xian said, "This man who betrays kindness and repays virtue—what connection has he to the matter?

If at that time he could not enter, was it ever intended to teach you how to enter? Now that you cannot find him by groping about, you are merely bringing blame upon Xuefeng; both were under the guidance of Laogan. While clearing away weeds, he asked a monk, "Where are you going?
The monk replied, "I am going to West Monastery to pay my respects to Master An. At that moment, there was a green [object] atop a bamboo.
[The Master] points to a snake and says, "If you wish to recognize the old wild fox spirit of West Cloister, it is simply this.
A monk asks, "What kind of thing can be placed upon this plot of ground at West Cloister? West Cloister replies, "A Buddha without form would be well-placed there.
The Master says, "That fine piece of ground has been defiled by you, brother, with your filth. While [the Master] was drawing noodles, a monk came for an audience. The Master drew [a line].
The Master showed him some noodles. The monk then departed. At evening, the Master asked his junior attendant, "Where did that monk go just now? The junior attendant replied, "He left immediately.

The Master said, "It is true that he left, but he only obtained one peg. (Xuedou Xian said: "Old Guan seems almost like someone who loses his money and suffers for it. Baoci Shui said: "Where is it that he is short by one peg?

Cuiyan Zhi said: "Old Guan says he only obtained one peg; this is much like forcing the virtuous to become lowly. Both are sons of the Buddha who have left the household life. Dongchan Guan [commented].

[The Master] said: "In general, this monk resembles that one. The entrustment at Vulture Peak has its place. Why did Old Guan say, 'He only obtained a single fragment'? Do you wish to understand? If you do not pay the price, how can you distinguish the true from the false?
When Caoshan was traveling on pilgrimage, he asked: "What is the Dharma-body Lord, the Vairocana Teacher? The Master said: "If I were to tell you..."
This refers to a distinct existence. Caoshan related this to Dongshan. Dongshan said, “What an excellent *huatou*!
It only lacks a follow-up question. Why not ask, ‘Why do you not speak? Caoshan then came forward and posed the subsequent question.
The Master said, “If I say ‘I do not speak,’ I would have my mouth gagged. If I say ‘I do speak,’ I would have my tongue tied. Caoshan returned.
He brought this up to Dongshan, who deeply approved of it.
Chan Master Zongche of Luohan Temple (a dharma heir of Huangbo Yun):
Chan Master Zongche of Luohan Temple in Hangzhou was a native of the Wu family in Huzhou. He ascended the hall. A monk asked: "How [is it]?"
"This is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West. The Master said, "The bones are crushed. The Master frequently used this phrase in response to various occasions;
thus, he was known at the time as "Master Bone-Crusher" (Gucuò Heshang).
The Layman Pei Xiu, Minister of State (Dharma-heir of Huangbo Yun).
The Layman Pei Xiu, courtesy name Gongmei, was a native of Wenxi in Hedong. While serving as the Governor of Xin’an, he encountered Master Yun.
Initially, at Mount Huangbo in Lingnan, [Master Yun] had left the monastic community to enter the Da’an Monastery, where he mingled with the laborers.
[The Master] swept and sprinkled the hall. When the Duke entered the temple to burn incense, the administrative official received him with due respect.

As they were observing the murals on the wall, the Duke asked, "What figures are depicted here? The official replied, "These are the true portraits of eminent monks. The Duke said, "The portraits may indeed be viewed, but where are the eminent monks themselves?
The official was unable to answer. The Duke asked, "Are there any practitioners of Chan here? [The official] replied, "Recently, there was a monk who..."

The temple attendants were quite like Zen practitioners. The Duke said, "May I invite him here to question him? Thereupon, he immediately sought out Huangbo. Upon seeing him, the Duke said with delight, "Enough!
I have a question, but the various masters were stingy with their words. Now I request the Master to provide a single response on my behalf.
Huangbo said, "I pray the Duke will pose his question. The Duke repeated the previous story, and Huangbo—

He called out in a loud voice, "Pai Xiu! The Master responded, "Yes. Huangbo asked, "Where are you? At that moment, the official understood the meaning, as if he had found the jewel within his topknot.
He said, "My teacher is truly a good spiritual friend; his instruction of others is so direct and precise.

From then on, he invited him into the government offices and performed the rites of a disciple. Although the Master repeatedly declined, the official pressed his invitation with persistence until he finally agreed to reside at Mount Huangbo. There was...
Whenever there was leisure, [Huangbo] would personally enter the mountain peak to pay his respects; sometimes he would invite him into the prefectural seat.

Since Master Pei had thoroughly penetrated the intent of the Patriarchs and was furthermore extensively versed in the characteristics of the various teachings, the Chan scholars of all quarters unanimously remarked: "Master Pei has not emerged from Huangbo’s gate for no reason."
Chan Master Dazui Fazhen (Dharma Heir of Changqing An).
Chan Master Dazui Fazhen of Yizhou was a native of the Wang family from Zizhou. He traveled south, where he first visited Yaoshan, Daowu, Yunyan, and Dongshan.
Subsequently, he went to the assembly of Damei outside the Ling Mountains, remaining there for several years. His food did not suffice to fill him, and he slept...
He did not seek warmth; he refined his practice through austerity and his conduct was beyond the common. Mount Gui (Miaoshan) held him in deep esteem.
One day, Miaoshan asked him, "While you have been here in my presence, Senior Monk, you have never asked a single turning word.
The Master replied, "Where would you have me begin? Miaoshan said, "Why do you not ask, 'What is the Buddha? The Master then made a gesture with his hand and covered [his mouth].
At Mount Gui, Mount Gui sighed and said, "My son has truly attained the marrow. From this, his fame spread throughout the four seas.

A monk asked, "When the kalpa-fire blazes forth and the great trichiliocosm is utterly destroyed, I wonder: does this [reality] perish or not? The Master said, "It perishes. The monk said, "If that is so, then it follows along with it.
The Master said, "It follows along with it. The monk did not accept this. Later, he went to Touzi and raised the same question.
In the previous account, Touzi prepared incense and paid respects from afar, saying, "An ancient Buddha has appeared in Western Sichuan.
He said to the monk, "Return quickly and repent. When the monk returned to Daisui, the Master had already passed away. The monk went back to Touzi, but Touzi had also passed away.
Beside the hermitage was a tortoise. The monk asked, "All sentient beings are skin wrapping bone; what about this one?"
"Sentient beings are nothing but skin wrapped around bones. The Master picked up his straw sandals and covered them over the back of a tortoise.

The monk remained silent. (Jingshan Xing said: "Do you understand? Great Master Suí picked up his straw sandals and covered the black tortoise; it was not out of a kind heart. This monk was speechless, his mouth like a millstone. The verse says: Skin wraps the bone, and bone wraps the skin; picking up straw sandals, he covers the black tortoise.

Blown by the wind and baked by the sun, there is nothing at all; he does not fear people coming to question him. He asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "I am going to Mount Emei to pay homage to Samantabhadra."
The Master raised his whisk and said, "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are both right here.

A monk drew a circle, tossed it behind him, and then prostrated. The Master called to his attendant, "Bring a cup of tea for this monk. Baofu Zhan said, "If he had not spoken those final words, one would have laughed at that monk.

Yungmen Yuan said instead, "In the West they cut off heads and arms; here, take your own lead and go out. Wuzu Ji said, "Great Sui did not gain a single bit of wisdom because of a single matter. Xuedou Xian said, "The sword that kills and the staff that gives life."

The Man and the Sword. Discern it with the eye of realization. Taisu Xiu said: "Daisui’s tea is not of the same kind as Zhaozhou’s tea. Since it is not of the same kind as Zhaozhou’s tea, those who obtain it are few. This monk has obtained it; yet what excellence does he possess? However, ill-gotten wealth is to me like floating clouds.

Tiantong Jue said: "One who knows the Dharma fears; one who deceives the enemy perishes. To discern milk in water, one must be a king of geese. [The Master] was sitting in the hall while the assembly of monks was in attendance.
The Master made a gesture with his mouth as if suffering from a wind ailment and said, "Is there anyone who can cure my mouth?
The monks vied with one another to send him medicine, and when the laypeople heard of this, they also sent much medicine. The Master accepted none of it.
After seven days, the Master pinched his own mouth to straighten it and said, "For so long a time, I have been drumming on these two pieces of skin; until now, no one has cured me."
He attained [enlightenment] and then sat upright and passed away.
Regarding Chan Master Rumen of Lingshu (a successor of Changqing An):
Chan Master Rumen of Lingshu was from Min. A nun presented a ceramic bowl to the Master, whom the Master [took].
Qingyuan asked, "From what does this emerge? Dongshan said, "It emerges from Dingzhou. (Qingliang Qin’s variant says: "It does not deviate from here. The Master then smashed [the bowl] to pieces;
the nun had no reply. (Baofu Zhan spoke on her behalf, saying: "He who deceives his enemy perishes. When the Prince of Guang was about to mobilize his army, he went in person to visit the monastery.

"Please let the Master decide what is right and wrong. The Master already knew this beforehand; he sat peacefully and passed away. The ruler of Guang was angry and asked the administrator, "When did the Abbot fall ill?
He replied, "He never fell ill. Just now, he sealed a letter and instructed me to present it to Your Majesty."
When the Lord of Guang opened the casket, he found a note that read: "The Eye of the Human and Heavenly Eyes; the Head Seat within the Hall.
The Lord of Guang realized the Master’s intent and consequently ceased hostilities. He then summoned the First Seat to open the hall and preach the Dharma (who was Yunmen Wenyan).
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin (Dharma heir of Changqing An).
Chan Master Lingyun Zhiqin of Fuzhou was a native of Changxi in that same province. Initially at Mount Gui, he attained enlightenment upon seeing peach blossoms.
He composed a verse which said: "For thirty years I have sought the swordsman; How many times have fallen leaves withered and sprouted anew?"
Zhi: "Ever since I first beheld the peach blossoms, until this very day I have had no further doubts.

When Guishan read the verse, he interrogated him regarding his realization and found it to be in perfect accord with the truth. Guishan said, "Having attained awakening through conditions, you shall never again fall back or lose it.

Guard and maintain it well yourself. (A monk later recounted this to Xuansha Shibei. Xuansha said, "How accurate! How very accurate! Yet I dare guarantee that you, elder brother, have not yet reached the ultimate end. The assembly doubted these words, so Xuansha asked Dizang, "I spoke thus; what do you think?")

"How do you understand this? Dizang said, "If it were not Guichen, he would have run everyone in the world to death. Changqing Ling asked a monk, "What was the meaning of Xuansha's intent? Changqing said, "I thought the barbarian’s beard was red; yet there is another with a red beard.
Cuiyan Zhi said, "Suppose someone were to ask today, 'What was the meaning of Xuansha? Tell me, has this person attained thorough penetration or not? Huanglong Xin said, "Everyone, tell me:

when Lingyun first saw it, was it a peach blossom or was it not a peach blossom? If it were a peach blossom, then everyone in the world who sees it should realize the Way. If it were not a peach blossom, how could it be that he saw a peach blossom? Where would you look for it? How would you explain what it means to 'see'?"

**Li:** Wuzu Yan said, "What do you mean by 'truthful and correct'? Go and practice for another thirty years. **Zhaojue Qin:** A crossbow with a thousand-jin draw does not fire its trigger for a field mouse. Since Lingyun has turned the celestial pivot, and Xuansha has overturned the terrestrial axis, tell me, where was it that he had not yet reached through?

**Jingshan Gao:** When one family has trouble, a hundred families are busy. **Chushih Qi:** If a person lacks far-sighted foresight, they will surely have immediate worries. Even if it were refined gold tempered a hundred times, it could not avoid being placed back in the furnace for further smelting.

**Jinshu Wu:** What need is there to say that when one family has trouble, a hundred families are busy? It is simply like one blind man leading a crowd of blind men. **Jingshan Xin:** Lingyun traveled as a wandering monk for thirty years and did not know [the Way].

"How many straw sandals have you worn out? If your eyes had not been pierced by the peach blossoms, even if you had traveled for another thirty years, it would still not be the end of your suffering. Xuefeng had a verse to send to Shuangfeng:
The final line says: "When the thunder ceases, its sound does not stop. The Master replied: "When the thunder rolls, one hears no sound.
Upon hearing this, Xuefeng said: "On the peak of Lingyun Mountain, the ancient moon appears. Later, Xuefeng asked: "The ancients said, 'Three before, three after.
What is the meaning of this? The Master said: "A fish in the water; a bird in the sky. Xuefeng asked: "What is the meaning of this?"
Sheng said, "The heights can be shot at; the depths can be fished. Changsheng asked, "Before the primordial chaos was divided, from where did sentient beings come?
The Master said, "It is like a pillar conceiving a fetus. [Changsheng] asked, "After the division, what is it like? The Master said, "It is like a fragment of cloud dotting the vast clarity.
[Changsheng] asked, "I wonder, does that vast clarity itself receive the dot? The Master did not answer. [Changsheng] said, "If that is so,"
"Sentient beings do not come," the Master replied, yet he did not answer further. [The monk] asked, "What is it like when one has attained pure clarity, utterly free from a single speck?

The Master said, "This is still the flow of the eternal and constant. [The monk] asked, "What is the flow of the eternal and constant? The Master said, "It is like a mirror that is perpetually bright.
[The monk] asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? The Master said, "There is. [The monk] asked, "What is this matter that lies beyond? The Master—

He said: "Bring me the mirror that has been broken, and I will see you. Bazhao Che said: "As soon as you see each other, it is finished. Furthermore, why break the mirror? Baizhao Yuan said: "If you do not break the mirror, how can you see each other?

Dayang Yan said: "It is already broken right now. Moreover, how do you see each other? He then said: "The illumination is exhausted and the essence has no dependence; the whole body is difficult to discern. Kaifu Ning said: "Excellent, all you Zen adepts!

Throughout the entire realm of the ten directions, there is but one mirror. How can you speak of the principle of 'breaking' it? Even if you were to have eyes that see clearly and hands that act with skill, such that light and object are both forgotten—like a hen brooding her eggs and the chick pecking at the shell simultaneously—you would still be fit to receive the retribution of Baoci."

[Zhaozhou] held up his staff. Why? "Zen practitioners who play with shadows are like hemp or millet. Huanglong Zhong said: "These two venerable masters revealed the great matter of their own division; it may be called 'cutting and rubbing,' 'carving and polishing.

It is not that they were not authentic, but when examined closely, it is very much like a sweatshirt pressed against the skin—it has not yet reached the state of total liberation. This causes certain types of people to produce interpretations based on words, calculating from the time before differentiation, or explaining principles at the point where the mirror was broken;

when will they ever attain realization? According to my view as Muan, what need is there to speak of the Chaos being divided or undivided, or the mirror being broken or not broken? Even if you understand it at the place where the pillar is pregnant, it is merely a single cloud dotting the vast clarity. Do you all truly understand?"

Simha said, "Wait until space falls to the ground, and then I will tell you. Tiantong Jue said: "Whether divided or undivided, the jade mechanism moves at night; whether marked or unmarked, the golden shuttle is cast in secret.

Even if it is a single color of pure clarity, one has not yet attained a ten-fold stable seat. But tell me, once the mirror is shattered, where do you meet him? Do you understand? When the old hare swallows the light in the clear autumn, and the azure dragon sheds its bones in the profound waters.
He asked a monk, "Where are you going? The monk replied, "To Xuefeng. The Master said, "I have a message to send to Xuefeng; would you take it? The monk said, "Please give it to me. The Master—
He took off one sandal and tossed it before him. The monk then departed for Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from?
He replied, "From Lingyun. Xuefeng asked, "Is Lingyun well? He said, "He has a message to entrust to you. Xuefeng asked, "Where is it?
The monk took off his other sandal and tossed it before Xuefeng. Xuefeng then desisted. (Wuishan Xiu said: Since Xuefeng did not...)

He was able to discern the essential point of the other’s letter. Yet this monk only knew how to follow a mold and copy a pattern; he left Lingyun hanging. Had Lingyun suddenly said at that time, "I have a letter to send him," and when the monk replied, "Please give it to me," Lingyun had simply remained seated.
How could this monk have conveyed the message? A true man of great capacity should act as a messenger for others; he must not leave another with not a single word to utter.
Chan Master Shijie of Mount Shou (a successor of Changqing An).
Chan Master Shijie of Mount Shou in Fuzhou once attended upon Dongshan. Dongshan asked, "Where is your place of origin, Lay Brother?

Chan Master Wenju of Guohuan (Dharma Heir of Changqing An).
Chan Master Wenju Huirì of Chongfu Monastery in Guohuan, Quanzhou. A native of the Huang family of Fuzhou, he was born with extraordinary qualities.
Upon reaching adulthood, he served as a jailer in the county prison; however, he frequently abandoned his duties to go to the Venerable Shenguang of Guan and to the West.
At the residence of Chan Master Yuan'an, the officials were unable to restrain him. Later, he visited Chan Master Tantong at the Wansui Pagoda to have his hair shaved;
however, he did not don the *kāṣāya* robe nor receive full ordination, wearing instead a sash made of various colored silks.
He then went to Shenguang, who said, "I am not your teacher; go and pay homage to Xiyuan. Carrying a small green bamboo staff, the Master entered Xiyuan.
In the Dharma Hall of the West Courtyard, Yaoyuan saw him from afar and said with a smile, "Go enter the Nirvana Hall. The Master responded with an "Amen" and entered while rolling his bamboo staff.
At that time, there were about five hundred monks suffering from the seasonal epidemic; as the Master pointed at them one by one with his staff, each rose as soon as he was touched.
Master Fuyang of Taizhou (a successor of Changqing An).
When Xuefeng arrived with his assembly and asked, "There are currently two hundred people staying here for the summer retreat;
is this permissible? The Master took up his staff, drew a line, and said, "It cannot be. Xuefeng then desisted.
Chan Master Wen-shu Yuan-ming (Dharma heir of Changqing An).

Chan Master Yuan-ming of Wenshu Monastery in Guangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Fuzhou. Having attained the essential meaning under Daomai, he later traveled to Xuefeng to seek further instruction;
the Dharma remained of one flavor. He once visited Mount Wutai and beheld a manifested transformation of Mañjuśrī. Thereupon—

Temples were established in various locations, with "Mañjuśrī" inscribed upon their nameplates. During the Kaibao era, Li Chonggu, the Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was touring and protecting the southern regions.
Upon entering a temple, he beheld an image of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and asked a monk, "Why does Kṣitigarbha extend his hand?"
The monk said, "The pearl in your hand has been stolen by a thief. Chongju then asked the Master, "Since you are Dizang, why were you robbed?
The Master replied, "I have caught him today. Chongju bowed in thanks.

Venerable Master Yan’yang Shanxin (Dharma Heir of Zhaozhou Shen). Venerable Master Yan’yang of Xinxing in Hongzhou was named Shanxin. Initially, he went to consult Zhaozhou, who asked him: "When you bring nothing at all, what then? Zhaozhou said: "Put it down. The Master said: "Since I am bringing nothing at all, what is there to put down? Zhaozhou said: "If you can't even put it down, pick it up! At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Later, while traveling through the mountains, he encountered a tiger. He called out to the tiger, saying: "Tiger, tiger! Do you have the Buddha-nature? The tiger roared and departed. When people asked about this, the Master said: "I was testing the tiger; the tiger did not test me. He later resided at Yan’yang Mountain. One day, a monk asked: "What is the Way? The Master replied: "A stone dog barks at the sky. The monk asked: "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied: "The cat has nine lives. "What do you set down? Zhaozhou replied, "If you cannot put it down, carry it away. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. A snake and a tiger often followed him, taking food from his hand.
(As Huanglong Nan’s verse says: "Not bringing a single thing; unable to bear it on two shoulders.

Suddenly realizing one's error at these words, there is boundless joy in the heart. Having cast aside malice, the snake and tiger become friends. Several hundred years have passed, yet the pure breeze remains. After he took up residence [at the monastery], a monk asked:
"What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A clod of earth. "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The earth is shaking.
"What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Eating porridge and eating rice. [Another] asked, "What is the water of Xinxing? The Master said, "The river right before you. (Jingshan Daokai said:

"A teaching such as this is like a child’s play. Only by entering such a teaching can one find peace and joy. As for Master Zhenjing, he took up and handled the teachings of the past and present; [he did not do so in this manner].")

Below Xuedou, the later traditions and practices have instead become mere verbal abuse. Small-minded practitioners do nothing but ask, "How did the Ancients act? or "What words did Zhenru use? or "What words did Yangqi use? You have no business meddling in such idle matters.

To cure an illness, one does not need medicine carried on a donkey. If one can match the medicine to the specific ailment, even a single blade of grass picked up at the base of a fence can heal the disease. What need is there to speak of cinnabar, *achyranthes*, ginseng, or *atractylodes*?
Chan Master Huiguang Huijue (Dharma heir of Zhaozhou Shen).
Chan Master Huiguang of Guangxiao Monastery in Yangzhou asked the State Councilor Song Qiqiu, "Do you understand how to speak?"
Qichou said, "If it is such a Way, one cannot attach to it. The Master said, "Whether it is 'is' or 'is not,' one cannot attach to it.
Qichou said, "It is not like that at all. The Master said, "What about that which cannot be attached to?
Qichou had no reply. The Master arrived at Chongshou. Fayan asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master said, "Zhaozhou. Fayan said, "I have heard..."
[The student] asked, "I have heard that Zhaozhou has the story about the cypress tree in the courtyard; is this true? The Master said, "No.
Fayen said, "Everyone who comes and goes says that when a monk asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, 'The cypress tree in the courtyard.'"
"Venerable Elder, how can you say it does not exist? The Master said, "The former master truly did not say such a thing. Preceptor, do not slander the former master. (Jingshan Gao said:
"If one says these words exist, one misses Jue Tiezui; if one says these words do not exist, one again misses Fayan. If one does not involve oneself with either side, one again misses Zhaozhou.

Even if one were to find another way through that is neither of these, one would enter hell like a shot arrow. (Gushan Gui said: "Jue Tiezui’s name was not given in vain; he simply never dreamed of Zhaozhou. (Chushih Qi said: "The Patriarch came from the West...")

"Intention! The cypress tree in the courtyard—this story has already circulated throughout the world. For what reason did Jue Tiezui say, 'The former master did not say this'? Among the assembly, there are often discussions suggesting that Zhaozhou’s words were merely a provisional expedient for a specific occasion."

One must not take this as a literal explanation. Thus it is said that there is none; such a chaotic reckoning slanders the ancient Buddhas no small amount. Miaoxi said: "If you say these words exist, you have missed Jue Tiezui; if you say these words do not exist, you have again missed Fayen."
"If you say the Way does not involve either side, you have missed Zhaozhou again. Today, there is no fishing in the misty waves; there is no need for a new crescent moon to serve as a hook.
A worldly man asked, "I have slaughtered oxen all my life; do I still incur sin? The Master said, "No sin. The man asked, "Why is there no sin?
The Master said, "For every one killed, one is returned."
Chan Master Muchen Conglang (Dharma Heir of Zhaozhou Shen).
Chan Master Muchen Conglang of Wuzhou once fell over. A monk asked, "Since it is the indestructible diamond body, why has it fallen over?
The Master struck the meditation seat and said, "Walking, standing, sitting, and lying down."
Master Duofu of Hangzhou (Dharma heir of Zhaozhou Sheng).
A monk asked, "What is the single cluster of bamboo at Duofu? The Master said, "One stalk, two stalks, leaning.
The monk said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "Three stalks, four stalks, curved. (Jingshan Hongzhi said: "Even if you have one stalk, two stalks...")
"Bent in three or four places, yet still my many-blessed cluster of bamboo—how can you explain this?
Master Ximù of Yizhou (a dharma heir of Zhāozhōu Cànshèn) ascended the hall.
A layman raised his hand and said, "The Master himself is already one head."
The layman said, "Donkey. The Master replied, "I, an old monk, have been ridden by you. The layman departed speechless.
Three days later, he returned and said, "The other day, I was robbed by bandits. The Master picked up his staff and drove him out.
Chan Master Changtong of Xuedou (Dharma heir of Chena of Changsha).
Chan Master Changtong of Xuedou in Mingzhou was a native of the Li clan from Xingzhou. He visited Changsha, who asked, "Where are you from?
The Master replied, "A man from Xingzhou. Changsha said, "I say you did not come from there. The Master said, "Indeed..."
"Has Shang ever lived here before? Changsha agreed with this and allowed him to enter the room.
As for Master Shengguang of Taizhou (a dharma heir of Zihu Cong):
when Master Longhua Zhao came to visit, the Master seized him and asked, "How is it? Longhua...
Longhua said, "Do not err. The Master then let go of his hand. Longhua said, "I have long admired your supreme radiance. The Master remained silent.
Longhua then took his leave and escorted him to the gate, saying, "After this parting, where shall we meet? Longhua laughed heartily and departed.
Master Rirong Yuan (Dharma heir of Zihu Zong).
When the Senior Monk Huo came to visit him, the Master clapped his hands three times and said, "A fierce tiger stands in the gateway."
“Who is the adversary? Huo said, “A fine hawk soars toward the heavens; who can catch it?
The Master said, “Both are difficult to overcome. Huo said, “Let us stop for now; there is no need to settle this public case. The Master took his staff and danced back to his quarters;

Huo was speechless. The Master said, “This fellow is dead! (Zhaojue Qin said: When strength is equal and power is balanced, it is not without merit that they face each other head-on. With eyes keen and hands discerning, neither side gains any advantage. In the end...)

It is a pity he let him go. Had he waited until the other had finished his staff-dance and returned to the abbot’s quarters, he should have clapped his hands three times and swept his sleeves away, departing immediately. Not only would the beginning and end have been complete, but he would also have avoided being subjected to others' critical scrutiny.

Even so, Master Huo was speechless; could he still have turned the situation around? As it is said: "When dawn breaks early, there are still travelers on the road. Daowei Zhi said: "Among the powerful, there are those even more powerful;

in all the world, there is originally no number one person. Do you know? He has no skill at all; Pāpīyas has lost his way. Reaching this point, there is nowhere for you to find understanding. Examine this for yourself!
Venerable Daowu of Guannan in Xiangzhou (Dharma Heir of Chang of Guannan).
When Venerable Daowu of Guannan in Xiangzhou was first passing through a village, he heard a shamanist musician performing for a deity who said, "The spirit knows no self.
Suddenly, he attained awakening. Later, he visited Master Chang, who certified his understanding. He subsequently traveled to the gate of Deshan.
The flavor of the Dharma becomes ever more manifest. Whenever the Master ascends the hall, he wears a lotus-hat, dons a monastic robe, and holds a ritual tablet.

As the drum is struck and the flute is blown, he calls out, "Master Sanlang of Lu. He says, "The spirit knows it; the non-spirit does not know it. Spirit after spirit comes from within emptiness and returns to within emptiness," whereupon he descends from his seat.
At other times he said, "The drum of Guannan is beaten; the song of Deshan is sung. A monk asked:
"What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master took his tally-stick and bowed, saying, "Yes.

At another time, he held a wooden sword across his shoulder and performed a dance. A monk asked, "Where did you get that sword in your hand? The Master threw it to the ground. The monk then placed it back into the Master's hand.
The Master said, "Where did you get it? The monk was speechless. The Master said, "I grant you three days' time."
The Master himself provided a substitute response. Holding a sword across his shoulder, he performed a dance and said: "Only by acting thus can one succeed.
When Zhaozhou visited the Master, the Master was wearing a leopard-skin loincloth and holding a *jiliao* staff.
He stood beneath the main gate, waiting with one foot raised. As soon as he saw Zhaozhou, he shouted a greeting at the top of his voice.

Chan Master Xuanjian of Deshan (Dharma Heir of Longtan Xin), the Fourth Generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Xuanjian of Deshan in Dingzhou was the son of the Zhou family of Jianzhou. He had previously lectured on the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. Later...
Hearing that the Zen seats in the south were flourishing, the Master felt indignant and said,

"If those who have left the household life cannot attain Buddhahood despite studying the Buddha’s majestic deportment for a thousand kalpas and studying the Buddha’s subtle conduct for ten thousand kalpas,

then these demonic offspring in the south dare to speak of 'directly pointing to the human mind' and 'seeing one's nature to become a Buddha. I shall tear open their lair and exterminate their kind, thereby repaying the Buddha's grace."
He then took up his *Qinglong Shuchao* (Commentary on the Blue Dragon) and traveled from Sichuan to Liyang.
On the road, he saw an old woman selling cakes; he rested his shoulder and bought some for a snack. The woman pointed to his pack and asked, "What text is this?

The Master replied, "The *Qinglong Shuchao*. The woman asked, "Which sutra do you lecture upon? The Master said, "The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*. The woman said, "I have a question for you."
"If you say you have it, I will give you a snack; if you say you do not have it, go elsewhere for now. The *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra* says:
"The past mind cannot be apprehended; the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended. I wonder, Elder, which of these minds will you provide as a snack?
The Master remained silent. He then went to Longtan and, upon reaching the Dharma Hall, said: "I have long heard of Longtan."
When he arrived, neither the pool nor the dragon appeared. The Dragon Pool raised its body and said, "You have truly come to the Dragon Pool.

The Master was speechless, and so he settled there to reside. Xuedou Xian said, "He takes the wrong for the right. Yunfeng Yue said, "Great indeed is Deshan; he has been drowned in a jar of pickled vegetables.

Huanglong Xin said, "Xuedou speaks thus, yet he does not know whether it was Deshan who took the wrong for the right, or whether it was Longtan who took the wrong for the right. "You should discern and grasp it. Do you understand its full significance? Even if you were able to plant it, it would not be timber for a great pillar. Jin-su said, "Since it is called 'the pond' yet neither dragon nor manifestation is seen, why do you say, 'You personally arrived at Longtan'?

This is very much like trying to fit a square block into a round hole. Tell me, where exactly was the place of personal arrival? Try to judge this! One evening, while the Master was standing in attendance, Longtan said, "It is deep in the night;

Lungtan held up a candle for his master. As the master reached out to take it, Lungtan blew it out. At this, the master attained great enlightenment and prostrated himself.

On the following day, Lungtan ascended the seat and said to the assembly, "Among you there is a man..."
His teeth are like a forest of swords; his mouth is like a blood-basin. Struck once with my staff, he will not turn back.

he walked from west to east and from east to west, looking back toward the abbot’s quarters and saying, "Is there anything here?

He then held up his whisk and said: “Depart, depart on the road to the Western Heaven; it stretches ten thousand miles and more. He died. A *jiao* dragon does not fear the sword; beneath the sword, its life ends. Although Yantou was within a tiger trap, he possessed his own path of transcendence; on the edge of the blade, there was the opportunity for a somersault.

Yet, if one examines this closely, he still lacks full awakening. Is there anyone here now who can act as a witness for Yantou? Come forth and meet Dahui! After a long silence, he let out a shout and gave a clap. This would have been enough to leave people with lingering doubts and increased ignorance.

Jiaochong Guang said: "Do you know where these three great elders fell? Deshan collapsed with his whole body; Dongshan dragged through water and mud. Had it not been for Yantou, possessing the eye that penetrates all directions and a mechanism beyond the ordinary, how could their merit and valor have been made manifest? But tell me, what is 'one hand'?"

Raising one hand at the point of grasping: it is the sword that kills, the blade that gives life. Chu-shih Chi said: "De-shan’s paws for biting pigs and dogs; Yan-tou’s refined, tempered gold. Meeting head-on, there is no room for evasion. Taking his eight *liang*..."
He obtained half a catty. Although Dongshan was a master, he could only stand by as an onlooker. Why did Miaoxi expend so much effort? (He picks up his staff, draws a circle, and says:
One. Xuefeng was serving as the head cook at Deshan. One day, when the meal was late, Deshan held out his bowl and went down from the Dharma Hall.
Seeing Deshan while Xuefeng was drying his hand-towel, Xuefeng said: "The bell has not yet rung and the drum has not yet sounded; where are you going with your bowl?"
He departed. Deshan then returned to his quarters. Xuefeng recounted this to the Master (Linji), who said, "Great as Deshan may be, he has not yet realized the final word.
When Deshan heard of this, he ordered his attendant to summon the Master, asking, "Do you refuse to acknowledge me, old monk?"
The Master secretly conveyed his intention to Deshan, who then desisted. The next day, Deshan ascended the hall; indeed, he was not at all like his usual self.
When the Master reached the front of the Sangha Hall, he clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying, "I am glad that the old fellow in the hall has finally grasped the 'last word.
Hereafter, no one in the world will be able to do anything with him. Nevertheless, he shall have only three years left to live. (Deshan indeed passed away three years later.)

Mingzhao Qian, acting on behalf of Deshan, said: "Tsk! Tsk! Nowhere to go! Nowhere to go! Xuedou Xian said: "I have heard it said that there was a 'One-Eyed Dragon,' but it turns out he has only one eye. What they do not realize is that Deshan is a toothless tiger.

Had it not been for Yantou’s ability to see through him, how could tomorrow have been different from yesterday? You who wish to understand this final phrase: I allow only the Old Barbarian to know it; I do not allow the Old Barbarian to understand it. Cuiyan Zhen said: "Deshan and Yantou—this case is settled once and for all.

This is the ground of Xuefeng, the teacher of fifteen hundred people. Weishan Zhe said: "Yantou was much like a high cliff where the rocks split apart; it was enough to cause the beasts of prey to vanish into their tracks for a hundred li."

If it were not for Deshan’s profound clarity and discernment, how could yesterday have been different from today? Guo of Mt. Wei said: "The path has never differed throughout antiquity and the present; those who attain it share the same way. To transcend beyond the realm of Wei-yin, one must clearly understand the talisman worn at the elbow."

Now tell me: where did Yantou see through Deshan? If you can discern this, not only will your eye for study be clear, but you will also have received the transmission from Xuefeng. Should you fail to distinguish the monastic from the lay, or to separate the heterodox from the orthodox, then—"The road is long and the night is deep;

do not keep the torch burning. Let us all blow it out and walk in the dark. Gao Feng Miaoyun said: "Among the karmic encounters of Buddhas and Patriarchs and the public cases of past and present, no confusion exceeds this one. Some may say that because Yantou’s wisdom surpassed his teacher, he was thus secretly enlightened to the meaning.

Little do they realize that he has committed a transgression as vast as the heavens and will suffer calamity for ten thousand kalpas. Now tell me: where does the harm lie? He clapped his hands and laughed loudly, saying: "Attendant, take this clearly to heart. Thirty years hence, someone will testify to it."

The Ming dynasty master Qianyan Chang said: "As for this final phrase, Deshan, Yantou, and Xuefeng—none of them could leap out of it. He then gave a shout and said: "A man of great character should be a true king; why settle for a counterfeit one? Tianqi Rui said:

"Yantou, Mingzhao, and Xuedou—these three patriarchs extended their broad and long tongues to cover the entire trichiliocosm. Yet, even so, they could not sing forth or praise Deshan’s final phrase. Why? Even if all the Buddhas of the three periods and the patriarchs of successive generations were to appear, they could not proclaim or expound it.

This mountain monk does not concern himself with the time beyond the kalpas or the present age; I point directly to the moment he first received his almsbowl and simply say: 'Heavens! Heavens! With nothing left unresolved. Do you understand, Great Assembly? Let us utter another..."

Verse: To serve as a fine mirror. The verse says: "Heaven! Heaven! Dense and continuous. Cutting off the elephant’s tracks, standing like a wall before the void. The horns of the sands of Ganges—all cast away here. Vast and open, he walks alone through the four quarters;

lofty and detached, he is unbound by the eight directions. A needle’s hair, a grain of millet, and a mustard seed all become a single melody. Clapping hands, following conditions, he sings ‘Rā-laṇ’. Jingshan Xìn said: "He secretly revealed his meaning and posted it on the wall.

The door gods bowed their heads and returned to the abbot's quarters, filled with such shame it would kill them. Truly, this was not like ordinary things. A difference of a hair’s breadth, and heaven and earth are suspended apart. Even so, one could only live for three years. I am the Dharma King; I have mastery over the Dharma. How could I allow myself to be defiled by others? *Du-du!* (A day)."
He was engaged in conversation with Xuefeng and Qinshan. Xuefeng suddenly pointed to a bowl of water. Qinshan said, "The water is clear; the moon appears.
Xuefeng said, "The water is clear; the moon does not appear. The Master kicked over the water bowl and departed.
The Master and Xuefeng took their leave of Deshan together. Deshan asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am taking my leave of the Master for a while to go down the mountain."
[The student] departed. [The Master] asked, "What will you do after I am gone? The Master said, "I shall not forget. [The student] asked, "On what basis do you make such a statement?

The Master said, "Have you not heard? Only when one's wisdom exceeds that of the teacher is one fit to receive the transmission; if one's wisdom is equal to the teacher's, one has diminished the teacher's virtue by half."
He said, "So it is, so it is. You must maintain this well. The two men prostrated themselves and withdrew. The Master resided at Yantou in Ezhou.
Encountering the suppression of the Buddhist order, he worked as a ferryman by a lake. He hung a board on each side of the bank; whenever someone wished to cross, they would strike the board once.
The Master would call out, "Who is there? Someone would reply, "I wish to go to that other side. Thereupon, the Master would ply his oars.
He went to meet him. One day, a certain old woman came carrying a baby and said, "I present my oars and dance with my rudders—this I do not ask about;
but tell me, from where did this child in the old woman’s hands come? The Master struck her immediately. The woman said, "The old woman has borne seven sons;
six have not met with one who understands them. This one alone is not even worth keeping," and she threw him into the water. (Langye)

Jueyun said: "He who deceives his enemy perishes. Dayi Zhi said: "Yantou’s karma lies within; he can only have his whole body covered in mud and water. Although the old woman possesses the skillful means of a man, it is still a family disgrace being broadcast abroad. Tianqi Rui said:

"A needle within cotton; a thorn within mud. This old woman possesses such a vision that even if it were not for Yantou, it would have been very difficult to respond. At that time, as soon as he saw the woman approaching, he simply rowed his boat away.

Even if one possessed the skillful means to sweep the entire world away, there would still be no place to display them here. Xigyan Bao laughed heartily and said, "What was this old woman aiming for? At that moment, Yantou should have waited until she had just cast her line, then given her a single stroke across the back, sending both of them plunging into the water—only then would it have been slightly better.

Why? Have you not heard it said: "This one alone is not even enough"? Jingshan Xin said, "If Yantou had been present, he would have sent this double-tufted old woman right along with her into the water."

[In the] midst [of this], he causes mother and son to join their heads, never parting from bone and flesh. The verse says: "How can one not understand this meaning? A foul old woman flaunting her private property. Thousand layers of evil waves roll over the waning moon; ten thousand mountains cut off sorrow as white clouds abound. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"I have once investigated the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra* for seven or eight years. I have observed two or three passages of meaning that seem like the talk of a patch-robed monk (*bhikṣu*).
I also say: 'Enough! Enough! At that time, a monk came forward, bowed, and requested the Master to cite [an instance]. The Master said: 'I shall teach you...'"
The meaning is as follows: it is like the three dots of the letter *i*. The first dot is placed toward the east; it opens the eyes of all Bodhisattvas.

The second dot is placed toward the west; it sustains the life-faculty (*jīvitendriya*) of all Bodhisattvas. The third dot is placed toward the zenith; it marks the crowns of the heads of all Bodhisattvas.
This is the meaning of the first section. Furthermore, it is said: "The intent of my teaching is like the [letter] *ma*..."
"Śiva split open his face and stuck out one eye; this is the meaning of the second section. Furthermore, he said:
'The intent of my teaching is like a drum smeared with poison: when struck once, everyone who hears it, whether far or near, perishes.
This is the meaning of the third section. At that time, the Venerable Xiaoyan asked, "What is the poison-smeared drum? The Master pressed down with both hands.
Bowing with his knees bent, he said, "Han Xin at court. Xiaoyan was speechless. (Jingshan Daokai, having finished the citation, shouted: "Withdraw your head! A monk under Jia Shan went to Shishuang.
As soon as he stepped across the threshold, he said, "I do not inquire after you. Shishuang said, "There is no need for that, Layman. The monk said, "In that case, take care.
He then went to the Master’s [Jia Shan’s] place and, as before, said, "I do not inquire after you. The Master sighed once.
Heheh! The monk said, "In that case, take care. As he was about to turn back, the Master said, "Though you are but a junior, you are indeed capable of maintaining the thread.

The monk returned and related this to Jia Shan. Jia Shan ascended the hall and said, "The master from whom you came yesterday—Rockhead and Stone Frost—come forward and relate the previous conversation exactly as it happened.
When the monk had finished speaking, Jia Shan said, "Great assembly..."
"Do you understand? The assembly had no reply. Jiashan said, "If there is no one who can speak, this old monk will not begrudge the two tufts of hair on my eyebrows;
I shall speak. He then said, "Although Shishuang possesses the 'sword that kills,' he lacks the 'sword that gives life.
Yantou also possesses the 'sword that kills' and likewise possesses the 'sword that gives life. (Jingshan Gaokong said: "One must not speak of dreams before a fool. [The Master] together with...
Luo Shan was selecting a site for a stupa. Midway through the path, Luo Shan suddenly called out, "Master! The Master looked back and asked, "What is it?
Luo Shan pointed his finger and said, "This is a fine piece of ground. The Master rebuked him, saying, "A melon-seller from Guazhou!
After traveling several more *li*, they stopped to rest. Luo Shan prostrated himself and asked, "Master, were you not here thirty years ago?"
Dongshan did not approve of Dongshan. The Master said, "He is. Dongshan asked again, "Does it not mean that you, Reverend, are a successor of Deshan?
Dongshan still did not approve of Deshan. The Master said, "He is. Luoshan said, "I do not ask about your disapproval of Deshan; I simply ask: what deficiency does Dongshan have?
The Master remained silent for a long while and then said, "Dongshan is a fine Buddha, he just lacks radiance. Luoshan—

Prostration. (Jingshan Daokai said: "Although Yantou and his son were skilled at 'darkness departing and light arriving,' if one examines them closely, they cannot avoid having their skulls clashing together.
He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From the Western Capital. The Master said, "After Huang Chao passed through, did you manage to recover your sword?
The monk replied, "I recovered it. The Master extended his neck forward and said, "Strike! The monk said, "Your head has fallen! The Master laughed heartily. Later, the monk went to Xuefeng.
Feng. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Yantou. Xuefeng asked, "What words did Yantou say?

The monk recounted the previous conversation. Xuefeng then struck him thirty blows and drove him out. (Zhaozhou Zhe said: "This monk, after Huang Chao had passed by, once managed to recover a sword.")

He then applied his skills before Yantou; yet when he arrived before Xuefeng, not even a trace of his sharp edge was revealed. Why? Because Yantou let out a great laugh, which caused heaven and earth to suddenly darken and all quarters to fall silent.

Had it not been for Xuefeng, this man would have nearly sunk into the mud without ever seeing the Way. [This is] the "sword that kills" and the "sword that gives life. Chengtian Zong said: "What a pity! This sort of fellow learned only the methods of victory and defeat, failing to realize that these are the causes of birth and death.

Had I seen him at that time, I would have simply told him, 'A true master! A true master! and let him carry his wooden board for the rest of his life. A monk asked Xuefeng: "When a Śrāvaka realizes their nature, it is like..."
Seeing the moon at night, a Bodhisattva sees his nature as clearly as one sees the sun by day. I do not know how the Master saw his nature.
Xuefeng struck his staff three times. Later, a monk cited these previous words and asked the Master [about them]. The Master gave him three slaps. (Xuedou Xian said:...)
Administering medicine according to the illness, give him three blows for now. (If one were to act strictly according to the rule, how many blows would he deserve?
One day, Deshan said to the Master, "I have two monks here who have been living in a mountain hermitage for some time. Go see what they are like. The Master then took an axe and went there;
he saw the two men sitting inside the hut. The Master raised the axe and said, "If you can say something, I shall strike you with this axe once."
"I cannot say," he replied, and brought down the axe once. The two men paid him no mind at all. The Master threw down the axe and said, "A true master!
A true master! Upon returning, he related this to Deshan. Deshan asked, "How did you describe him? The Master replied, "Under the gate of Dongshan."
It is not that they are entirely absent. If one were under the gate of Deshan, one would not have even dreamed of it.

A monk asked, "How does one discern the master amidst the dust? The Master said, "A copper gong filled to the brim with oil. (Qingzhuo asked Luoshan, "Yantou said, 'A copper gong filled to the brim with oil.

What was the meaning of this? Luoshan called out, 'Great Master! Qingzhuo responded. Luoshan said, 'A monkey has entered the Dharma hall. Luoshan then asked Mingzhao, 'If someone asks you, what will you say? Mingzhao said, 'An arrow piercing the shadow of the red sun.')
Jingshan Hongzhi’s verse says: “The monkey enters the Dharma hall; An arrow pierces the shadow of the red sun. Two ancient sages Carry snow together to fill the well.
(He lets out a shout. ○ Ruigan asked, “What is the Master of Vairocana? The Master said, “Say what? Ruigan asked again. The Master said, “You are seventeen or eighteen years old, are you not?
The Master once said to the assembly, “When this old fellow departs, he will go with a great roar. In the Tang dynasty, Guang...
After the founding of the Qi dynasty, bandits rose up in the Central Plains. While everyone fled their lands, the Master remained seated calmly as usual.

One day, a great number of rebels arrived and demanded that he provide them with provisions. They then drove their blades into him; the Master’s expression remained composed, and he ended his life with a single loud cry that was heard for many tens of li.
Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun (Dharma heir of Deshan Jian).
Chan Master Xuefeng Yicun of Fuzhou was the son of the Zeng family from Nan’an in Quanzhou. Having long participated in various Chan assemblies, his karmic affinity was established with Deshan.
During the Xiantong era of the Tang dynasty, he returned to Min and founded a monastery at Xuefeng; his disciples gathered in great numbers. [Emperor] Yizong...

He was posthumously titled Chan Master Zhengjue (True Enlightenment) and was further granted a purple *kāṣāya*. Initially, while traveling with Yantou to Aoshan Town in Lishu, they were detained by snow.
Throughout this time, Yantou did nothing but sleep, while the Master sat continuously in meditation. One day, Yantou called out to him:
"Brother, brother, please get up. Yantou asked, "What are you doing? The Master said, "In this life I have found no way through.
I have been traveling with that fellow Wensui, and everywhere we go, I am brought low by him. Today we have arrived here, and yet he does nothing but sleep.
Yantou shouted, "Eat your fill and go to sleep! Sitting on your bed every day, you are just like a common rustic from the seven villages!"
Later, on another day, while a man and woman from a household possessed by a malevolent spirit were away, the Master struck his own chest and said, "I am not yet settled here;

I do not dare to deceive myself. Yantou said, "I thought that one day you would build a grass hut atop a solitary peak and propagate the Great Teaching, yet you still speak such words. The Master replied, "It is truly so."
[The Master] was not yet settled. Yantou said, "If you truly see things this way, bring forth your realization point by point;
where it is correct, I will certify it for you; where it is incorrect, I will clear it away.

The Master said, "When I first arrived at Yanguan, I heard him ascend the hall and expound on the meaning of form and emptiness, and I attained a point of entry. Yantou said, "From now until thirty years hence, you must strictly avoid [speaking of it]."
He brought up another instance: he also cited Dongshan’s verse on crossing the water, which says: "One must by all means not seek it from others;
to do so is to distance oneself from me. He is now precisely me; I am now not he. Yantou said, "If it is like this, you have not even thoroughly saved yourself yet.
The Master further said, "Later, I asked Deshan about the matter of the ancestral vehicle (*zongcheng*): does a student still have a share in it?"
[The Master] said, "There is none. Deshan struck him with a staff and asked, "What do you say? At that moment, it was as if the bottom of my bucket had fallen out.
Yantou shouted, "Have you not heard it said? That which enters through the gate is not one's own family treasure. The Master asked, "How should it be after this?
Yantou replied, "If, in the future, you wish to propagate the Great Teaching, everything must proceed from yourself."
He brought forth what flowed from his breast and said, "Give this to me to cover heaven and earth. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment;
he immediately prostrated himself, then rose and cried out repeatedly, "Elder Brother, today at last the Dao is perfected on Mount Ao!
Later, while serving as the head cook at Dongshan, as he was washing rice, Dongshan asked him, "Washing the sand away to keep the grain; washing the grain away to keep the sand? The Master...
Xuefeng said, "The rice and millet have all gone at once. Dongshan asked, "What will the assembly eat? The Master then turned over the rice basin.

Dongshan said, "According to your karmic conditions, you should have been at Deshan. (Tiantong Jue said: "Xuefeng climbed higher and higher step by step, unaware that the heel of his straw sandals had snapped.")

If one is truly upright and impartial, turning things over in every way, then striking and singing proceed together; naturally, words and spirit accord, and father and son meet in harmony. But tell me: when Dongshan refused Xuefeng, what was his intention? "Ten thousand miles of cloudless sky have their faults;

the jade pool is like a mirror, yet the moon finds it hard to enter. Xuedou Zong said: "A straight tree does not harbor phoenixes; a golden needle has already embroidered the mandarin ducks. Had it not been for the Old Man of Xinfeng, [the truth] would have seen its ice melt and its walls crumble.
One day Dongshan asked the Master, "What have you been doing? The Master replied, "I have been hewing a trough. Dongshan asked, "How many blows of the axe did it take?"
[The wood] was finished. The Master said, "It was finished with a single stroke of the axe. Dongshan said, "That is still a matter of this side. What about the matter of that side?
The Master said, "It has reached the point where there is no place for the hand to descend. Dongshan said, "That is still a matter of this side. What about the matter of that side?
The Master stopped speaking (Fenyang Zhao spoke on his behalf, saying, "I am already exhausted"). The Master took his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan said, "You..."
“Where have you gone? he asked. The Master replied, “I have gone back into the mountains. Dongshan said, “By which path did you come out at that time?
The Master replied, “I came out by the Feiyuan Ridge. Dongshan said, “Now, by which path are you going back?
The Master replied, “I am going by the Feiyuan Ridge. Dongshan said, “There is a person who does not go by the Feiyuan Ridge; do you recognize him? The Master replied:
“I do not recognize him. Dongshan asked, “Why do you not recognize him? The Master said, “He has no face.

Dongshan said, “Since you do not recognize him, how do you know he has no face? The Master was speechless. (Langye Huijue said: “Those with coarse minds miss the point. ○ The kitchen steward Xi asked:
An ancient said, "Only one who knows the matter that lies above the Buddha has a share in the discourse. [The monk] Qixi asked, "What is this discourse?
The Master seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! Qixi had no reply, so the Master kicked him down, and Qixi broke into a sweat at that very moment.
The Master said to the assembly, "How many years old is this water buffalo? The assembly all remained silent. The Master spoke on their behalf, saying, "Seven."
[Case] Nineteen. A monk asked, "Why did the Master go off to become a water buffalo?
The Master said, "What fault is there in that? A monk asked, "Where are you going? He replied, "I am going to pay my respects to the Master at Mount Jing.
The Master said, "If the Master at Mount Jing asks you, 'How are the Buddha-dharma here? how will you respond? The monk said, "I will speak when he asks."
The Master then struck him. Later, he raised this case to ask Jingqing, "Where did this monk’s fault lie?
Jingqing said, "He asked until Jingshan was utterly exhausted. The Master said, "Jingshan was in Zhejiang; why did he ask until [the monk] was utterly exhausted?
Jingqing said, "Have you not heard it said that when the distant asks, the near answers? The Master said, "So it is, so it is. One day, he said to Changqing:
The Master said: "I once saw Moshan ask Yangshan, 'Where have all the sages of the past gone? He replied, 'Some are in the heavens;
some are among humans. What do you say, Yangshan’s meaning? Changqing said, "If one were asked where the sages appear and disappear, saying it is so would not be permissible.
The Master said, "You flatly refuse to admit it. Suppose someone suddenly..."
The Master asked him, "How would you say it? Changqing said, "Just say 'wrong. The Master said, "That is not wrong for you. Changqing said, "How is this any different from being wrong?
A monk asked, "A student has newly entered the monastic community; I beg the Master to point out a way of entry.
The Master said, "I would rather let my own body shatter into fine dust than ever dare to blind the eyes of a single monk. The monk took his leave.
He visited Lingyun and asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Lingyun raised his whisk. The monk asked, "And how was it after he appeared in the world?
Lingyun also raised his whisk. The monk then returned. The Master said, "Did you return too soon?

The monk replied, "I went there to inquire about the Buddha-dharma; as it did not accord with my understanding, I have returned. The Master asked, "What question did you ask? The monk recounted what had occurred.
The Master said, "Ask, and I shall speak for you. The monk then asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world?

The Master raised his whisk. [The monk asked again,] "And how was it after he appeared in the world? The Master lowered the whisk. The monk bowed, and the Master struck him. Later, the monk took this up and questioned Xuansha Shibei.

Xuansha said, "Do you wish to understand? I will give you a parable. It is like a man selling a piece of land; he has already concluded the contracts for all four directions—east, west, south, and north—at once. Yet, as for the tree in the center..."
[Chongshou] Chouyun said: "It seems you still belong to me. You should strike him where he understands; there is another principle involved. A monk asked, "Where have you come from?

The monk replied, "I have recently left the region of Zhejiang. The Master said, "Did you come by boat or by land? The monk replied, "I did not travel either way. The Master said, "How then did you get here?
The monk replied, "What obstacle could there be? The Master struck him. A monk asked, "The student cannot speak it."
[The Master] said, "I am sparing people for the sake of the Dharma. He asked Huìquán, "How is it that you have attained entry?
Huìquán said, "I have already discussed this with the Master. The Master said, "Where did you discuss it? [Huìquán] said, "Where would I go and come from?
The Master said, "And how is it that you have attained entry? Huìquán had no reply. The Master—
[The Master] struck [him]. Quan Tan asked: "On level fields and shallow marshes, deer and elk gather in herds.
How does one shoot the leader among the elk? The Master called out, "Quan Tan! Quan Tan responded, "Yes. The Master said, "Go drink tea. [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from?"
[The monk] said, "Guishan came. The Master asked, "What words did Guishan have? He replied, "I once asked him, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
and Guishan remained sitting as he was. The Master said, "Do you approve of him? He replied, "I do not approve of him.
The Master said, "Guishan is an ancient Buddha; you should go quickly and repent. (Xuan Sha Bei said: "That old fellow on the mountain head has surpassed Guishan.")
The King of Min asked, "I intend to build a Buddha hall; what do you think of that?

The Master said, "Great King, why not build a Hall of the Empty King instead? The King said, "I ask the Master for a model. The Master extended both hands. (Yunmen Wenyan said: "One movement, forty-nine.
The Master raised his whisk to show it to a monk, who immediately went out. (Changqing Xuanling showed this to the Grand Marshal Wang Yanbin.)

[The Master] understood. He then said, "This monk should have been called back and given a beating. The King asked, "What kind of mental state is this, Preceptor? [The Master] replied, "How many times could I let him go?
○ The Master asked Changqing, "The ancients said, 'Three before, three after. What is the meaning of this? Changqing then went out. ○ [The Master] asked a monk, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Lantian. The Master said, "Why did you not enter the grass? (Changqing Ling said, "Dangerous! ○ Entering the hall, [the Master spoke of] Nanshan.
"There is a snake with a tortoise-like nose. You all must watch it very carefully.
Changqing came forward and said, "Today, many in this hall will lose their lives. Yunmen then brandished his staff before the Master, making a gesture of fear.
A monk reported this to Xuansha, who said, "It must have been Brother Leng; only he could do that. Nevertheless, even so..."
"I am not like that. [The monk] asked, "How about you, Preceptor? Xuansha said, "What use is Mount Nanshan? [Baofeng Wen said: "Xuefeng lacks the marks of a great man.

However, as the saying goes, "A snake does not move without a head. Changqing was just like a new bride who fears her mother-in-law; he immediately said, "There are many people in the hall who have lost their lives.

Yunmen took his staff, brandished it before him, and made a gesture of fear—this is like drawing legs for a snake. Xuansha said, "What use is Mount Nanshan? Though he claimed his own realization was intimate and direct, he could not avoid remaining within a conceptual nest; there was not a single person among them who possessed even a trace of natural, spontaneous spirit. —Baoning)

The monk was speechless. Xuedou Xian said, "Alas! Alas! Baoning Yong said, "Why does the Master not hear [the call] when facing him directly? The Second Patriarch did not go to the Western Heaven; Xuefeng approved of this. When [Xuefeng] ascended Mount Xianggu, he and the Master labored together to establish the monastery.

Great men, take care not to waste your years and months inside a ghost cave! * *Sour rice and a clay tea stove*: A metaphor for the ordinary and the mundane being the very ground of enlightenment. * *Ancient mirror and fire stove*: Symbols of the absolute and the relative, or the enlightened mind and its manifestations, shown here as non-dual.

* *Head straight, tail straight*: Refers to the total integrity and consistency of the teaching. * *According to the family’s abundance or scarcity*: An expression of naturalness and spontaneity, responding without artifice to the immediate situation. * *Whose world... whose mirror?* : Challenging the student to realize that subject and object are not separate. * *Split into two parts*: Refers to dualistic thinking that separates the phenomenal world from the ultimate reality. * *Sit and cut off Xuefeng and Xuansha*: To attain such realization is to transcend even the great masters of the past. * *Ghost cave*: A metaphor for delusion, ignorance, or the conceptual mind. To remain there is to fail in one's spiritual practice.

Chan Master Changqing Huileng was a native of Yanguan in Hangzhou. His secular surname was Sun. He traveled extensively to study under various masters of the Chan gardens before finally meeting Lingyun.
He asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Lingyun replied, "The donkey’s business is not yet over."
