One day, as Xuefeng saw the Master, he suddenly seized him and said, “The entire universe is this gate of liberation; I am holding his hand, yet he refuses to enter.
[The Master] said, “Master, it is not that I do not wish to comply. Xuefeng pushed him away and said, “Even so.”
"But what can be done about all those monks behind us? The Master then cited the inscription on the National Teacher’s stele, saying:
"To attain it in the mind, the *yilan* becomes a sandalwood tree; to lose it in its essential meaning, the nectar becomes a garden of thorns.
He asked a monk, "A single phrase must encompass both the meanings of gain and loss. How would you say it? The monk raised his fist and said, "No."
"One might call this a fist," the Master said, but he did not approve. He then raised his own fist and said otherwise: "It is precisely because one calls this thing a 'fist' [that it is so].

Xuedou Xian said: "A fellow who binds himself with no rope; he does not even recognize a fist. Dayue Xiu said: "Xuedou and Anguo both claim to be lofty and beyond the mundane world, yet when they face the enemy on the front line..."

Furthermore, he followed along with the crowd. I want a phrase that possesses both the meanings of gain and loss, so that when [An Guo] raises his fist and says, "One must not call this a fist," you can ask him, "Then what do you call it?

From this, one may hear him express both the meanings of gain and loss; yet even within this, there is no one who sees clearly, as they merely mix mud and water. What clarity is there? Tiantong Hua said: "If you see Xuedou thoroughly, then you will see that An Guo has a dragon's head but a snake's tail.

If you do not see through it, then *eranda* grass becomes a sandalwood tree, and nectar becomes a garden of thorns. Dongchan Guan said: "This monk could not clamp An Guo’s mouth shut; An Guo could not stop Xuedou’s words; and Xuedou could not escape the Great Moshan."

[The Master] deliberated: "How pitiful these great elders! They move about in groups and crowds, yet they cannot withstand a single punch. When they say, 'I want a phrase that encompasses both gain and loss,' one should simply say to them, 'Stop.

Why is this so? A single drop of lion’s milk scatters ten bushels of donkey’s milk. The Master raised an example: When Master Ling was residing at Zhaoqing, he stood in the eastern corner of the Dharma Hall and said to a monk, "A good question can be posed here.
The monk then asked, "Why does the Master not occupy the central seat? Ling—
[The Master] said, "You have come in such a manner. [The monk] asked, "What is it right now? Ling said, "What use have you for your eyes?
Having finished citing this, the Master said, "When he asked in that way, it was a different principle altogether. How would you answer now?"
Later, Anguo said, "In that case, the assembly may all disperse at once. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "In that case, the assembly shall all prostrate themselves at once."
Chan Master Jinlun Kego (Dharma Heir of Xuefeng Cun).
Chan Master Jinlun Kego of Mount Nanyue was the son of the Xue family of Fudang. He went to study under Xuefeng. Xuefeng said, "Come closer.
As the Master approached to pay his respects, Xuefeng gave him a kick. The Master suddenly attained awakening. He served [Xuefeng] for ten...
Two years later, he again traveled through various monasteries. After taking up residence [at a temple], he ascended the hall and said: "When I was at Xuefeng, I encountered his one kick;
even until now my eyes have not opened. I do not know what kind of realm this is. At that time, the monastery head of Xuefeng sent a letter inviting him, saying:
"The Master on the mountain is advanced in years; why does the Elder not enter the mountains once more? The Master returned.
The Record says: "I shall re-enter the mountains only when I find that Master Shantou has some other insight.
A monk asked, "What is Xuefeng’s insight? The Master said, "I am startled as well."
Chan Master Jiaoran of Changsheng (Dharma Heir of Xuefeng Cun).
Chan Master Jiaoran of Changsheng Mountain in Fuzhou was a native of that prefecture.
Having long relied upon Xuefeng, one day while he was cutting down a tree with a monk, Xuefeng said, "Stop when you reach the heartwood. The Master said, "Cut it away! Xuefeng said, "The Ancients..."
"Man transmits mind to mind. Why do you say, 'Cut it down'? The Master threw down his axe and said, "Transmitted.
Xuefeng struck him with a staff and departed. A monk asked Xuefeng, "What is the first phrase? Xuefeng remained silent for a long while. The monk reported this to the Master.
The Master said, "This is the second phrase. Xuefeng then sent the monk back again to ask the same question.

"What is the first phrase? The Master said, "Heaven! Heaven! During a communal work period (*pǔqǐng*), Xuefeng asked, "An ancient said, 'Who would have known that beneath this scholar’s cap lies none other than a man of former sorrows? What was the intent of the ancients?
The Master tilted his bamboo hat sideways and said, "Whose words are these? Xuefeng asked the Master, "Can one who upholds the sutras..."
“Carrying the Tathāgata on one’s shoulders. “What is it to carry the Tathāgata on one’s shoulders? The Master then took up Xuefeng and held him toward the meditation seat.
Once, during a communal work session (*pingsheng*), Xuefeng was carrying a bundle of rattan. On the road, he encountered a monk; he immediately threw the bundle down.
As the monk reached out to pick it up, Xuefeng kicked him over. Upon returning, he said to the Master, “I kicked that monk with great force today. The Master said, “And...”
Shangque said, "This monk must enter the Nirvana Hall first. Xuefeng then stopped speaking. (Xuedou Xian said:

"Changsheng is much like a neighbor from the east whose family has died, and the neighbor from the west comes to offer condolences—it would be well to give him a kick. Baizhen Yuan said: 'Xuefeng wins five hundred outside, but loses one thousand within his own house. Shuzhong Yun said: "This monk ate Xuefeng’s kick and saw ghosts in broad daylight;
Changsheng ate Xuefeng’s kick and became an immortal on level ground. Great and small Fushan missed the mark by no small amount. ○ Xuefeng asked: "When light and its object both cease..."
"Lost. "What kind of thing is this? The Master said, "Let Jiaoran pass. Xuefeng said, "I let you pass; how do you speak?
[Jiaoran] said, "I also let the Master pass. Xuefeng said, "I grant you twenty blows."
The Master then paid his respects.
Zen Master Zhifu of Goose Lake (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun):
Zen Master Zhifu of Goose Lake in Xinzhou was a native of Fuzhou. Once, when Jingqing asked him, "What is the immediate [point]?"...
"Now, the bottom. The Master said, "Why 'now' again? Jingqing said, "How many times have I been supported by you? The Master said, "The words are contrary, but the meaning is compliant.
One day the Master did not go to the hall. The attendant came to invite him to the hall.
The Master said, "Today I am at the manor, eating oil-cakes until I am full. The attendant said, "The Master has never gone out. The Master said, "You simply go and ask."

The master of the estate was being summoned; just as the attendant was about to step out the gate, he suddenly saw the master of the estate returning to offer his thanks, saying, "The Master has come to our estate to eat oil-cakes.
This refers to Chan Master Longshou Shaoqing (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun).
Chan Master Xingfa Shaoying of Longshou Monastery in Zhangzhou was the son of the Chen family of Quanzhou.

While attending Xuefeng as they were walking in the mountains, he saw the leaves of a taro plant move. Xuefeng pointed to the moving leaf and showed it to him. The Master said, "Shaoying is very much afraid."
Xuefeng said, "This is what is within your own house; why are you afraid? At these words, the Master attained realization.
Guiben of Yun’gai (a Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cunen):
Master Guiben of Yun’gai Shuangquan Monastery in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao Prefecture. He first visited Xuefeng.
After paying his respects, he sat upon the meditation seat at Xuefeng’s feet, straddling it from behind. At this, the Master attained a realization.

There was a Confucian scholar in Nan’uan Heshang of Luojing (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun), who had extensively studied the past and present and was commonly called "Zhang Baichui. He went to visit [Nan’uan].
The Master asked, "Are you not Zhang Baihui? He replied, "I dare not say so. The Master drew a line in the air with his hand and asked, "Do you understand?
He replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "If you do not even understand 'one,' from where have you obtained 'Baihui'?"
Chan Master Zongjing of Longxing Monastery (Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun).
Chan Master Zongjing of Longxing Monastery in Hangzhou was a native of Taizhou. Initially, he visited Xuefeng and vowed to serve as the head cook.
He labored for over ten years. Once, while in the assembly hall, he bared one shoulder and nailed up the curtains.

Seeing this, Xuefeng remarked, "In the future, you shall dwell with a thousand monks, yet not a single one among them will be a true *zhendi* (patch-robed disciple). The Master repented his error and returned to Zhejiang to reside at Liutong Monastery.
King Qian summoned him to reside at Longxing Temple, where there were over a thousand followers, all of whom were lecturers on the Three Studies.
As for those who recite [this], it was indeed just as Xuefeng had foretold.
Regarding Chan Master Shina of Yueshan (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cunen):
Chan Master Shina Jianzhen of Yueshan in Yuezhou first encountered Xuefeng and gained a preliminary understanding; later, due to Min...
The King invited him to a vegetarian feast at Qingfeng Lou. After sitting for a long time, he raised his eyes and suddenly beheld the sunlight;
he was instantly enlightened and uttered a verse: "Ascending Qingfeng Lou for the official feast, On this day, my lifelong eyes are suddenly opened wide.
Only now do I believe that the events of the distant Putong era Were not brought from the Pamir Mountains. He returned and presented this to Xuefeng, who approved it.
Chan Master Xuannu of Fucing (Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun).

Chan Master Xuannu of Fucing Monastery in Quanzhou was a native of Goryeo. When the Duke Wang, the Governor of Quanzhou, asked, "What is the matter within the School of the Patriarchs? the Master rebuked him.
The Dream-Pen Monk (a dharma successor of Xuefeng Cunfa).
The King of Min invited the Dream-Pen Monk of Jianzhou for a meal and asked the Master, "Have you brought your pen with you?
The Master replied, "It is not a silk-wrapped brush from Mount Ji; it is not the rabbit-hair brush from within the moon. Since Your Majesty has deigned to inquire, I shall speak of my mountain."
The assembly dares not fail to present this for your inspection. He asked again, "What is the Dharma King? The Master said, "This is not the style of the Dream-Pen family.
Chan Master Yanzong of Chaoshan (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cui).
Chan Master Yanzong of Chaoshan in Jizhou once came to visit Chan Master Zifu. As he arrived, the Master descended from his meditation seat to receive him. Zifu...
Fú asked, "Master, how many years have you lived on this mountain? The Master said, "A dull bird nests in the reeds; a weary fish rests in the marsh.
Fú said, "In that case, you are a true man of the Way. The Master said, "Sit and drink tea for now."
Upāśaka Fu of Taiyuan (a dharma heir of Xuefeng Cui).
Initially, while Upāśaka Fu was at Guangxiao Temple in Yangzhou, lecturing on the *Nirvāṇa Sūtra*, there was a Chan practitioner who, because of heavy snow, went to listen to the lecture.
When the discourse reached the section on the three causes of Buddha-nature and the three virtues of the Dharma-body, the lecturer spoke extensively on the subtle principles of the Dharma-body.
The Chan practitioner laughed in derision. After the Master finished his lecture, he invited the Chan practitioner to drink tea and said, "My own aspirations have always been narrow and inferior;

I rely on the literal text to explain the meaning. Having just been ridiculed by you, I hope you will instruct me. The Chan practitioner replied, "I truly laughed because you, the *zhu-zu*, do not recognize the *dharmakāya*.
The Master asked, "In such an explanation, what is there that is not correct? The Chan practitioner said, "Please, Master, explain it once more."
[Puquan] said, "Pervasive. The Master said, "The principle of the Dharma-body is like the great void: vertically it exhausts the three periods of time, horizontally it spans the ten directions;
it encompasses the eight extremities and includes both meanings. Responding to conditions and meeting with stimuli, there is nowhere it does not pervade.

Puquan said, "I do not say that what you, Master of the Seat, have said is incorrect; however, you have only described the extent and boundaries of the Dharma-body. You truly do not yet recognize the Dharma-body itself. The Master said:
"Since this is so, Zen Master, you should speak for me. He asked, "Preceptor, do you believe it? The Master replied, "How could I dare not believe?
He said, "If it is so, Preceptor, suspend your lectures for ten days. Sit upright in quiet meditation within your room, withdrawing the mind and gathering the thoughts.
Let go of all conditions of good and evil at once. The Master followed these instructions exactly, from the first watch of the night until—
At the fifth watch, he heard the sound of drums and horns and suddenly attained awakening. He immediately went to knock on the door. The meditator asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I.
The meditator scolded him, saying, "I have instructed you to transmit and uphold the Great Teaching and to preach the Dharma in place of the Buddha.
Why were you drunk and lying in the street last night? The Master said, "Virtuous meditator, I have been lecturing on the sutras all along; I was merely using the noses of my biological parents..."
Kong Niunie said, "From this day forward, I shall never again dare to act like this. The Chan master said, "Go for now; we shall meet tomorrow.

The Master then ceased his lectures and traveled extensively throughout all regions, his fame spreading across the land. Once, while traveling through Zhejiang, he attended a Dharma assembly at Mount Jing.
One day, in front of the Great Buddha Hall, a monk asked him, "Have you ever been to Mount Wutai? The Master—
The monk said, "I have been. The Master asked, "Did you see Mañjuśrī? The monk replied, "I saw him. The Master asked, "Where did you see him?
The monk replied, "I saw him in front of the Buddha Hall at Mount Jing. Later, when this monk traveled to Minchuan, he recounted the incident to Xuefeng.
Xuefeng said, "Why did you not tell him to come over the mountain pass? Upon hearing this, the Master packed his belongings and set out. He first arrived at Xuefeng’s monastery to rest his staff.
The Master gave some tangerines to the monks. Changqing asked, "Where did you bring these from? The Master said, "I brought them from beyond the ridges.

Changqing said, "It was no easy matter to travel such a long distance; how did you manage to carry them back? The Master replied, "Tangerines, tangerines. The next day he went up the mountain. When Xuefeng heard of this, he assembled the community.
Upon arriving at the Dharma Hall, the Master looked toward Xuefeng and then immediately went down to attend to the administrative affairs. (Xuedou)

Xuedou Xian said: "A spiritual friend of fifteen hundred people was, upon being glanced at by Old Fu, immediately raised his banner of surrender. The next day, he went up to pay his respects and said, "I offended you, Master, yesterday.
Xuefeng said, "Knowing it was such a matter, let it be. Yunmen Wenyan, when asked by a monk, "What is the point of offense? struck him. Xuedou Xian said:

"Even if he had struck a hundred thousand or ten million times, what use would that have been? One must have all the people of the great earth eat the staff before one can truly uphold Xuefeng. But tell me, what did Elder Fu possess?"

"Eye. It is also said, "Indeed so. The *Píngyán* (Rocky Cliff) Verse says: "His heroic spirit like a rainbow ascends the Dharma Hall; Binding the *gāndī* to the fence is exactly appropriate. If one says he offended the Old Monk, It is like adding frost to snow, quite groundless. Yunju Shun said: "Big or small Xuefeng was once deluded by Upāsaka Fu.
This very Upāsaka Fu is also like one carrying a cangue while passing through the legal records. Xuedou Zong said: "He knows only the first part, but not the second.

He does not realize that while Xuefeng planned his strategy from within the tent and secured victory a thousand miles away, Upāsaka Fu, though exhausting all his lifelong insights, remained entirely within Xuefeng’s circle. One day, Xuefeng saw the Master.
He then pointed at the sun to show it to him. The Master shook his hand and went out. Xuefeng said, "Do you not agree with me?
The Master said, "When the Abbot shakes his head, I wag my tail. Where is there any disagreement? Xuefeng said, "You must conceal this everywhere.
One day, during the evening assembly, Xuefeng was lying down in the central courtyard. The Master said, "The five provinces..."
Within this jurisdiction, there is only this old monk who is slightly superior [to others]. Xuefeng then rose and departed.
Xuefeng once asked the Master, "I have heard it said that Linji has three phrases; is this true? The Master replied, "Yes. Xuefeng asked, "What is the first phrase?
The Master raised his eyes and looked at him. Xuefeng said, "This is still the second phrase. What is the first?"
The Master folded his hands and withdrew. From then on, Xuefeng held him in deep esteem; he no longer traveled elsewhere but remained to attend to the bathhouse.
One day, Xuansha went up to inquire after Xuefeng’s well-being. Xuefeng said, "There is a little mouse here in this place; it is currently in the bathhouse.
Xuansha said, "I shall wait to examine it for you, Master. Having spoken, he went to the bathhouse.
In his quarters, he encountered the Master drawing water. Xuansha said, "I have come to see you, Senior. The Master replied, "We have already met.
Xuansha asked, "In what kalpa did we ever meet? The Master said, "Why are you so drowsy? Xuansha then returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Bānxuefeng said, "I have already scrutinized him thoroughly. Xuefeng asked, "How did you scrutinize him?
Xuansha recounted the previous dialogue. Xuefeng said, "You have been robbed! Gushan asked the Master, "Before your parents were born, where was your nose?
The Master said, "Brother, you speak first. Gushan said, "Now that they are born, tell me where it is."
"Where? The Master refused to consent. Gushan then asked, "How about this? The Master said, "Bring me the fan in your hand.

Gushan gave him the fan and again questioned him regarding the previous statement. The Master shook the fan and did not answer. Gushan was at a loss. He then struck the Master with a fist. (Zhaojue Qin said:

The Master said, "He is not yet there. Xuefeng said, "He is a man of ultimate penetration.
The Master said, "If you do not believe me, wait until I go and examine him myself. He then pursued him halfway along the road and asked, "Brother Teacher, where are you headed?"
"Go," said Gushan. "Go into the nine-layered city. The Master asked, "What if you encounter the three armies surrounding you?
Gushan said, "He has his own path that reaches through the heavens. The Master said, "In that case, you have left the palace and lost the hall.
Gushan said, "Where would he not be called the Honored One? The Master shook his sleeves and turned back. Xuefeng asked, "How was it? The Master [related the exchange].
He said, "What a fine, solitary arrow! It has been broken in mid-flight. He then recounted the previous story. Xuefeng said, "The fellow’s words remain.
The Master said, "This old, frozen lump still retains a trace of his hometown sentiment. (Miaoshan Zhe said: "There have been many discussions among the assembly regarding this story.")
