"When that monk heard this, he suddenly attained realization and never traveled elsewhere again. Upasaka, do you understand now? If you do not understand, what is it that you see every day? Jing.

Shangao said: "The wealthy lament that a thousand mouths are too few; the poor regret that a single body is too many. [He] invited Baofu to a vegetarian feast and sent someone to deliver this message:
"We request the Master’s compassion to deign to honor us with your presence. Baofu asked: "For whom is there compassion? The Master said:
"When you speak thus, Master, it is entirely a lack of compassion. He asked a monk: "Where have you come from? The monk replied: "From Qinzhou. The Master said: "What have you brought with you?"
[The Master] said, "Come forward. The monk replied, "I have not brought anything with me. The Master said, "Why do you speak such falsehoods before the assembly? The monk was speechless.
The Master then asked, "Is it not true that Aingwu birds come from Qinzhou? The monk replied, "Aingwu birds come from Longxi. The Master said, "That is not much of a difference.

(Weishan Zhe said: "This monk has just come from Qinzhou; why did the Master call him a liar before the assembly? Do you wish to understand? He was diligent as a guest, but he has brought trouble upon his host.)
(Plunging through mud and wading through water) ○ Imperial Tutor Wang went up to Xuefeng to offer robes to the assembly of monks.

At that time, the senior monk Conggan was absent, so the Master’s disciple received the robes on his behalf under the senior monk’s name. When Conggan returned, the disciple said, "I have already offered the robes for my elder brother."
[Zhaozhou] asked Gan, "What is the name of the road you take? Gan had no reply. The Master (Zhaozhou) spoke on his behalf, saying, "Brother, you are so greedy. He asked again, "Where is the greed?
Again he spoke on his behalf, saying, "Twice you have mentioned your name" (Yunju Xi said: "Where is the place where Upādhyāya Gan twice mentioned his own name?").
The Master, along with Changqing and Baofu, entered the prefectural city. They saw a screen painting of peonies. Baofu—
[The Master] said, "What a beautiful peony flower! Changqing said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said, "What a pity for such a fine flower. (Baoci then remarked:

"Regarding the words of these three venerable elders, is there any distinction between them being close or distant? As for Lohan speaking thus, where does he land? Huanglong Xin said: "According to the realization of these three men, one surpasses the Buddhas and Patriarchs;

one benefits both self and others; and one deceives himself. He then asked a monk, "Tell me, who is it that deceives himself? The monk said, "Do not let your eyes deceive you. The Master said: "From here, go deeper into the night when it is quiet and utterly deserted, and then [look again])."
One must go and deliberate with him before one can succeed).
Chan Master Huìqiú of Ān-guó (dharma heir of Xuánshā Běi):
Chan Master Huìqiú Jìzhào of Ān-guó Yùan in Fúzhōu (also known as Zhōngtǎ). He was a native of Pútian in Quánzhōu. Xuán...
In the Sandalwood Room, [Yunju] was foremost among those who came for instruction. He asked, "What is the first moon? Xuan Sha said, "What would you do with that moon of yours?
From this, the Master attained awakening. In the second year of the Kaiping era of the Liang dynasty, as Xuan Sha was about to pass away...
The Military Governor of Min, Wang Shi, sent his son to inquire after [Xuansha’s] illness and requested that he secretly indicate who would succeed him in preaching the Dharma.
Xuansha replied, "Qiuzi will attain it. Wang silently took note of this final instruction and then asked Drum Mountain (Gushan), "Who is fit to hold the seat of the Dharma at Wulong?
Drum Mountain named twelve venerable elders from the city who possessed the full eye of the Dharma; when the time came for them to open the hall for their first sermon, [Qiuzi was chosen].
One day, officials and monks gathered together at a Dharma assembly. The King suddenly asked the assembly, "Who is Elder Qiú? Thereupon, the people pointed out the Master.
The Wang family then invited him to ascend the seat. Ascending the hall, he said:

"The causes and conditions regarding the rice gruel and meals here are for the sake of my brothers; though I chant them forth, they are ultimately not permanent. If you wish to attain the essential point, it is rather the mountain."
Heaven, Earth, and the Great Rivers shall reveal it to you. Since that Way is eternal, it can also bring about ultimate realization.
If you enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī, all unconditioned things—earth, wood, tiles, and pebbles—will assist you in triggering the awakening.

If you enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara, all sounds and voices—even those of frogs and earthworms—will assist you in triggering the awakening. If you enter through the gate of Samantabhadra...

"Without moving a step, one arrives. I have shown you these three gates as skillful means, like using a single broken chopstick to stir the waters of the great ocean, so that the fish and dragons therein may know water is their life-sustenance.

Do you understand? If you lack the eye of wisdom to examine this with discernment, then no matter how many hundreds of clever and ingenious methods you employ, they will not lead to the ultimate realization.
Chan Master Qirú of Dazhang Mountain in Fuzhou (a dharma heir of Xuansha Shibei).
He was a native of that prefecture. Resolving to explore the Way of the Patriarchs, he entered the chamber of Xuansha.
Having attained a sharp awakening to the profound essence, Xuansha recorded: "Your meditation has already transcended the ordinary; in the future, you shall require but one..."
People held that he stood [in this manner] without moving. From then on, the Master no longer applied himself to gathering disciples or maintaining attendants;
he lived in seclusion at Xiaojie Mountain, hollowing out a large, rotten fir tree to serve as a small hermitage, which could accommodate only his body.
A monk asked Master Yuntai Qin, "What is the true word? Qin replied, "Namo Buddhāya. The Master said otherwise, "What? What?"
The two senior monks, Qinghuo and Chongxu, had previously heard of the Master’s reputation but had never met him. One day, they went to visit him together and happened upon him gathering millet.
Qinghuo asked, "Where is the Abbot? The Master replied, "From where have you come?
He said, "From the foot of the mountain. The Master asked, "How did you manage to get here? He replied, "What is it that is 'here'?"
At the dwelling, the Master greeted them with a bow and said, "Go down and drink some tea. Only then did the two gentlemen realize it was the Master;
they proceeded to his hut and sat in conversation. Unbeknownst to those around them, at night they saw jackals and tigers rushing to the front of the hut, circling it naturally and submissively.
The Venerable Sijing of Guoqing Temple (Dharma Heir of Xuansha Shibei).
The Venerable Sijing of Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai first encountered Xuansha, who addressed the assembly, saying:

"All of you, if you can for the duration of a single lifetime act as if you had lost your parents, I guarantee that you will attain thorough penetration. The Master followed up on these words and asked:
"Just as it is said in the teachings: 'One must not use the mind of known objects to fathom the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed knowledge and vision.
But how about this? Xuansha said, "If you say you have thoroughly investigated the mind of known objects to its very bottom, would you still be able to fathom it?
From this, the Master entered the faith.
Chan Master Daokuang of Zhaoqing (Dharma heir of Changqing Ling).
Chan Master Daokuang of Zhaoqing Monastery in Quanzhou was a native of Chaozhou. When Master Ling first resided at Zhaoqing, [Daokuang was among his disciples].
The Master then entered the room to serve as an attendant and subsequently served as the head of the work crew (*tǒngtóu*). He would often engage in conversation with the assembly of monks.
One day, Changqing saw him and said, "What are you doing all day long, talking so incessantly? The Master replied, "If one does not work for a day, one does not eat for a day.
Changqing said, "In that case, you are sharpening your bow and honing your arrows. The Master said, "I am waiting specifically for Wei Chi."

"Come," [Longqing] said. When [Changqing] arrived, Longqing asked, "What is it like after Weichi has come? The Master replied, "He will leave his sinews and bones spread across the earth, and his eyes will bulge out.
Longqing then went out. Later, when Longqing was summoned, the Master succeeded him as the abbot.
Chan Master Mingyuan of Jiu Ling Peak (Dharma heir of Changqing Leng).
Chan Master Mingyuan of Jiu Ling Peak in Xiangzhou first visited Changqing. Changqing asked, "What is your name?
The Master replied, "Mingyuan. Changqing asked, "How is it on that other side? The Master stepped back two paces. Changqing said, "..."
Changqing said, "Why do you retreat two steps for no reason? The Master was speechless. Changqing said, "If you had not retreated, how would one have known that [the Way] is bright and far-reaching?
Thereupon, the Master understood the meaning.
Chan Master Baoci Guangyun (Dharma heir of Changqing Ling).
Chan Master Guangyun Huijue of Baoci Monastery in Fuzhou asked a monk, "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Wolong."
The Master asked, "How long have you been there? He replied, "I have spent the winter and passed through the summer. The Master said, "There are no overnight guests at Longmen;
why have you stayed there for so long? He replied, "In a lion’s den, there are no other beasts. The Master said, "Try to let out a lion’s roar.
He replied, "If I were to let out a lion’s roar, there would be no more Master. The Master said, "Out of consideration for you as a newcomer, I let you go."
"You get thirty blows. (Xuedou Xian said: "How strange, O Zen adepts! If one were to unfold it evenly, neither would be harmed; if one were to enforce the command, both would be in peril.
Can you still examine this? ) The King of Min asked, "How far is Baozi from Shenquan? The Master said, "If one speaks of distance, it is not as good as arriving there in person.
The Master then asked, "The Great King's daily responses are a thousandfold in their differences; what mind is this? The King said, "Where [is that]?"
"Have you attained the mind? The Master said, "How could there be such a thing as 'no-mind'? The King asked, "What about that other matter?
The Master said, "Please ask about that other matter. The King said, "The Great Master may deceive others, but he cannot deceive me."
Chan Master Xianze of Guangyan Monastery at Mount Lingyin in Hangzhou (Dharma heir of Changqing Hui Leng). Initially, he visited Baofu. Baofu asked, "What is your name?
The Master replied, "Xianze. Baofu said, "If you suddenly encounter a place that is parched and dry, what then? The Master replied, "Who?"
"This is the one who is parched. Baofu said, "I am he. The Master said, "Preceptor, do not deceive people.
Baofu said, "In fact, it is you who are deceiving me."
Master Gwisang of Silla (a successor of Changqing Huiqiu). Regarding Master Gwisang of Silla:
Someone mentioned that Prime Minister Pei had established a Dharma assembly. He asked a monk, "What sutra are you studying?
The monk replied, "The *Sutra of the Silent Youth*. The official asked, "How many fascicles does it have? The monk said, "Two fascicles. The official said, "Since..."

"This is wordlessness. [The monk asked,] "Why then are there two fascicles? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "If we discuss wordlessness, it is not merely two fascicles."
The Layman Wang Yanbin, Grand Tutor and Dharma heir of Changqing Ling:
One day, while entering the Buddha Hall at Zhaoqing, the Layman Wang Yanbin, Grand Tutor, pointed to an alms bowl and asked the hall master:
"What kind of bowl is this? The temple master replied, "A Bhaisajyaguru bowl. The Master said, "I have only heard of the Dragon-subduing Bowl.
The temple master said, "It will subdue the dragon as soon as one appears. The Master said, "What if a dragon were suddenly to come leaping through the clouds and crashing through the waves?
The temple master said, "It would not even look back. The Master said, "Your words have fallen short" (Xuan Sha Bei added: "Even with all your supernatural powers, where could you run to?").

Baofu Zhan said: "I take refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. Bai Zhang Heng made the gesture of overturning his alms bowl. Yunmen Wenyan said: "In a future life, when you are reborn in the heavens, do not let the old monk down. Miaoyan Zhong said: "The temple director only knows how to look forward; he does not know how to look back.

The Great Minister’s divine majesty has been displayed, yet the temple director’s alms bowl remains overturned. Daguang Daowei said: "If Daguang had seen him at that time and asked, 'What about when [the waves] seize the clouds and surge over the billows? he would have lifted up his alms bowl and said, 'Exhaust all your spiritual powers!'"

"Even if the Eight Great Dragon Kings were to arrive, they would have no choice but to cower in awe. Changqing said to the Grand Tutor, "When Xuefeng held up his whisk to show the monk, the monk immediately left.
According to this monk’s conduct, you should have called him back and given him a severe beating for his pains. The Grand Tutor asked, "What kind of mental state was that?
Changqing replied, "I almost let him off the hook. The Grand Tutor went to Zhaoying to partake in the tea ceremony. Master Lang...
The Master was seated with Mingzhao as they were handling a tea kettle. Suddenly, the tea kettle overturned. The Master asked, "What is that beneath the tea stove?
Lang replied, "It is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove. The Master said, "If it is the Spirit Who Supports the Stove, why did you overturn the tea?

Lang replied, "To serve an official for a thousand days, yet to fail him in a single morning. The Master shook his sleeves and departed. Mingzhao said, "Upādhyāya Lang, you have eaten me! (i.e., you have defeated me).
After the celebratory meal was finished, Lang went outside to gather firewood. Lang asked, "What are you doing, Zhashang? Zhaoqing said, "No one would have taken advantage of the situation.

(Xuedou Xian said: "At that time, he should have simply kicked over the tea stove. Miaoshan Zhe said: "Wang Taifu was much like Zhao Chuo seizing the jade; his anger made his hair stand on end. Mingzhao was also unable to restrain himself, for such a swift opportunity is hard to encounter.

If Daopei had been in Lang's place, when he saw this question, he would have simply laughed loudly. Why? 'If you do not seize it when you see it, it will be difficult to pursue for a thousand years. [Note: The original text contains a commentary by Xuedou Xian and Miaoshan Zhe regarding the missed opportunity.]
Chan Master Daohui of Ba’en Monastery in Zhangzhou (Dharma heir of Baofu Zhuan).
Initially, [Daohui] accompanied Baofu in delivering a letter to Imperial Protector Wang of Quanzhou.
The Imperial Protector asked, "Has the Monk of Zhangnan been performing the work of a man lately? The Master replied, "If one says he has performed it..."
The man then bowed to the Master. [The Master] said, "If you say it is not for the sake of others, that would again be a slight to the Grand Marshal.
He came forward and asked the Grand Marshal, "Speak one phrase. The Grand Marshal said, "Wait until the iron ox can chew grass and the wooden horse can breathe smoke.
The Master said, "I am sparing my mouth to eat my rice. After a long silence, the Grand Marshal asked again, "Donkey comes, horse comes? The Master said, "Donkey."
Horses do not share the same path. The Grand Marshal said, "How did you manage to get here? The Master said, "I have come specifically to thank the Grand Marshal for understanding my words.
Chan Master Xingzong of Zhaoqing Temple in Quanzhou (a dharma heir of Baofu Zhuan).
Chan Master Xingzong Jingxiu of Zhaoqing Temple in Quanzhou first visited Baofu. One day, Baofu entered...
In the main hall, seeing a Buddha image with its hand raised, the Master pointed at it and asked the Teacher, "What is the meaning of the Buddha acting in this way?
The Teacher replied, "Even you, Master, are lying prostrate. Baofu said, "I myself shall take up that protruding part.
The Master said, "Master, you are not merely lying prostrate. Baofu approved of this.
Chan Master Ziyi of Tiantong (Dharma Heir of Yanshou of Gushan):
Chan Master Ziyi Xin-yin Shuiyue of Tiantong, Hangzhou. He was the son of the Chen family of Leqing, Wenzhou.
Initially traveling to seek instruction, he visited Gushan and asked: "I, Ziyi, have come from three thousand *li* away to join this Dharma assembly; today is no ordinary day."
At that time, the Master came forward and requested a non-timely response from Guishan. Guishan said, "I must not leave you, my worthy friend, in a state of dullness.
The Master asked, "What is it like at the point where effort is saved? Guishan replied, "Why do you exert such effort? At these words, the Master attained realization.
Chan Master Baibun Zhizuo (Dharma Heir of Yanshan of Gushan).
Chan Master Jianzhou Baibun Zhizuo Zhenji was the son of the Zhu family of Yongzhen. He received the tonsure at Mount Gu.
One day, at Gushan, the Master ascended the hall and called to the assembly. When the assembly all turned their heads, Gushan opened his robe to show them;
the assembly was at a loss, but only this Master clearly awakened to its meaning and entered the room for certification.

Later, while attending the assembly, Gushan called out, "Come forward. The Master stepped forward. Gushan asked, "When Nanquan called for the head monk, what was his intention? The Master folded his hands.
With a dignified countenance, he withdrew and stood aside.
Master Gushan Zhiyue (the dharma heir of Gushan Yan) looked upon him with a smile and marveled at him.
Chan Master Gushan Zhiyue Liaozong of Fuzhou Gushan was a native of that same prefecture. Initially traveling to seek instruction, he arrived at Ezhou.
Huanglong. [The Master] asked, "I have long heard of Huanglong; yet now that I have arrived, I see only a striped red snake.
Huanglong said, "You see only a striped red snake, and you do not recognize Huanglong. The Master asked, "What is Huanglong? Huanglong said:
As he was speaking thus, the Master said, "If you suddenly encounter a garuḍa, what then? Huanglong said, "Your life and nature would be difficult to preserve.
The Master said, "In that case, you will be swallowed by it. Huanglong said, "Thank you for your offering, Dharma brother.
The Master then bowed.
Chan Master Baoguo Zhao (Dharma heir of Longhua Zhao).
Chan Master Zhao of Baoguo Monastery in Fuzhou: A Buddhist stupa was struck by lightning. Someone asked, "Why were the ancestral stupas and temples struck by lightning?
The Master said, "It is the functioning that penetrates heaven. [The questioner] said, "If it is the functioning that penetrates heaven, why..."

"What is it that strikes the thunderbolt? The Master said, "In what place of activity do you see a Buddha? [The monk] said, "What can be done about this mess? The Master said, "What do you see? (Jingshan Xing says:
"Not striking the Buddhas and Patriarchs, he further tells him to strike them. Which one is it? The verse says: Suddenly from the blue sky comes a thunderclap;

the entanglements are crushed to dust and the gate of the stupa opens. The family treasures are not permitted to be recommended to the vulgar; the Buddha-stupa lies deep and silent, like the ashes of the empty kalpa.)
Chan Master Zhiyuan of Zifu (Dharma Heir of Jingqing Huo).
Chan Master Zhiyuan of Zifu Monastery in Fuzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He visited Jingqing and asked, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
Jingqing said, "Everyone wants to know. The Master said, "If that is so, then it is difficult for the many eyes [to see]."
[He] departed in secret. Jingqing said, "Principle can bind even a leopard.
Because of this, the Master attained awakening to the profound essence [of the Dharma]. Chan Master Yiyuan of Wugu:
Chan Master Yiyuan Kaibing of Wugu Mountain in Quzhou was a native of the Xu family of Wuxing. During the Guangqi era, he followed...
His father was stationed in Xin’an and forcibly arranged a marriage for him; the Master did not consent and subsequently traveled through various regions.

Having attained spiritual resonance with Jingqing, he returned to visit his parents and established a separate residence south of the city walls to fulfill the Master’s aspiration. Beside this residence stood the temple of Minister Chen.
There was a portrait of Master Lin. When the Master went to pay his respects, he lost sight of where the master had gone.

Later, while the Prefect was performing a sacrificial rite at the shrine, he saw the Master entering meditative absorption (*samādhi*) amidst a thicket of bamboo behind the temple; ants were gnawing at his robes, and withered leaves reached his thighs.
Some said that he was the son of General Xu. From this point on, he emerged from and entered into *samādhi* at will. This was Master Neng of Zihu.
The Master did not yet know the depth of the Master’s realization and asked, "The meditative concentration in which you abide is merely that of the Lesser Vehicle.

At that time, they were just drinking tea; the Master picked up his bag and presented it, saying, "Is this great or small? Nan was struck with awe. He then went to visit Chan Master Deyan of Mount Tang in Kuocang.
Deyan asked, "What is your surname? He replied, "My surname is Xu. Deyan said, "Who authorized you [to have such a name]? He replied, "No one."
Yan silently took note of this and subsequently granted him the tonsure and ordination. Once, Yan ordered him to pick peaches; ten days passed without his returning.
When Yan went to search for him, he found the Master leaning against a rock by the peach tree, serenely absorbed in meditative concentration (*samādhi*). Yan snapped his fingers to rouse him from it.

During the Kaiyun era, while traveling to Jianglang Rock, he beheld a stone grotto and said to his disciple Huixing, "I shall enter meditative concentration within this place; you must pile up stones to seal the entrance."
"Go out the gate. Do not harbor thoughts of me. Huixing followed these instructions. The following year, Huixing felt that his teacher had passed away.
He opened the coffin to look upon the master; white hair covered his shoulders, and his chest was still warm. He slowly rose from within himself, appearing no different than before.
He returned once more to Wugu. The Court Gentleman Lord Shen was stationed in Xin'an. He commissioned the monk Shou Rong, a scholar of the Abhidharma, to propagate Master Fu’s Way.
When he pressed the Master on the defining characteristics of meditative concentration, the Master did not engage him in debate. Daorong took this as a sign of contempt.

At that time, people of Xin'an were vying with one another to paint portraits of the Master and worship them, all of whom obtained *śarīra*. Daorong, consequently filled with shame and submission, prostrated before the portrait to apologize for his transgressions; he too obtained *śarīra*.

He sighed and said, "Henceforth, I shall not dare to fathom [the Dharma] with my shallow understanding. King Qian Zhongyi, moved by the Master’s appearance in his dream, dispatched an envoy to have his portrait painted and sent it to the Master.

At that time, the King suffered from an eye ailment; upon unfolding the portrait and prostrating before it, just as he had seen in his dream, śarīras rained down, and his eye disease was instantly cured.
Consequently, the King bestowed upon him the title "Kaiming" (Illuminator). At the beginning of the Endong era, Emperor Taizong heard of the Master’s power of meditative concentration.
The Emperor issued an edict for the local province to accord him special honors as he was dispatched to the capital. The Master declined the honor with great earnestness;

however, when the imperial envoys arrived again to convey the decree, he was specially permitted to enter the private audience chamber in a sedan chair. The Emperor bade him sit and presented him with tea, then inquired about his meditative practice. His responses were concise and exhaustive, deeply resonating with the Emperor’s intent.
Chan Master Zhidu of Rui Feng Monastery in Linyang, Fuzhou (Dharma heir of An Guo).
Chan Master Zhidu of Rui Feng Monastery in Linyang, Fuzhou, was a native of this province. Initially, he visited An Guo.
A monk asked him, "What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena? An Guo held up a finger. The monk did not [understand].
Jian entered the room and said to the Master, "Just now, when I saw that monk asking his question, Zhi-duan had a moment of realization.
An-guo asked, "What principle did you perceive? The Master also raised a finger and said, "What is this?
An-guo approved of him, and the Master bowed in gratitude.
Chan Master Qinghuo of Baofu (Dharma heir of Shuilong Pu).
Chan Master Qinghuo of Baofu Monastery in Zhangzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He visited Master Ru’an of Mount Dazhang.
(The dialogue is as in the chapter on the Hermitage Master. Later, he visited Shuilong. Shuilong asked, "Dharma Master Huo, which venerable master have you come to see?
Have you attained awakening yet? He replied, "I once visited Dazhang and gained a place of conviction. Thereupon, Shuilong ascended the hall.
He gathered the assembly and called out, "Liaoshi Huo, come forth! Burn incense before the assembly and speak of your realization; I, the old monk, shall bear witness for you.
The Master stepped forward from the assembly, took up the incense, and said, "The incense has already been offered. As for realization—I have not realized it.
Suilong was greatly pleased and granted him permission.
The Eighth Generation under Nanyue:
Master Heishui of Jiazhou (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Qi).
Regarding Master Heishui of Jiazhou: Initially, he visited Huanglong and asked, "What is it like when snow covers the reeds? Huang—
Long said, "Fierce! The Master said, "Not fierce. Huanglong spoke again, "Fierce! The Master again said, "Not fierce.
Huanglong then struck him. At this, the Master attained realization and immediately prostrated himself.
The Realized Man Lü Yan (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Ji).
The Realized Man Lü Yan, courtesy name Dongbin, was a native of Jingchuan. During the late Tang dynasty, he failed to pass the imperial examinations three times.
While at a wine shop in Chang’an, he happened upon Zhongli Quan, who bestowed upon him the art of prolonging life; from then on, no one could fathom his abilities. He once traveled...
At Guizong on Mount Lu, he inscribed upon the wall of the bell tower: "One day of pure leisure and self-mastery, The six spirits harmonize, signaling peace and well-being.
A treasure dwells within the *dantian*; do not seek the Way elsewhere. When facing objects, remain without mind; do not inquire about Chan.

Not long after, as he traveled through Huanglong Mountain, he beheld purple clouds forming a canopy. Suspecting there might be a person of extraordinary character there, he entered to pay his respects, arriving just as Huanglong was striking [the bell].
As the drum sounded and he ascended the hall, Huanglong saw that it must be Master Lü. Desiring to lead him forward, Huanglong said in a stern voice, "Beside the seat is one who steals the Dharma.
Lü stepped forth resolutely and asked: "A single grain of millet conceals a world; half a pint of a cauldron boils mountains and rivers. Tell me, what is the meaning of this?
Huanglong pointed at him and said, "This is a ghost guarding a corpse. Lü replied, "How can you say such a thing?"
Nainang possessed the medicine of longevity and immortality. Huanglong said, "Even if one passes through eighty thousand kalpas, in the end, one will surely fall into emptiness and oblivion.
Lü Boya was astonished; he flew his sword to threaten him, but the sword could not penetrate. He then prostrated himself twice and requested instruction on the ultimate goal.
Huanglong rebuked him, saying, "I shall not ask about boiling mountains and rivers within a half-pint cauldron; how is it that a single grain of millet contains [the universe]?"
At these words, Shijie attained immediate realization. He composed a verse, saying: "I have cast away my gourd-bag and smashed my lute;
Now I no longer crave mercury within gold. Since first beholding Huanglong, I have finally realized that all my previous efforts were misplaced.
Huanglong instructed him to provide protection for him.
Chan Master Hongjin of Qingxi (Dharma Heir of Luohan Chen).
Chan Master Hongjin of Mount Qingxi in Xiangzhou was the First Seat while under the guidance of Dizang.

One day, when Dizang ascended the hall for discourse, two monks came forward and bowed. Dizang said, "Both are wrong. The two monks were speechless. After the discourse ended, they requested [instruction].
Yixiu was the mountain master. Yixiu said, "You yourself are towering and majestic; yet you pay obeisance and intend to question others—is this not a mistake?
When the Master heard this, he did not approve. Yixiu then asked, "I wonder, Senior Monk, what about you?

The Master said, "You are yourself lost in darkness; how can you act as a teacher for others? Yixiu became indignant and went to the abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction. Dizang pointed [at him].
In the corridor, [Dongshan] said, "The head cook has gone into the storehouse. Xiu then realized his error.
On another day, the Master asked the mountain master Xiu, "You clearly know the principle that birth is non-birth; for what reason, then, are you carried away by birth and death?
Xiu replied, "A bamboo shoot will eventually become a bamboo stalk. Now, could it still be used as a strip of bamboo? The Master said, "You..."
Later, Xiu attained enlightenment on his own. He said, "My understanding was only this much. What is the meaning of your teaching, Senior Monk?
The Master pointed and said, "This is the Director's quarters; that is the Steward's quarters. Xiu then prostrated himself in gratitude.
Chan Master Xiufu of Qingliang (Dharma Heir of Luohan Chen):
Chan Master Xiufu Wukong of Qingliang Yuan in Shengzhou was the son of the Wang family of Beihai. He traveled to seek out the masters of the school.
For years he had relied on the *Kṣitigarbha Sūtra*, yet it did not accord with his realization; he fell ill and entered the Nirvāṇa Hall.
One night, Kṣitigarbha went to visit him and asked, "Is the Senior Monk [Fur] at peace? The Master replied, "I have been opposed by the karmic conditions of my Preceptor.
Kṣitigarbha pointed to a lantern and said, "Do you see this? The Master replied, "I see it. Kṣitigarbha said, "Even this very thing is not opposed. The Master [attained realization].
Upon hearing these words, he attained realization. Later, while serving as a mountain master, he went to inquire after the health of Dizang.
He said, "Throughout hundreds and thousands of kalpas and lifetimes, I have at times been at odds with you, Venerable One. Now, moreover, I find you unwell.
Dizang then held up his staff and said, "Even this very thing does not oppose me. At this, the Master suddenly attained enlightenment. [He] asked Zhong, the Dharma Seat Master:
"What sutra are you lecturing on? he asked. "The Lotus Sutra," [Chong] replied. The Master said, "Wherever the *Lotus Sutra* is being preached, I manifest this jeweled stupa to serve as a witness.
Great Virtue, when you lecture, who will act as your witness? Zhong had no reply. (Qingliang Qin spoke on his behalf, saying: "I thank the Master for acting as my witness.")
Chan Master Longji Shaoshou (Dharma Heir of Luohan Chen).
Chan Master Longji Shaoshou of Fuzhou initially studied with Fayan and Dizang together; he considered his realization to have reached the ultimate.
Later, when they parted ways and traveled to Jianyang, during their conversation along the road, Fayan suddenly asked: "The ancients said, 'Ten thousand..."
"Among the myriad phenomena, the elephant alone reveals its body. This [statement] negates the myriad phenomena; does it not negate them? The Master said, "It does not negate them.
Fayen asked, "What do you mean by 'negating' or 'not negating'? The Master was bewildered and did not know how to respond. He returned to Dizang, who asked, "You have been gone but a short time;
why have you come back? The Master said, "I had a matter that I could not resolve; how could I have feared the toil of traveling over mountains and rivers? Dizang...
Dizang said, "You have traveled across many mountains and rivers; it was no small feat.
The Master did not yet understand the meaning and asked, "The ancients said, 'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. What is the intent of this?

Dizang asked, "Do you say that the ancients rejected the myriad phenomena, or did they not reject them? The Master replied, "They did not reject them. Dizang said, "Then there are two. The Master was struck with awe.
He pondered deeply, yet asked: "I do not know for certain—did the ancients negate the myriad phenomena, or did they not negate them?
Dizang said, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? At these words, the Master attained realization. He took his leave of Dizang once more and went to visit Fayan.

Fayan’s words and meaning were identical to those with which Dizang had instructed him, consistent from beginning to end. Later, the Master resided at Longji Mountain. He ascended the hall and addressed the assembly:
They are fully possessed of the dharmas of ordinary beings, yet ordinary beings do not know them. They are fully possessed of the dharmas of sages, yet sages do not perceive them.
If sages were to perceive them, they would be ordinary beings; if ordinary beings were to know them, they would be sages. These two phrases share one principle but have two meanings.
If a person can discern them, there will be no hindrance to finding a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma. If you cannot discern them, do not—
"The Way does not doubt what is good. Take care. (Huanglong Qing said: "Master Xiu only knows how to spread the net and set the trap, yet he fails to realize he has caught himself.

Do you wish to find a way out? This also contains one principle and two meanings. If anyone can discern this, they will fall forever into the Avīci Hell. (Jingshan Gao said: "It is easy to turn iron into gold and jade; it is difficult to persuade people to eliminate their right and wrong.

(Jingci Yi said: "Even if there were a path of entry, what would you do with it? An ordinary person remains an ordinary person; a sage remains a sage. Now tell me, when both ordinary and sage have vanished, how do you speak this one phrase? 'Leisurely holding a scroll, leaning against a pine, he smiles and asks: 'Where have you come from?'")

Chushi Qi said: "Master Xiu says, 'What one is familiar with is difficult to forget. This is like bamboo shoots sprouting in winter in a foreign land. Tianqi Rui said: "If there were such a point of entry, do not speak of the monks from the ten directions; take it for granted that Master Xiu has not yet emerged from the realm of sages and ordinary beings.

Yet he wishes to further benefit all people and lead them on—leading them instead into the pit of birth-and-death hell. What more can be said of knowing or not knowing, understanding or not understanding? Although he exerts himself for the sake of the assembly, alas, the disaster originates within his own gate.

It would have been better to pierce the divination chart with a needle to avoid boring the tortoise shell and striking the tiles. [He] asked a monk: "Where have you come from? The monk replied: "From Cuiyan. The Master said: "What is there at Cuiyan?"
He spoke these words to instruct his disciples, saying: "The ordinary way is this: when you go out the door, you meet Maitreya; when you enter the gate, you see Śākyamuni.
The Master said, "How can it be right to speak in such a way? The monk asked, "How about you, Master? The Master replied, "When you go out the door, whom do you meet?
When you enter the gate, what do you see? Upon these words, the monk attained realization.
The Zen Master Yuxian the Wine Immortal (Dharma Heir of Longhuaqiu).
The Zen Master Yuxian the Wine Immortal was a native of the Lin family of Changzhou in Gusu. His appearance was grand and strange; his mouth could accommodate two fists.
At seven years of age, he once submerged himself in a deep abyss, yet his clothes remained dry. He went to attend the Dragon Flower Assembly (Longhua), where he realized the Mind-Seal (Xinyin).

Upon returning, he resided at Mingjue Monastery, devoting himself solely to drinking wine. When intoxicated, he would compose songs and hymns to admonish both the clergy and the laity; consequently, he was known as the "Wine Immortal" (Jiuxian). He composed a verse:
"By green waters and red peach blossoms, I have wandered through front streets and back alleys more than a hundred times. Zhang San knows me; Li..."
Fourth: "Recognizing me, not recognizing me. Between these two fists, which one is larger? Of the two, one is large;
it once split open the void with a single blow. Rubbing it, he makes it return to suchness; picking up Mount Sumeru as a pillow, he lies down.
At the Yangtze River, the waves are deepest; when travelers reach this point, they all hesitate. In the future...

If you reach a place where there are no waves, yet you still apply your mind as if waves were present—just as one hears the golden goblet being filled with the Jasper Mountain wine, yet reports that it has already run dry so that the night-watchmen need not hasten the hours;
or as one buys cinnabar to paint the moon, only to find that, upon calculation, the effort was in vain.
It is better to lie drunk beneath the green willow shade than to rise and forcibly preach "True Suchness. A clay figure, even if urged repeatedly...
A reminder: do not let the jewel within your robes be lost. One-six, two-six; the matter is already complete. One-nine, two-nine; I wish to drink some wine.
Stretching out my two legs, I sleep one awakening; upon rising, heaven and earth remain as they were.
Before the gate, the green trees have no singing birds; beneath the courtyard, the gray moss has fallen blossoms. I shall briefly discuss this matter with the east wind. Ten.
To whom does the springtime belong? When autumn arrives, the mountains grow cold and the waters chill; when spring comes, the willows turn green and the flowers turn red.

A single movement follows ten thousand transformations; in the river village, the mist and rain are thick and dim. Is it existent? Is it non-existent? Is it empty? Is it not empty? With a bamboo sieve, one scoops up the northwest wind.
Born into this Jambudvīpa world, human sentiments abound with likes and dislikes; one simply wishes to drink a little wine.
Child, this is why you lie prostrate in the streets and on the roads; after death, you shall instead be reborn in the Sahā world rather than aspiring to be born in the Pure Land.
Why is this? For in the Western Pure Land, there are no wine shops.
Chan Master Yuantong Yuede of Mount Lu (Dharma Heir of Qingxi Jin):
A native of the Huang family of Lin’an, he traveled extensively throughout various regions during the Southern Tang kingdom.

The Master established a monastery on Mount Lu and invited the Teacher to expound the Dharma. When the general Cao Han and his troops crossed the river and entered the temple, the Zen practitioners fled in alarm.
The Master sat calmly as if it were an ordinary day. When Han arrived, the Master neither rose nor bowed.
Enraged, Han shouted, "Elder, have you not heard of a general who kills men without blinking? The Master stared at him intently and said, "How [dare you...]"
"Are you not afraid of birth and death, Master? Han asked, greatly astonished; he merely increased his respect. He then said, "Why have the Zen practitioners dispersed?
The Master replied, "They gather when the drum is struck. Han sent a subordinate officer to strike it, but not a single Zen practitioner arrived.
Han asked, "Why did they not come? The Master replied, "It was because you had a murderous intent. The Master then rose and struck the drum himself, and the Zen practitioners [all returned].
Thus collected.
*Jiaowai biezhuan* (The Special Transmission Outside the Teachings), Volume Seven and Volume Eight (Linji School).
Chan Master Linji Yixuan of Zhenzhou (Fourth Generation under Nanyue; Dharma Heir of Huangbo Xiyun).
Chan Master Linji Yixuan was a native of the Xing clan from Nanhua in Caozhou. From his youth, he bore the aspiration to transcend the mundane world.
As for Zhi: after he had shaved his head and received full ordination, he aspired to the Chan school. Initially, while in Huangbo’s assembly, his conduct was pure and singular.
At that time, Muzhou served as the First Seat (Dharma Seat Holder) and asked, "How long have you been here, Senior Monk? The Master replied, "Three years."
Muzhou asked, "Did you ask Caoshan? The Master replied, "I did not ask him. I do not know what I should have asked.
Muzhou said, "Why did you not ask the Abbot, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma'? The Master then went to ask him.
Before he had even finished speaking, Huangbo struck him. The Master came back down, and Muzhou asked, "How was your inquiry?"
The Master said, “Before my question had even finished, the Abbot struck me. I do not understand. Muzhou said, “Just go and ask again.
The Master asked once more, and Huangbo struck him again. This happened three times; he asked three times and was struck three times.

The Master said to Muzhou, “I have already benefited from your encouragement to inquire about the Dharma, and I have repeatedly received the Abbot’s blows. I only regret that my karmic obstacles hinder me.”
"Since you do not grasp the profound meaning, I shall now take my leave. Muzhou said, "If you are going, you must first take leave of the Abbot before departing.
The Master bowed and withdrew. Muzhou went first to Huangbo’s quarters and said, "That monk who came to question me, though he is but a youth,"
This is truly extraordinary. Had he come to take his leave, you should have used skillful means to receive him; later, he would have become a great tree, providing shade for all people under heaven.
The next day, the Master took his leave of Huangbo. Huangbo said, "There is no need for him to go elsewhere;
go directly to Daoyi at Tancheng in Gaoyang. He will surely explain it for you. When the Master arrived at Daoyi’s place, Daoyi asked, "From where have you come?"
[The Master] arrived. The teacher said, "Huangbo has come. Dayu asked, "What words did Huangbo say?
The Master replied, "Three times I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma, and three times I was struck. I do not know whether I was at fault or not."
Dayu said, "Huangbo’s grandmotherly heart was so earnest that he has worn you out; yet you come here again to ask whether you have committed an offense or not.
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "So it turns out, Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma amounts to nothing more than this.
Dayu grabbed him by the collar and said, "You bed-wetting little devil! Just now you asked whether you had committed an offense or not! As he spoke...
"Now you say, 'Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much. What principle have you seen? Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
The Master struck Daoyu three times under the ribs. Daoyu pushed him away and said, "Your teacher is Huangbo; it is none of my business.
The Master took his leave of Daoyu and returned to Huangbo. Upon seeing him, Huangbo asked, "This fellow has come back again?"
"Go away, go away! When will there ever be an end to this? The Master said, "It is simply because my grandmotherly heart is so earnest.

Having finished his formal greetings, he stood in attendance. Huangbo asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Yesterday, I received the Compassionate Command of the Honored One, ordering me to go to Daoyu;
that is where I have come from. Huangbo asked, "What words did Daoyu say? The Master recounted the previous conversation. Huangbo said, "Old Daoyu..."

Hanshao said, "You talkative fellow! Wait until you come back, and I will give you a thorough beating. The Master said, "What is the use of saying 'until you come back'? I shall strike you right now! He then slapped him.
Huangbo said, "This madman has come here to stroke a tiger’s whiskers. The Master then gave a shout.

Huangbo called to his attendant, "Take this madman away to the meditation hall. (Later, Guishan Lingyou raised this case and asked Yangshan Huiji: "At that time, did Linji receive the Dharma from Dayu?")

[He] obtained the power of Huangbo. Yangshan said, "Not only can he ride the tiger’s head, but he also knows how to grasp its tail. Baizhang Yuanwen’s verse says: With one punch, he topples the Yellow Crane Tower; With one kick, he overturns the Parrot Isle. When there is spirit, he adds to his spirit;

Where there is no elegance, he is nonetheless elegant. Baoning Yong’s verse says: Thunder and lightning roar, mountains and rivers darken; A household grieves, closing their doors in the rain. A wild wind suddenly rises and the dark clouds disperse; The bright sun fills the sky, and the stars and constellations divide.
One day, while on a communal work assignment (*pǔqǐng*), the Master [Yangshan] was walking behind Huangbo. Huangbo turned his head and saw that the Master was empty-handed.
Huangbo held up his hoe and asked, "Where is the hoe? The Master replied, "Someone has taken it away. Huangbo said, "Come closer;
let us deliberate on a matter together. The Master approached him. Huangbo held up the hoe and said, "This very thing—why is it that no one in the world can lift it?
The Master snatched it from his hand, held it up, and said, "Why is it that [you]..."
[The mattock] was in the hands of Huangbo. Huangbo said, "Today there is someone else who has been invited for communal labor," and he immediately returned to the monastery.

(Later, while Yangshan was attending Muzhou, Muzhou brought up this story before finishing it. Yangshan then asked, "The mattock was in Huangbo's hands; why was it then snatched away by Linji? Muzhou said, "The thief is a petty person, yet his cunning surpasses that of a gentleman.
Once, while the Master was plowing the field during communal labor, he saw Huangbo approaching. He stood with his mattock resting on his shoulder. Huangbo said, "This fellow is exhausted."
The Master said, "Before the mattock has even been raised, what is there to be exhausted? Huangbo struck him. The Master caught the staff and pushed him down with a single shove.
Huangbo called out to the *vina*, "Help me up! When the *vina* helped him up, he said, "How can you, O Monk, tolerate this madman's impertinence?
As soon as Huangbo rose, he struck the *vina*. The Master was hoeing the ground and said:

In other regions, people are cremated; here, we are buried alive. (Miaoshan asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning behind Huangbo’s beating of the *karmadāna*? Yangshan replied, "The real thief has fled, and the one who seized the stolen goods receives the beating.

Zhenjing Wen composed a verse: "Seizing the banner and pulling the drum requires spirit; though father and son are close, the Dharma is not so. To report this to the Zen guests from the four quarters: do not act like those who wait by the stump.

Yuedang Chang composed a verse: "Huangbo treats the living as if dead; Linji treats the dead as if alive. The *karmadāna* did not hear the matter correctly; he could not help but call a bell a jar. One day, the Master was in the Sangha Hall.
[The Master] was sleeping inside. Huangbo entered the hall and, seeing him, struck the head of the wooden board once with his staff.
The Master raised his head; seeing it was Huangbo, he went back to sleep. Huangbo struck the head of the board again, then went up to the upper section of the hall.

Seeing the Head Seat practicing *zazen*, he said, "The junior monks in the lower section are practicing *zazen*, yet you are here indulging in such deluded thoughts? The Head Seat... [remained silent].
Zu said, "What is this old fellow doing? Huangbo struck the head of the wooden board once more and then went out.

(Miaoshan raised this as a question for Yangshan, asking, "As for Huangbo’s intention, what was it? Yangshan replied, "Two colors, one match. While the Master was planting pine trees, Huangbo asked, "Why are you planting so many pines in the deep mountains?
The Master said, "First, to provide a scenic setting for the mountain gate; second, for those who come after."
The man set up a signpost, saying, "I have finished," and struck the ground three times with his mattock.
Huangbo said, "Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me. The Master struck the ground three times again and let out a long sigh.

Huangbo said, "When my lineage reaches you, it will flourish greatly in the world. (Miaogushan raised this question to Yangshan: "At that time, Huangbo instructed only Linji; was there anyone else? Yangshan replied: "There was.")

Yangshan said, “I have it. It is simply that the era is so remote that I do not wish to bring it up to you, Master. Miaoshan said, “Even so, I still wish to know. Just bring it up and see. Yangshan said, “One person points south; his commands prevail throughout Wu and Yue, yet they cease when encountering a great wind.

Master Zhe of Miaoshan said, “Linji acting like this is much like falling flat on one’s face on level ground. Nevertheless, only by remaining unchanging in the face of peril can one be called a true man. Huangbo said, “When my lineage reaches you, it will flourish greatly in the world.”

"This is pitying the child without realizing their ugliness. Tiantong Hua said: "Huangbo said, 'Even so, you have already received thirty blows from me. Such is the very nature of raising a child. Although Linji’s true command was put into practice, it is a pity he allowed himself to be buried alive by the mattock.

Yangshan’s understanding did not transcend the common flow; it was not merely that he stopped when encountering a great wind. Why did he not say at that time: 'Only when the realm of empty space is exhausted shall this story finally be widely practiced'?

Would this not be having both head and tail straight? Today, Ying’an pulls down his own face to meet you all. [Suddenly] picking up his staff, he strikes once and says: 'To startle the masses, one must be a man of heroic spirit; to overcome the superior, one must be a lion.'"
Once Huangbo entered the kitchen and asked the head cook, "What are you doing? The cook replied, "I am sorting the rice for the monks' meal.
Huangbo asked, "How much do they eat at one sitting? The cook said, "Two and a half *shí*. Huangbo said, "Is that not too much?
The cook said, "I am still afraid it might be too little. Huangbo then struck him. The cook reported this matter to the Master (Linji). The Master—
He said, "I shall examine this old fellow with you. As soon as they arrived and stood in attendance, Huangbo brought up the previous conversation.
The Master said, "The head cook does not understand; please, Preceptor, provide a turning phrase on his behalf. Huangbo said, "Just bring it up. The Master said, "Is that not too much?
Huangbo said, "Tomorrow you shall eat another meal. The Master said, "What do you mean by 'tomorrow'? Right now!"
He then ate it. Following this, [Baizhang] gave him a slap. Huangbo said, "This madman comes here again to stroke a tiger’s whiskers. The Master let out a shout and departed.

(Later, Guishan raised this case and asked Yangshan, "What was the meaning of these two venerable elders? Yangshan said, "What about you, Master? Guishan said, "Only by raising a child does one come to know a father's kindness.

Yangshan said, "Not so. Guishan said, "And what do you say? Yangshan said, "It is very much like inviting a thief to ruin the house. In the middle of the summer retreat, the Master went up [to the hall].
At Mount Huangbo, he saw Huangbo reading a sutra. The Master said, "I took you for someone special; it turns out you are just an old monk chanting 'Oṃ' and eating black beans.
After staying for several days, the Master took his leave. Huangbo said, "You arrived after the summer retreat has ended; why did you not stay for the full term?
The Master replied, "I came only briefly to pay my respects to the Master. Huangbo then struck him and drove him away. The Master departed.
After traveling several *li*, he had doubts about this matter and returned for the remainder of the summer retreat. Later, he took his leave of Huangbo, who asked, "Where are you going?
The Master replied, "Not south of the Yellow River; I am going back north of it. Huangbo struck him. The Master grabbed him and gave him a slap.
Huangbo laughed loudly, then called to his attendant, "Bring the meditation board and desk of our late master Baizhang! The Master...
[The Master] said, "Attendant, bring me some fire. Huangbo said, "Not so. You simply take it away;

later on, you shall sit and cut off the tongues of everyone under heaven. (Later, Guishan raised this question to Yangshan: "Did Linji not fail Huangbo? Yangshan said, "Not so. Guishan asked, "How do you understand it?")

Yangshan said, "Only by knowing gratitude does one understand how to repay it. Miaoshan asked, "Has there ever been anyone since antiquity who has repaid this debt of gratitude? Yangshan replied, "There has been, but because the time has been so long ago, I do not wish to cite it. Miaoshan said, "I do not yet know; you simply go ahead and cite it.

Yangshan said, "For instance, at the assembly on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, Ānanda praised the Buddha, saying: 'To offer this profound mind to every dust-mote world—that is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.

Is this not an act of repaying gratitude? Miaoshan said, "So it is, so it is. When one's view is equal to the teacher's, one lacks half the teacher's virtue; only when one's view surpasses the teacher's is one fit to receive the transmission. Arriving at the stupa of Bodhidharma, the caretaker asked, "Which shall we worship first?"

The Master first paid obeisance to the Patriarch. The Master said, "I pay obeisance to neither Patriarch nor Buddha. The Stupa Guardian asked, "What grievance do you have against the Patriarchs and Buddhas?
The Master shook his sleeves and departed. The Master traveled on behalf of Huangbo to Mt.
Miao, where he was conversing with Yangshan. Yangshan said, "In the future, you shall go north; there will be a place for you to dwell. The Master asked, "Is there anyone who..."
"What is this matter? Yangshan said, "Just go. In the future, there will be one person who will assist you;

this person will have a beginning but no end, a start but no finish" (this was a prophetic prediction regarding Puhua). Later, when the Master resided at Linji in Zhenzhou, disciples gathered like clouds.
One day, he said to the two senior monks Puhua and Ke Fu, "I wish to establish the Huangbo lineage here."
[The Master said: "As for the fundamental purpose, you two shall first strip me of it. The two men bowed respectfully and went down.
Three days later, Puhua came up and asked, "What did you say three days ago, Preceptor? The Master struck him.
Three days later, Kefu came up and asked, "Preceptor, why did you strike Puhua the other day? The Master struck him as well. (Changlu Ren said: "Puhua and Kefu must not be let off.")

The Old Man Linji must not let this pass. If it were Chan’an, he would have spent his whole life carrying a wooden board with no one to strip it from him. Nevertheless, you must know that beyond the distant mist and waves, there is another way to deliberate.
In the evening, for the small assembly, he said: "Sometimes the person is taken away but the environment is not; sometimes the environment is taken away but the person is not;

sometimes both person and environment are taken away; and sometimes neither person nor environment is taken away. (The words of the question and answer are contained in the *Kefu Zhang*. Zhongfeng Ben says: "Sometimes taking away the person is an error...")

At times there is an error of seizing the object; at times there is an error where both person and object are seized; and at times there is no error where neither person nor object is seized. When the Great Master Linji reached this point, he locked up the throats [of all].
Is there anyone who can speak out for him? You must by all means avoid taking error for truth. [Once], while attending a donor’s vegetarian feast together with Puhua, the Master asked:
"A hair swallows the vast ocean; a mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural state of things? Puhua kicked over the table.
[One day,] Puhua kicked over the rice table. The Master said, "That was quite crude. Puhua replied, "What kind of place is this, where you speak of coarse or fine?
The next day, they went to a meal together again. The Master asked once more, "How does today’s offering compare to yesterday's?
Puhua again kicked over the rice table. The Master said, "It is well done, indeed; yet it was rather crude. Puhua shouted, "Blind fellow! You talk of the Buddha-dharma!"
"What is coarse and what is subtle? The Master then stuck out his tongue. (Xuedou Xian said: "These two old thieves have not even finished their meal; they deserve thirty blows.

Although the blows were dealt, which one was the real thief? Zhaojue Qin said: 'If fine gold is not refined a hundred times, how can its brilliance be seen? If a supreme treasure is not appraised for its value, how can one distinguish the true from the false?

It was not Linji who could test Puhua, nor was it Puhua who could withstand Linji. This is what is called 'water entering water' and 'gold matching gold. Nevertheless, if you let them pass, both are masters; if you examine them closely, both suffer loss. Those who possess the eye of discernment—please try to judge this!')"

Nantang Jing said: "These two venerable masters were like two dragons contending for a pearl—grasping at clouds and seizing mist without stirring a ripple; like two tigers competing for food—vividly capturing and seizing alive without harming a living creature.

If someone were to ask, "The hair swallows the vast ocean; the mustard seed contains Mount Sumeru. Is this the wondrous function of spiritual powers, or is it simply the natural way of things? One should simply say: "Have you not heard the former master say: 'With one punch, he toppled Yellow Crane Tower; with one kick, he overturned Parrot Isle? When there is spirit, he adds to his spirit; where there is no elegance, he is nonetheless elegant.

Nanhua Bing said: "Linji calls forth directly before one's face; Puhua responds with his full capacity. It is such that the turtle-nosed snake of the South Mountain swallows the carp of the Eastern Sea; the iron [man] of Shanfu..."

"A bull knocks over the Great Image of Jiazhou. Why is it so? 'When meeting, one does not dismount; each goes on their own way. Tiantong Huahua said: "One emerges and one submerges; one goes and one comes. Snatching food from the mouth of a fierce tiger and scratching an itch on the head of a venomous snake—nevertheless, this does not yet measure up to the deeds of a great man.

These two elders were famous throughout the universe and their reputation was heavy in their time. How could this mountain monk keep his three inches [of tongue] tightly shut? If I let both pass, it is because they were playing with the false as if it were the real.

If I let neither pass, it is because they were being too excessive in their deception. As for you all, if you discuss this as if it were the Buddha-dharma, the school of Bodhidharma will be swept away to its very foundations. A monk asked: "What is..."
"The true Buddha, the true Dharma, and the true Way—I beg the Master to reveal them to me. The Master said: "The Buddha is the purity of the mind;
the Dharma is the luminosity of the mind; the Way is the pure light that is unimpeded everywhere. These three are one; they are all merely empty names."

Yet they do not truly exist. Just as a genuine practitioner of the Way maintains a state of mind that is uninterrupted from moment to moment—since the Great Master Bodhidharma came from the Western Land, he sought only one who would not be deluded by others;

later, upon meeting the Second Patriarch, he was enlightened in a single word and finally realized that all his previous efforts had been in vain. As for my own realization today, it is identical to that of the Patriarchs and Buddhas.
There is no distinction. If one realizes it within the first phrase, one is fit to be a teacher to the patriarchs and Buddhas.
If one realizes it within the second phrase, one is fit to be a teacher to humans and devas. If one realizes it within the third phrase, one cannot even save oneself.
A monk then asked, "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "The seal of the three essentials opens; the vermilion dot is narrow, allowing no room for hesitation."
The Master distinguished between the host and the guest, saying: "What is the second phrase? The Master replied: "How could wondrous understanding fail to admit the question of Wuzhuo?
How could Upāli fail to contend with the power of cutting off the stream? He asked: "What is the third phrase? The Master replied: "Just look at the puppeteer on the stage;
all the pulling and manipulating depend entirely upon the person inside. Then he said: "In general, when expounding the Dharma of the Patriarchal School, a single phrase..."
Within this, one must possess the three gates of mystery (*san-hsüan-mên*). Each gate of mystery must possess the three essentials (*san-yao*):
there is the provisional and the real; there is illumination and function. How do you all understand this? The Master said to the monks:
"Sometimes a single shout is like the precious sword of the Vajra King; sometimes a single shout is like a crouching lion; sometimes a single shout is like a probing rod."
Once, when Yingcao uttered a shout, it did not function as a shout. How do you understand this? When the monk hesitated, the Master shouted.
Addressing the assembly, he said: "Those who study the Way must be extremely discerning. It is like the meeting of host and guest, where there is an exchange of words;
or appearing in form in response to things; or functioning with one's entire being; or employing skillful means through displays of joy or anger."
Sometimes he manifests half his body; sometimes he rides a lion, or rides an elephant king.

When a true student of the Way lets out a shout, [the master] first produces a lacquer basin. The spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) fails to discern it as an objective environment and thus enters into that other's realm.
Acting out a mere imitation, he was again shouted at by the student. The former person refused to let go;

this is a terminal illness, beyond the reach of medical treatment. It is called "the guest looking for the host," or perhaps it is a case where a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) does not bring forth any object.
He simply seizes [the object] from wherever the student asks for it. When the student is thus seized, they refuse to let go even at the cost of their lives;
this is the host looking after the guest. Or, there may be a student who presents a single pure object before a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).
If the spiritual friend recognizes that it is such an object, he seizes it and hurls it into a pit. The student says, "Excellent, O spiritual friend! and the spiritual friend—
[The Master] said, "Alas! You do not know good from evil. The student then prostrated. This is called "the host looking at the host.
Or there may be a student who comes before a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) already wearing a cangue and shackles; the spiritual friend then places another layer of cangue and shackles upon them.
The student was delighted; yet, failing to discern between them, he called it "the guest looking at the guest.
"Virtuous One," the mountain monk says that all I have raised are means for distinguishing demons and selecting the extraordinary, so as to know what is heterodox and what is correct.

The Master asked Luopu, "Since the beginning of time, one person has practiced the staff and another has practiced the shout. Which of these is more intimate? Luopu replied, "Neither is intimate. The Master said, "What is the place of intimacy?"
Luopu then gave a shout. The Master then struck [the floor] with his staff and ascended the hall. There is one person who, for kalpas, remains on the road yet never leaves home;
there is another person who leaves home yet is not on the road. Which of these two deserves the offerings of devas and humans?

(Jingshan Gao said: "The thief’s identity is already revealed. Yunyan You said: "Recognize the meaning at the tip of the hook; do not mistake it for the fixed point on the scale. Chushi Qi said: "Heaven dawns with the white clouds; the water flows with the bright moon.")
The Master asked the head of the monastery, "Where have you been? He replied, "I have been to the prefectural city to sell yellow rice.
The Master said, "Did you sell it all? The head of the monastery said, "I sold it all. The Master drew a line with his staff and said, "Can you sell this as well?
The head of the monastery then shouted. The Master struck him. When the head cook arrived, the Master brought up the previous conversation. The head cook said, "The head of the monastery..."

“[The Abbot] did not understand Master Huanglong’s meaning. The Master said, “And what about you? The kitchen steward bowed, and the Master struck him as well. Huanglong Nan said: “When the temple head let out a shout, he could not have let him go. When the kitchen steward bowed, letting him go was also unacceptable. Linji’s command was being carried out; Guizong let him go. Thirty years later, someone will explain it clearly. Huanglong Xin said: “The kitchen steward’s bow had fault but no merit. The temple head’s shout had merit but no fault. Since there was merit, why was he struck? The eyes upon the staff are as clear as the sun; to recognize true gold, one must look within the fire. Jingshan Guangzhao composed a verse: The temple head’s shout was like thunder— The whole world was deafened. The kitchen steward’s bow was like a dragon— The whole world was startled. Linji’s staff was like a sword— The whole world was cut through. Guizong’s letting go was like a mirror— The whole world was reflected. If you wish to see the bright moon, Look at the water in the valley stream. If you wish to see the golden mountain, Look at the clouds atop the peak. If you wish to see the great ocean, Look at the waves on the shore. If you wish to see the great void, Look at the sky above your head. If you can see thus, Then you will know the meaning of this case. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never understand the meaning of this case. If you can see thus, Then you will see the Buddha-nature. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the Buddha-nature. If you can see thus, Then you will see the Patriarchs. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the Patriarchs. If you can see thus, Then you will see the Buddhas. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the Buddhas. If you can see thus, Then you will see the Dharma. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the Dharma. If you can see thus, Then you will see the self. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the self. If you can see thus, Then you will see the mind. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the mind. If you can see thus, Then you will see the Way. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the Way. If you can see thus, Then you will see the truth. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the truth. If you can see thus, Then you will see the reality. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the reality. If you can see thus, Then you will see the essence. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the essence. If you can see thus, Then you will see the function. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the branch. If you can see thus, Then you will see the leaf. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the leaf. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the fruit. If you can see thus, Then you will see the beginning. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the beginning. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the unconditioned. If you can see thus, Then you will see the relative. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the relative. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the mundane. If you can see thus, Then you will see the supramundane. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the supramundane. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the nirvana. If you can see thus, Then you will see the delusion. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the delusion. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the many. If you can see thus, Then you will see the self. If you cannot see thus, Then you will never see the self.
