Yunmen said: "A mass of red flames stretches across the clear sky; it makes no distinction between gold, silver, iron, or tin. Once one enters within, it causes everything to turn to water; how could it allow even a mosquito or a gnat to settle therein? Tiantong Huo said:

"Although these two venerable masters forcefully uphold the essential principles, when examined closely, they cannot avoid merely clinging to the grass and perching on the wood. Little do they realize that Linji, both great and small, has had his house broken up and his home scattered by these two fellows. Do you understand? This is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life.
[He] ascended the hall and said: "One person is atop a solitary peak with no way out; another person is at the crossroads of the street, likewise..."
There is no turning away or turning toward. Now tell me: which one is in front? Which one is behind? Do not act as Vimalakīrti;
do not act as Fu Dashi. Be careful! An old master came to visit and asked, "Is it right to prostrate, or is it right not to prostrate?
The Master gave a shout. The old master then prostrated. The Master said, "What a fine grass-thief! The old master said, "Thief! Thief!"
He then went out. The Master said, "Do not say that all is well. At that time, the Head Seat was standing in attendance.
The Master asked, "Is there any fault here? The Head Seat replied, "There is. The Master asked, "Is the fault on the guest's side or the host's side? [The Head Seat] said, "Both sides have faults.
The Master asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Head Seat then went out. The Master said, "Do not say that all is well."

When Nanquan Yuan heard this, he said, "The government horses trample one another. Baoning Yong said, "This group of bandits—among them are both the primary thief and the grass-thief. Which one is the primary thief? Which one is the grass-thief? Can you distinguish them? Confessions are easy to make, but stolen goods are hard to identify.

Huguo Yuan said, "This monk thrusts his body against a white blade; Linji’s sword was not applied in vain. The Head Seat did not observe from the sidelines well enough and got himself covered in mud and water. Even so, tell me: how does 'no affair' at the beginning compare to 'no affair' at the end?

If you can clearly distinguish black from white here, not only will you pierce Linji’s nostrils, but I grant that your eye-sight will blaze through the four quarters of the world. If it is not yet so, do not even speak of it."
[No good thing] (O). The Master went to the capital to practice *dhūta* (alms-round). Arriving at the gate of a house, he said, "I hope your household will fill my bowl.
A woman said, "You are truly insatiable! The Master said, "I have not even received any rice yet; why do you say I am insatiable?
The woman then shut the door. The Master ascended the hall. A monk came forward, and the Master gave a shout. The monk also shouted, then bowed. The Master—
[He] struck [him]. (Cuiyan Zhi said: "Linji’s mind was coarse; it was fortunate that this monk was there. If it had been a patch-robed monk of these modern times, how could he have escaped?
Dongchan Guan said: "Linji would simply not act; if he were to act, the ten thousand apertures would roar in fury. This monk seized the *fuyao* wind and ascended ninety thousand li.

When Zhaozhou arrived at the monastery during his travels, while he was washing his feet in the rear hall, the Master asked him, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Zhaozhou replied, "I happen to meet the mountain monk."

[The Master] was washing his feet. The Master [Baizhang] approached and made a gesture as if listening. Zhaozhou said, "If you understand, then understand; why do you keep picking at it? The Master then returned to his quarters.

Zhaozhou said, "Thirty years of traveling on pilgrimage, and today I have mistakenly provided a commentary for others. (An alternative version reads: "When Zhaozhou was traveling on pilgrimage, he visited the Master.

While meeting the Master as he was washing his feet, Zhaozhou asked, 'What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master replied, 'It happens to be the time when the old monk is washing his feet. Zhaozhou then approached and made a gesture as if listening.")

Shi said, "I would need to pour a second ladle of foul water over him. Zhaozhou then went down. Fayun Xiu said, "Among the assembly, some discuss this, saying that Zhaozhou did not recognize Linji as a thief, yet he nonetheless provided a commentary for him."

At that time, Linji made a gesture as if listening. Why did he not immediately strike him with his palm? If you deliberate in such a manner, when have you ever dreamed of Zhaozhou or come to know Linji? You do not realize that both were old thieves; you must know that one was a true master. I ask you all: which of them was the master?
Let those with eyes discern this! Jiaozhong Guang said: "Linji possessed the eye to test people; Zhaozhou, moreover, was well-versed in the monastic community.

When they casually revealed their standards, naturally head and tail were straight. Do you understand? If one does not encounter flowing water, one must surely pass over other mountains. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Dingzhou. The Master took up [the case].
"Stick! The monk hesitated; the Master struck him immediately. The monk did not accept this, and the Master said, "In the future, you will encounter those with clear eyes.
Later, the monk went to visit Sansheng; as soon as he brought up the previous conversation, Sansheng struck him. The monk hesitated, and Sansheng struck him again. (Tiantong Huo said:

"If Linji and Sansheng had possessed a turning phrase at that time, the descendants of later generations would not have been reduced to mere dust. [Suddenly picking up his staff: There is yet another—where does he go? [He strikes the ground once with the staff].")

The Master frequently used the shout (*he*) in response to the capacities of his audience. His disciples under him also learned the Master’s shout. The Master said: "You all learn my shout from me. Now I ask you:
suppose one person comes out from the eastern hall and another comes out from the western hall, and both let out a shout at the same time.
Can you distinguish guest from host here? How would you go about making that distinction? If you can distinguish them—"
It is not permitted. From now on, you must not imitate this old monk’s shout. [He] addressed the assembly: "Sometimes I first illumine and then act;

sometimes I first act and then illumine; sometimes illumination and action are simultaneous; sometimes illumination and action are not simultaneous. When I first illumine and then act, there is a person present.
When I first act and then illumine, there is a Dharma present. When illumination and action are simultaneous, I drive away the plowman."

To take the food from a starving man’s mouth, to strike his bones to extract the marrow, and to apply needles and awls with piercing pain—these represent the timing of Illumination (*zhào*) and Function (*yòng*).
When there is questioning and answering, when guest and host are established, and when water and mud are mixed together, one responds to the occasion and engages with beings.

If you are a person of transcendent capacity, before the question has even been raised, you should spring up and go; even so, you would still have a slight advantage. (Fenyang Shanzhao said: "First illumination, then function; let us discuss this with you.")

"Regarding 'measuring': first there is the measuring, then the illuminating; only then can you be considered a person. When illumination and function are simultaneous, how will you respond? When illumination and function are not simultaneous, how will you find your footing? Langye Huijue said: "First illumination, then function."

He bares the claws and fangs of the lion; first the function, then the illumination. He unleashes the fierce majesty of the elephant king; illumination and function are simultaneous. Like a dragon obtaining water, it brings forth rain and soars with clouds;

illumination and function are not simultaneous. He guides the infant and looks down with pity upon the child. This is how the ancients established the Dharma gates: is it appropriate to be thus, or is it inappropriate? If it is appropriate to be thus, Ji Xin rode the nine-dragon palanquin; if it is inappropriate to be thus, Xiang Yu lost his thousand-li steed.

Is there anyone here who can vent their indignation on behalf of Langye? If there is none, this mountain monk shall speak for himself. (He plants his staff and descends from the seat. Ciming Yuan said: "Sometimes illumination comes first and function follows; sometimes function comes first and illumination follows; sometimes illumination and function are simultaneous; sometimes..."

"Shining and functioning do not occur at the same time. Therefore it is said: 'There is light and there is darkness; there is arising and there is falling. [The Master] lets out a shout and says: 'Tell me, is this shining or is this functioning? Is there anyone here who can distinguish between them?

If there is, come forth and show your clumsy face. If there is not, the mountain monk loses today. Jingshan Gaofeng said: "If one shines first and then functions, one blinds the eyes of all people. If one functions first and then shines, one opens the eyes of all people. If one shines..."

If simultaneous, then half-blind and half-open. If illumination and function are not simultaneous, then entirely open and entirely blind. Among these four statements, one case has the guest but no host; one case has the host but no guest; one case has neither guest nor host; and one case fully possesses both guest and host.

Now, suppose someone among this assembly—one who cannot be deceived—should come and say: "What kind of place is this, where you speak of existence and non-existence, of the empty and the real, and of illumination?"

Regarding the "Explanation": The speaker addresses the listener, seizing them by the chest and pulling them down from the meditation seat, striking them with a heavy blow. One cannot blame him for this. When the Master was traveling on pilgrimage, he arrived at Longguang.
On the occasion of ascending the hall, the Master stepped forward and asked, "Without deploying a sharp edge, how can one achieve victory?
Longguang remained seated. The Master said, "Great *kalyāṇamitra*, do you have no skillful means? Longguang stared at him with wide eyes and said, "Ha!

The Master pointed his finger and said, "This old fellow has been defeated today. (Jingshan Gao said: It is a pity that Longguang let this man off. Nevertheless, he must first save the old man Linji.)
Next, he went to the place of Master Sanfeng Ping. Ping asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Huangbo.
Ping said, "What words or phrases did Huangbo have for you? The Master said, "Last night, the Golden Ox was covered in mud and filth; even until now, his tracks are nowhere to be seen.
Ping said, "The golden wind blows through the jade flute; who is it that knows this sound? The Master said, "It penetrates directly through ten thousand [miles]."
The Double Barrier. Píng said, "Your question just now was far too high. The Master said, "A golden phoenix born from a dragon breaks through the azure lapis lazuli.
Píng said, "Sit for a moment and drink some tea. He then asked, "Where have you recently come from?"
The Master said, "Longguang. Ping asked, "How is Longguang these days? The Master then went out. Later, he went to Fenglin.
On the road, he encountered a woman. She asked, "Where are you going? The Master said, "I am going to Fenglin. The woman said, "It happens that Fenglin is not here at the moment.
The Master asked, "Where has he gone? The woman then walked away. The Master called out to her; she turned her head back, and the Master [simply stood there].
He set out. (An alternate version reads: "The Master said: 'Who says he is not here? Upon arriving at Fenglin, Fenglin asked, "May I ask you something? The Master replied: "Yes."
"How can you carve out flesh to create a wound? Fenglin said, "The sea moon is clear and shadowless; the wandering fish alone is deluded.
The Master said, "Since the sea moon has no shadow, how can the wandering fish be deluded? Fenglin said, "Observing the wind, one knows the waves arise; gazing at the water, the wild sail drifts.
The Master said, "The solitary moon shines alone as the rivers and mountains fall silent; with one long啸 (shout/sigh), heaven and earth turn autumnal."

Fenglin said, "Let Zhang San-inch wield heaven and earth; try to speak a single phrase on the spot. The Master said, "When meeting a swordsman on the road, one must present a sword; if one is not a poet, one does not offer a poem. Fenglin then ceased. The Master then offered this verse: "The Great Way is beyond sameness; One may go west or east as one pleases. The spark of flint cannot catch up; A flash of lightning cannot penetrate. (Maizhou Daowu asked Baizhang Huaihai: "Master, what is the meaning of the Patriarch coming from the West? Baizhang said, "The cypress tree in the garden. Maizhou said, "I have already understood. Baizhang said, "If you had said so at the time, I would have hit your mouth with my staff. Maizhou said, "If you had struck me then, I would have hit your head with it. Baizhang said, "Now that you have hit my head, where will you go? Maizhou said, "I will go where there is no road. Baizhang said, "If there is no road, how will you go? Maizhou said, "I will go by means of the pathless way. Baizhang said, "If you go by the pathless way, you will fall into the pit of the pathless way. Maizhou said, "If I fall into the pit of the pathless way, who will save me? Baizhang said, "I will save you. Maizhou said, "If you save me, I will bite off your nose. Baizhang said, "If you bite off my nose, I will give you my head. Maizhou said, "If you give me your head, I will take it back. Baizhang said, "If you take it back, I will give you my eyes. Maizhou said, "If you give me your eyes, I will see through them. Baizhang said, "If you see through them, I will give you my ears. Maizhou said, "If you give me your ears, I will hear through them. Baizhang said, "If you hear through them, I will give you my tongue. Maizhou said, "If you give me your tongue, I will speak through it. Baizhang said, "If you speak through it, I will give you my teeth. Maizhou said, "If you give me your teeth, I will chew through them. Baizhang said, "If you chew through them, I will give you my skin. Maizhou said, "If you give me your skin, I will wear it. Baizhang said, "If you wear it, I will give you my bones. Maizhou said, "If you give me your bones, I will break them. Baizhang said, "If you break them, I will give you my marrow. Maizhou said, "If you give me your marrow, I will fill it. Baizhang said, "If you fill it, I will give you my life. Maizhou said, "If you give me your life, I will preserve it. Baizhang said, "If you preserve it, I will give you my death. Maizhou said, "If you give me your death, I will transcend it. Baizhang said, "If you transcend it, I will give you my Nirvana. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Nirvana, I will enter it. Baizhang said, "If you enter it, I will give you my Samsara. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Samsara, I will transform it. Baizhang said, "If you transform it, I will give you my Buddha-nature. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Buddha-nature, I will realize it. Baizhang said, "If you realize it, I will give you my Dharma-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Dharma-body, I will manifest it. Baizhang said, "If you manifest it, I will give you my Response-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Response-body, I will serve it. Baizhang said, "If you serve it, I will give you my Transformation-bodies. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Transformation-bodies, I will employ them. Baizhang said, "If you employ them, I will give you my Vajra-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Vajra-body, I will shatter it. Baizhang said, "If you shatter it, I will give you my Lotus-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Lotus-body, I will open it. Baizhang said, "If you open it, I will give you my Jewel-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Jewel-body, I will polish it. Baizhang said, "If you polish it, I will give you my Sun-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Sun-body, I will illuminate it. Baizhang said, "If you illuminate it, I will give you my Moon-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Moon-body, I will reflect it. Baizhang said, "If you reflect it, I will give you my Star-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Star-body, I will align it. Baizhang said, "If you align it, I will give you my Earth-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Earth-body, I will support it. Baizhang said, "If you support it, I will give you my Water-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Water-body, I will wash it. Baizhang said, "If you wash it, I will give you my Fire-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Fire-body, I will burn it. Baizhang said, "If you burn it, I will give you my Wind-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Wind-body, I will blow it away. Baizhang said, "If you blow it away, I will give you my Space-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Space-body, I will encompass it. Baizhang said, "If you encompass it, I will give you my Time-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Time-body, I will measure it. Baizhang said, "If you measure it, I will give you my Non-time-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Non-time-body, I will transcend it. Baizhang said, "If you transcend it, I will give you my No-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your No-body, I will be it. Baizhang said, "If you are it, I will give you my Not-it-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Not-it-body, I will be neither it nor not-it. Baizhang said, "If you are neither it nor not-it, I will give you my Middle-way-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Middle-way-body, I will walk upon it. Baizhang said, "If you walk upon it, I will give you my Void-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Void-body, I will dwell within it. Baizhang said, "If you dwell within it, I will give you my Non-void-body. Maizhou said, "If you give me your Non-void-body, I will be free from both void and non-void. Baizhang said, "If you are free from both void and non-void, I will give you my Unobtainable-body. As for Upāsaka Ding (a dharma heir of Linji Xuan):
When Upāsaka Ding first visited Linji, he asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma? Linji [pushed him] down from his meditation seat.
He seized him. As the Master hesitated, Linji gave him a slap. The Master stood there reflecting; a monk standing nearby said, "Master Ding, why do you not prostrate?
Only then did the Master prostrate, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Later, while traveling south, he met Yantou, Xuefeng, and Qingshan on the road.
Yantou asked, "Where have you come from, Senior? The Master replied, "I have come from Linji. Yantou...
[The monk] said, "May the Abbot be well. The Master said, "The Abbot has already passed away.
Yantou said, "We three specifically went there to pay our respects, but due to our meager merit, we did not meet him. I do not know what sayings or phrases he had while alive;
I request you, Venerable Sir, to cite one or two instances. The Master then cited: When Linji was ascending the hall, he said, "Upon this ball of red flesh, there is a..."
"The Person of No-Rank constantly enters and exits the face-gates of all of you. Those who have not yet attained realization, look! Look!
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the Person of No-Rank? Linji seized him by the collar from his meditation seat and said, "Speak! Speak!"
As the monk hesitated, Linji pushed him away and said, "The 'true person of no station'—what kind of dried piece of shit is that?
Yantou involuntarily stuck out his tongue. Xuefeng said, "Linji is very much like a stealthy thief.

Qingshan said, "Why not say that upon this lump of raw flesh there is no 'true person of no station'? The Master then seized him and said, "'The true person of no station' and 'not [the true person of no station]..."
"The True Man of No Rank—how far apart are we? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Qingshan was thus cornered;
his face turned yellowish-green, and he could not utter a word. Yantou and Xuefeng said, "This new monk does not know good from evil;
he has offended the Senior Monk. Please show him some compassion. The Master said, "If it were not for these two old fellows, I would have beaten this little shit to death!"
While Master Chuang Guizi was at a vegetarian feast in the Prefectural Government Office, he returned and sat upon a bridge.
He encountered three *zuozhu* (seminar masters), one of whom asked, "What is the bottom of the deep river of Chan? The Master seized him and prepared to throw him over the bridge.
The other two *zuozhu* stepped forward and pleaded, "Please do not take offense at our intrusion; we pray you show us compassion. The Master—
He said, "If it were not for these two masters, I would have driven him to his ultimate limit.
This was Master Huo (a Dharma heir of Linji Xuan).
When Master Huo left Linji and went to visit Deshan, as soon as Deshan saw him, he descended from his meditation seat and began to fold up his sitting mat.
[Shi] said, "Set this aside for a moment. Suppose someone were to come whose mind and environment are as one—what would you say to him so as to avoid being censured by those in all quarters?
Deshan said, "He would still be three steps behind me from days of old;
he must become a true master himself. [Shi] then gave a shout. Deshan remained silent. [Shi] said, "I have stuffed this old fellow's throat shut!"

[He] was choked. He shook out his sleeves and departed. (When Guishan Ying heard this being cited, he said: "Although Master Huo gained the advantage, what can be done? It is like covering one's ears while stealing a bell. Jiangshan Qin said: "Master Huo’s single shout—")

The guest and host were clearly defined; Deshan was speechless, and his words spread throughout the world. Old Man Guishan added frost to snow. If one examines this closely, neither can be let pass. (He then threw down his staff. Furthermore, he visited Baizhang.

After the tea had been served, Baizhang said, "Is there anything you would like to ask me? The Master said, "Fortunately, it is not a matter of words; why do you need this cup of tea? Baizhang said, "If that is so, then I permit your question.
Baizhang said, "Have you recovered An? (Note: "An" refers to the name of a specific object or state).
Nan. Again, when Youse was in the north, the Master [Nanyue] tore open his own chest and said, "In this way, not in this way.
Baizhang said, "In any case, it is difficult to grasp; in any case, it is difficult to grasp. The Master said, "If you know, you will attain it; if you know, you will attain it. (Yangsuan Ji said:
"If there is anyone who can discern where these two men have fallen, they are truly extraordinary. If you cannot distinguish it, it is much like losing one's way at midday.")
The Sixth Generation under Nanyue (the Second Generation under Linji):
Chan Master Huiyong of Nan’uan (Dharma Heir of Xinghua Jiang).
Chan Master Huiyong of Nan’uan in Ru Prefecture (also known as Baoying) ascended the hall and said: "Upon this mass of flesh, it stands like a cliff ten thousand fathoms high."
A monk asked, "The 'bare flesh-ball' stands ten thousand fathoms high—was this not said by you, Master? The Master replied, "Yes.
The monk then overturned the meditation seat. The Master said, "This blind donkey is acting recklessly. As the monk hesitated, the Master struck him. (Jingshan Daoyuan said:)

"I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never prove false. Tiantong Huahua said: "This is like inviting a thief to ruin one's house. Had it not been for this monk’s daring to pull the tiger’s whiskers, who would have seen the great merit of Nan-yuan’s martial exploits?

Nevertheless, I, this mountain monk, shall provide another path: 'Upon the bare flesh-ball, it stands ten thousand fathoms high. If a monk comes forth, strike him across the back! Why? Because it is the sword that kills and the sword that gives life. Let those with eyes look! Chushi Qi said:

"This monk dared to scratch his itch upon the head of a venomous snake and scale the jaws of a blue dragon. Who would not admire his great audacity? It is only that at the end he lacked a single move: 'Once he has emerged from the cave, there is no hand that can rival him; where one may yield to another, one should yield.'"
[The Master] questioned a monk: "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "From Changshui. The Master said, "Does it flow east or flow west?
The monk said, "It is not like that at all. The Master said, "How then? The monk said, "Take care! The Master then struck him. A monk came for an interview.
The Master raised his whisk. The monk said, "Today you have failed. The Master lowered the whisk. The monk said, "There is still this one remaining. The Master then struck him.
The Master questioned a monk: "Where have you recently come from? The monk replied, "Xiangzhou. The Master said, "What brings you here?

"Originally it was you who struck me; I shall strike you back for now, so that these words may spread far and wide.

To grasp the Three Mysteries, one must return to Nan-yuan before it can be attained. Why did Xuedou instead say, "The whisk does not know its place of origin"? Miaoxi also said, "Blind! This is merely to ensure that both may see one another.

"Why is it that you have instead acquired the razor of Jiangxi? Thinking of Ming pinched the Master’s hand. The Master said, "Attendant, take this away.

The monk then asked, "What is the simultaneous application of the chick pecking and the hen pecking? The Master said, "A master does not wait for the pecking;

The monk said, "I have lost. The Master then struck him. The monk was unwilling to accept this. (Cuiyan Zhen said: "To deliberate within the tent and decide victory a thousand miles away—although Nanyuan’s total strategy was used to face the enemy,")

Is there now any monk of true substance? Come forth and meet with Dapui. The entire army was victorious; it was like grass bowing before the wind. Nan-yuan was like a lion: even when pouncing on a rabbit, he preserved his full strength. Later, while at Yunmen’s assembly, he heard two monks discuss this story.

"You have understood my words and acted accordingly; I shall not strike you now, for you have grasped this saying of mine.

Chan Master Siming of Xiyuan in Ruzhou. When the senior monk Congyi arrived at his Dharma seat, after ten days had passed, he would often say to himself:

Ming said, "The old man was wrong. Yi said, "It was I who was wrong. The Master said, "Wrong, wrong! He then said, "Upādhyāya, stay here for the summer retreat;

Every time he brought up the previous conversation, he would say, "When I was traveling as a mendicant, I was blown by a malignant wind to Ju-chou. There was a West..."
"Venerable Elder, you have committed two consecutive errors regarding me; please let me stay for the summer retreat so that we may deliberate together.
I do not say it was an error at this moment; I already knew it was an error when I first set out for the South. (Shoushan Nian said:)

According to Tiantong’s interpretation in this way, he has not even dreamed of Xiyuan. Why? Because the words remain. Zhaojue Renqin said: "If people nowadays hear him say that he set out toward the south, they already knew it was wrong."

He then went off to speculate, saying: "Before I set out on my travels, I did not possess such a multitude of Buddhist teachings, Chan, and the Way. Yet, upon traveling, I was thoroughly deceived by those in all directions. It cannot be that before I traveled I was calling earth heaven and mountains water; fortunately, there was not a single speck of such nonsense.

If this were all merely a matter of common, worldly interpretations, why not simply buy a hat and wear it so we could all pass the time? What use would there be for the Buddha-dharma? The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of this sort."
Master Baoshou (the successor of Master Baoshou Zhao).
[He was] the second patriarch of Baoshou. Previously, while serving as the ritual master at Baoshou, Baoshou asked him:
"Before your parents were born, bring me back your original face. The Master stood there until late at night, yet his responses did not accord with the truth. On the following day...
He took his leave. Baoshou asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "Yesterday I received the Master's question, but I did not find it resonant.
I am going south to visit spiritual teachers. Baoshou said, "In the south, they prohibit the summer retreat but not the winter.

Here, we prohibit the winter but not the summer. For now, go about the streets as a wandering monk and pass the summer here. As for the Buddha-dharma, it is found even in the midst of the marketplace."
In the midst of the vast and turbulent red dust of the world, he constantly preached the True Dharma, and his disciples did not dare to disobey him.
One day, seeing two people quarreling on the street, he struck out a single fist and said, "How can you be so shameless? At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He rushed to see Baoshou; before he could utter a word, Baoshou said, "You understand! There is no need to speak. The Master then prostrated himself.

Zhaojue Qin said: "Wherever it strikes or bumps, the local scenery of the original ground is revealed right before one's eyes. Responding to sounds and forms, there is not even a hair’s breadth of leakage. Do you understand how he could speak in such a way that he has no face?
When the dragon-sleeve is swept aside, the whole body is manifest. When Baoshou was about to pass away, he instructed Sansheng: "Please request the Master to open the hall [for his first sermon].
When the Master opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk; the Master then struck him. Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher in this manner, you will not only blind this one..."

At the Bajiao Hermitage on Mount Nanyue was Chan Master Guduan of the Great Way. He was a native of Quanzhou. Having received the Dharma from Fenyang, he roamed freely through the Lake and Xiang regions.

when fallen leaves touched the waves, thunder and rain would inevitably rage for days, such that passersby dared not even breathe.
As the Master and Ciming were returning at dusk, the Master seized Ciming’s robe and said, "We should bathe together. Ciming pulled his arm away and went straight on. Thereupon, the Master undressed.

He leaped into [the water]. A thunderclap followed immediately; a stench-filled wind blew and rain fell, shaking the trees and forest. Ciming crouched among the grass, thinking the Master must have died. After a short while, the sky cleared and brightened.

Suddenly, [Ciming] extended his neck out from amidst the waves and said, "Jingshan, believe me! Guquan is merely making a wind and making a storm. (Jingshan Xinyun noted: "Guquan was acting like one possessed by a wind.")

The venomous dragon did not dare move so much as a single hair. This old man Ciming, even at his advanced age, still had this [capacity] remaining. He composed a verse: "Guquan was far too murderous, acting like one driven mad; A single shove sent the dragon’s pool surging, its waves sweeping the heavens.

Thunder and rain continue to this day without ceasing; Ciming lies sleeping amidst the dead grass. Once, when the monk Yiyu came to visit, he asked, "Is the abbot of the hermitage here? The Master said, "Who is it? He replied, "I am a traveling monk.
The Master asked, "What do you want? He replied, "I wish to pay my respects to the abbot. The Master said, "It happens that the abbot is currently..."

He replied, "People say you are the Abbot; they say you have personally seen Fenyang. The Master stripped his robe and shook it out, saying, "Do you think I saw Fenyang? How much...?"

Ou-yang suddenly called for the board to be cleared and requested a Dharma talk based on the game of chess. The Master immediately ordered the drum to be beaten.

He struck the drum. Ascending the seat, he said: "If one were to discuss this matter, it is like two parties engaged in a game of Go. What does this resemble? It is a match between equals who understand one another;

when the opportunity arises, there is no yielding. If one merely strings together five stones while conceding three, even if a single path is opened, one can only achieve the level of those who know how to secure life within their own territory by closing the gates.
They do not understand how to seize the corner, break through the barriers, or confront the hard nodes where they are level with the tiger’s mouth."
Once the game is lost, all your maneuvers are in vain. Thus it is said: "The fat edges are easy to find; the thin belly is hard to seek. If you think and act, you will often fail;
your mind is coarse and stuck, and from time to time you strike your head against things. Do not boast of being a master of the board, nor speak in vain of being an immortal.
Whether winning the game or losing the pieces is not the question; tell me, when black and white have not yet been distinguished, where does that first move fall?

What has been attained and what has been created does not constitute awakening to the mind-ground; how could one possibly possess such a wondrous principle?

Lù said, "A cat sleeping beneath a peony flower. Master [Yunmen] became increasingly puzzled and alarmed. One day, during a communal work assignment (*yǒnpǐng*), Gùyǐn asked, "Are you carrying firewood today?
The Master replied, "Yes. Gùyǐn said, "When Yúnmén asked a monk, 'As for the person carrying firewood and the firewood being carried, how do you understand this?
You had no answer. Gùyǐn continued, "This matter is like a person learning to write: it depends on the strokes and characters."

That which can be emulated is skillful; that which cannot is clumsy. This is because one has not yet been able to forget the dharma. One must reach the state where the brush forgets the hand, and the hand forgets the mind—only then is it possible.
The Master then attained silent realization and, after a long while, said: "As Shitou said: 'The very act of grasping at things is fundamentally delusion.'"
"It accords with principle, yet it is not awakening. Guoyin said, "Do you consider this medicinal speech to be diseased speech?
The Master replied, "It is medicinal speech. Guoyin rebuked him, saying, "You take disease for medicine; how can that be right? The Master said, "The fact is like a box finding its lid;
the principle is like an arrow’s straight point. How could there be anything more wondrous than this? Yet you still consider it to be truly diseased; you have not yet grasped the essential meaning."
Guyin said: "Miaozhi is likewise merely a designation for principle and phenomenon (*li-shi*). The intent of the Patriarchs cannot be reached by intellectual consciousness;
how much less can principle and phenomenon exhaust it? Therefore, the World-Honored One said: 'Knowledge of principle obstructs right view;

knowledge of phenomena obstructs the continuity of birth and death. Master [Yunmen] was as if awakened from a dream and asked: 'How does one make use of this? Guyin replied: 'Words do not depart from their nest.'"
"Mortar! How could you possibly escape the shroud of entanglements? The Master sighed and said, "As soon as it passes through the lips, it falls into the realm of conceptual thought;
these are all dead ends, never the living path. Ascending the hall, he said, "The Buddhas of the three periods of time are my servants; the entire Great Canon of teachings is my spittle.
After a long silence, he asked, "Tell me, whose servants are the Buddhas of the three periods? Then, taking up his whisk, he drew a circle.
He drew a single line and said, "The Buddhas of the three periods have all passed over this side. Now tell me: who is it that spat upon the entire Great Canon?
The Master then spat once himself.
Chan Master Dedun of Dachen Mountain in Tangzhou (Dharma heir of Guyin Cong).
Master Dedun asked Guyin, "What was the meaning when the ancients asked for fire? Guyin said, "Let it go out.
The Master asked, "What is it like after it has gone out? Guyin said, "The first and the eleventh. The Master said, "If that is so..."
"This is indeed a fine occasion. [The Master] said, "What principle have you seen? The Master replied, "Today I am utterly exhausted.
Gu-yin then struck him. The Master then composed a verse: "The mechanism of requesting fire is truly swift; The subtle function of concealing the point is rarely guessed.
If you wish to understand my Master’s direct intent, When the furnace fire is spent, no more wood is added."
Chan Master Yongqing Guangpu (Dharma heir of Guyin Cong).
Chan Master Yongqing Guangpu of Guozhou initially asked Guyin, "The ancients said, 'Tomorrow there is a vegetarian feast at Dabeiyuan. What is the meaning of this?
[Guyin] replied, "The sun rises from the sheltered side; sitting in the cold, one does not lift one's head. The Master entered [the path].
In the quarters, Guyin asked, "Regarding the causal conditions just now, how do you understand them? The Master said, "If one understands, it is for use on the journey;
if one does not understand, it is merely worldly discourse. Guyin said, "Not yet—speak further! The Master shook his sleeves and departed.

The Layman Li Zunxū, Prince Consort and Commander-in-Chief, visited Guyin and inquired about the matter of leaving the household life.
Guyin answered him with the kōan concerning Duke Cui’s question to Master Jingshan. Upon these words, the Duke attained great enlightenment and composed a verse, saying: "Studying the Way..."
One must be an iron man; when the hand touches the heart, one must judge immediately. Proceed directly toward unsurpassed Bodhi, and do not concern yourself with any matters of right or wrong.
One day, Master Huangbo was seeing off Senior Monk Jian. The Master asked, "You recently departed from Shangdang and have now arrived at the Capital.

Qingliu said, "I do not yet understand how matters are handled here and there. What is it like? Jian replied, "The sharp sword sweeps through, and heaven and earth are silent;
the frosty blade is raised, and the Dipper and Ox are cold. Gong said, "It happens that today my ears are deaf. Jian said, [and remained silent].

The Layman Xia Song, Duke Ying (Dharma heir of Cóng of Gùyǐn).
The Layman Xia Song, Duke Ying, styled Zǐqiáo, attained realization of the fundamental principle under Gùyǐn and daily associated with elderly monks.
By chance, Chan Master Shanglan Pu arrived. The Duke asked, "When the hundred limbs fall apart and scatter, which one is the Elder’s own self?
Shanglan replied, "I left Qiyang on the twentieth day of last month. The Duke stopped speaking.
Shanglan then asked, "When the hundred limbs fall apart and scatter, which one is the Duke’s own self? The Duke gave a shout. Shanglan said, "As for that shout—"
"It is not that there is nothing. After all, which one among these is the Master’s own? The Master replied with a verse: "Do not mistake the foremost pivot before the wind;
Where in the vast void can thought be lodged? If this mountain monk wishes to convey the message, It is when the moon rises over ten thousand miles of cloudless sky.
Shanglan said, "This too is merely playing with the spirit."

Chan Master Daolong of Huayan in Dongjing first visited Master Cheshen of Shimen and asked: "The ancients said..."
"Simply by being able to find peace and naturalness wherever one is, one accords with the ancient tracks. Although these words exist, the mind of doubt has not yet ceased.
At that time, how should one proceed? Shimen said: "Only when you know 'there is' can you find peace and naturalness wherever you are, like a person living in a prefecture or a county."
Whether heard or seen, there were thousands of wonders and hundreds of anomalies; yet he treated them all as ordinary matters, remaining unaware of them and dwelling in peace.
It was like a person living in a village who, upon encountering a few sights and sounds, would treat them with alarm and wonder. Master [Fengxue] attained realization upon hearing these words.
Shimen fully transmitted to him the essential principles of Dongshan. Later, he became the successor of Guanghui. One day, Fuyan received...

He then said, 'Put it down and you will be at peace. At that moment, I gave my assent to him. Thereupon, he recounted his time with Shimen.

At first, he was bewildered, yet he began to develop a slight degree of reverence and faith. Later, he met with Lord Li of the Hanlin Academy, who urged him to seek instruction.

The Duke said, 'Please, Master, offer another turn of phrase. Guanghui then made a gesture with his hand."
Pulling at his nose, he said, "This beast is still leaping about! At these words, the official was suddenly liberated from doubt.

He said, "All sinful karma arises from wealth and treasures; one should therefore exhort people to distance themselves from profit and gain.

The Master said, "Two thousand years since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, and bhikṣus have little sense of shame. Once, while suffering from a slight illness, the Master asked Grand Master Huan, "I have suddenly become unwell today;

The Master then made a gesture as if vomiting. Huán said, "Affection and love result in affliction. While Huán was preparing medicine, the Master cried out, "Thieves!
Huán administered the medicine and stood to one side with his hands folded before the Master. The Master stared at him with wide eyes and said, "A young man from the monastic groves.
Huán shook his sleeves and left. On another day, he asked, "My four great elements wish to disperse; Great [Master], [what shall I do?]"

overcome with affection, he could not bear to leave and subsequently shaved his head. Whenever he read the sutras, his mind merged with them and his spirit attained realization.
He humbled himself to seek instruction from veteran masters; when Ciming moved from Nanyuan to Daowu and then to Shichuang, the Master served as his assistant in both places.
