"Is that so? The Master said, "Elder of Hunan. He then asked, "Is there anyone else who wishes to ask a question?
Come forth and meet me! Yangqi’s life today rests in your hands; you may drag him about as you please, pulling him this way and that.
Why is this so? A man of great character must make his decision in public, not in secret—like water [flowing freely]."
"It is like pressing down on a gourd; let us bring it out for inspection before the assembly so that you do not turn red in the face.
Is there such a thing? Is there? Come forth and let us resolve this! If there is none, Yangqi has lost ground today. The Master then descended from his seat.
Monk Jiufeng Qin grabbed him and said, "Today I am happy to have found a fellow practitioner. The Master asked, "What is the matter of being a fellow practitioner?"
Dafu Qin said, "Jiufeng was plowing the furrow; Yangqi was pulling the harrow. The Master said, "At such a time as this, is Yangqi in front?
Is Jiufeng in front? As Dafu Qin hesitated, the Master pushed him away and said, "I thought you were a fellow student; it turns out you are not.
On the anniversary of Ciming’s death, when the assembly had just gathered for the vegetarian feast, the Master placed both hands in fists at his head before the portrait of the deceased.
The Master drew a line on his sitting mat with his staff, struck a circle, and then burned incense. Stepping back three paces, he performed a prostration like that of a woman.
The Head Seat said, "Stop making such a fuss. The Master asked, "How about you, Head Seat? The Head Seat replied, "Venerable Sir, stop making such a fuss.
The Master said, "That is like a rabbit eating cow's milk. The Second Seat stepped forward, struck a circle, and then—
He burned incense, then stepped back three paces and performed a woman’s bow. The Master stepped forward and made a gesture as if listening. The Head Seat hesitated;

the Master struck him with his palm and said, "This lacquer bucket is acting recklessly! (Jingshan Gao said: "The old fellow Yangqi is much like one who has already sunk an entire boat of hemp, yet comes to scoop it out with a dipper.
When Master Longxing Ziji passed away, a monk arrived to deliver his final letter. The Master asked, "The World-Honored One..."
Upon entering extinction, the outer coffin revealed his two crossed feet. When asked, "The Master has returned to the truth; what sign did he leave behind? the monk remained silent.
The Master beat his breast and cried, "Heaven! Heaven! In the meditation hall, he questioned a monk:

"As for the chestnut thorn, how will you swallow it? As for the diamond ring, how will you penetrate it? Dongshan Guangyao’s verse says: "The diamond ring and the chestnut thorn, Xuanzha’s three kinds of illness, Shigong’s single bow— I shall explain them directly for you: Silla."
(At Haedong) ○ One day, three new arrivals came. The Master asked, "When three people travel together, there must be one who is wise.
He held up his sitting mat and said, "Head Seat, what do you call this? The monk replied, "A sitting mat. The Master said:

"Is it really that? he asked. "Yes," replied the man. The Master asked again, "What do you call it? "A sitting cloth (*zuoju*)," he replied. The Master looked around at his left and right and said, "The head of the assembly indeed has eyes.
He then questioned the second person: "If one wishes to travel a thousand li, the first step is the beginning. What is this very first phrase?
"When we have come to your presence, Reverend, how would we dare to bring forth our hand? The Master then drew a line with his hand.

[The Master] drew a picture. The monk said, "Understood. The Master spread out both hands. The monk hesitated. The Master said, "Understood. He asked the third person, "Where have you recently departed from?
[The monk] replied, "Nanyuan. The Master said, "Today Yangqi has been exposed by you, Venerable Sir. Sit and drink some tea."
Chan Master Huinan of Huanglong (Dharma heir of Shishuang Yuan).
Chan Master Huinan of Huanglong was a native of the Zhang family in Xinzhou. He relied upon Chan Master Leduan Cheng of Litan.

He shared his seat with others to receive visitors, and his reputation resounded throughout all quarters. Once, while traveling through the Western Mountains together with Master Yunfeng Yue, they discussed the Dharma-way of Yunmen at night.
Yunfeng remarked, "Although Master Cheng is a successor of Yunmen, his Dharma-way is different.
The Master questioned him as to why it was different. Yunfeng replied, "Yunmen is like a nine-refined cinnabar; it points iron toward gold. Cheng..."

The Master said, "Public medicine is like mercury and silver; it may be admired from afar, but it flows away when placed in the furnace. Enraged, he threw his pillow at him. The next day, Yunfeng apologized for his transgression.
The Master spoke again, saying, "Yunmen’s presence was like that of a king; could he have been content with dying under his words?
Master Cheng had a method to transmit to people, yet it was a dead word. Can a dead word bring life to others? He then turned his back and walked away. The Master called after him, saying:
"If that is so, who would agree with you? Yunfeng said, "Shishuang Chuyuan’s skillful means surpass those of all other regions;
you should go see him, and you must not delay. The Master reflected silently to himself, "Master Yue favored Cuiyan, yet he tells me to see Shishuang.
What does this have to do with Yue? He immediately set out for Shishuang. On the way, he heard that Ciming was not attending to his duties and had suddenly retired to a thicket.

Lin then ascended Mount Heng and went to pay his respects to Xian of Fuyan. Xian appointed him as the Secretary for Records. Shortly thereafter, Xian passed away, and the Prefectural Governor appointed Ciming to fill the vacancy.
Upon arriving, [Lin] observed that Ciming had disparaged various points from other schools one by one, labeling them as erroneous interpretations.
Lin was disheartened by this and consequently entered Ciming’s quarters. Ciming said, "A secretary like you travels with a retinue; even if you were to..."
"I have a doubt; we may sit together to discuss it. The Master’s plea became even more earnest. Ciming said, "You study Yunmen Chan and must surely be well-versed in its essential meaning.
For instance, when it is said that Dongshan was given three blows of the staff, did he have a share in receiving those blows, or did he not?"
The Master said, "There is a reason you deserve a beating. Ciming, with a solemn expression, replied, "From morning until evening, the crows and magpies have been chirping;
they all deserve a beating. Ciming then sat upright, received the incense from the Master, and prostrated.
Ciming asked again, "Zhaozhou said, 'I have thoroughly exposed the old woman of Mount Tai. Now, where exactly was it that he exposed her?"
The Master stood there, perspiring, unable to offer a reply. The next day he went to visit him again, but Ciming scolded and reviled him incessantly.
The Master said, "Is this scolding the compassionate Dharma-giving? Ciming asked, "Do you understand this as scolding? At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He composed a verse, saying: "Standing out among the groves is Zhaozhou; The old woman’s discernment leaves no room for further inquiry."
Now the four seas are as clear as a mirror; let travelers not treat the road as their enemy. He presented this to Ciming, who nodded in approval. Later, he opened the Dharma at Tongan.
On the day he first accepted the invitation, Lengtan sent a monk to examine the words of his teaching.

[The monk] said: "The ocean of wisdom has no inherent nature; through the awakening to delusion, one becomes an ordinary person. Since the awakening to delusion is fundamentally void, it is the very mind of the ordinary person."

Upon seeing the Buddha, he simply stopped; he had presumed that Tong’an lacked a point of resolution, following whatever whims he fancied, saying, “Seven in the Southern Dipper, eight in the Northern.
When the monk returned and reported this to Cheng, Cheng was displeased. From that time on, the old friendship between [Tong’an and] Letan was severed.
Later, when a dharma-teacher returned from his travels, [Cheng] ascended the hall and said: "In the world there are five things that are not easy. First, the one who transforms [others]..."

"Easy. Second, the two kinds of giving are not easy. Third, transforming the raw into the cooked is not easy. Fourth, eating while sitting upright is not easy. There is yet another kind that is not easy:
who is this person? After a long silence, he said, "Hmm. He then descended from his seat. (At that time, Cuiyan Zhen was the head seat.

The Librarian asked, "Just now the Master spoke of a fifth kind that is not easy; who is this person? Cuiyan said, "To see the cheek from behind the head—do not associate with such a one. [In] the Master’s quarters:
He would frequently ask the monks, "Everyone has their own karmic conditions of birth (*jìngyuán*); where is the Venerable’s own birth-condition?
Just as they were engaged in the clash of question and answer, he would instead reach out his hand and say, "How is my hand like the Buddha’s hand?

He would also ask, "What have you attained from the masters you have visited in all quarters? Then, lowering his foot, he would say, "How is my foot like a donkey’s foot? For over thirty years, he demonstrated this.
Regarding these three questions, among scholars there was none who could grasp their essential meaning. Even when someone offered a response, the Master never once affirmed or denied it.
The monastic communities came to designate them as the "Three Barriers of Huanglong. The Master himself composed a verse on them: "The conditions of birth—everyone recognizes this;
But how has the water jelly ever been apart from the shrimp? When one sees the sun rising in the east, Who can still go on drinking Zhaozhou’s tea?"
My hand and the Buddha’s hand are raised together; Zen practitioners, realize this directly! Without moving a blade, the Way is manifested;
right where you are, you transcend Buddhas and Patriarchs. My feet and the donkey’s feet walk side by side; at every step, one treads upon the Unborn.

When you understand that the clouds have gathered and the sun has rolled up, only then will you know this Way extends in all directions. The general verse says: Where the conditions for birth are severed, stretch forth the donkey’s feet; the donkey’s feet...
When he extended [his hand], the Buddha’s hand opened. To repay those students who have come from the Five Lakes, may each of the Three Barriers be penetrated and brought forth.
Chan Master Zhenke of Cuiyan (dharma heir of Shishuang Chuyuan):
Chan Master Zhenke of Cuiyan in Hongzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He once studied under Ciming and subsequently went to Jinluan.
He sat in summer retreat together with the attendant Shan. Shan was a high-ranking disciple of Ciming; Daowu Zhen and Yangqi Hui both submitted to his authority.

The Master prided himself on having personally seen Ciming and believed there was no one in the world who could satisfy him. When Shan spoke with him, he realized the Master had not yet attained thorough penetration and laughed at him.
One day, while walking in the mountains, as they engaged in a sharp exchange of debate, Shan picked up a piece of tile or rubble and placed it upon a flat rock.
Shishang said, "If you can utter a turning word right here, I will grant that you have personally seen Ciming. The Master looked left and right, intending to respond;
Shan chided him, saying, "Your mind is stalled in deliberation and your consciousness has not yet penetrated. When have you ever even dreamed of it?"
The Master felt ashamed and terrified; he immediately returned to Shishuang. When Ciming saw him coming, he rebuked him, saying, "A practitioner of true caliber must know the proper timing.
What urgent business is there that you have come here so early, before the summer retreat has ended?

The Master wept and said, "My elder brother Shan harbors a poisonous heart that ultimately obstructs people; therefore, I have come to see you, O Monk. Ciming suddenly asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma?"
The general gist is as follows: The Master said, "Cloudless skies arise above the peaks; the moon with its light descends into the heart of the waves.
Ciming glared at him and shouted, "With hair white and teeth gone, you still harbor such a view! How will you ever escape birth and death?
The Master was struck with awe and begged for instruction. Ciming said, "Ask me. The Master repeated his previous statement and asked him about it. Ciming roared, "No!"
Clouds arise above the peaks; the moon descends into the heart of the waves. Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
His spirit was fresh and transcendent, his wit and eloquence swift and sharp; the monastic communities stood in awe of him.
Chan Master Zanyuan Jiaohai of Jiangshan (Dharma heir of Shishuang Yuan).
He was a native of Yiwu in Wuzhou, surnamed Fu, and was a descendant of the Great Being (Bodhisattva).

Having cultivated the seeds of wisdom from an early age, he became a monk at the age of seven and traveled to study under various masters at fifteen. He journeyed afar to visit Shishuang and ascended [to the hall].
In the master’s chamber, Ciming saw him at once and said, "Go, go; attend to the fodder trough. The Master then brayed like a donkey.
Ciming said, "Truly a vessel of the Dharma! He appointed him as his attendant. For twenty years, he carried water and hauled firewood, undaunted by cold or heat.
He personally sought the Way with his own hands.
Chan Master Dezhang of Lingyin (dharma heir of Shishuang Yuan).
Chan Master Dezhang of Lingyin initially resided at the Western Sutra Repository Hall of the Great State Preceptor’s Temple in the eighth year of the Qingli era.
On the first day of the ninth month, Emperor Renzong issued an imperial decree for the Master to partake in a vegetarian feast at the Yanchun Pavilion.
The Emperor, addressing him as Great Master Puzhao, asked: "What is the single phrase that meets the occasion? The Master replied: "A single word transcends the azure heavens;

one walks on the precipice before the ten-thousand-fathom peak. The Emperor asked: "How does one walk on the precipice? The Master then gave a shout and said: "Before the Emperor, how can one not be cautious?"
"It is so," he said. The Master said, "One must not let this pass. The following year, he was again summoned to an imperial banquet.
Emperor Shunzong again called upon Puzhao to ask, "What is it to take away the person but not the environment? Puzhao replied, "The thunder startles the fine grass, and its sprouts begin to emerge."
"Advance toward the high peaks; do not delay. [The student] asked: "What is 'seizing the environment but not seizing the person'? The Master said:
"Wearing horns and shrouded in fur, they differ [from others]; coming and going, they move with total freedom. [The student] asked: "What is 'seizing both the person and the environment'?

The Master said: "Stepping out the gate, one is far beyond the heavens; flowing light and shifting shadows are not real. [The student] asked: "What is 'neither seizing the person nor seizing the environment'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
In the cold forest there are no overnight guests; in the great ocean one hears the dragon’s roar.

Later, when the imperial decree was issued for another vegetarian feast in the Huacheng Hall, Xuanshou Xian asked, "The vegetarian banquet has been grandly opened; how shall we repay the Sage Ruler? The Master said, "Seeking bird tracks in the sky."
[The monk] asked, "What is the meaning? The Master said, "Seeking the tracks of a fish within the water.
Chan Master Fang of Zhenru Monastery in Zhenzhou (a dharma heir of Langye Huijue).
Chan Master Fang of Zhenru Monastery in Zhenzhou went to attend Langye, where he focused solely on the koan of the "Pine Tree. Whenever he entered the inner room [for instruction],...
He set forth what he had perceived, yet found no words with which to express it; he was frequently driven out by [Langya’s] shouts.

Suddenly, one day, he attained great enlightenment and went straight to the abbot’s quarters, saying, “I understand! Langya asked, “How do you understand? The Master replied, “Last night the bedding on the bed was warm.”
One night he awoke at dawn. Langye Kezhi [was his master].
Chan Master Tan of Xingjiao Monastery in Xuancheng (a dharma heir of Langye Jue):
Chan Master Tan of Xingjiao Monastery in Xuancheng was the son of the Niu family of Yongjia. His occupation was silver-smithing; it was while sharpening a vessel that...
His capacity was already refined; he immediately left the household life to visit Langye, where his spiritual faculties and words were instantly in accord.

Later, he relied upon Chan Master Tianyi Huai, who was then residing at Xingjiao Monastery. He was promoted to the position of First Seat. When Tianyi accepted an invitation elsewhere and wished to go to Wenzhou, he requested the Master to succeed him.
At that time, Scholar Diaojingchun was serving as the governor of Wanling. Fearing that Jingchun might involve himself in external disputes, Tianyi [thereupon...]
Before Guanyin, he prayed: "If the Head Seat Tan possesses clear insight into the Way and is fit to serve as abbot, I pray you show him a sign in a dream to Scholar Diau Jingchun.
That night, Jingchun dreamed of an ox standing upon the Dharma seat at Xingjiao Temple. At dawn the next morning, Tianyi took his leave of the Prefect.
Jingchun recounted his dream, and Tianyi laughed loudly. When Jingchun asked for the reason, Tianyi said: "Tan, the Head Seat..."
The master’s surname was Niu (Ox), and he was also born under the Ox constellation. When Jingchun took his seat, he presented a formal invitation.
The Master accepted the invitation and ascended the seat. Xuedou Huazhu Shengzong stepped forward and asked: "Before the Buddhas appeared in the world, everyone’s nostrils reached the heavens;
after they appeared in the world, why is there no news at all? The Master replied: "Before Mount Jizu, the wind is still. Shengzong—
[Zhaozhou] said, "That is not it; speak further. The Master said, "Great snow fills Chang'an. Xingzong said, "Who understands this meaning? It makes me remember Nanquan.
He then brushed his sleeves and returned to the assembly, refusing to prostrate. The Master said, "Xingzong has lost ground today.
He immediately returned to his quarters and sent someone to invite Xingzong to come. The Master said, "Just now, you gave a mistaken response."
[The Master] shifted the topic. [He asked,] "Before this assembly of devas and humans, why did you not bow, but instead covered yourself over?
Xingzong said, "A great man has gold beneath his knees; how could he be willing to bow to an eyeless old monk? The Master said, "I have another saying.

Xingzong then reasoned through the previous words until reaching the point where [the Master had said], "Not yet—speak further! The Master said, "I have thirty blows of the staff which I entrust to you."
He struck Xuedou. Xingzong then prostrated.
Chan Master Ke-xuan of Gui-zong (a dharma successor of Lang-ye Jue):
Chan Master Ke-xuan of Gui-zong in Jiangzhou was a native of Hanzhou. He became a monk in his prime and immediately left the gorges to rely upon Lang-ya.
"Wrong! A single word was suddenly uttered, and his many doubts were instantly extinguished. Langye approved of him. Before long, he was ordered to share the teaching seat.

When the layman Guo Gongfu of Jingkong visited him to inquire after the Way, they became close friends. Later, when the Master took charge of Guiyang, Gongfu happened to be serving as the Magistrate of Nanchang.
Shortly thereafter, the Prefect became resentful because the Master did not pay him formal courtesy and began to persecute him severely. The Master then wrote a letter to Gongfu, saying:
"My karmic conditions for this life still have six years remaining. However, as the local governor is pressing me so hard, I must cast off my remaining breaths and take rebirth in your family.
I pray that you will not obstruct me. When Guo Gongfu read the letter, he was both surprised and delighted, and nodded his head in agreement.
In the middle of the night, his wife saw the Master enter her bedchamber in a dream; she cried out in alarm, "This is not where the Monk comes from! Gongfu shook her awake and questioned her.

His wife told him the matter in detail. He called for a lamp, took the letter, and showed it to him; they laughed together without ceasing. Consequently, she became pregnant. When the child was born, he was named Xuānlǎo (Xuánlǎo).
At one year of age, his memory and questioning were as they had been before. When he reached three years old, Chan Master Báiyún Duān arrived at their home.
Upon first seeing him, he said, "My nephew has come! Báiyún asked, "How many years have passed since we parted from you, Master? Xuán counted back on his fingers.
[Daowu] said, "It has been four years now" (implying that he died one year after parting from Xiang). Baoyun asked, "Where did you part? [Daowu] replied, "At Bailian Zhuang."
Baiyun asked, "What will be the proof? [Xuan] replied, "Father and Mother, invite the Master for a vegetarian meal tomorrow.
Suddenly, they heard the sound of a cart being pushed. Baiyun asked, "What is that sound outside the gate? Xuan made a gesture with his hand as if pushing a cart.
Baiyun said, "What happens after it passes? He replied, "Two ruts on level ground. Indeed, after six weeks, he passed away without illness.
Lecturer Zixuan of Changshui (Dharma heir of Langye Jue).
Lecturer Zixuan of Changshui in Xiu Prefecture was a native of Jiaxing in that commandery. From the time he shaved his head, he recited the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* without ceasing.
Following Dharma Master Hongmin, he reached the passage on the "two aspects of movement and stillness being clearly non-arising" and attained realization. He said:

Ming said: "To strike at emptiness or beat upon wood—even with bamboo [instead of wood]—still leaves one behind the trap and the snare. To raise an eye or lift a brow has already become a matter of conceptual deliberation."

Only by departing from these two paths can one accord with this principle. Min Fu realized this through personal experience; yet, wishing to explore the source of Chan, he was at a loss as to where to turn.
Hearing that Langya Huijue was highly esteemed in his time, he immediately went to attend his lectures. He arrived just as the Master was ascending the hall for the discourse.
Stepping forward, Min asked: "The nature is originally pure and still; why do mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? Langya responded with a commanding presence: "Originally pure..."
"However, how is it that the mountains, rivers, and the great earth suddenly arise? The Master attained realization.
This was Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng at Nanyue (a dharma heir of Dayu Zhi).
Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng at Nanyue was a native of the Xu family from Nanchang. Initially, he went to visit Dayu and heard his public address.
He said, "When the whole community gathers to eat a stalk of pickled vegetables, if you call it 'a single stalk of pickled vegetables,' you will fall into hell as fast as a shot arrow.

He then descended from his seat. The Master was greatly startled and went to the Abbot’s quarters that night. Dayu asked, "What do you seek by coming here? The Master replied, "I seek the Dharma of the mind.
Dayu said, "The Wheel of the Dharma has not yet turned; the Wheel of Food turns first. You, a latecomer, should take advantage of your physical strength while it is robust."
"I am not going out to beg for alms for the sake of the assembly. I am occupied with enduring hunger; how would I have the leisure to explain Zen to you?
The Master did not dare disobey. Before long, Dayu moved to Cuoyan. After the Master had submitted his formal letter of resignation, he again went to Cuoyan to seek instruction.

Cuoyan said, "The Buddha-dharma has not yet reached you; it will rot away [within you]. The snow is cold; you should go out to beg for charcoal for the assembly. The Master also obeyed this command. He was able to—
When the business was concluded, he returned to the Abbot’s quarters. Cuiyan said, "The Hall administration is lacking personnel; I now entrust this task to you.

The Master accepted it with displeasure, resenting that Cuiyan had not yet removed [delusions] from his mind. Later, while sitting on the rear rack, the hoop of a wooden bucket suddenly came loose and fell from the rack onto him.
The Master suddenly attained enlightenment, seeing at once the functional application of Cuiyan’s teaching. He hurriedly adjusted his *kāṣāya* robe and ascended to the dormitory hall.
Cuiyan met him with a smile and said, "Venerable Karmadāna, rejoice! The Great Matter is now complete. The Master bowed twice without uttering a single word and departed.
He served under him diligently for eight years. Later, he emerged into the world at Cuiyan. A monk asked: "In the steep mountains and rocky cliffs, is there still a Buddha?"
The monk said, "There is no Dharma. The Master said, "There is. The monk asked, "What is the Buddha-dharma of the steep mountains and rocky cliffs?

The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree upside down. (Jingshan Gao said: If one can believe, accept, and practice this, the business of a lifetime of study is finished. A layman asked, "What is the Buddha?"

The Master said, "Wearing clothes and eating food is measured according to one's household circumstances. [The monk] said, "If that is so, then I shall step back three paces and place my hands together at my chest.
The Master said, "It is better to have no cup added after one is already drunk than to drink it."
Chan Master Jushui of Jingzhu Monastery (dharma heir of Jinshan Ying):
Chan Master Zhenneng of Jingzhu Monastery in Hangzhou studied under Daguan. He then asked, "I have a rough understanding of the sutras and treatises, yet I do not believe in Chan at all.
I pray that you, Master, will resolve my doubts. Daguan said, "Since you do not believe in Chan, how can you..."

[The Master] said, "The sutras clarify the principle. Chan is the mainstay of the sutras; the sutras are the net of Chan. By grasping the mainstay, the net is set right; by understanding Chan, one sees the sutras.
The Master said, "Explain Chan for this person's sake. Daguang said, "What follows is a long discourse. The Master said, "If it is so, then the sutras and Chan are of one essence.
Daguang said, "The Buddhas and the Patriarchs do not have two minds. It is like the hand forming a fist, or the fist being formed by the hand."
Master Shou was thereby enlightened. He then composed a verse, saying: "For over twenty years I have used my mind in vain speculation;
How many times have I tried to extinguish this heart? Now, in my decline, I have met one who knows me: Li Bai was all along a scholar."
The Layman Li Duanyuan (Dharma Heir of Jinshan Ying).
When the layman Li Duanyuan was a child in the state academy, he frequently read Chan texts. Although he later married and entered official service, he remained devoted to his studies.
However, being resolute in his commitment to the ancestral Way, he subsequently built a dwelling in his rear garden that resembled an *ārāma* (monastery) and invited Daguan to reside there.

Morning and evening they consulted and studied one another, to the point of forgetting both sleep and food. One day, Daguan looked at the official and said, "Were it not for the power of manifesting [through skillful means], how could you have reached this state?
Alas, what place is there for you to enter? The official asked, "Are heaven and hell ultimately real or not?"
"No. "Please, Master, explain this clearly. Daguang said: "The Buddhas speak of existence within non-existence; it is like seeing flowers in the sky with one's own eyes.

Your Excellency seeks non-existence within existence; it is like grasping at the moon reflected in water. It is truly laughable that you see a prison before your eyes yet do not avoid it, while hearing of heaven outside your mind and desiring to be born there.
You fail to realize that joy and fear reside in the mind, and that good and evil constitute the external objects. Your Excellency should simply—"
"Once you have realized your own mind, naturally there will be no delusion. The Duke asked, "How does one realize the mind? Da Guan replied, "Do not deliberate upon good or evil at all.
The Duke asked, "After not deliberating, where does the mind go? Da Guan said, "First, please allow the Great Marshal to return home.
The Duke asked, "As for when a person dies, where does the mind go? Da Guan said, "If you do not yet know life, how can you know death?"
[The Master] died. The Duke said, "As for life, I already know it. Da Guan asked, "From where does life come? The Duke was at a loss.
Da Guan rose, pressed his hand against the Duke's chest, and said, "It is right here. What else is there to contemplate? The Duke said, "I understand.
Da Guan asked, "How do you understand? The Duke said, "I only knew how to hurry along the road; I did not realize I had missed the way. Da Guan [departed].
Guantuo opened his eyes and said, "A hundred-year dream—I have only this morning awakened from it. He then spoke a verse: "At thirty-eight years of age, I was muddled and ignorant.
Now that I possess knowledge, how am I any different from my former ignorance? The waters of the Bian River flow on; the embankments of Sui remain faintly visible.
Master, you must return; the arrow-like waves rush eastward."
Chan Master Jingduan of Xiyu (Dharma Heir of Longhua Yue).

Chan Master Jingduan of Shizi at Xiyu in Anji Prefecture was a native of that prefecture. His surname was Qiu. Initially, upon seeing a lion being played with, he attained enlightenment regarding the essentials of the mind.
He went to see Master Longhua, received his seal of approval, and subsequently returned to his hometown. There, he had a lion made of dyed silk.
The Master wore a lion skin; consequently, he was called Duan Shizi (Lion-Duan).

There was a mad monk who turned his head while facing the meat and wine of the Magistrate of Danyang, Lü Gong. The Master went straight up to him and pointed, saying, "At such a time as this, what is the Buddha?
The monk could not respond. The Master struck him on the head and pushed him over before departing. Furthermore, there was a sorcerer who styled himself "Bu Tuo" (Non-Entrustment).
At a site outside the city walls of Xiuzhou, there was a Buddha image upon which a pagoda had been built; the entire city held it in faith and reverence.
When the Master saw this, he grabbed the image and said, "What is the Buddha? Without allowing for any deliberation or hesitation, he kicked it away and departed. [Later], Prime Minister Zhang Dun...
Admiring his Way, [the Emperor] personally requested that he open a Dharma assembly at Mount Wu. His transformative influence spread widely.

On the day of the opening of the hall, when the monk announced the arrival of the official proclamation, the Master pushed it over and turned back; he kicked over the incense burner and did not support it. Before the seven fascicles of the Lotus Sūtra had been recited, the sound of the "Fisherman's Song" was heard first. The Master stopped him.
Thereupon, he ascended the seat, offered incense to pray for the Emperor, and after finishing, raised his voice and chanted: "Originally this is the Xiao..."
"Xiang-yi, the Fisherman! From the west, from the east, from the north, and from the south! The assembly responded with a chorus of acclaim.
The Master looked at them and laughed, saying, "Observe closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; the Dharma of the Dharma King is thus. He then descended from his seat.
One day, Chancellor Zhang invited him for a meal. The Master spoke this verse in a fit of anger: Zhang Dun, Zhang Dun! You invite me to view your graves, Yet you insist that I eat meat!
He then ate meat. Dun laughed heartily. On another occasion, because Dun invited him to a meal, he was tricked into eating some *huántún* (dumplings). The Master spoke in verse:
"Fragrant dumplings, plain dumplings, Served full in the bowl, swallowed whole. Garbage passes right over the sandbar."

The Dragon Palace and the Ocean Treasury are naturally clear and distinct. When Daoxun was departing for his summons to court, the Master said, "For now, you must protect and cherish the Buddha-Dharma.

Daoxun replied, "Neither promoting nor abolishing—this is how one protects and cherishes the Buddha-Dharma. The Master ordered an attendant to bring some sugar to present to the official as he departed.
As Daoxun was eating the sugar, the Master asked, "Is it sweet? Daoxun said, "It is sweet. The Master said, "If it is sweet, then stay. Daoxun... [remained].
Xiao then rose from his seat. The Master was in the capital when Lord Wang Jinggong invited him to lecture on Chan. A vegetarian feast was prepared at the Great Xiangguo Temple.
While they were reading the scriptures, Lord Jinggong entered the hall; after the incense had been burned, he asked the assembly: "Before the Buddha appeared in the world..."
"What sutra are you reading? The assembly remained silent. The Master said, "When Confucius and the Duke of Zhou had not yet appeared in the world, what books did they read?
The official replied, "A clever monk! The Master added, "Namo Avalokiteśvara! He speaks all manner of dharmas;

those who have drowned throughout past and present cry out in lamentation for the Bodhisattva, voice after voice. The Master arrived at Huating. The assembly requested him to ascend the hall. At Ling Shan...
"O Lion! Roaring from amidst the clouds! The Buddha-dharma is beyond discussion; it would be better to perform a somersault.
With this, he descended from his seat. At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, Chan Master Yuanzhao retired from Huilin Temple in the capital and returned to Gusu.
There he saw Shizi at Ganlu Temple and said, "Are you not the Master Shizi? Shizi replied, "I am. Yuanzhao teased him, saying, "A village master!"
"Only a child," the Master replied at once. "A lion from the village; a village lion playing with its eyebrows, both eyes moving all at once.
Opening its mouth, it is straight and blunt within; it cares not for human service. Even if one were to play with it all the way to the imperial palace."
It was also a case of empty clamor. Entering the hall: On the second day of the second month, what does the Zen elder have to say?
The spring breeze touches every eye and the hundred flowers bloom; the sons of nobles and princes are intoxicated day after day. Yet there is only that Dragon Pine before the Hall that remains sober.
It does not conform to the tastes of the fashionable; for those in the Zen school, this alone is sufficient. Do not overthink it. After the meal, all is tranquil.
Tea in a bowl. On a long bed, he stretched out his legs and slept. "Tou! [The student] asked, "How is it when the antelope has not yet hung its horns? The Master said, "I am afraid.
[The student] said, "Since you are a *kalyāṇamitra* (spiritual friend), why are you afraid? The Master said, "I have never seen such a strange beast.
Later, the Master traveled south to Zhiang and met the Venerable Chao of Shangfang. There was a nun there...
[The nun] came to visit. The Master said, "Come back tomorrow at the third watch of the fifth watch. The next morning, the Master sat with his face smeared with red powder.
When the nun entered and saw him, she was startled and immediately attained awakening. Once, while suffering from a toothache, he told the assembly of monks, "Tomorrow I shall pass away.
The assembly took this to be a joke. They requested that he speak a verse. The Master asked for a brush and wrote in large characters: "Duan Shizi is too... (The text ends here).
Languid and indolent, his teeth decayed even before he died. When the two daily assemblies went to the hall, he could never manage to catch up with the rice gruel and meals.
Now that he has obtained death, it is a great advantage; he sleeps long and does not concern himself with a hundred affairs.
First, he need not attend to officials; second, he need not eat rice gruel or meals. Thus, at the fifth watch, he passed away.
The Twelfth Generation under Nanyue (the Eighth Generation under Linji):
Chan Master Baoyun Shouduan (Dharma Heir of Yangqi Hui).
Chan Master Baoyun Shouduan of Shuzhou was a native of the Ge clan from Hengyang. He went to study under Yangqi, who—
One day, Rujing suddenly asked, "Who was your preceptor? The Master replied, "The Venerable Yuru of Chaling.
Rujing said, "I have heard that he had an awakening after falling while crossing a bridge; he composed a verse about it that was truly extraordinary. Can you recite it? The Master recited:
"I possess a bright pearl, Long locked away by the dust of worldly toil. Today, the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, Shining through mountains and rivers across ten thousand miles."
Duo. Yangqi smiled and rose to leave. The Master was startled and did not sleep all night. At dawn, he went to consult him. It happened to be the end of the year;
Yangqi said, "Did you see those who were performing the exorcism ritual yesterday? He replied, "I saw them. Yangqi said, "In this one matter, you are not their equal.
The Master was again struck with wonder and asked, "What is the meaning of this? Yangqi said, "They love to be laughed at."
"You fear being ridiculed by others. The Master attained great enlightenment. He served as an attendant for a long time.
Chan Master Renyong of Baoning (a dharma successor of Yangqi Hui).
Chan Master Renyong of Baoning in Jinling was the son of the Zhu family of Siming. He visited Chan Master Mingjue of Xuedou.
Mingjue thought that Yixing was capable of being entrusted with the Great Dharma. He ridiculed him, saying, "Master Yixing, you are merely a pedantic lecturer.

Enraged and frustrated, Yixing descended the mountain and, gazing toward Xuedou, bowed and said, "In this life, I shall travel as a wandering monk to study Chan; if my realization does not surpass Xuedou, I vow never to return home.
He then went to Letan, where for more than a decade his doubts remained unresolved. Hearing that Yangqi had moved to Yungai and was capable of acting as a spiritual gatekeeper, he set out for there.
When Xuezhai went directly to his quarters, before a single word had been exchanged, he suddenly realized the Mind-Seal.
After Yangqi passed away, he traveled with the Chan Master Baiyun Yuan, who was his fellow student, and investigated the most profound and subtle mysteries to their ultimate limit.
Chan Master Zuxin of Huanglong (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan):
Chan Master Baojue Zuxin of Huanglong in Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Wu family of Nanyong.
He studied under Chan Master Yunfeng Yue for three years without attaining anything, whereupon he took his leave. Yunfeng said, "You must go and rely upon Chan Master Huangbo Nan."
The Master went to Huangbo, but for four years he did not achieve great enlightenment. He took leave again and went up to Yunfeng;
however, Yunfeng had passed away, so he stayed at Shishuang. While reading the *Chuan Deng Lu* (Transmission of the Lamp), he came upon a monk asking Duofu, "What is Duofu’s grove of bamboo?
Duofu replied, "One stem, two stems, leaning. The monk said, "I do not understand. Duofu said, "Three stems, four stems."
At this point, the Master attained awakening and thoroughly perceived the workings of the two masters. He returned directly to Huangbo;
as soon as he unfurled his sitting cloth, Huangbo said, "You have already entered my room. The Master leaped for joy and said, "The Great Matter has always been like this.
Why did you, Preceptor, instruct people to 'examine the phrase' and search for it by every possible means? Huangbo replied, "If I had not instructed you in this way..."
Investigate thoroughly until you reach a place where no person exists; when you see for yourself and affirm it for yourself, I shall bury you.
The Master constantly raised his fist in his room and asked the monks: "To call it a 'fist' is to encounter resistance (touch); not to call it a 'fist' is to turn one's back (contradiction).
What do you call it?"
Chan Master Bǎofēng Kèwén (Dharma Heir of Huánglóng Nán).

Chan Master Yún'ān Zhējìng Bǎofēng Kèwén of Lóngxīng Prefecture was the son of the Zheng family of Shǎnfǔ. While sitting out the summer retreat at Dàtáiméi, he heard a monk cite a question posed to Yúnmén:
"Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon reflected in water? Yúnmén replied: [The moon is not in the water.]
"In the clear waves there is no path through. The Master then attained understanding. Having gone to see Huanglong, however, he did not find accord and said, "I have something excellent;
this old fellow does not recognize me. He then went to Xiangcheng to see Master Shun. Shun asked, "Where have you come from?"
The Master said, "Huanglong has come. [The monk] asked, "What have been Huanglong’s recent sayings?
The Master said, "Recently, the local government commissioned Elder Huangbo. Huanglong gave this instruction: 'Reciting hymns on the bell tower;
planting vegetables under the bed. If anyone can provide a phrase that accords with this, they shall go to serve as abbot. The Venerable Sheng said, "A fierce tiger stands before me."
While sitting on the road, Huanglong ordered him to go and stay at Huangbo. Shun, unaware, said, "If the Head Seat had only uttered a single turning phrase, he would have secured Huangbo's stay;
yet he has not even dreamed of the Buddha-dharma. Upon these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Only then did he realize the scope of Huanglong’s application [of the Dharma]. He returned to see Huanglong, who asked, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "I have come specifically to pay my respects to the Master. Huanglong said, "It happens that the old monk is not here. The Master asked, "Where have you gone?
Huanglong said, "To Tiantai for a communal work session (*puqing*), and to Nanyue for a mountain tour. The Master said, "In that case, I, this student, have gained..."
[The Master] went off with ease. Huanglong asked, "Where did you get those shoes on your feet? The Master replied, "I bought them at Mount Lu for seven hundred and fifty wen.
Huanglong said, "When did you ever attain mastery? The Master pointed to his shoes and said, "When have they not been free? Huanglong was struck with wonder.
On the day he ascended the hall, after offering incense to pray for the Emperor and completing the exchange of questions and answers, he said: "Question—"
Let us stop here for a moment. You know only to inquire about the Buddha and the Dharma, yet you do not realize the source from which the Buddha-Dharma comes.
Tell me, from where does it come? He extended one foot and said: "In the past, Huanglong personally issued this command;
none of the Buddhas of the ten directions dared to disobey it, and none of the ancestral masters of successive generations or all the holy sages dared to transgress it. This is the single..."
The ultimate, wondrous meaning: the tongue of the old *ho-shang* of the world has been a single seal from beginning to end; none dare differ from it.
Setting aside for a moment the fact that there is no difference, where does this seal reside? Do you see it? If you see it, you are neither monk nor layman;

without partiality and without faction, I shall entrust it to each of you individually. If you do not see it, I shall take it back myself. Thereupon, he withdrew his foot, gave a shout, and said: "Soldier! (Bing!)
Following the seal, he moves; about to pursue the talisman, he walks. An old man with the hands of a Buddha and the feet of a donkey—what a painful sight! I shall give him thirty blows of the staff.
Now, is there anyone in this assembly who is not dissatisfied? If there is, it is truly extraordinary.
If there is none, then this new elder is deceiving you all.
Chan Master Wusheng Weisheng of Huangbo (Dharma heir of Huanglong Nan).

Chan Master Zhenjue Weisheng of Huangbo in Ruizhou was a native of the Luo family of Tongchuan. While he was living among a community of lecturers, his fan happened to strike against the window lattice with a sound.
Suddenly, he recalled a passage from the teachings: "When drums are struck in the ten directions, they are heard in all ten places at once."
At that time, upon hearing [the teaching], he attained great enlightenment. He informed his original lecturer, who instructed him to engage in inquiry. The Master went directly to Huanglong.
Later, due to the Prefect of Ruizhou’s commissioning of Huanglong to select a successor as the abbot of Huangbo, Huanglong gathered the assembly and delivered this statement:
He was reciting hymns atop the bell tower while growing vegetables beneath his bed.

When someone asked, "If you can explain this, you may go to serve as abbot," the Master stepped forward and replied, "A fierce tiger sits blocking the road. Huanglong was greatly pleased and subsequently sent him forth; from that time on, he was revered by the various schools.
Chan Master Ziqi of Kaiyuan (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan).

Chan Master Ziqi of Kaiyuan in Qizhou was a native of the Xu family of Quanzhou. Having mastered the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* and the *Complete Enlightenment Sūtra*, he abandoned his studies to visit Chan Master Zhen of Cuiyan.
He asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma. Cuiyan spat on the ground and said, "This single drop has fallen..."
"Where is it? the Master asked, as he rubbed his chest. "Today my spleen aches," he replied. Cuiyan smiled and took his leave to go study under Jicui.
After more than a year, he had fully mastered the Way. While attending Jicui during a break, they were discussing matters of antiquity and the present when it began to snow heavily.
Jicui pointed and asked, "Can this be swept away with a single broom? The Master replied, "It cannot. "Then when the sky clears and the sun shines—"
The clouds and mists disperse; how could they possibly remain? One who knows the ultimate ground approaches all words and phrases like splitting bamboo:
though there be a hundred nodes, each shall be severed at the first touch of the blade. How could there be room for sound in deliberation or conjecture?

One day, a monk from Jicui sent a messenger to pose a question: "How do you understand the Old Monk’s Three Barriers? The Master replied with a stern voice, "You have been pondering this for a long time."
When asked, "What is the activity of the remote past? Jici (Ji-cui) heard this and marveled at its excellence; thus his reputation became renowned throughout the monastic community.

After Jici passed away, Chan Master Sijuzu Yan appointed him to share the seat [of the abbot]. In his meditation hall, he posed this critical phrase (*chuyu*): "There is one person who has a mouth but cannot speak; what is his name?
Later, when this teaching was transmitted to Donglin, Chan Master Zong sighed and said, "The Head Seat Qi is like iron."

Mount [Xuefeng] rises ten thousand *zhang*; it is ultimately difficult to follow its verbal lineage. Before long, Kaiyuan was established as a Chan monastery, and the Master was invited to serve as its first patriarch.
This was followed by Chan Master Xingwei of Yangshan (a dharma successor of Huanglong Nan).

Chan Master Xingwei of Yangshan in Yuanzhou was a native of Heshuo. Having studied the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra* (*Yuánjué jīng*), he harbored slight doubts and set out on a journey with his traveling bag to seek the meaning of the Patriarchs' intent.
He arrived at the Dharma seat of Nan Chan Master, where he spent six years. One day, he requested instruction and was immediately struck with a shout and driven out.
As he stepped across the threshold, he suddenly realized the profound essence. He subsequently emerged in the world at Yangshan, and his reputation for the Way spread widely.
Biography of Chan Master Shouzhi of Yungai (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan).
Chan Master Shouzhi of Yungai in Tanzhou was a native of the Chen family of Jianzhou. While traveling, he arrived at Dajian in Yuzhang.
At that time, Chan Master Facha of Yuchi was sequestered in the Western Mountains. Hearing that he had completed his extensive training, the Master went to visit him.
Facha asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Daining. Facha asked again, "The main gate collapsed last night;
did you know of it? The Master was startled and said, "I did not know. Facha said, "In Wuzhong, there is a stone Buddha that many people have never seen. The Master [was moved].

Overwhelmed with wonder, he immediately prostrated himself. Fachang sent him to visit Chan Master Zhen of Cuiyan; although he spent a long time there, he attained no realization. Yet, he did not waste a single moment of his time.
When he finally visited Huanglong at Jicui, he was able to exhaust all his doubts. The Master resided in the Eastern Hall of the monastery.
In the Xinhao year of the Zhenghe era, Sishi retired from Huanglong and entered the mountains from Hunan to pay his respects. Every day...
It was already evening. An attendant monk announced his arrival. The Master, dragging his sandals, walked along speaking, saying, "Bring a candle;
let us see what his face looks like—he who has caused his fame to resound throughout the universe. Dead Heart (Sīcitta) also cried out, "Come closer! as the Master seized him.
"I want to see whether this is my true master uncle or my false master uncle. As soon as he said this, the Master struck him once squarely in the chest with his fist.
Sishin said, "But this is truly real," and then prostrated himself. The guest and host were in perfect accord, their joy being profound.
Chan Master Qingxian of Longqing (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan).
Chan Master Qingxian of Renshan Longqing Monastery in Jizhou was the son of the Zhuo family of Fuzhou. At the age of twenty, he traveled extensively to consult various masters.
Later, he went to pay his respects to Huanglong at Huangbo. Huanglong asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Baizhang.

Huanglong asked, "When did you leave there? The Master said, "The thirteenth day of the first month. Huanglong said, "Your heels must ache; give him thirty blows! The Master said, "Not merely thirty blows.
Huanglong shouted, "After traveling on pilgrimage for so long, you have not a breath of spirit! The Master—

[The Master] said, "Even the hundreds of thousands of Buddhas are likewise so. [The Master] said, "When you came here in such a manner, when did you ever arrive at the realm of the Buddhas by even a hair's breadth?
The Master said, "The Buddhas have not necessarily arrived at the realm of Qingxian.
Huanglong asked, "What is the place of your birth and origin? The Master said, "In the morning I ate white congee; now I feel hungry again. [Huanglong] asked, "My hand—"
"How is it like a Buddha’s hand? The Master said, "Playing the lute under the moon. "Is my foot like a donkey’s foot?
The Master said, "A heron standing in the snow is not of the same color [as the snow]. Huanglong sighed and looked at him, saying, "You have shaved off your hair and beard;
for what purpose do you do this? The Master said, "I simply wish to be without affairs. Huanglong said, "If that is so, then 'a few sounds of the clear chime are beyond right and wrong.'"
"There is one idle man in the world. The Master said, "What words are these? He replied, "A sharp and clever monk. The Master said, "That too is unnecessary.
Huanglong said, "There is a Venerable Bian here; you must be alert. The Master asked, "What longings does he have?
He replied, "If he were to pat you on the back once, what would you do? The Master said, "What would that accomplish?"
Mò said, "He spreads his two hands. The Master said, "Where did you learn this pretense?
Huanglong laughed loudly. The Master then spread his two hands; Huanglong shouted at him. He asked again, "Lung-lung, loose and relaxed—two people sharing one bowl.
How do you understand this? The Master said, "In pieces. [Huanglong] said, "The entire earth is a single Mount Sumeru; can you grasp it in your palm?"

[The Master] said, "In the midst [of this], how do you understand it? The teacher replied, "It is a case of double layers. [The Master] said, "Here, you may speak as you please in barbarian tongues or Chinese;
but if you were to reach Tong'an, how would you pass through? (At that time, Ying of Shaowu was serving as the Head Seat at Tong'an, and the teacher wished to go see him. The teacher said:
"He must reach this very state before it will do. [The monk] said, "Suddenly he points to the brazier and says, 'This is a black-lacquered brazier;
that is a black-lacquered incense table. Where is there a place he has not reached? The Master said:
Before Qingxian, he spoke in this manner for a while. "If it were anyone else," [Qingxian] said, "they would laugh at the Master.
Huanglong gave a clap; the Master then let out a shout. The next day, they went together to look at the monks' hall. [Huanglong] said, "A fine monks' hall. The Master said, "Excellent craftsmanship.
[Huanglong] asked, "In what way is it excellent? The Master said, "One beam supports one pillar. [Huanglong] said, "This is not yet the point of excellence."
The teacher said, "And what about the Master? Huanglong pointed with his finger and said, "This pillar is so round;
that beam is so flat. The teacher said, "A great teacher of humans and devas must indeed be you, Master."
He immediately hurried away. The next day, he stood in attendance. Huanglong asked, "When you have obtained a seat and put on your robes, how will you provide for those who come after?
The Master said, "When meeting a square, I am square; when meeting a circle, I am circular. Huanglong said, "Speaking like that, you still have lips and teeth.
The Master said, "Qingxian is indeed like this; but what about you, Master? Huanglong said, "Come closer, and I shall tell you."

The Master clapped his hands and said, "That which you have been using for thirty years has been caught red-handed this very morning! Huanglong laughed loudly and said, "They are one and the same in their spiritual quickness.
The Master shook out his sleeves and departed. From then on, students vied with one another to seek him out.
Chan Master Hongying of Letan (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan).
Chan Master Hongying of Letan in Longxing Prefecture read the *Huayan Shiming Lun* and thereby realized the essential point of the school.
He immediately went to the seat of Chan Master Nan of Huangbo. Huangbo spoke with him until dawn and said, "The responsibility for carrying the Great Dharma rests entirely upon you."

"You must take care of yourself and love yourself deeply. He then went to see Cuiyan Zhen Dianxiong. Just as he was entering the room, Zhen asked, "What is the meaning of the woman emerging from meditative concentration?
The Master reached out his hand, pinched Zhen’s knee, and departed. Zhen laughed and said, "The customer who sells spoons and chopsticks has not yet arrived.
From this point on, Zhen recognized his wit and eloquence; seeing that he had cast off all conventional molds, he praised him highly.
Chan Master Xuefeng Daoyuan (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Nan).
Chan Master Xuefeng Daoyuan of Nan’an County was a native of Nanxiong. He relied upon Jicui for his practice and would sit in meditation until dusk.

Once, as the board signaling the end of the session was being lowered, two monks were discussing the "Wild Fox" kōan. One said, "Even 'not obscuring cause and effect' has not yet allowed one to escape the status of a wild fox."
"Body. One person said, "It does not fall into cause and effect; how could it have ever fallen as a wild fox? Upon hearing this, the Master was struck with awe.

He went to Jicui Hermitage, and while crossing a mountain stream, he attained a sudden, profound realization. He composed a verse, saying: "Not falling, not being obscured— Between monk and layman, there is originally no taboo.
A man of spirit has the bearing of a king; Why would he accept being confined within a bag or covered by a cloak? With a single staff, he moves freely in all directions."
A wild fox leaps into the ranks of the golden-haired lions; Jici saw this and rejoiced.
Chan Master Zhiguan of Qionglong, Suzhou (dharma heir of Dinghui Xin), ascended the hall and said:
"When fortune arrives, I do not speak of Chan; with nothing to do, I sleep late in the day."
When someone asked about the meaning of the Patriarch, he struck them two or three times in succession. Tell me, O assembly: why did he do so?
It was because that person disturbed my sleep.
The Thirteenth Generation under Nanyue (the Ninth Generation under Linji):
Chan Master Wuzu Fayuan (Dharma Heir of Baiyun Yuan).
Chan Master Wuzu Fayuan of Qi State was the son of the Deng family of Mianzhou. Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he studied the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Consciousness-Only).
In the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*, it is recorded that when a Bodhisattva enters the Path of Seeing (*darśana-mārga*), wisdom merges with principle and the object merges with the spirit;
thus, the means of realization and the object realized are not distinguished. Once, a non-Buddhist from the Western Regions challenged a Bhikṣu, saying:

"If you do not distinguish between the means of realization and the object realized, then by what means do you realize? No one could respond. The non-Buddhist disparaged him, ordering that the bells and drums no longer be sounded, and he was forced to retreat.
Donning his *kāṣāya*, the Tripitaka Master Xuanzang arrived there. To resolve this point, he said, "It is like a person drinking water:

whether it is cold or warm, they know it for themselves. This cleared up the difficulty. The Master said, "The coldness and warmth may indeed be known, but what is the matter of 'knowing for oneself'?
He then questioned the original lecturer, saying, "I do not understand the principle of 'knowing for oneself. How is it so? The original lecturer could not evade him.
The questioner said, "I merely wish to guide you by saying: if you desire to clarify this, you should go to the south and seek out those who have transmitted the Buddha-mind school.
The Master immediately took up his book-bundle and departed through the pass. Whichever venerable elders he encountered, he consulted them all on this matter; yet his doubts remained unresolved.

Finally, upon visiting Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben, the karmic conditions of past and present were fully resolved, with the sole exception of not understanding the case where a monk asked Xinghua about the "Four."
"When the eight directions come at once, how is it? Xinghua said, "Strike the one in the middle. The monk bowed.

The Layman Guo Xiangzheng, Provincial Commissioner for Judicial Review (Dharma heir of Baiyun Yuan).
The Layman Guo Xiangzheng, styled Gongfu and titled the Layman Jingkong, was one whose aspirations delighted in springs and rocks, having no envy for worldly splendor.
He went to visit Baiyun, who ascended the hall and said: "Last night upon my pillow, I composed a mountain verse as a thanksgiving."
Gongfu is a great Confucian scholar and an old friend from twenty years at Mount Lu. His diligent effort in visiting me from afar today must be presented to the assembly for their request;
later, you shall clearly present this to the various quarters.
