Chan Master Wuxin of Huanglong (the Dharma heir of Huanglong Xinfu) at Longxing Prefecture’s Huanglong Temple was a native of the Huang family of Shaoshan. At birth, he had a purple birthmark on his flesh.
He wore his upper garment draped over the left shoulder with the right arm bared, in the manner of a *saṃghāṭī*. Traveling to Huanglong, he went to visit Huìtáng.
Huìtáng held up a fist and asked, "To call this a 'fist' is to commit the fault of *chù*; not to call it a 'fist' is to commit the fault of *bèi*. What do you call it? The Master was at a loss.
It took two years before he finally attained realization; yet, he still engaged in debate without being refuted. Huìtáng—
Huitang was concerned about him. One day, while conversing with him, when the Master reached the point of his sharpness, Huitang suddenly said, "Stop, stop!

Talking about food—how can it satisfy one's hunger? The Master was cornered and said, "I have come to this point; my bow is broken and my arrows are spent. I pray that the Master will show me compassion and point out a place of peace and happiness.
Huitang said, "A single speck of dust flies up and obscures the heavens; a single mustard seed falls and covers the earth. This is the place of peace and happiness."
Master Zhengji said to the Elder, "You have many antiquities; you must truly die away the entire mind that has persisted for immeasurable kalpas before it will do.
The Master stepped out. One day, hearing the administrative official strike a novice, a sudden clap of thunder struck, and he attained great enlightenment immediately.
He hurried to see Huìtáng, forgetting to put on his sandals. He immediately praised himself, saying, "All people under heaven have merely attained Chan through inquiry;
I am one who has realized it. Huìtáng laughed and said, "To have won the first rank in the selection for Buddhahood—how could you possibly be matched?
For this reason, he was given the title "Old Man Sīxīn" (Dead Heart).
Chan Master Huanglong Weiqing (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Xin).
Chan Master Huanglong Lingyuan Weiqing of Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of this prefecture.

Having received the seal of mind from Huaitang, he would often say to people: "As for those who study today, they have not yet escaped birth and death. Where does their sickness lie? Their sickness lies..."

The thieving mind has simply not yet died. However, this is not the fault of the student; it is the fault of the teacher. It is like Emperor Gaozu of Han, who deceived and killed Han Xin. Although Xin was dead, was his mind truly dead?
As for those who studied in antiquity, they attained liberation from birth and death upon hearing a single word.

Where is the evidence of this efficacy? It lies in the fact that the thieving mind has already perished. Yet, this is not something the student can achieve on their own; it is truly [the work of the teacher].

For one who acts as a teacher, the tongs and hammer must be subtle and precise. It was like Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, who, upon seeing Hou Jing in the Great Hall, did not move a muscle nor change his expression;
yet the heart of Jing was already withered and drained of all remaining strength. What is taught by various schools is not without its beauty.
In short, it is like the flowers painted by Zhao Chang: although the flowers are lifelike, they are not real flowers.
Chan Master Shanqing of Letan (a dharma heir of Huanglong Xin):
Chan Master Shanqing of Caotang at Letan in Longxing Prefecture was the son of the He family from Nanxiong Prefecture. Initially, he visited Da... [text fragment ends]
Chan Master Weizhe attained nothing [in his practice]. Later, he visited Huanglong, who showed him the "wind and banner" koan.
For a long time, he failed to reach a realization. One day, Huanglong asked, "How do you understand the 'wind and banner' koan?
The Master replied, "I have no way of entry; I beg the Master for a skillful means. Huanglong said, "Have you seen a cat catching a mouse? Its eyes do not blink, and its four paws..."
His feet were planted firmly on the ground; his faculties were directed in harmony; from head to tail he was perfectly straight; wherever he aimed, there was nothing that did not hit the mark.

"If you, my son, can truly be thus—without other conditions in the mind, with the six sense-faculties naturally stilled, and investigating in silence—you will surely never miss the one. Following this, the Master withdrew from all distracting conditions.
After more than a year, he attained a sudden and expansive realization. He addressed Huanglong with a verse, saying: "Following, following, following. In the past..."
"Night after night, following and following behind, no one recognizes him. When night falls and the bright moon ascends the high peak, it turns out he is simply this very thief.

Huanglong accepted this and further told him: "To attain the Way is not difficult; to propagate the Way is difficult. To propagate the Way depends on oneself; to preach the Dharma for others is difficult.
Once you have attained clarity, it lies in your power to put it into practice. Generally speaking, this is the essence of our school."
The Master taught the Dharma. Within a single phrase, he possessed the Three Mysteries; within each Mystery, he possessed the Three Essentials. You have entered the true path;
having attained your seat and donned your robes, look back upon yourself hereafter, and you will naturally proceed with the seven openings and eight thoroughfares unimpeded.

The Master remained in attendance for another seven years, after which he took his leave to travel extensively through the monastic forests. Later, he appeared in the world at Huanglong and passed away at Letan.
Chan Master Qingyuan Weixin (Dharma heir of Huanglong Xin).
Chan Master Qingyuan Weixin of Jizhou ascended the hall and said: "When this old monk was thirty years ago, before I had studied Chan..."

At first, one sees mountains as mountains and waters as waters. Later, upon meeting a true teacher and gaining a point of entry, one sees mountains as not being mountains and waters as not being waters.
Now, having attained a place of rest, one again sees mountains as simply mountains and waters as simply waters.
O Great Assembly, are these three modes of seeing the same or are they different?
If there is someone, whether monastic or lay, who can produce [this work], I grant that you have personally seen the old monk.
Chan Master Xiaochun of Jia Shan (dharma heir of Huanglong Xin):
Chan Master Xiaochun of Lingquan Monastery at Jia Shan in Liuzhou. He once had a wooden carving made of a beast—a lion.
He had the head of an ox and the legs of a horse. Whenever he ascended the hall, he would hold it up and show it to the assembly, saying:
"If you call this a lion, it has the body of a horse; if you call it a horse, it has the legs of an ox. Tell me, in the end, what should it be called?
He then commanded the monks to offer a response, but none were able to reach a point of accord.
Chan Master Benquan of Baofu (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Xin).
Chan Master Benquan of Baofu was a native of Linzhang in Zhangzhou. By nature he was straightforward and courageous in the pursuit of the Way.

At the instance of Huītáng’s raising of his fist, he attained thorough realization of the fundamental source. His wit and eloquence emerged with swift agility. When Huang Shan谷 first [encountered him]...
Huìtáng entered and asked, "Who here is capable of engaging in dialogue? Huìtáng replied, "Quán of Zhāngzhōu. At that time, the Master (Dàoxi) was supervising laborers in the cultivation of fields;
Huánggǔ went with Huìtáng to visit him and posed the question: "Does the steward know that the pillar has given birth to a child?"
The Master said, "Is it a boy? Is it a girl? Huangbo (Shangu) hesitated; the Master struck him. Heitang said to him, "You must not be so rude.
The Master said, "This block of wood—when do you expect me to strike him otherwise? Huangbo laughed heartily.
The Grand Historian, Layman Huang Tingjian (Dharma heir of Huanglong Xinfang), the Layman Valley (Shan谷) Huang Tingjian, styled Luzhi.
Possessing the karmic predispositions of past lives for Prajñā, he remained as detached as if in a high office despite his prominent career.
Although he moved between the various Chan schools, he found no definitive direction; he was fond of composing flowery verses and once visited Yuan Tong Xiu.
The Chan Master Xiu scolded him, saying, "A man of great character! Why would you deign to apply such mastery of brush and ink to this?
At that time, Xiu was just beginning to instruct Li Bashi on the matter of painting horses; the Master rebuked him, saying, "Are you not going to place me once again within the belly of a horse?"

Xiu said, "With your flowery words, you have stirred the lustful hearts of all people under heaven; it is not merely that they will end up in the bellies of horses, but I fear they will be reborn in the hells.
Gong was struck with awe and repented, apologizing profusely. From then on, he ceased his writing and devoted himself solely to the Way.

He composed a text of vows, strictly forbidding himself from alcohol and sexual indulgence, eating only morning gruel and the midday meal. He went to rely upon Huìtáng, seeking instruction on the direct and swift path.
At that place, Huìtáng said, "As for Confucius saying, 'Disciples, do you think I have anything hidden from you?
I have nothing hidden from you,' how would you explain this, Master Tàishǐ? As the Master was about to respond, Huìtáng said, "Not so, not so.
The Master remained in a state of confusion and distress. One day, while attending Huìtáng on a mountain walk, the rock-plantains were in full bloom. Huìtáng—
Huitang asked, "Do you smell the fragrance of the osmanthus? The official replied, "I do. Huitang said, "I have hidden nothing from you.
The official was suddenly relieved and prostrated himself, saying, "How deeply compassionate and earnest is the Master’s heart! Huitang smiled and said, "I only wish for you to reach home.
After some time, he went to visit Chan Master Sixin Xin of Yunyan. Following the assembly, he entered the room. Sixin...
Xinjian opened his eyes wide and asked, "The new Elder has died; the Scholar has died. They have been burned into two mounds of ash.
Where shall we meet? Xinjian was speechless. Sishin Yu stepped forward and said, "What you attained under Huichang has not yet taken root.
Later, while serving in exile in Qian-nan, his power of the Way grew even more eminent. Amidst a state of non-thought, he suddenly and fully realized Sishin’s teaching.

In response to the question, he sent a letter saying: "In years past, I was repeatedly and earnestly exhorted by you, yet I remained as if in a long dream, lingering vaguely within the light and shadow.
This was because my doubts were not fully exhausted and the root of my life-destiny was not severed; thus, I retreated in awe, like one gazing at a precipice.
While on the road to Qian Nan during my exile, I was napping in the daytime, and upon waking, I suddenly began to reflect: [I have been] by the elder monks of the world..."
"How many have been deceived! Only the Venerable Sishin refused; this was truly the foremost act of true concern.
Layman Wu Xun, Secretary (a dharma heir of Huanglong Xin).
Layman Wu Xun, whose courtesy name was De-fu, resided at Huìtáng. On one occasion during his entry into the inner chamber, Huìtáng said to him: "Píng..."
"You have produced scholarly understanding, memory, and extensive learning; I do not question those. But before your parents were born, bring me a single phrase.
As the Master hesitated, Heidong struck him with his whisk, whereupon he grasped the profound meaning and presented three successive verses.
The latter says: "Ho! You worldly fellow of vast knowledge! Having gnawed through all the public cases of the past and present, you suddenly pick up a dung ball from a heap of filth.
It is not worth a single coin, yet ten thousand taels of gold would not buy it.
You casually pick it up and show it to others, simply because a sliding tray is difficult to watch. Heh!"
Chan Master You Rui of Baqin (Dharma heir of Donglin Zong).
Chan Master Fohai You Rui of Baqin Jingde Monastery in the Eastern Capital was a native of the Chen family of Xinghua Prefecture.
Initially, he went to visit Chan Master Huanglong Nan. Huanglong asked, "Have you come for the sake of people, or have you come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma? The Master replied:
“I have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma. Huanglong said, “If you have come for the sake of the Buddha-dharma, I shall entrust it to you this very moment.
He then struck once with his whisk. The Master said, “Even a monk like you should not trouble people. Huanglong immediately recognized his potential.
Later, he followed Zhaojue and deeply realized the profound mysteries.
Chan Master Shaoci of Wanshan (Dharma Heir of Donglin Zong):
Chan Master Shaoci of Wanshan Monastery on Mount Lu was the son of the Zhao family of Guizhou.

He studied under Chan Master Zhaojue, who asked him, "Aside from the golden robe bestowed by the World-Honored One, what else was transmitted? Zhaojue held up his whisk. The Master said, "Ultimately, what is it?"
Shengzhao struck him across the mouth with his whisk. As the Master prepared to open his mouth, Shengzhao struck him again. At this, the Master attained realization;
he then seized the whisk and prostrated. Shengzhao asked, "What principle have you seen that you prostrate?"
The Master said, "The whisk belongs to me. Zhaojue remarked, "A veteran of thirty years has been defeated today by a mere recruit.
From this point on, his mysterious influence spread widely, and he was promoted to the position of head monk at Donglin.
Venerable Huìyuán (Dharma Successor of Tóng of Dōnglín).
Venerable Huìyuán was the son of the Qián clan of Suānzǎo in Kāifēng. By nature he was blunt and simple, yet he was diligent in the ancestral Way.

He sat steadfastly without lying down for several years. Having received full ordination, he traveled to Mount Lú and arrived at Dōnglín, where he constantly requested instruction regarding his own spiritual practice.
Question: His companions saw that his appearance was coarse and his deportment awkward; they all mocked him. One day, while walking through the palace courtyard, he suddenly tripped and fell.
He attained sudden enlightenment and composed a verse, instructing a practitioner to write it on the wall, which said:
"This one fall, this one fall— Even ten thousand taels of gold would be worth it. A hat upon my head, a bundle at my waist— The pure breeze..."

Carrying the bright moon upon the tip of his staff, he departed from Donglin that very day. The news spread to Zhaojue, who was greatly pleased and said, "If a monk’s investigation reaches this level, no greater excellence could be added.
He ordered someone to track his destination, but in the end, no one knew where he had gone.
(Dahui’s *Wuku* states that this was not the speech of Zhengwu Yong; however, that is incorrect.)
The Inner Secretary, Layman Su Shi (Dharma heir of Donglin Zong).
The Inner Secretary, Layman Dongpo Su Shi, styled Zizhan, while staying at Donglin, attained realization through a discussion with Zhaojue on the "discourse of the insentient.
At dawn, he offered this verse: "The sound of the stream is the broad and long tongue; Are the colors of the mountains not..."
"Pure Body," he recited eighty-four thousand verses throughout the night. He thought, "How can I present this to others on another day? Before long, he arrived at Jingnan.
Hearing that Master Chan Master Hao of Yuquan possessed a kōan-penetrating sharpness (jīfēng) that could not be provoked, the official intended to suppress him.

He immediately sought an audience in plain clothes. Yuquan asked, "What is your honorable surname, Great Official? The official replied, "My surname is Chéng (Scale). [Yuquan continued,] "It is for weighing the elders of the world."
[The Master] weighed [the matter]. Yuquan shouted, saying, "Tell me, how much does this shout weigh? The Master had no reply. (Dingshan Xing spoke on his behalf, saying:

"The scale-pan pointer has exploded! Thereupon, he treated him with great reverence. (Dingshan Xing said: "Why not simply be like this? Later, when he passed by Mount Jin, there was someone who wished to paint his portrait.
The Master playfully inscribed it, saying: "My mind is like wood whose fire has been extinguished; my body is like an unmoored boat. I ask you, what is level?"

He accomplished his meritorious deeds in Huangzhou, Huizhou, and Qiongzhou. (Dingshan Xìn’s verse says: "Huangzhou, Huizhou, Qiongzhou; going and coming, he was always alone. He managed to obtain a single scale, yet when he let out a shout, he was still empty-handed.

His life was one of carefree wandering; its subtlety lay in his tongue’s ability to stir things up. He composed this literature for ten thousand ages, like the rustling of autumn winds. He was like a bag of lime powder—left in disarray, requiring no broom to sweep it up.
If you ask further how it was or what it was, he did not know how to speak of Chan; he only knew how to eat meat and drink wine)."
Chan Master Congyue of Doushuai (Dharma heir of Baofeng Wen).
Chan Master Congyue of Doushuai in Longxing Prefecture was a native of the Xiong clan of Ganzhou. Initially, he led the assembly at Daowu.
Carrying several layers of patched robes, he went to visit Master Zhì of Yúngài. Before Yúngài had spoken more than a few sentences, he fully understood what was stored within [the visitor].
He then smiled and said, "I observe that the Senior Seat's temperament and bearing are extraordinary; why is it that your speech and breath are like those of a drunkard?"

The Master’s face flushed with heat and sweat as he said, “I pray that the Venerable Master will not begrudge his compassion. Yun’gai spoke to him again, probing him with sharp words; the Master was utterly bewildered.
He then requested to enter the room for private instruction. Yun’gai asked, “Have you ever met Master Fachang Yu? The Master replied, “I have read his recorded sayings;
they are sufficient for my own understanding, so I have no wish to meet him. Yun’gai said, “Have you ever seen Master Dong...?”
"Shanwen, is that you? The Master replied, "A man from Guansi has no sense. Dragging along a hempen skirt and exuding the stench of urine—what excellence is there in him?
Yun'gai said, "You should simply investigate within the stench of urine. Following these instructions, the Master went to visit Dongshan, where he deeply grasped the profound essence.
He then visited Yun'gai again, who said, "I have seen that man from Guansi."
Later, [the student] asked, "What about the Great Matter? The Master said, "Had you not received the instructions of the Abbot, you would have let this life pass by in vain.
Thereupon, he paid his respects and took leave. The Master subsequently visited Zhenjing. Later, he took up residence at Lüyuan.

There was one named Qing Su who had long studied under Ciming; he lived in a single room and never associated with others. Once, while the Master was eating lychees preserved in honey, he happened upon Qing Su.
As he passed through the gate, the Master called out, "This is the local fruit of this elder's village; you may eat it together with me.
Qing-su replied, "Since the passing of my late teacher, I have not been able to obtain this food for a long time. The Master asked, "Who was your late teacher? Qing-su said, "Ciming.
I have had the honor of serving him for thirteen years. The Master then said in astonishment, "Thirteen years of enduring service!"
"Regarding the service of attending upon others, how could it be anything other than attaining the Way? He then offered me some leftover fruit and gradually grew intimate with me.
Qing-su asked the Master, 'Who was it that you saw? The Master replied, 'Dongshan Wen. Qing-su asked, 'Whom did Wen see? The Master said:
Huanglong Nan said to Qing-su, "The Junior Monk Nan saw the former Master; before long, his Dharma path has flourished in such a manner.
The Master became even more suspicious and alarmed, so he placed incense in his sleeve and went to pay respects to Qing-su. Qing-su rose and avoided him, saying, "I am of meager merit;
the former Master gave me a prediction that I am not permitted to take on disciples. The Master was even more reverent, whereupon Qing-su said, "I pity you..."
"Cheng, you have violated your late teacher’s prediction. Try telling me what you have realized throughout your life. The Master fully disclosed his insights.

Chingsu said, "This may allow one to enter the Buddha-dharma, but it cannot allow one to enter the realm of Māra. The Master asked, "What do you mean? Chingsu replied, "Have you not seen the ancients say:
'The final phrase is where one finally reaches the secure barrier'? This went on for several months, after which Chingsu then...
He gave his seal of approval and further cautioned him, saying: "The texts shown to you all contain correct knowledge and correct view;

however, you departed from the texts too early and were unable to exhaust their subtle wonders. I shall now point them out for you, so that you may attain mastery and great freedom in their application."
"In the future, you must by no means succeed me. The Master later succeeded Zhenjing, just as he had previously cautioned.

One day, the Commissioner of the Circuit, the Layman Wujin Zhang Shangying, while inspecting the prefectures, passed through Fenning. He invited the elders of the five monasteries to preach the Dharma at Yunyan.
The Master was the last to ascend the seat; crossing his staff horizontally, he said: "Just now, all you good spiritual friends [crossed...]"
Holding up, setting down; standing upright, tossing askance; shifting steps, moving the body; hiding the head, exposing the horns.
Since you have each suffered defeat before the Scholar, you cannot avoid receiving a severe blow from the hand of Doushuai. Reaching this point, it is beyond whether one is willing or unwilling.
Why? Because when one sees an injustice, how can one bear to endure it? A Zen monk must personally carry out the true command. *Zhuo!* (The staff strikes.)

[The Master] lowered his staff and descended from the seat. In the meditation hall, he established three questions to test the practitioners. The first was: "One brushes away the weeds and shoulders the wind, seeking only to see one's nature.
Where, right now, does this person's nature reside? The second was: "Only by recognizing one's own nature can one be liberated from birth and death.
When the light of the eyes falls to the ground, how will you be liberated? The third was: "Once you have been liberated from birth and death, you will know..."
As for the place of departure: when the four elements separate, where does one go? In the winter of the sixth year of the Yuanyou era, after bathing, he gathered the assembly and spoke this verse:
"Forty-eight years, saints and ordinary folk all slain; Not a hero, indeed—Longan's path is slippery."
He passed away suddenly.
Chan Master Fa-yun Gao (dharma heir of Bao-feng Wen):
Chan Master Fa-yun Fo-zhao Gao of Dongjing. From his youth, he traveled to various regions and visited Chan Master Yuan-tong Ji.
Next, during the entry into the hall, Yuantong raised a case. A monk asked Touzi, "When one who has undergone the 'great death' returns to life, what is it like?
Touzi said, "Night travel is not permitted; you must arrive by dawn. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The kindness is so great that it is difficult to repay."
Yuantong was greatly pleased and subsequently appointed him as the head of the assembly. That evening, he was asked to preside over the *bifu* (the incense offering) for the community;

however, his responses were slow and his speech halting, causing the assembly to laugh. The Master felt abashed. The following day, while serving tea in the Sangha Hall, the tea ladle slipped from his hand and fell to the ground.
Seeing the ladle bounce, he attained the *samādhi* of responding to stimuli. Later, while relying on Zhenjing, he read a verse by the Patriarch which said: "The mind is identical to empty space."
Regarding the realms: he demonstrated the dharma that is equal to empty space. When he realized emptiness, there was neither "is" nor "non-is.

He attained a sudden and great enlightenment, and would often say to others: "On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month in the third year of the Shaosheng era, I realized the Chan of the square inch [of the mind]."
Chan Master Létán Wénzhǔn (Dharma heir of Bǎofēng Wén).
Chan Master Létán Zhàntáng Wénzhǔn of Lóngxīng Prefecture was the son of the Liáng family of Xīngyuan Prefecture. Initially, he visited Zhējìng.
Zhējìng asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "Dàyǎng. Zhējìng asked, "Where did you spend the summer retreat? The Master—
[Daowei] said, "Daming. Zhenjing asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "Xingyuan Prefecture. Zhenjing spread out his hands and asked, "How does my hand compare to the Buddha’s hand?
The Master was at a loss. Zhenjing said, "Just now, when you were responding, everything was luminous and every thing was authentic.
Yet, as soon as you spoke the words 'How does my hand compare to the Buddha’s hand,' it became an obstruction. Tell me, what is the illness?"
The Master asked, "Where is it? Zhengnan said, "I do not understand. Zhenjing said, "Everything is already manifest; who else would you have teach to understand?
At that moment, the Master was instantly relieved. He served him diligently for ten years. In the third year of the Shaosheng era, Zhenjing moved to Shimen. The assembly grew even more prosperous.
Whenever monks came to question him, he would simply sit upright with his eyes closed and offer no instruction. When he saw those who had come to study, he would go out to tend to them.
He tended a vegetable garden as his regular practice. The Master said to his companion, the Elder Gong: "Does this old man have no interest in the Way of the Dharma?
One day, while raising his staff to clear a channel, water splashed onto his robes; he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Zhenjing scolded him, saying: "How dare you act so recklessly?
From then on, the Master’s traces became even more hidden, yet his fame grew ever greater. The Master returned from Zhejiang to Le’an.

He went to the abbot’s quarters to communicate his insight, but Shēn shouted at him and sent him out. Consequently, Wù lost his resolve and hanged himself in the Yǎnshòu Hall.

When he reached the dialogue concerning the "dog of Master Zi-hu," Wuzu suddenly turned his face away and said, "That is not it. The Master asked, "If it is not that, then what?
Wuzu said, "If this is not it, then everything preceding it is also not it. The Master said, "I hope for the Master’s compassion..."
Bi pointed this out. Wuzu said: "Look at what he says: 'Zihu has a dog that bites people on the head, bites people in the waist, and bites people on the feet.
When someone enters the gate, look well; as soon as the monk enters the gate, he immediately says, 'Look at the dog!
Now, regarding Zihu’s saying 'Look at the dog,' provide a turning word that leaves Zihu tongue-tied and causes this old monk to clench his mouth."

"This is precisely where you have reached certainty. The next day, the Master entered the room and silently presented his understanding. The Fifth Patriarch smiled and said, "I do not say that you are not right;
you are a person who has brought matters to a thousandfold completion and a hundredfold resolution.

These words are exactly like those spoken by my late teacher. The Master said, "What kind of person am I to be like Master Duan? The Fifth Patriarch replied, "It is not so. Although I have inherited his lineage,"
This refers to the Master’s critique of Yuanluo Gong’s clumsy speech; it was because Yuanluo Gong’s methods for engaging people were merely those of a distant observer.
For instance, when the Old Monk [Linji] was with Yuanluo Gong, he would have walked hand-in-hand with Baizhang, Huangbo, Nanquan, Zhaozhou, and their peers.

As soon as he saw such clumsy speech, he deemed it intolerable. The Master thought this was not the case, so he took up his staff and crossed the river, only to find that the great waters were overflowing.
Because he remained with the Fourth Patriarch, his peers urged him to return home. After another two years, the Fifth Patriarch finally gave his approval.

Once, while discussing the past and present, the Master took the teacher’s hand and said, "To understand your explanation, you must have my raising of it; to understand my raising of it, you must have your explaining of it.
From this day forward, the secret essentials of the Buddhas and Patriarchs and the pivotal points of all quarters shall not escape your grasp."
There was an old master who gave a turning word, saying: "At the crossroads of the main street, one erects a small thatched hut;
it simply does not permit anyone to defecate. A monk cited this to question the Master. The Master said: "You have already defecated first; what else can you make someone do?"
Upon hearing this, the elder monk burned incense and gazed afar; Da sui bowed twice in thanks.
Chan Master Wúwéi Zōngtài (a dharma heir of Wǔzǔ Yǎn):
Chan Master Wúwéi Zōngtài of Hánzhōu was a native of Fúchéng. Having left the pass, he traveled extensively among the monastic communities until he reached the Fifth [Patriarch].
On the day the Patriarch offered incense, the Fifth Patriarch brought up the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl and instructed him to investigate it.
When [Huairang] entered the room, the Patriarch raised this story and asked the Master: "Tell me, what did Zhaozhou say to that monk? Why did that monk attain awakening immediately?
The Master replied, "He said, 'Go wash the alms bowl. The Fifth Patriarch said, "You know only the matters of the road; you do not know the flavor of the road. The Master [remained silent].
The Master said, "Since you already know what happens on the road, what flavor is there on the road? Wuzu said, "Do you not know?
He asked again, "Have you ever traveled through Zhejiang? The Master replied, "No. Wuzu said, "You have not yet attained realization.
From that time forward, for five years, the Master was unable to respond. One day, Wuzu ascended the hall and looked at the assembly, saying, "An eighty-year-old man rolls..."
Xiuqiu immediately descended from his seat. The Master joyfully stepped out from the assembly and said, "Venerable Sir, try rolling it once and see.
Wuzu made a gesture with his hands as if striking a war drum and sang a folk song from Mianzhou in the Shu dialect:
"On Mount Doushi they beat the earthen drums; On Mount Yangping they scatter white rain. As the white rain falls, they fetch the Dragon Maiden; She weaves two zhang and five chi of silk."

"Half belongs to Lujiang; half belongs to Wuxuan. Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He covered the Fifth Patriarch’s mouth, saying, "It need only be chanted up to this point.
The Fifth Patriarch laughed heartily and returned home.
Chan Master Biaozhi of Wuzu (Dharma heir of Wuzu Yan).
Chan Master Biaozhi of Wuzu was a native of Huai’an in Qizhou. He initially relied upon Wuzu for the longest period of time without yet having attained realization.
At that time, Yuanwu served as the Seat-Head (Zuoyuan); the Master went to seek his instruction. Yuanwu said, "Brother, try telling me where you have doubts."
My teacher then brought up the story of Deshan’s informal discourse (xiaocan): "I do not answer questions; those who ask questions shall receive thirty blows.

Yuanwu said, "Bow down to me; I can handle you. You have not yet understood the story my teacher brought up. After the teacher had finished bowing, Yuanwu ordered him to repeat the previous statement.
The teacher said, "Deshan’s informal discourse: 'I do not answer questions. Yuanwu covered his mouth and said, "Just..."

"Look at it this way," the Master said, stepping forward and raising his voice: "How unjust! How unjust! Is there really a public case here? It is simply to teach people the principle of looking into a single phrase.
A monk said to the Master, "Brother, you should not speak like that. The Head Seat must have had some skillful means;
through quiet sitting and investigation, he suddenly resolved his doubts within ten days. He then went to pay his respects to Yuanwu, who said, "Brother..."
"I now know that I have not deceived you. He then went to the Abbot’s quarters, where Wuzu greeted him with a smile. From that day on, [the teachings] became increasingly profound and esoteric.
Regarding Chan Master Qing-su of Jiuding Peak (a dharma heir of Wuzu Yan):

Chan Master Qing-su of Jiuding Peak in Jiazhou was the son of the Guo family of that prefecture. Having traveled extensively to knock at the doors of various Chan masters, he finally visited Wuzu late in life.

When the Fifth Patriarch heard Mazu recount the story of Shoushan’s answer regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey, he attained sudden enlightenment. He composed a verse, saying: "Inverted, inverted, inverted!
The new bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads. To act so is utterly groundless; Turning one's head, one does not realize one's robe has been torn.
Upon seeing this, the Fifth Patriarch asked, "And what about Baizhang’s story of the wild fox? How do you explain it? The Master replied, "It comes."
"To speak of right and wrong is itself to be a person of right and wrong. The Fifth Patriarch was greatly pleased for a long time;

he took his leave and returned to reside at Qingxi, later moving to Jiuding. Once, when Governor Lü came to behold the Great Image, he asked, "Since this is a great image, why does it have two pillars resting upon its shoulders?
The Master replied, "There are no idle laborers on a boat. When they reached the pavilion below, they beheld the Avalokiteśvara image.

He asked again, "Maitreya’s realm has been transformed; from where does Guanyin come? The Master said, "When a family is wealthy, the young child is spoiled. When the Governor arrived, he paid his respects to the old monk Qín.
The Master asked, "When the sword is poised at the throat during a dance, what then? He replied, "I humbly pray you will partake of the offering.
The Master scolded him, saying, "You old thief! Go die! You were asking me about Qín; ask him about the previous words. The Master then crossed his hands.
Yi said, "Drag it apart.
The Head Seat Yuanli (a dharma heir of Wuzu Fayan). Head Seat Yuanli was a native of Min.
Initially, he studied under Master Yan at Baiyun; whenever he entered the master's room for instruction, [the master] would invariably say:
He said, "The family of patch-robed monks clearly distinguishes between the black and the white. The Master, still harboring doubts, could not cease his reflections.

One day, Wuzu ascended the hall and cited the saying of Shoushan: "The bride riding the donkey, the mother-in-law leading her. He then said, "Do you all wish to understand? Do not ask about the bride or the mother-in-law;
this will spare you the trouble of bickering on the road. When meeting rice, eat rice; when meeting tea, drink tea. Fellow practitioners..."
Coming and going, his karmic enemies from past lives were suddenly cleared away beneath the Master’s words. He said, "Today, the distinction between the ordained and the laity is clear.
Puyong Zhizang (Dharma heir of Wuzu Fayan).
Puyong Zhizang was a native of Fuzhou. When he entered the inner room of Wuzu, Wuzu raised the case of the "Clever Woman Leaving Her Husband."

*Hun-hua* (Soul-talk). When questioned, he reached a point of accord and presented this verse: Two women joined together to become one daughter-in-law; The turning wheel is severed, impossible to reverse.
From of old, coming and going have left no trace; Travelers need not ask the road by which they came.

Whenever local monks came to visit him, he would speak in the Min dialect and recite these vernacular lines: "At the beginning of the letter, I instruct my mother to be diligent in her rest and labor; at the end of the letter..."
"Instruct your daughter not to doze off. [The Master] asked, "Tell me, what did he say in between? The monk prepared to respond, but the Master immediately pushed him out.
Dharma Chu (a successor of Wuzu Fayan) had long relied upon Wuzu, yet he had not yet attained realization. One day he entered the master’s quarters, and Wuzu asked him, "Not..."
"Who is it that dwells as a companion to the myriad dharmas? Fachu said, "It is not so.
The Fifth Patriarch pointed his finger and said, "Stop, stop! Fachu, if it is not so, then how is it? At this, the Master attained awakening.
Later, he went to the seat of Chan Master Xianming of Donglin, where he saw that he had attained the principle of "plain reality. One day, [the Master] held up a flower.
He walked around the meditation seat once, turned his back to it, and thrust his hand into the incense burner, saying, "Master, tell me:
how did you cross over? He offered several responses, but none were in accord. After two months had passed, he finally asked the Master to explain them for him. The Master said:
A certain person merely took some flowers and inserted them into the incense burner. The Master himself wondered, "What business has this person come for?
Yudao Po of Jinling (a dharma successor of Langye Huijue):
Yudao Po was a native of Jinling. She made her living by selling oil-cakes (*youci*). She regularly accompanied the assembly to consult Langye. Langye...
Xie used the story of Linji’s “True Person Without Rank” to instruct her. One day, she heard a beggar singing a *lianhua* song that went:
"Were it not for Liu Yi delivering the letter, by what means could one reach Lake Dongting? She suddenly attained great enlightenment; she threw her rice cake tray to the ground.
Her husband looked on askance and said, "Are you mad? His wife slapped him and said, "This is not within your realm. She then went to see Lang [Huijue].
Xie Langye Wangzhi recognized his profound realization and asked, "Which one is the 'Person of No Rank'? Ba responded at once:
"There is a person of no rank with six arms and three heads who exerts himself in wrath; with a single strike, he splits Mount Huashan in two."
For ten thousand years the flowing water has known nothing of spring. Thus her fame spread far and wide. Whenever a monk arrived, she would say, "My son! My son!
If the monk hesitated or deliberated, she would immediately shut the door. Chan Master Fodeng Xun went to test her.
When the old woman saw him, she asked the same questions as before. Fodeng said, "Where is your father? The old woman turned around and bowed toward a pillar. Fodeng then stepped on it.
Daowu said, "I thought there was something truly extraordinary here," and he stepped out. Baqie started up and said, "My child, my child!
Come here; I cherish you. Fodeng did not look back at all. When Head Seat An arrived, Baqie asked, "Where have you come from?
The Head Seat replied, "From Deshan. Baqie said, "Deshan Tai is the son of an old woman. The Head Seat asked, "And who is the old woman's son?"
The Master said, "Son, when the Elder asked that one question, it was as if he stood there urinating. Later, the Master composed a verse on the occasion of Mazu’s illness, saying:
"The face of the sun, the face of the moon, like lightning flashing in the void.
Though it cuts off [all speech], the tongues of the monks of the world are clear; yet they can only say half of it."
Ancestor Xingkong Miaopu (Dharma heir of Huanglong Xin).
Ancestor Xingkong Miaopu of Huating in Jiaxing Prefecture was a native of Hanzhou. Having long relied upon Sishi, he attained realization.

He then arrived at Xiushui, where he followed the legacy of Chuanshi (Bo Juyi). He built a thatched hut in the wilds of Qinglong and amused himself by blowing his iron flute, composing many poems and lyrics.
At the beginning of the Jianyan era, the rebel Xu Ming passed through Wuzhen; the local people mostly fled, but the Master alone went forth carrying his staff.
The rebels were enraged and intended to execute him, but the Master said, "A man of great character—if you want my head, simply chop it off! Why [waste your effort]?"
"Because of this anger, my death is certain," he said. "I wish to have one meal as a parting offering for my final journey. The bandit brought him meat and grain.

The Master finished his usual midday meal and the ritual for the living, then said, "Who shall compose the inscription for my sacrifice? The bandit laughed but did not answer. The Master sought a brush and wrote in large characters:
"Alas! O Spirit, you have made me labor with life; this is the fault of the Great Mass (the Earth). You have employed me..."
If one’s lifespan is diminished, it is due to the imbalance of yin and yang; if one is impoverished, it is because the five elements are not in harmony;

if one is beset by misfortune, it is because the timing and days are inauspicious. Alas! How profound this is! Fortunately, there is the Way that transcends the mundane, which awakens my nature and its wondrous mind.
As for this wondrous mind, with whom could it share its intimacy? Above, it accords with the true transformation of all Buddhas; below, it harmonizes with...
The ignorance of ordinary beings does not stir so much as a speck of dust; it is fundamentally and spontaneously perfected. How wondrous! How wondrous indeed!

The sun and moon are not sufficient to represent its brilliance; heaven and earth are not sufficient to represent its vastness. It is磊磊落落 (leilei luoluo—lofty and expansive), without obstruction or hindrance.

For over sixty years, he blended his light with the world and mingled with the mundane; for forty-two years since his ordination, he has wandered at ease and in freedom. Whenever he encounters people...
Xī (Joy). Seeing the Buddha, he did not bow. "To laugh! To laugh! What a pity for this young man;
his elegance is too radiant. Return with ease to the spring breeze; your body is like empty space, ultimately indestructible. He then raised his chopsticks and ate heartily.
The bandits laughed loudly. After finishing his meal, he spoke again: "Since we have encountered these times of calamity and chaos, I am truly happy."
Lieh Han said, "Now is precisely the time to act; I pray you, cut him in two with a single stroke! He then shouted, "Kill! Kill!

Just as the bandit was struck with awe and alarm, he prostrated himself to apologize for his transgression. Lieh Han ordered guards to escort him out of the dwellings of Wu Town, sparing them from being burned;
this was truly the kindness of the Master. There was a monk who saw the Master seeing the Buddha and not bowing. He asked in opposition, "Since you have seen the Buddha, why do you not prostrate?"

"Why do you not bow? The Master struck him with his palm and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not understand. The Master struck him again with his palm and said, "A household has no two masters.
In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangshi era, he constructed a large basin, bored holes in it, and plugged them up.

He wrote a letter to Chan Master Chih of Xuedou, saying: "I shall undergo a water burial. When Chih arrived in the Renshu year, he saw that [the Master] was still alive. He composed a verse in mockery: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
He said, "Alas! Old Xingkong is stubborn; he wants to feed the fish and turtles. He will not leave of his own accord, but merely goes on talking to people.

The Master read the verse and said with a smile, "I shall wait for my brother to come and provide witness. He then ordered that the announcement be made throughout the fourfold assembly, and when the assembly had gathered, [he summoned him].
The Master preached the essentials of the Dharma for him, then spoke a verse: "To die while seated or standing is not as good as water burial.
First, it saves on firewood for cremation; second, it saves on digging a grave. To cast off one's hands and go forth—how unimpeded and exhilarating! Who is the one who knows this?
The Monk of the Boat—his lofty style is difficult to follow after a thousand years. Few can sing this single melody of the fisherman’s song. Thereupon, he sat cross-legged within the basin.
Going downstream with the current, the entire assembly followed him to the seashore, where their gaze was nearly blinded by the distance. The Master took up a scoop to dam the water and turned back;
the crowd pressed forward to watch, but the water had no place to enter. He then rode the current away once more, singing: "The Boatman returned to his hometown in those days;
Where his traces vanished, the wondrousness is immeasurable. The true wind is sent everywhere to those who know it; The iron reed is blown crosswise."
The assembly dispersed. As the sound of the flute wailed and sobbed, amidst the vast expanse of space, he was seen casting his flute into the air and vanishing.
Three days later, he was found sitting cross-legged upon the sand as if alive.
The Head Seat Daolong of Zhongshan (a successor of Huanglong Xin).
Head Seat Daolong of Zhongshan in Yanzhou was the son of the Dong family of Tonglu. Later, he arrived at Huanglong’s Sishin (Si Xin), who invited him to serve as the head of the assembly.
After Sishin passed away, he retired to live in seclusion at Mount Zhongshan, admiring the world-transcending character of the elder master Chen.
Every day he would unwind his spinning wheel for his own amusement, and no one recognized him. He always wore a single sock on his hand;
whenever a Chan practitioner arrived, he would hold it up and show it to them, saying, "I have worn this old monk’s sock for thirty years now."
Regarding the Chan Master Zhītōng of Kōngshì (a new Dharma heir of Hónglóng):
The Chan Master Zhītōng of Kōngshì was the daughter of Fàn Xūn, whose rank was recorded in the *Lóngtú*. She was intelligent from childhood.

Upon reaching maturity, she married Tí, the grandson of Chancellor Sū Sòng. Not long after, she grew weary of worldly phenomena and returned home to seek ordination. Her father opposed this, so she subsequently... [cleansed herself].

Xiu practiced meditation by contemplating the *dharmadhātu* (Dharma-realm). Suddenly, he attained a profound realization and composed two consecutive verses to express his insight. The first says: "In the vast expanse of the dusty world, the essence is one and the same;
Transverse and vertical, intermingling, they seal the Vairocana. The entire wave is water, yet the wave is not water; The entire water forms waves, yet the water remains distinct.
The second says: "Things and self are fundamentally non-different; The myriad phenomena are like reflections in a mirror. Brilliantly transcending..."
The principal and its attendants are clearly and thoroughly realized as the true void; a single essence contains manifold dharmas, interlacing within a net of Indra.

In this place of infinite, layered depth, movement and stillness are both perfectly pervasive. Later, when his parents had both passed away, his elder brother Jian took up the post of Magistrate of Fening.

Tong accompanied him on the journey. Hearing that the reputation of Sishin was great, they went to visit him. Upon seeing them, Sishin recognized what they had attained and immediately asked, "Sadāprarudita..."
The Bodhisattva said, "If you sell off your heart and liver, who will be taught to study Prajñā? Zhitong replied, "If you have no mind, I shall also desist.
He asked again, "When moistened by the same rain, the roots and sprouts differ; upon ground where there is neither yin nor yang, what can grow?"
Zhìtōng said, "One flower with five petals. He asked again, "Throughout the twelve periods of the day, where do you establish yourself and sustain your life?
Zhìtōng said, "Preceptor, spare your eyebrows. Hǎosīxīn struck him and said, "This woman is creating disorder out of sequence!
Zhìtōng bowed; Hǎosīxīn approved. Thereupon, his reputation for the Way became widespread. (During the Zhènghé era.)
While residing in Jinling, he once established a bathhouse at Baoning Temple and posted a notice on its door that read: "One thing is not present; what is there to wash?
If even a speck of dust exists, from where does it arise? Speak a single phrase of the profound mystery, and only then may you all enter the bath together.
Guling only knew how to scrub backs; when did the Bodhisattva ever clarify the mind? If you wish to realize the Stage of Freedom from Defilement (*vimalā-bhūmi*), [you must do so now].
One must experience perspiration throughout the entire body. Everyone says that water can wash away filth, but who knows that water itself is also dust?
Even if water and filth are suddenly removed, when one reaches this point, even that [realization] must be washed away. Later, she became a nun named Weijiu (Venerable Long) and resided at Gusu.

The monastics and laypeople of India questioned him day and night; those who attained his Way were quite numerous. Suddenly, he manifested illness, wrote a verse, sat in the lotus posture, and passed away.
Chan Master Shàngfēng Běncái (Dharma heir of Huánglóng Qīng).
Chan Master Focin Cai of Shangfeng in Tanzhou was the son of the Yao family of Fuzhou. While traveling, he arrived at Dazhong and relied upon Chan Master Haiyin Long.

There he saw the elder master Dadao reading a sutra; when he reached the passage, "At the tip of a single hair, a lion appears, and from the tips of its ten billion hairs, they all appear simultaneously," the Master pointed and asked:
"How does a lion at the tip of a single hair manage to have ten billion hairs appear all at once?"
The myriad hairs on his head all appeared at once. Da said, "You have only just entered the monastery; how can you immediately concern yourself with such matters?

The Master was thus filled with doubt and subsequently resolved to take up the position of *jingtou* (cleaner). One night, while he was sweeping, Haiyin happened to be giving the evening instruction (*yecan*).

Upon arriving, he encountered the conclusion of the session. Throwing down his staff, [Haiyin] said: "If one realizes it, the tip of a hair swallows the vast ocean; only then does one know the Great."

Upon seeing a single speck of dust on the ground, the Master suddenly attained realization. He then traveled from Min to Mount Huanglong in Yuzhang, but his mental resonance did not accord with Siji (Dead Heart).
He subsequently studied under Lingyuan. Whenever he entered the inner chamber and emerged, he would invariably weep and reproach himself, saying, "I have seen this matter very clearly;
it is only that when facing the critical moment, I cannot bring it forth. What can be done about this? Lingyuan recognized [his sincerity].

The Master was diligent and earnest; he told him that one must achieve great penetration (*da che*) before attaining mastery. Not long after, [Zhaozhou] secretly observed a monk at the neighboring desk reading the *Extensive Record of Cao Dong*.
When it reached the passage where Yaoshan returns from gathering firewood and a monk asks, "Where have you come from?", Yaoshan replies, "I have come to gather firewood.
The monk points to the knife at Yaoshan’s waist and asks, "That thing making such a 'miao-peo-peo' sound—what is it? Yaoshan...

Drawing his sword, he made a gesture as if to strike. The Master suddenly smiled with delight; he seized a monk at the neighboring table, gave him a single slap, and stepped through the curtain, rushing out.
As he went, he spoke this verse spontaneously: "Piercing! Piercing! The great ocean dries up; empty space bursts asunder. In the four directions and eight points, all obstructions vanish;
the myriad phenomena of the universe are simultaneously revealed."
Chan Master Yingduan of Falun, Tanzhou (Dharma Heir of Huanglong Qing).
Chan Master Yingduan of Falun in Tanzhou was a native of the Xu family of Nanchang. He visited Chan Master Zhenjing Wen, but their spiritual resonance did not harmonize.
Upon arriving at Yunju, he encountered Lingyuan presiding as the seat-holder; as he inspired the assembly with vigor, the Master inquired into his essential meaning. However, because...

Miaoru was arrogant regarding his mastery of the various sutras. Lingyuan once severely rebuked him, whereupon the Master cited the pivotal dialogues of Mazu and Baizhang, as well as the essential tenets of the Avatamsaka Sutra, as evidence of his realization.
Lingyuan laughed and said, "While Mazu and Baizhang were certainly mistaken, the essential tenets of the Avatamsaka have no connection whatsoever with this matter.
The Master became indignant and wished to leave; he therefore requested leave to depart.
He then lifted the curtain. Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment, and sweat poured down his back. When Lingyuan saw this, he said, "This son now knows good from evil.
Mazu and Baizhang—Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra—nearly suffered because of you. Later, he opened the Dharma at Baizhang.
Chan Master Daozhen of Huanglong Mountain, Longxing Prefecture (Dharma heir of Letan Qing).
He was the son of the Zhao family of Jinling. In his youth, he relied upon Chan Master Jueyin Ying as a novice.
When Ying moved to Puzhao Temple in Si, it happened that the Imperial Consort Shu was selecting young novices for ordination.

After the Master had received full ordination for some time, he took leave to visit Chan Master Danxia Chun. One day, while discussing the fundamental tenets of the Dongshan school, the Master presented a verse, saying:
"White clouds deeply shroud the ancient, cold crag; Strange herbs and numinous flowers are carried by the wondrous phoenix.
At midnight, the sun rises; it is now midday. Riding a cow with its back turned, one puts on boots and a robe. Danxia esteemed him highly. The Master considered this for himself...

Aiai abandoned his reliance on Cao Tang; upon seeing him once, they were in perfect accord. Every day he would take the Tripitaka to read. One night, hearing the drum for the evening *zana*, he stepped out from the sutra hall.
Looking up, he saw the moon and attained great enlightenment. He hurried at once to the abbot’s quarters; as Cao Tang saw him from afar, he recognized it.
He immediately granted his seal of approval.
As for Chan Master Fayi of Wannian on Mount Tai (a successor of Litan Qing):
Chan Master Xuechao Fayi of Wannian, Taizhou. The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Xiangyang, Lord Li, respectfully exhorted him.

He was the great-great-grandson of [the aforementioned]. His family had resided for generations in Xiangfu County, Kaifeng. His mother dreamed that an elderly monk arrived before she gave birth to him.
At the age of seventeen, he sat for the examination at the Imperial Academy (Shangxiang). When his paternal uncle, who held office in Huainan, sought to appoint him to an official post, he refused.

Intending to renounce his home, he went to serve the Chan Master Cijue Ze of Changlu; however, his grandfather would not permit it. His mother said, "This boy must surely have been a śramaṇa in a previous life; I pray you do not deprive him of this."
Such was his resolve. Before long, Cijue passed away. In the first year of the Daguan era, he visited Chan Master Tongzhao Yuan of Lingyan to shave his head and receive full ordination.

He remained under Yuan’s guidance for ten years, yet he felt bewildered and unable to penetrate the teachings. He then went to pay respects to Yuanwu at Jiangshan, who remarked, "This is a vessel of the Dharma.
When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to move to Tianning Monastery in the capital, the Master attended him on his travels. This was toward the end of the Jingkang era.
He visited Cudao at Shushan; upon a single word being exchanged, the Great Dharma was suddenly clarified.
Regarding Chan Master Putong Pujiao of Tiantong in Qingyuan Prefecture (a dharma heir of Ledu Tan Qian):
he was the son of the Bi family from Wanling in the prefecture. He went to Nanping to listen to the teachings.

In the Tiantai school, because a lay patron was performing a *sāṃmā* (confession), someone asked him: "The transgressions you are confessing—do you confess them for yourself, or do you confess them for another?

If you are confessing your own transgressions, from where does the nature of the transgression arise? If you are confessing the transgressions of another, that other person's transgression is not yours; how can you confess it?
The Master was unable to respond, so he changed his robes, traveled to various regions, and went to Lestam. As soon as his feet touched the ground...

As he entered the gate, Leduim scolded him. As the Master was about to ask a question, Leduim simply took up his staff and drove him away. One day, Leduim suddenly called for the Master; when he arrived in the abbot’s quarters, Leduim said, "I have an ancient public case that I wish to discuss with you. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, Leduim struck him. The Master then bowed. Leduim said, "What is this? The Master replied, "The staff is still in your hand. Leduim said, "You have attained it. The Master then departed. Later, he related this to Yangshan, who said, "This is the 'Staff' (zhuan) case. The Master asked, "What is the 'Staff' case? Yangshan said, "It is like a person holding a staff who says, 'I am not a staff-bearer. If you say, 'I am a staff-bearer,' you will be struck by the staff. If you say, 'I am not a staff-bearer,' you will also be struck by the staff. The Master said, "If one does not speak at all, will one avoid being struck? Chan Master Zongxian of Xinsiang Monastery (a dharma successor of Zhaojue Baofa), the Chan Master Zhengjue of Xinsiang Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture.
He was a native of the Wang family of Tongchuan. In his youth, he served as a jinshi scholar.

There was a man named Chengsheng. Once, while playing by scooping up mountain stream water during the day, he thought of it at night; consequently, he saw the water coolly filling his room. He wished to draw some, but could not;
yet the dusty world of sensory objects became empty of itself. He exclaimed, "The net of worldly existence has been torn asunder! He then went to rely upon Zhaojue.
Having attained the full perfection of the precepts, he subsequently joined the assembly for consultation and study.

One day, Zhaojue asked the Master, "Standing atop the highest peak, walking on the bottom of the deepest sea—how do you understand this? The Master attained sudden enlightenment at these words and said, "My heels have been nailed down.
Zhaojue picked up his whisk and asked, "And what about this? The Master gave a smile.

"I do not ask about Zhaozhou’s bridge," [Wuzu said], "but what is the pivot? Wuzu replied, "You stay outside the gate for now. The Master stepped forward.
With one step, he withdrew. The Fifth Patriarch said, "For so long you have been eating this tea and rice;
surely there is someone who knows its flavor. The next day, [the Master] entered the room. The Fifth Patriarch said, "Are you the monk who questioned me yesterday?
I certainly know the extent of your realization, yet you have not yet passed the 'White Cloud Barrier'. The Master said, "I take my leave," and departed. At that time, it was Yuanwu.
He served as an attendant. His teacher tested him with the meaning of the "White Cloud Barrier" (Baiyun guan). Yuanwu said, "You must simply realize it directly.
The Master smiled and said, "It is not that I do not understand; it is simply that I have not yet become familiar with this old fellow.
I wish to deliberate with him once more. The next day, Wuzu went to Shucheng; the Master and Yuanwu followed after him, meeting him there at Xing'an.

Chan Master Jicheng of Jingyin (Dharma heir of Zhihai Ping):
Chan Master Pan’an Jicheng of Jingyin in Dongjing was a native of the Liu family of Yichun in Yuan.

The Master, together with Yuanwu Keqin, Fazhen, Cishou, and ten other great Dharma masters—totaling one thousand monks from both the Chan and Lecture traditions—attended the banquet hosted by the Grand Marshal, Lord Chen Liang.
At the Retinue Office (Bifufu), Emperor Huizong went there in private to observe the rites. The Grand Preceptor, Duke of Lu, was also present.
There was one Shan Huiyan, who was a "tiger among scholars" regarding the teachings of the Xianshou school. Addressing the assembly, he questioned the various Chan masters, saying:
"Our Buddha established his teachings ranging from the Small Vehicle up to the Perfect and Sudden. He swept away both emptiness and existence to uniquely realize the True and Constant. Only then..."
Only when adorned with the ten thousand virtues is one truly called a Buddha. One often hears it said that a single shout of the Chan school can transform an ordinary person into a sage;
this seems to contradict the various sutras and treatises. Now, if a single shout can enter our school, then the five teachings are considered the correct exposition;
if it cannot enter, they are considered false expositions. When the various Chan masters looked toward their teacher, the teacher said: "As the Dharma Master has stated..."
Question: "The three great Chan masters are insufficient to provide a worthy response. The junior elder of Jingyin can cause the Dharma Master to be free from delusion.

There is indeed a meaning [to this]. The Initial Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of emptiness (*śūnyatā*). The Final Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of neither being nor non-empty.
The Sudden Teaching of the Mahāyāna is the meaning of being-emptiness and emptiness-being simultaneously.
The Perfect Teaching of the One Vehicle is the meaning of not being yet being, and not empty yet empty (or, as some say: empty yet not being, being yet not empty). It is as I...
A single shout. It is not only able to enter the five teachings; it can even enter the fields of craftsmanship, the arts, and all the various schools of thought.
The Master let out a thunderous shout and asked Shan, "Did you hear that? Shan replied, "I heard it.
The Master said, "Since you heard this one shout, you are able to enter the Small Vehicle teaching. A short while later, he asked Shan again, "Did you hear it? Shan replied, "No."
[The disciple] said, "I did not hear it. The Master said, "Since you did not hear the single shout just now, you are unable to enter the Initial Teaching (Śakyadeśanā).
Then he looked at Shanhui and said: 'When I first gave the shout, you said there was a shout; when the sound had long since faded, you said there was no shout.

If there is no shout, then it must have truly existed originally; if there is a shout, then it must truly not exist now. To be neither existent nor non-existent is how one can enter the Final Teaching (Niṣṭhādeśanā). I... [text fragment].

When there is one shout, it is not that existence exists because of a cause and non-existence does not; thus, when there is one shout, existence and non-existence are one. When there is no shout, it is not that non-existence exists because of a cause and existence does not;
thus, non-existence is immediately existence and immediately non-existence. To be able to enter the Sudden Teaching, you must know this one shout of mine.

He did not utter a single shout; its function transcends both existence and non-existence. When conceptual understanding is forgotten, when the Way seems to exist, not even a speck of dust stands forth;

when the Way seems to be absent, it pervades the void horizontally. This very one shout enters into hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts, and hundreds of thousands of millions of shouts enter into this one shout.
Therefore, he was able to enter the Perfect Teaching (Yuanjiao). Shan then rose and bowed twice to the Master.
He further said: "It is not only the case with a single shout.

Even down to a single word or a single silence, a single movement or a single stillness—from antiquity to the present, throughout the ten directions of empty space, amidst the myriad phenomena of the forest-like array, the beings of the six realms and four modes of birth, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, all the sages and worthies, the eighty-four thousand Dharma gates, the hundreds of thousands of samādhis, and the immeasurable subtle meanings that accord with principle and accord with reality..."
The capacity (jī) is one body with heaven, earth, and the myriad things; this is called the *dharmakāya*. The three realms are mind-only; the myriad dharmas are consciousness-only.
The four seasons and eight nodes of time are of one essence with yin and yang; this is called the *dharmatā*. Therefore, the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* says:
"The *dharmatā* pervades all places. Whether with form or without form, in a single sound or a single color, it is entirely contained within a single speck of dust, encompassing the four [realms]."
The principles of meaning and reality are boundless and all-pervasive; they are without remainder, neither mixed nor disparate, yet neither blended into one.

Later, when he went to visit again, the Master further instructed him to see Yuanwu. The Master arrived at Tianning Monastery, and one day he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall.

Suppose someone were to ask me, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? I would say: "The moon in the sky is reflected in the well."
He simply said to him: "The fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow a subtle coolness.
At these words, the Master’s past and future suddenly severed. Although the appearance of movement did not arise, he remained sitting in a state of pure nakedness.
Yuanwu said to him, "It was no easy matter for you to reach this stage. It is a pity that you have died and cannot yet live again; you do not yet doubt."
Words and phrases are a great illness. It is said that one must not see the Way; one must let go over a precipice and personally accept it.
Only after death can one be revived; this cannot be faked before the Sovereign. You must believe that such a principle exists.

Consequently, he was appointed to reside in the Zhemu Hall (the place where court officials rest) as a non-administrative attendant, entering the room for private instruction daily with the Master. Whenever Yuanwu would raise [a koan], there was...
"Phrases and non-phrases are like a vine leaning against a tree. When asked this, as soon as the Master opened his mouth, Yuanwu said, "Not so, not so.
After half a year had passed, the Master then asked Yuanwu, "I heard that when you were at Wuzu’s place, you once asked about this same matter.
I wonder what Wuzu said. Yuanwu smiled but did not answer. The Master said, "At that time, Master..."
"One must question before the assembly; what harm is there in speaking as we do now? Being at his wit's end, Yuanwu said to him, "I shall ask:
'The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning are like a vine leaning against a tree. What is the intent of this? Wuzu replied, "It cannot be traced, nor can it be painted.
Yuanwu asked again, "When the tree falls and the vine withers, what then? Wuzu replied, "He has come along with us."
The Master immediately felt relieved and said, "I understand. Yuanwu then cited several *nidānas* (precedents) to interrogate him; the Master responded without hesitation.
Yuanwu said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you," and he subsequently composed the *Record of the True Lineage of Linji* and entrusted it to him, appointing him as head of the secretarial office.
Before long, he was ordered to share the teaching seat. In the meditation hall, he wielded a bamboo cane to test his students. [End of] the Monastery Record.

Lin Haoran esteemed him deeply, and his fame resounded throughout the capital. The Right Chancellor, Lord Lü Shuntu, submitted a memorial requesting that he be granted the purple robe and the title "Buddha Sun" (Furi).
During the Xixia rebellion, the chieftain intended to take several dozen Chan monks; the Master was among those selected, yet he managed to escape.
He then proceeded to Huqiu on Mount Wu to spend the summer retreat, where he studied the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* up to the point where the Bodhisattva ascends to the seventh stage.

He realized the *anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti* (the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena). He thoroughly understood the circumstances regarding the alms bowl that Yaśodharā (Yangjue Moluo) carried when she went to the house of a woman in childbirth—the very matters he had previously inquired about with Zantang.
When Yuanwu was summoned to reside at Yunju, the Master went there to pay his respects;

upon arriving at the mountain, the following day Yuanwu immediately requested him to serve as the First Seat (*zhuzuo*). At that time, the assembly contained many "dragons and elephants" (eminent masters), for Yuanwu had long left the position of the First Seat vacant, waiting [for such a successor].

When the Master arrived, he harbored a sense of resentment. When it came time for him to hold the whisk at the winter solstice, Chan Master Zhaojue Yuan stepped forward from the assembly and asked, "What is it like when a sword is suspended between the eyebrows?
The Master replied, "Blood splatters against the Brahma Heaven.

Yuan, while still in his seat, gestured with his hand and said, "Stop, stop! That question was excellent, and that answer is even more extraordinary. Thereupon, Yuan returned to the assembly. [From] Conglin.

Lin’s perspective was thus transformed. Whenever the Master entered the room for private instruction, Yuanwu would often come to listen to his discourse. One day, after the session had ended, Lin went up to the abbot’s quarters. Yuanwu said, "Suppose there were a Zen practitioner who could match me; how would you deal with him? The Master replied, "How fortunate I would be! It is just as东坡 (Sū Dongpo) said: 'To serve as an executioner. Yuanwu said, "That is not so. The Master said, "I am simply saying that if such a person were to appear, I would treat them exactly as I do myself. Yuanwu then said, "If you can handle yourself this way, then you will be able to handle others. The Master bowed and withdrew. Yuanwu remarked, "This fellow has finally begun to understand. Later, when the Master was about to leave, Yuanwu asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "To the place where there is no mountain. Yuanwu said, "Even if you reach the place where there is no mountain, you must still carry your staff. The Master said, "I have already carried my staff all along. Yuanwu said, "If you can speak like this, you may go. The Master bowed and departed. Yuanwu called out to him from behind the door, "Wait! The Master turned his head. Yuanwu said, "The staff is still here. The Master replied, "It has been here since I arrived. Yuanwu said, "What is it that you have been carrying? The Master remained silent. Yuanwu said, "You have finally understood. The Master bowed and left. Yuanwu sighed and said, "This fellow is truly extraordinary. He then composed a verse for him: "Entering the room, he speaks with ease; Leaving the room, he carries his staff. A single phrase, like a dragon leaping from the deep; A single step, like a tiger pouncing on its prey. He is truly a man of great capacity; He is truly a man of great potential. If he does not meet a true master, He will surely become a great teacher. Later, when the Master was traveling through Jiangxi, he stayed at the monastery of 大愚 (Dayu). Dayu asked, "Where did you come from? The Master replied, "From the place where there is no mountain. Dayu said, "Why didn't you say so before? The Master said, "Because I was afraid you would strike me. Dayu said, "If you had said so before, I would have struck you. The Master said, "Even if you had struck me, I would still have said so. He then composed a verse for him: "The staff is long, the robe is wide; The path is straight, the destination clear. If you wish to know the source of the Way, Look at the staff in his hand. By chance, he encountered a stout man who was being flayed. Yuanwu laughed heartily and said, "You have actually entered my room and squeezed me right up against the wall!
Yuanwu asked again, "When Bodhidharma came from the West, what did he transmit? The Master replied, "One must not take everything as the view of a wild fox spirit.
Yuanwu asked again, "Seizing the tiger’s head and gathering the tiger’s tail—what is the foremost [principle]?"
The phrase clarifies the fundamental purpose. "What is the first phrase? The Master said, "This is the second phrase.
Yuanwu often remarked, "Lately, everywhere has become a mere trap. Under the Fifth Patriarch, there were only myself, Fojian, and Foyan."
These three men formed a society to practice Zen; even now, their flaws have leaked out.
Under the lineage of Fojian, there is a certain type who act like dogs barking or magpies chirping, merely making a laughingstock of others.

Under the lineage of Foyan, there is another type who stare at lanterns and pillars, pointing east and painting west as if they were seeing ghosts with their own eyes. Here, in my place, there are neither of these two maladies.
The Master said, "The spark struck from flint, the flash of lightning—this has led countless people to dabble in their own karmic consciousness.
To understand it the very moment it is raised—is this not the great den of the Buddha-dharma? Yuanwu involuntarily stuck out his tongue and said, "Do not concern yourself with that."

"I shall only accept you when you have attained realization through personal verification. If you do not attain realization, I will by no means let you pass. The Master said, "I can indeed grant it upon attainment.
However, I fear that you might simply transmit it in this manner—claiming to have awakened the moment a kōan is raised, stubbornly insisting on 'the spark struck from flint' or 'a flash of lightning.
Such a state of deluded consciousness (*karmic ignorance*) will never come to an end. Yuanwu deeply approved of this. Yuanwu returned.
In Shu, the Master established a hermitage at the ancient site of Yunmen on the slopes behind Mount Yungju to reside there. Students gathered like clouds.
After some time, he entered Min Province and built a thatched hut at Yangyu in Changle. Thirteen people followed him and attained the Dharma.
He was subsequently moved to Yunmen Hermitage at Xiaoxi. In response to the summons from Chancellor Zhang Wei-gong Xu to Mount Jiangshan, he ascended the hall and said:
"The earth-bull beneath the water chews raw iron; Kubjita bites his own tongue. The Sea God, enraged, brandishes a coral whip;
Mount Sumeru and King Dīpa suffer beyond measure. In the meditation hall, he questioned a monk: "The other day, I had one..."
[The Master] asked, "You were here yesterday; you answered me then. Why are you dozing off now? The monk said, "Just so, just so.
The Master said, "What did you say? The monk said, "Not so, not so. The Master struck him twice with his staff, saying, "One blow for saying 'just so,' and one blow for saying 'not so.
[Case 10] He raised his bamboo whisk and asked a monk: *Note: The circle (○) indicates a break in the text where the original narrative or commentary ends.*
[The Master] said: "If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of contact; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of turning away.
You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. Speak quickly! Speak quickly! The monk said: "Please, Master, set down the bamboo stick, and then I will speak to you."
The Master set down his bamboo staff. The monk brushed out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "Attendant, recognize this monk! He then raised the same question for another monk.
The monk replied, "Are you afraid the turtle will escape from the jar? The Master descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and said, "Whose words were those?
Speak quickly! The monk said, "Truly, I dare not deceive the Master; these were the words of Zen Master Zhuan’an."
"Teach me how to speak thus," [the disciple] said. The Master struck him several times with his staff and said, "Present this clearly to all quarters.
The Master, being advanced in years, requested to retire. He withdrew to reside at the Bright Moon Hall (Mingyue Tang). Soon thereafter, he manifested a slight illness.

When his disciples came to inquire after his health, the Master urged them to propagate the Way. He then said slowly, "I shall depart tomorrow. At the fifth watch, he personally wrote his final testament and also composed a letter of farewell to the Purple [Robe].
When the layman Yan and his attendant monk Liaoxian requested a verse, he wrote it out in large characters, saying: "Life is just like this;
death is just like this. Whether there is a verse or no verse—what a great fuss! He then threw down his brush and passed away peacefully.
Chan Master Shàolóng of Hǔqiū (Dharma heir of Zhāojié Qín).
Chan Master Shàolóng of Hǔqiū in Píngjiāng Prefecture was a native of Hánshān in Hézhōu. He visited Chan Master Xìn of Chánglú and grasped its general principles.
When someone arrived bringing the recorded sayings of Yuánwù, the Master read them and sighed, saying: "I imagine the vinegar has turned sour."
Although this liquid has not yet moistened my intestines or bathed my stomach, it has nonetheless brought me a sense of joy and relief; my only regret is that I have not yet heard his voice.
He then proceeded from Baofeng to rely upon Zantang, stayed as a guest at Huanglong, and sought instruction from Chan Master Sishin.

Next, he visited Yuanwu. One day, while entering the inner quarters for private instruction, Yuanwu asked him: "When seeing the very act of seeing, that seeing is not [the ordinary] seeing. Seeing is already detached from seeing. Seeing...
[The master] could not reach it. [Wuzu] raised his fist and asked, "Do you see? The Master said, "I see. Wuzu said, "Placing a head on top of a head.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization. Wuzu rebuked him, saying, "What have you seen? The Master replied, "Dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through.
Wuzu approved of him and soon appointed him to oversee the library. Someone asked Wuzu, "Master Long is gentle..."
"If it is as easy as this, what can one possibly achieve? Yuanwu said, "It is merely a 'dozing tiger.
Chan Master Fozhi Duanyu of Mount Yuyang in Qingyuan Prefecture (a dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin). He was a descendant of the King of Wuyue. At eighteen...
Having received the full ordination, he went to rely upon the Chan Master Yizhao of Jingci. Not long after, he happened to hear a monk strike a pillar and say, "Why do you not speak of Chan?
At that moment, the Master suddenly attained a slight awakening. He then went to visit Dayuan of Longmen, Fayan of Ganlu, and Huixiang of Letan.
All were esteemed for their exceptional brilliance and insight. Later, he met Yuanwu at Zhongfu Mountain.

One day, Yuanwu asked, "Who knew that the Eye of the True Dharma would be extinguished upon this blind donkey? Is it extinguished right now, or not? The Master replied, "I ask the Master to shut his mouth.
Yuanwu said, "This is still within the realm of ordinary sentiment. As the Master was about to respond, Yuanwu struck him.
Through this, the Master suddenly cast off all that obstructed him.
