Chan Master Jingyuan of Huguo (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin):
Chan Master Jingyuan of Ciyun at Huguo Temple in Taizhou was a native of the Zhang family of Nanxi in Yongjia. He studied the teachings of the Tiantai school.
For three years, he went to visit Yuanwu at Zhongfu. There, upon hearing a monk reciting the words from Sishin’s *xiaocan* (small public discourse):
"Since one is deluded, one must attain awakening; since one has awakened, one must recognize delusion within awakening and awakening within delusion.

When both delusion and awakening are forgotten, one establishes all dharmas from the place where there is neither delusion nor awakening," the Master was struck with doubt. He immediately rushed to the Buddha hall and, with his hands, pressed against...
When the door-panels were opened, he attained a sudden and vast enlightenment. Subsequently serving as an attendant, his wit and eloquence emerged with extraordinary brilliance.
Yuanwu called him the "stubborn attendant Yuan.
This was Chan Master Nanfeng Yunbian (a dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin).
Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng in Pingjiang Prefecture was a native of that region. He received the full precepts under Zhang of Ruipeng in Min.

Upon returning home, he visited Qionglong Yuan and suddenly attained realization; he then presented his insights to him. Yuan said, "Although you have gained entry, you have not yet reached the ultimate point.

You must truly spur yourself forward. Thereupon, he took his leave and visited various seats of learning. Later, he attended on Yuanwu, and just as he entered the inner quarters—*cái*... [text breaks off]
He followed him to the door. Yuanwu said, "Look beneath your feet. The Master struck a pillar once.
Yuanwu said, "Why do you not speak a single word that hits the mark? The Master said, "If the teacher shakes his head, the disciple wags his tail.
Yuanwu said, "Try wagging your tail for me. The Master performed a somersault and left. Yuanwu laughed heartily. From this, he became widely known.
Chan Master Huiyuan of Lingyin (Dharma Heir of Zhaojue Qin).
Chan Master Fohai Huiyuan of Lingyin, Lin’an Prefecture. A native of the Peng family of Meishan.
At the age of thirteen, he took the tonsure under Zongbian of Yaoshi Monastery. He went to Daci to study the scriptures, then left to rely upon Chan Master Weiming of Lingyan.
He had a realization. When Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue, the Master went to him. Hearing Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pǔshuō*), Yuanwu raised the kōan concerning Layman Pang’s question to Mazu:
“Not being a companion to the myriad dharmas. At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment; he collapsed among the assembly.
As the assembly helped him up, the Master said, “I have awakened from my dream. Later, during the night *xiao-cān* (small private session), the Master stepped forward and asked, “Naked and bare...”
"Empty; there is not a single thing. I am destitute, possessing not a single coin. My doors are broken and my family is ruined. I beg the Master for relief.
Yuanwu said, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent house.
Yuanwu said, "If the pivot of action does not leave its station, one falls into a sea of poison. As soon as Yuanwu spoke these words, the Master let out a shout. Yuanwu struck him with his staff.
The Chan master said, "Have you eaten the staff yet? The Master shouted again. Yuanwu shouted twice in succession. The Master then bowed.
From that time on, his spiritual acuity emerged with sharp brilliance, meeting no obstruction. One day, as the drum was beaten for the formal assembly, the Master sat hidden within the curtains.
An attendant monk searched for him; the Master suddenly pulled back the curtain and said, "Right here! Why [do you not see me]?"
[The monk] did not see him. The assembly had no response.
Chan Master Anmin of Huazang [Temple] (dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin):
Chan Master Anmin Miyin of Huazang [Temple] in Jiankang Prefecture was the son of the Zhu family of Jiading Prefecture. Initially, he lectured on the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra*.

Yan resided in Chengdu and became a center where those seeking study in the Dharma (yixue) flocked. At that time, Yuanwu was residing at Zhaojue Temple. The Master [Yan] and Chan Master Sheng were friends; consequently, he went to visit him.
There, he heard Yuanwu’s *xiaocan* (informal sermon), in which he cited the karmic occasion (*yinyuan*) of the National Teacher calling his attendant three times.

Zhaozhou commented on it, saying: "It is like a person writing characters in the dark; though the characters themselves do not take shape, the traces of their brilliance are already manifest. "Where," [Yuanwu asked,] "is..."

When the patterns of his literary brilliance had already become manifest, the Master harbored doubts about him. He summoned him into his room. Yuanwu asked, "Seat-Master, what sutra do you lecture on?
The Master replied, "The Śūraṅgama Sūtra. Yuanwu said, "In the Śūraṅgama, there are the 'seven locations where the mind is sought' and the 'eight returns that distinguish seeing.
Ultimately, where does the mind reside? The Master presented many of his scholarly interpretations, but Yuanwu rejected them all. The Master then requested further instruction.

Yuanwu instructed that in all circumstances one should form the realization that "the patterns are already manifest. Once, when a monk requested instruction on the *Ten Mysterious Gates*, Yuanwu raised the question:
"What is the appearance of the mind-seal you hold? Yuanwu spoke with a stern voice, saying, "The patterns are already manifest.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained a realization; he then sought formal certification. Yuanwu applied the hammer and tongs of his true style, yet the Master was at a loss. One day...
Baizhang said to Yuanwu, "Master, do not bring up this story; wait until I have spoken of it. Yuanwu consented.

Baizhang said, "When you habitually brandish the mallet or raise the whisk, is that not what the sutras say: 'All phenomena in all worlds, every mark that exists, are all the wondrously luminous true mind of bodhi'?
Yuanwu laughed and said, "So, you have been making your living right here all along! Baizhang [replied].
He also said, "When one shouts 'Down! and strikes the meditation seat, is this not 'returning the hearing to hear the self-nature,' whereby that nature accomplishes the Unsurpassed Way?
Yuanwu said, "Have you not seen it stated in the sutras: 'The wondrous nature is perfectly luminous, transcending all names and marks'? At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened.
When Yuanwu left Sichuan to reside at Jia Shan, the Master ceased his lectures and accompanied him as an attendant. Yuanwu served the assembly...
During a night session, the Master brought up the kōan concerning the ancient sail not yet hoisted. Having heard it but not yet grasping its meaning, the Master sought a definitive resolution.
Yuanwu said, "Ask me. The Master repeated the previous story. Yuanwu said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard.

At that moment, the Master attained clear penetration and said to Yuanwu, "The ancients said, 'It is like a single drop cast into a vast ravine. Little did they know that the great ocean could be cast into a single drop."
*Dī*. Yuanwu laughed and said, "What can one do about this fellow? Shortly thereafter, he ordered him to share the seat [of the abbot].
Later, the Master visited Fojian at Jiangshan. Fojian asked, "Foguo had a phrase that he never spoke of indiscriminately to others;
has he ever spoken it to you? The Master replied, "Shut that dog's mouth! Fojian raised his voice and said, "That is not the principle. The Master—
[The Master] said, "No one has snatched away your salt and tea bag; what would you call it? Fojian said, "If Foguo would not explain it for you, I shall explain it for you.
The Master said, "When the Master is in doubt, retire from the monastery and go elsewhere to study.
Fojian laughed loudly.
Chan Master Dao-yuan of Zhaojue (Dharma heir of Chan Master Qin of Zhaojue).
Chan Master Dao-yuan of Che’an at Zhaojue in Chengdu Prefecture was a native of the Deng family of Mianzhou.

In his youth, he received full ordination at Jiangji Temple. He traveled east to visit Chan Master Daobiao of Dabie, whereupon, while contemplating the words "Vast emptiness—no sage," he suddenly [attained awakening].
Er Shi laughed and said, "Damo has been here all along. Daoyu praised him and sent him to study under Fojian and Foyan, where he received their recognition.
He then followed Yuanwu at Jingshan and reported his insights to him, but Yuanwu did not approve.

When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, the Master followed him there; although he attained a degree of conviction, he felt that a certain obstruction remained in his chest that had not yet been removed.
This was a point of doubt for him. Later, when Yuanwu asked the assembly of practitioners, "When birth and death arrive, what then?
a monk replied, "The incense altar laughs at the Master. Yuanwu then asked the Master, "What about you? The Master said, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated.

Yuanwu said, "If someone were to ask you this, how would you respond? As the Master was about to answer, Yuanwu rebuked him, saying, "The grass bandit is utterly defeated! At that, the Master immediately—
Upon his complete realization, Yuanwu struck him with his fist. The Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Yuanwu asked, "What did you see that makes you act like this?
The Master replied, "The poisonous fist has not yet been repaid; I shall never forget it for eternal kalpas."
Chan Master Zhongren of Zhongtianzhu in Lin’an (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin).

Chan Master Zhongren of the Huantang Hall at Zhongtianzhu in Lin’an Prefecture was a native of Luoyang. He came to the Tripitaka Translation Institute and thoroughly investigated the sutras and śāstras;
however, he remained particularly unconvinced by the Gate of the Patriarchal School (*Zongmen*). At that time, Yuanwu resided at Tianning Monastery. Ling...

He went to pay his respects in the morning. At that time, Yuanwu was leading the assembly into the inner room for private instruction. Upon seeing him, the Master felt deep reverence and, with a surge of resolve, stepped forward.

Yuanwu said, "To explain the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to depart from a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!

As the Master prepared to respond, Yuanwu struck him across the mouth with his staff, causing him to lose a tooth. Thereupon, he attained great enlightenment. [Later,] Yuanwu ascended the hall and said:
He raised the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature and said: "A beauty of sixteen years embroiders slowly; beneath the purple *zhijing* flowers, the yellow oriole warbles.
How pitiable, this boundless spring melancholy—all lies within that moment of silence when the needle is set aside.

On the eighth day of the fourth month in the Jiamu year of the Chunxi era, Emperor Xiaozong summoned him to the palace, granted him a seat, and requested a Dharma discourse. The Emperor raised the koan of "not giving..."
All phenomena are the conditions for companionship; let us take them up and bring them forth. Having finished taking them up, the Master spoke in verse:
"Pressing a scale-weight to extract oil—enough with idle talk and long-winded speech. With a hundred thousand strings of cash girded at the waist, one rides a crane up to Yangzhou."
Chan Master Yuanjue of Xiang’er (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Qinqin):
Chan Master Yuanjue of Mount Xiang’er in Meizhou was the son of the Yuan clan of that commandery. He received ordination after passing the scriptural examinations; his original name was Yuanjue.

When the Prefectural Governor filled out the temple registration document, he mistakenly wrote "Yuan" instead of "Yuan. Suspecting that the Master was dissatisfied with this, the Governor jokingly said to him: "One..."
"Is it appropriate to give me a name? The Master smiled and said, "Even one character is too many. The Prefect was struck by this as extraordinary.

Having received full ordination, he left Sichuan and visited various venerable elders who possessed the Way. Later, he went to Daguang Moshan and relied upon Foxing. After a short while, he entered the inner quarters to present his insights.
Foxing said, "You are far too distant from it. Nevertheless, knowing him to be a vessel for the Dharma, he appointed him as an attendant to manage the reception of guests.
Whenever Shishuang attended upon Foxing, Foxing would invariably cite the four characters of the *Lotus Sūtra*—*kai-shi-wu-ru* (open, show, awaken, enter)—and command him to provide a response.
He further said, "Only when I nod my head vertically shall you be correct. Once, due to negligence in his duties, he was dismissed. [End of] Excerpt.
Having no fixed abode, he stayed in the home of a layman. One day, while reciting the *Lotus Sūtra*, he reached the passage:
"Furthermore, one does not know what is fire and what is the house. At that moment, he attained a sudden awakening. Upon returning home after his ordination, Yuanwu nodded his head in approval.
When Yuanwu later received the imperial decree to reside at Yunju, the Master went there and reported his realization to him. Yuanwu rebuked him, saying: "The original..."
"This is a pure ground. Why are you defecating here? At these words, the Master’s doubts were suddenly resolved.
As for Chan Master Zu’jue of Huayan at Zhongyan in Meizhou (the dharma heir of Chan Master Zhaojue Qin):
he was the son of the Yang family of Jiazhou. From his youth, he was intelligent and well-versed in the classics and histories.

He could recite from memory upon merely glancing at a text. He composed writings to refute the teachings of Śākyamuni, but when a terrifying vision suddenly appeared before him, he repented and left the household life.

He relied upon the Chan Master Huiri Neng; not long after, an abscess broke out on his knee, which no physician could cure for five years. Consequently, he began writing the *Huayan jiaoli lun* (Treatise on the Combined Meanings of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra).
At the end of the night, he had a wondrous dream. At dawn, he immediately cast aside his staff and began walking. One day, while reciting to the "Chapter on Manifesting Signs," he came to the verse:
"The Buddha-body has no birth, yet it can manifest birth; the nature of phenomena is like space, and all Buddhas dwell therein. Without dwelling and without departing, the Buddha is seen everywhere.
He then attained realization of the essential tenets of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*. Subsequently, he was enrolled in the monastic registers by the local administration.
The Military Commander invited the Master to lecture at the Qianbu Hall. His eloquence was grand and expansive, earning the admiration and respect of all present.

At that time, Chan Master Jing of Nantang happened to visit him and said to the Master, "Observing your lectures, you are peerless in the southwest; it is only a pity that you have not yet transcended the marks of words and letters.
If you were to seek the Way beyond the secular world, you would be the Zhi Zhikai (Jingang) of today. The Master joyfully ceased his lectures and [proceeded] south.
He traveled and relied upon Yuanwu at Zhongfu. One day, he entered the inner chamber for instruction. Yuanwu raised the following passage:

"When there are words, one occupies the tiger's head and gathers the tiger's tail; beneath the first phrase, the fundamental principle is clarified. When there are no words, the sharp point of the pivot is laid bare."
"It is like a lightning whisk. How do you understand this? The Master was unable to respond. He spent day and night in investigation until he suddenly attained realization.
He presented a verse to Yuanwu, which read: "My home is atop a solitary peak; For many years the door has been half-closed. I lament that my body is already old;
My livelihood is entrusted to my descendants. Upon seeing this, Yuanwu gave his approval. The next day, [the Master] entered the room for private instruction. Yuanwu asked again: "Yesterday..."
"What is this public case about? When the Master was about to respond, Yuanwu gave a shout and said, "The Buddha-dharma is not a matter of this kind.

The Master remained for another five years, becoming even more confused and distressed. Later, while at Qixian on Mount Lu, he read Chan Master Fushan Yuan’s *Treatise on Eliminating Attachments*, which states:
"If one says that there is intimacy or distance in awakening, how could there be [a distinction] within a sandalwood grove?"... yet [there is].
While tending to stinking weeds, he attained sudden and profound enlightenment. He composed a verse and sent it to Yuanwu, saying:

"Leaving the forest, I have returned to the weeds; The vast net of Heaven cannot be escaped. Who would believe that karmic conditions offer no refuge? I return home, unafraid of loud voices. Yuanwu was greatly pleased.
Holding it up for the assembly, he said, "Jue has penetrated the depths of the Avatamsaka Sutra."
Chan Master Mingyin Tanwan (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin).
Chan Master Mingyin Tanwan of Mount Xi in Pingjiang Prefecture was the son of the Huang family of Wenzhou. He traveled extensively, visiting various monastic centers to seek instruction.
In the gengzi year of the Xuanhua era, he returned to Mount Zhong. At that time, the court had changed the title of monks to "virtuous practitioners" (deshi).

The Master, along with several like-minded companions, entered Tou-tuo Rock and lived there, subsisting on pine nuts. After some time, Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside on this mountain;

he personally visited the rock and ordered them to shave their hair and beards. When Yuanwu was subsequently appointed by imperial edict to Tianning Monastery in the capital, he traveled there together with the Master.
He was appointed to oversee the Fragrant Ocean (Gandhodadhi). Not long after, while striking the drum with his mallet, he suddenly attained profound realization of the Great Dharma.
Whenever anyone questioned him, he would invariably reply, "Do not concern yourself with it. Consequently, his peers all came to call him "Mo-li-hui" (Do Not Concern Yourself).
Dàozǔ Shòuzuō (Dharma heir of Zhāojié Qín).
He was the head seat at Zhāojié Monastery in Chéngdū Prefecture. Initially, upon meeting Yuánwù, he attained enlightenment under the phrase "this very mind is Buddha.
After some time, Yuánwù ordered him to share the teaching seat. One day, while leading the assembly into the inner quarters, there were about twenty people remaining.
The Master suddenly asked, "When birth and death arrive, how can one avoid them? The monk had no reply. The Master threw down his whisk and passed away abruptly.
The assembly was all struck with astonishment and immediately informed Yuanwu. When Yuanwu arrived, he called out, "Head Seat Zu! The Master opened his eyes and looked at him.
Yuanwu said, "Rouse your spirit and pass through the barrier. The Master nodded his head and finally passed away.
When he was about to pass into stillness, the Head Seat Zongzhen (a dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin) was there.
Head Seat Zongzhen of Yunju in Nankang Commandery was a native of Danqiu. He had relied upon Yuanwu at Yunju. One—
One day, while gazing up at the bell pavilion, he suddenly attained realization. When someone questioned him about it, the Head Seat (Shouzuo) responded with three verses.
The last of them read: "I have a single function; I reveal it directly to you. Like a thunderclap in the blue sky, like lightning rolling and stars racing.
Deshan’s staff and Linji’s shout are merely empty displays. What loss could there be for you regarding this untransmitted wondrous mystery? Yuanwu saw this and was greatly pleased.
The Layman Xu Fu, Minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Qín).
Xu Fu, styled Shichuan and known as the Layman Donghu, served his late father, the Dragon Diagram Official (Longtu), whenever they visited Fachang and Lingyuan.
Although they engaged in discourse with them all day long, when the official heard of it, he treated it with contempt. Later, when Fachang passed away, [Xu Fu] was laughing.

During their conversation, the Duke was struck by his extraordinary character and began to place deep faith in this Way. Later, while observing the mourning period for his father, he reflected that there was no way to repay his boundless debt of gratitude.
He therefore commanded Lingyuan to return to Xiaozhi Monastery to preach the Dharma. When Lingyuan ascended the seat and the questions and answers were concluded, he said: "O virtuous ones!"
"As for Longtu, in his daily life he read ten thousand scrolls of books; it was like water being passed from one vessel to another, not a single drop left behind.
But tell me, where did he usually keep them? Now that he has cast off consciousness, where will he place those ten thousand scrolls?
Upon hearing this, Lingyuan attained a sudden realization and said, "I have no regrets. Lingyuan.
The master descended from his seat. The monk asked, "Scholar, what did you just see that you speak in such a manner?
The official said, "If there were anything seen, I would have left the Master at a loss. Lingyuan said, "In that case, I am not your equal.

The official asked, "What kind of mental state is yours, Master? Lingyuan laughed heartily. At the beginning of the Jingkang era, he served as a Ministerial Secretary (Shangshu Waibang). Together with...
A fellow practitioner among the court officials hung his alms bowl at Ze-mu Hall in Tian-ning Temple and applied himself diligently to the study of Yuanwu.
Yuanwu, too, rejoiced in his transcendent insight. One day, he went to the secretary’s quarters and, pointing to Yuanwu’s portrait, said:
"This old fellow’s heels have not yet touched the ground," Yuanwu said, turning his face away. "How could the turtle ever have escaped from the jar?
The official replied, "I am glad to see the old fellow's heels touching the ground. Yuanwu said, "Do not slander him.
The official then withdrew.
The District Prince, Layman Zhao Lingjin (Dharma heir of Zhaojue Chengqin).
The District Prince Zhao Lingjin, whose courtesy name was Biaozhi and style name Chao Ran Layman, served as the governor of Nankang; his administration was successful and his affairs were simple.
He frequently associated with Zen monks. In his official residence, he occasionally established a "room for Maqie" (Vimalakīrti). It happened that Yuanwu was residing at Mount Oufu;

the Master was delighted and went to submit himself to his training. Yuanwu did not grant him any concessions. The Master pressed him earnestly, and Yuanwu said, "If you wish to attain realization in this matter, you must simply undergo a 'death' once.
The Master attained a profound understanding and once recorded it in a brief note, the gist of which is as follows:
He said, "My family is poor and has been robbed; who knows that everything has been stripped away? The house is empty and no one is there; several times thieves have come and beaten us.

When Yuanwu saw this, he instructed him to provide protection. In the winter of the Gengshen year of the Xiangxing era, the Duke, together with Grand Secretary Wang Zao, Councilor Li Bing, and Minister of Personnel Zeng Kai, went to Jingshan to visit Dahui. Upon hearing of their arrival, Dahui ordered the gong to be struck.
Dagu entered the room. The Master (Wang Jie) joyfully stepped forward with incense in his sleeve. Dahui asked, "How do you understand the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl?
The Master replied, "What kind of bowl are you looking for? and brushed his sleeves and went out.
Dahui rose and grabbed him, saying, "The ancients attained enlightenment right here; why do you not attain it? The Master was about to respond when Dahui—
[The Master] struck him and said, "What bowl are you seeking? The official replied, "Only by returning this old man [to his true nature] will it be so.
Li Mīxùn, the Layman (a dharma heir of Zhāojié Qín), was a Minister.
The Layman Lǐ Mīxùn was styled Pùxiàn. In his youth, he studied the classics; he could read five lines at once. At the age of ten...

8. He was recommended from his home district and passed the examinations in the capital. He soon rose through the ranks of high office until, at the age of twenty-eight, he became a Secretariat Drafter (Zhongshu Sheren).
He frequently entered the quarters of Yuanwu. One day, returning from the early court audience, he reached Tianjin Bridge when his horse leaped;

suddenly he attained realization, and sweat poured down his entire body. He went straight to Tianting Monastery, where he happened upon Yuanwu as he was leaving the gate. Seeing him from afar, Yuanwu called out, "Ji! (Reside!)
The official was pleased that the great matter had been concluded. The official said in a stern voice, "Monk, why are you blinding me with your eyes?
Yuanwu then gave a shout; the official also shouted. From then on, their exchanges were swift and sharp; in every dialogue with Yuanwu, he never yielded when the moment for action arrived.
Later, the official was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and requested a temple stipend. He returned to Lianjiang in Fujian, where he built a hermitage to enjoy himself. One day, suddenly—
Manifesting a slight ailment, he suddenly asked for hot water. Having finished bathing, he sat cross-legged and composed a verse, saying:
"In vain have they spoken of Mu and Hu from of old; today it is clearly revealed. Empty space crushes down Mount Sumeru—what need is there to speak of the path beyond?
He threw down his brush and passed away.
The Daoist Nun Jue’an of the Zu clan (a dharma heir of Zhaojue Qin).
The Daoist Nun Jue’an of the Zu clan was the niece of You Chayuan of Jianning. From her youth, she resolved never to marry.
He applied himself to the ancestral Way and attained clear understanding upon hearing the words of Yuanwu’s public address.
Yuanwu said, "You must cast away what you have seen before you can attain true freedom. Zu replied with a verse: "The pillar puts forth its horizontal bones;
Space brandishes its claws and fangs. Even if one attains profound realization, It is still but sand in the eye."
Lady Fan of Chengdu (Dharma heir of Qín of Zhāojié).
Lady Fan of Chengdu Prefecture had lived as a widow for many years and habitually sat rather than lay down.

Hearing that Yuánwù was residing at Zhāojié, she went there to pay her respects and requested instruction on the causes and conditions for entering the Way. Yuánwù instructed her to contemplate: "It is not the mind, it is not..."
"The Buddha is not a thing; what is he? For a long time, Fan had no realization. He wept and said to Yuanwu, "Master, what expedient means do you have that might allow me to understand more easily?
Yuanwu replied, "There is indeed an expedient. He then instructed him to simply look into "what this is.
Later, Fan attained enlightenment and said, "I never realized it was so close all along!"
Chan Master Wenshu Xindao (Dharma heir of Taiping Qin).
Chan Master Wenshu Xindao of Changde Prefecture was the son of the Xu family of Meizhou. At the age of thirty, he received full ordination.

He went to Chengdu to study the *Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi* (Consciousness-Only), believing that he had reached the ultimate understanding. A fellow student challenged him, saying: "The three realms are mind-only; all phenomena..."
"Only consciousness! Now, with the myriad phenomena resplendent before our eyes, where does the mind-consciousness reside? The Master was at a loss and did not know how to respond;

he subsequently left the mountain pass and traveled throughout the Jianghuai region. Upon arriving at Taiping in Shu, he heard Chan Master Fojian’s night discourse, in which he raised Zhaozhou’s "Cypress Tree" koan.
When it reached the point where Jue Tiezui said, "The former master did not say such words; do not slander the former master," [the Master attained realization].
"Very well. Because of his great doubt, he maintained his alertness for a long time until one night it suddenly opened up.
He immediately went to the master’s quarters, intending to recount what he had realized. As soon as Fojian saw him coming, he closed the door. The Master said, "Master, do not deceive me.
Fojian said, "The ten directions have no walls; why do you not come through the door? The Master punched a hole through the window paper, whereupon Fojian opened the door.
[The Master] grabbed him, saying, "Speak! Speak! The Master cupped his hands over Foguan’s head and made a sound with his mouth as if blowing on it, then departed.
He subsequently presented this verse: "Zhaozhou has a story about the cypress tree; Zen practitioners have passed it down throughout the world.
Most pick at the leaves and search for the branches, Unable to directly realize the source. Jue said, "To say there are no such words is precisely evil."
This refers to "insulting him to his face. If a Zen practitioner possesses the eye that penetrates all quarters, they should skillfully discern the true from the false within this.

Fojian deeply agreed with this, and every time he addressed guests, he would praise [the master] ○. In the spring of the third year of the Jianyan era, he addressed the assembly, citing the circumstances of Linji’s entry into extinction and his entrustment to Sansheng.
The Master said: "The treasury of the true Dharma-eye was extinguished by a blind donkey; when did Linji ever have one?"
This is what was said. People of both ancient and modern times have all falsely transmitted this; do not believe it, but simply observe what happened in the third month thereafter.

When the intercalary third month arrived, the rebel Zhong Xiang rose up, and his followers wished to lead the Master southward. The Master said, "The purpose of studying the Way is to bring an end to birth and death;
why should there be any avoiding? When the rebels arrived, the Master said, "Kill me quickly to satisfy your hearts. The rebels then raised their spears.
He cut it off; the blood all turned into white milk. The bandits were terrified; they drew their mats over it and departed.
Zen Master Longya Zhicai (dharma successor of Taiping Qin):
Zen Master Longya Zhicai of Tanzhou was the son of the Shi family in Shuzhou. At an early age, he served diligently under Fojian.
He took his seat and did not shrink from the duties of the monastery; his reputation had already spread throughout the monastic communities.

While traveling, he arrived at Huanglong at dusk, just as Sīxīn was at the main gate. When asked where he had come from, he gave his name, and Sīxīn immediately recognized him as the capable administrator of Tàipíng in Shūzhōu.
The following day, he entered the room for instruction, and Sīxīn asked: "If you have realized the original phrase, then..."
To understand the final phrase, once you have understood the final phrase, you will understand the initial phrase.
Setting aside both the initial and the final, how do you understand Baizhang’s story of the wild fox? The Master said: "Upon entering the door, one already knows the visitor's understanding."
"What need is there to further mention trampling through the mud? Sīxin said, "The new elder has already died in the hands of the senior monk.
The Master said, "Though the words differ, the ultimate principle is without discrepancy. Sīxin asked, "What is this matter that is without discrepancy?
The Master said, "If one does not strike the horn of the Yellow Dragon, how can one know the pearl beneath its chin? Sīxin then struck him. [End of] Chapter One.
While residing at Mount Yue-lu, on the day he opened the hall for formal instruction, a monk asked:

"Regarding De Shan’s staff and Lin Ji’s shout—today we request the Master to provide a critical assessment. The Master said: "Suru suru. The monk asked: "In 'suru suru,' is there still the meaning of the West?
The Master said: "Suru suru. Because of this, the monastic community called him "Talent-Suru."
Chan Master Shouchun of He Mountain (Dharma heir of Taiping Qin):
Chan Master Shouchun Fodeng of He Mountain in Anji Prefecture was the son of the Shi family of that commandery.

Having failed to find resonance while studying under Chan Master Guangjian Ying, he subsequently traveled to Taiping to seek instruction among the assembly. Finding no entry whatsoever, he then sealed his bedding.
He said, "If I do not thoroughly penetrate this life, I vow never to unfold this [mat]. Thereupon, he sat by day and stood by night as if mourning for his deceased parents.
After more than seven weeks had passed, Master Fojian ascended the hall and said, "The myriad phenomena of the universe and all things are the seal of a single Dharma.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He went to see Fojian, who said, "What a pity! A bright pearl has been..."
The madman Shide questioned him, saying, "Lingyun said, 'Since the moment I first saw the peach blossoms, until now I have had no further doubts.
What is it that he does not doubt? The Master replied, "Do not say that Lingyun has no doubts;
even now, if you try to find a place where there is doubt, it is utterly unobtainable. Fojian remarked, "Xuansha said, 'It is profoundly correct...'"

"It is indeed so. I dare say you, elder brother, have not yet attained full penetration. Where is it that you have not penetrated? The Master replied, "I know well that the Master’s heart is filled with a motherly concern.
Fujian (Fo-jian) approved of this. As the Master rose from his prostrations, he presented a verse, saying: "Throughout the day I gazed at the sky without raising my head;
Only when the peach blossoms were in full bloom did I lift my gaze. Even if you had a net to cover the heavens, How could one ever penetrate its firmness?"
The matter was settled there; Fojian instructed him to protect and uphold [the Dharma]. That evening, he said to the assembly in a stern voice, "This time, Upāsaka Xun will sleep soundly.
When Yuanwu heard this, he suspected it might not be so and said, "I must examine him first before I can accept it.
He then sent someone to summon him. While they were wandering the mountains together, they happened upon a mountain pond, and Yuanwu pushed the Master into it.
He entered the water and asked abruptly, "When Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch, what was it like? The Master said, "The pool is deep, and the fish gather.
Yuanwu asked, "After he saw him, what was it like? The Master said, "The tree is high, and it beckons the wind. Yuanwu asked, "What is it like when he has seen him and when he has not yet seen him?
The Master said, "Stretching out one's legs is within drawing them back. Yuanwu praised him greatly.
Chan Master Qinghai of Dazhong Xiangfu (Successor of Taiping Qin).

Chan Master Qinghai of Dazhong Xiangfu in Jizhou first visited Fojian. Fojian asked, "If the Buddhas of the three periods of time have been swallowed up in a single mouth, where else could there be sentient beings to be taught and transformed?
What is the principle behind this? The Master was about to respond when—
[The monk] stepped forward to speak. Fojian gave a shout, and the Master suddenly grasped the essential meaning.
Chan Master Shigui of Zhuanan at Longxiang (dharma heir of Yuan of Longmen):
Chan Master Shigui of Zhuanan at Longxiang in Wenzhou was the son of the Shi family of Chengdu. Initially, he relied upon [Master] Zong of Daci.
Yaya was so captivated by the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* that more than five autumns passed. He traveled south to visit various venerable masters and finally ascended the Dragon Gate (Longmen).
There, he reported to Foyan what he had previously attained. Foyan said, "Your understanding of the mind is already ultimate;

you simply lack the exertion required to open your eyes. He subsequently appointed him to serve in the Hall Office. One day, while standing in attendance, Foyan asked: "What is it like when all dualities are transcended?"
Foyan said, "It is just like the way you strike the gavel in the Sangha hall. The Master was at a loss for a response.
That evening, Foyan went to the Hall Office. The Master recounted their previous conversation, and Foyan said, "Idle words. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Chan Master Shawu of Gaoan at Yunju in Nankang Commandery (Dharma heir of Longmen Yuan).
A native of the Li family from Yang Prefecture, he left home at the age of eleven to study the sutras and receive ordination.
Possessing innate wisdom, he heard Chan Master Chong recounting the karmic conditions concerning Emperor Wu’s question to Bodhidharma.

As if recovering an old possession, he suddenly said, "Since I have attained a state of total openness (*kuòrán*), what 'victory' could there be? Fénghóng found his words extraordinary and urged him to travel south for further study.
There, at Longmén, he received a prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*). One day, a monk had his foot bitten by a snake; Fényǎn asked him:
"Since he is from Longmen, why was he bitten by a snake? The Master immediately replied, "Indeed, he has manifested the marks of a great man;
Foyan has benefited the vessel. Later, when these words reached Zhaojue, Yuanwu said, "Is there such a monk at Longmen?
The Dharma-way of Dongshan has not yet become desolate!"
Chan Master Huanglong Fazhong (Dharma Heir of Longmen Yuan).

Chan Master Huanglong Muan Fazhong of Longxing Prefecture was the son of the Yao family of Siming. He studied the Tiantai teachings and awakened to the principle of the three contemplations in one mind (*ekacitta-trivipaśyanā*).
Yet, as he was unable to efface his traces, he traveled extensively to consult renowned masters. Upon reaching Longmen, he observed a water mill.
He turned [the wheel] and revealed the essential point of the mind, then spoke this verse: "The turning of the Great Dharma Wheel envelops all before one's eyes;
if you ask further how it is, it is like water pushing a stone mill. He presented this to Foyan. Foyan asked, "What is the matter within it? The Master said:
The water flows long in the mountain stream. Foyan said, "I have one final phrase; I shall entrust it to you.
The Master immediately covered his ears and departed.
This was Chan Master Wugu Daoheng (a dharma heir of Longmen Yuan).
Chan Master Daoxing of Xuedang at Wugu in Quzhou was the son of the Ye family of Chuzhou.
He received the full precepts under Chan Master Ying of Puzhao in Sizhou and subsequently went to study under Fuyan. One day, he heard [Fuyan] raise the story of Xuansha stubbing his toe.
He then attained great enlightenment.
[This concerns] Chan Master Baiyang Fashun (a dharma successor of Yuan of Longmen).
Chan Master Baiyang Fashun of Fuzhou was the son of the Wen family of Mianzhou. Having relied upon Fuyan, he heard a general discourse on the Dharma.
He cited the *Mind-King Inscription* by Master Fu Dashi, which says: "The flavor of salt in water, the blue pigment within the lacquer—these are certainly present, yet their forms are not seen.
Upon these words, the Master attained realization; later, while observing a rapidly spinning jewel-treasury, he suddenly clarified the Great Dharma.

He hurried to the master’s chamber and paid his respects, presenting a verse that said: "A strange peak crowns the summit as clouds drift lazily; The source has no separate streams, yet the water flows cool and clear.
If one wanders the mountains without reaching their ultimate end, In the end, the green peaks will obstruct the eyes. Buddhyan (Foyan) smiled and approved it.
Chan Master Faru of Yunju (Dharma Heir of Longmen Yuan).
Chan Master Faru of Yunju in Nankang Commandery was the son of the Hu family of Danqiu. He relied upon Chan Master Rui of Huguo.

Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he traveled extensively to visit the various masters of the various schools in the region of Zhejiang. Later, he arrived at Longmen and reported to Foyan what he had realized during his daily practice.
Foyan said, "These are all merely intellectual understandings; they are not the ultimate matter. If you wish to resolve the problem of birth and death, you must seek wondrous enlightenment.

The Master was struck with awe and came to believe this deeply. One day, Foyan appointed him to oversee the Xiangji (Gandha) Hall, but the Master firmly declined on the grounds that his cultivation of the Way was not yet complete.
Foyan encouraged him, saying, "Go ahead and take up your post. Among those there, there will be someone who will preach the Dharma for you.
Not long after, as he rose at dawn and opened the kitchen door, he caught sight of the Holy Monk (Śākyamuni). Realizing what he had not yet realized, he immediately informed Foyan.
Foyan asked, "Do you see the Holy Monk here? The Master went before him, paid his respects, and stood with palms joined. Foyan said, "I told you so."
There was a great man who expounded the Dharma for you:
Chan Master Zhengxian of Guizong in Nankang Commandery (a dharma heir of Yuan of Longmen).
Chan Master Zhengxian, whose lay surname was Chen, was a native of Tongchuan. He traveled to Chengdu and relied upon [the teachings there].
The Great Compassionate Master Xiushu studied the sūtras and śāstras; he could recite any scripture from memory after reading it once. His peers called him "Sūtra-Treasury Son.

He left Sichuan to visit various venerable masters and later sought instruction from Fuyan. One day, upon entering the inner quarters for private instruction, Fuyan raised the phrase, "With such earnestness, one embraces the sandalwood tree.
Before the words had even ceased, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. Fuyan said, "Sūtra-Treasury Son has let it all slip away!"

From then on, he discussed the profound and abstruse teachings with the Master; their discourse was tireless and inexhaustible. Foyan praised him as excellent and personally inscribed the two characters "Zhenmu" (True Herder) to bestow upon him.
Chan Master Mingbian of Daochang Monastery (Dharma Heir of Longmen Yuan).
Chan Master Mingbian of Zhengtang at Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture was the son of the Yu family of that prefecture. He visited various renowned masters.
Upon arriving at Shaolin in the Western Capital, he heard a monk cite a poem by Fuyan to elucidate the story of King Kaniṣka of Kaśmīra beheading the Venerable Siṃha:
"On the banks of the Yangtze River, the willows are in spring; the willow blossoms grieve the traveler crossing the river.

At twilight in the farewell pavilion, a single sound of the Huns' flute rings out; you head toward Xiangxiang, while I head toward Qin. The Master felt a silent resonance within himself and immediately hurried [to see him].

Longmen requested to enter the inner circle. Foyan asked, "Regarding the causes and conditions recorded in the texts concerning the ancestral masters of the past, I allow that you have understood them.
Suddenly, he raised his fist and said, "Why is this called a fist? As the Master was about to respond, Foyan struck him in the mouth and said:
"One must not employ rationalization. Thereupon, he suddenly cast away all knowledge and views.
In his room, he posed a question: "Why does a cat love to catch mice? He also said: "When the board sounds, why do the dogs bark? The master's style was stern and cold;
beginners often felt intimidated by it. Thus, he praised Bodhidharma, saying: "At the foot of the Shengyuan Tower, one is full of shame; on the peak of Mount Luoyang..."
The boundaries are distorted; the skin and marrow have been passed down as a mere tale. A single sandal has no place to be buried.

Were it not for this piercing cold that penetrates the very bones, how could one obtain the plum blossom’s fragrance that strikes the nose? When Xuedou saw this, he praised it highly, saying, "The former master still has such a person!
He remarked, "This eulogy alone is sufficient to cut off the tongues of all people under heaven."
Shiqui Shouzuo (Dharma successor of Longmen Yuan).
Shouzuo was a native of Chengdu. Having studied under various masters, he eventually went to Longmen. One day, while sitting in meditation, he dozed off;
hearing a chorus of frogs suddenly croaking, he mistakenly took it for the sound of a shaving board. He hurried toward the source, where a monk [awoke him].
Someone said, "The sound of a frog croaking is not the clapper. The Master was suddenly enlightened. He went to the Abbot’s quarters to reveal his realization.
Foyan said, "Have you not seen Rāhula? The Master immediately stopped him, saying, "There is no need for the Master to mention it;

I shall go and see for myself. Not long after, he attained further insight and composed this verse: "In the night I heard the sound of the clapper; After waking, I heard the frog croak. The frog and the clapper—"
Xiang [said], "The mountain peaks all resonate at once. Thereupon, he redoubled his efforts in investigation and attained profound mastery of the mysterious and abstruse.

Foyan commanded him to share the seat [with him], but the Master firmly declined, saying, "This is no trivial matter. It is like piercing the eye with a golden needle; if there is a discrepancy even as fine as a hair’s breadth, the eye will be destroyed.
I wish to remain in the stage of study throughout successive lifetimes to refine myself by my own effort. Foyan then praised him with a verse.
The Layman Feng Jie (Jichuan), Court Official and Dharma Heir of Longmen Yuan:
The layman Feng Jie, titled Jichuan, had sought instruction from various renowned masters since his youth.
Finally, he resided at Longmen, where he studied under Chan Master Foyan Yuan for two years. One day, while walking with Yuan in the Dharma Hall, a young boy happened to run across the courtyard.
He composed a verse: "Among the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. He then patted the Master’s back and said, "How wonderful! At that, the Master attained realization.
In the Ding-si year of the Xiaoshing era, he was appointed as a Censor. Upon meeting Chan Master Dahui at Mingqing Temple for the opening of the hall, Dahui descended from his seat.
The Master pulled him back and said, "Every time you speak before the scholar-officials, you say: 'In this life, I shall certainly not...'"
Having acted as such a creature, why have you failed today? Daowei said, "The entire earth is this Venerable Gaokong; where do you see him?
As the Master was about to respond, Daowei struck him with his palm. The Master said, "I brought this upon myself.
A month later, he specifically requested alms to spend the summer retreat at Mount Jing, naming his quarters the "Immovable Pavilion" (Budong Xuan). One day—
Dahui ascended the seat. He cited the case where Yaoshan asked Shitou: "I have a rough understanding of the Three Vehicles and the twelve divisions of the teachings.
However, I have heard that in the South there is the 'Direct Pointing to the Human Mind for Seeing One's Nature and Attaining Buddhahood,' which I truly do not yet understand clearly.
I humbly hope you will show me your compassion and grant me instruction. Shitou said, "'It is so' is not acceptable; 'it is not so' is also not acceptable. 'It is so'..."
"It is not so in any way. What do you do? Yaoshan was at a loss. Shitou said, "Your affinity does not lie here;
you should go to Jiangxi to see Master Mazu. Yaoshan went to Mazu’s place and asked him the same question as before.
The Patriarch said: "Sometimes I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink; sometimes I do not instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink.
Sometimes that which I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink is correct; sometimes that which I instruct them to raise their eyebrows and blink is not."

Yaoshan attained great enlightenment. After Dahui had finished presenting the case, the Master followed him to the abbot’s quarters and said, "I have now understood the kōan you just presented. Dahui asked, "How do you understand it?
The Master replied, "'Thus' is not permitted—*sulu svāhā*. 'Not thus' is also not permitted—*śiri svāhā*. Thus..."
"It is not so; in every way it is not permitted. *Suruṣiri svāhā*. Great Wisdom sealed this with a verse:

"The Sanskrit and the Chinese are forged into a single block. Alas, the worldly man has attained this samādhi! Later, when he served as the Governor of Qiongzhou, he remained serene and unflagging wherever he went.
He once composed a verse of self-praise: "In the intervals between public affairs, I delight in sitting in meditation; rarely have I [been otherwise]."
He lay on his side upon his bed to sleep; although he manifested the appearance of a secular official, the name "Elder" was renowned throughout the four seas.
In the autumn of the twenty-third year, he requested retirement and notified his relatives and acquaintances, setting October the third as the date for his passing.
On the appointed day, he had a high seat prepared in the rear hall and received guests as usual. Between the hours of the Dragon (7–9 a.m.
and the Snake (9–11 a.m.), he descended the steps and, facing the imperial palace, performed a solemn prostration. He then requested the Transport Commissioner to assume the affairs of the monastery.

Donning monastic robes and sandals, he took his place upon the high seat and exhorted all officials, both clerical and lay, to turn toward the Way, support the teachings, and raise the banner of the Dharma. Thereupon, he grasped his staff and struck it down.
His knees detached from his body and he passed away. The Commissioner of the Transport Canal requested, saying, "Your Highness’s coming and going is so free and at ease;
why not leave behind a verse to record this rare occurrence? The Master opened his eyes, sought out a brush, and wrote: "The third and the eleventh, the middle nine and the lower seven.
The old man has finished speaking; Guige’s eyes are red. Having said this, he finally departed for eternity.
Chan Master Shitou Zihui (Dafu Jingshi’s Dharma heir) of Diaoyutai, Tiantai Prefecture.
He was a native of that region. By profession he had been a stonemason; though illiterate, his aspirations were set upon the school of Emptiness (*śūnyatā*).
He frequently sought out others to orally transmit the *Lotus Sūtra* to him until he was able to recite it from memory. He then abandoned his home and entered the monastic life.

Daisu served him by sweeping and sprinkling water. He ordered Daisu to fetch stones from the cliffside; the Master did not let go of his hammer and chisel from his hands, yet he recited the sutras without ceasing.
Seeing this, Daisu said, "Today there is the sound of chiseling; tomorrow there will be the sound of chiseling.
When birth and death arrive, what settlement will you make? The Master was startled; he set down his tools, prostrated, and requested to hear the ultimate Dharma. Thereupon, he followed [the Master].
He went to the Abbot’s quarters. Dàsuì told him to stop reciting the sutras for a while and instead contemplate the karmic encounter of Zhàozhōu examining the old woman.
The Master kept this thought in mind at every moment. After some time, while he was chipping away at a stone that was somewhat hard, he struck it with all his might.

Suddenly, he caught sight of a flash of light and attained sudden, thorough realization. He ran to the Abbot’s quarters, prostrated, and presented a verse, saying: "I have exhausted my efforts, yet there is not a single clue."
The sparks of fire scattered; [the master] was originally right here. Dasui said with joy, "You have attained thorough penetration.
He then offered a verse on Zhaozhou’s examination of the old woman: "The three armies do not move, yet the banners flash; The old woman is precisely the foot of the Mara King.
Zhaozhou’s handleless iron broom Sweeps away the dust and smoke until all is empty and stark. Dasui approved it and subsequently ordained him as a monk.
Fu. Because he was a stonemason by trade, he was known as "Huishou" (Stone-Head).
Chan Master Hujing of Husheng Monastery (the dharma heir of Daisui Jing):
Chan Master Hujing Yuchiu of Husheng Monastery in Tongchuan Prefecture. He was the son of the Yang family of Chengdu. At the age of fourteen, he paid his respects...
Baiba (Baima) took Anhui as his teacher. Having heard of Nantang’s reputation for the Way, he went to rely upon him.

Nantang brought up the story of Xiangyan regarding the dragon crying within the withered tree; through their back-and-forth exchanges and interrogations, the Master attained great enlightenment beneath these words.
One day, Nantang asked: "Do not guard the green grass on the cold crag; sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not subtle. How do you understand this?"
The Master said, "You must simply brandish the sword; if you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut. Nantang looked startled and said, "This little fellow!
The Master said, "Take care," and then departed.
The Ascetic of the South of Jianmen (Dharma Heir of Da sui Jingfa).
The Ascetic of the South of Jianmen was a man of profound integrity. Having attained a karmic accord through a single word from Da sui, he served him with unwavering diligence.
Later, he went to pay his respects to Chan Master Chonghua Yun. During their session, Yun questioned him regarding the Three Seals of the Zen School. Nan—

It is said: "Sealing the sky, sealing the mud, sealing the water—on level ground, cold waves rise in competition. Even if one manages to go and come with full mastery, it is still like a divine tortoise dragging its tail."
The Minister of State Mo Jiang (Dharma Heir of Dawsui Jingfa).

Minister Mo Jiang, whose courtesy name was Shaohu, was a native of Fenning in Yuzhang. Having served as an official in Western Sichuan, he went to visit Chan Master Nantang Jing to inquire about the essentials for resolving his mind.
Nantang instructed him to maintain mindfulness toward the "good place. Just as he happened to enter the latrine, suddenly—
Smelling a foul odor, he hurriedly covered his nose with his hand and suddenly attained realization. He immediately presented this verse: "From of old, my natural grace has loved elegance;
I have often laughed at those who seek it outwardly. Though there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences, there is no place to find it;
When attained, it was all along at the tip of one's own nose. Nantang replied: "When a single dharma is penetrated, all dharmas are complete; its wondrous function extends in every direction."
“What is he seeking? A blue serpent emerges from its case; the demon armies prostrate. The blue-eyed barbarian monk smiles and nods his head. (Jingshan Xìn said:

“If Minister He had felt even a trace of that stench at the tip of his own nose, he would have blown it out to熏熏 [overwhelm] everyone. The old fellow Nantang deserves thirty blows of the staff. Why? It is the father’s fault for failing to teach his son.

The verse says: “Feeling the gold, he is suddenly filled with grief; though his appearance is elegant, his charm is in vain. Had he used it as he does now, he would have cut off the stinking nose of the Minister.”)
The Layman Wang Xiao, titled Longtu (Dharma heir of Jìngfǎ of Dàsuí):
The layman Wang Xiao, whose courtesy name was Guānfù, attained a realization upon hearing the sound of the board signaling the end of meditation while staying at Zhāojié.
He asked Nantang, "I have a certain point of view, yet as soon as someone questions me, I am unable to speak.
I do not know where my fault lies. Nantang replied, "The fault lies in having a certain point of view. Nantang then asked, "When did you arrive at your post?
The official said, "On the fourth day of the eighth month last year. Nantang asked again, "How long has it been since you left your position as an Inspector?"
At the Yaya, the Duke said, "On the twentieth day of last month, Nantang asked, 'Why is it said that one cannot open one's mouth?
At this, the Duke attained awakening.
This refers to Chan Master Zhice of Mount Jing (a successor of Yunyan Tansheng).
Chan Master Tudu Zhice of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Chen family of Tiantai.

At the age of nineteen, he went to Guoqing Temple to pay his respects to Jishì Guang, upon which he attained a sudden and clear realization. He subsequently visited Dàyuán at Wànshòu Temple in Míng, where Dàyuán asked him, "Where have you come from?
The Master replied, "From Tiantai. Dàyuán asked, "Have you seen the Great Master Zhìzhě? The Master replied, "I have."
"Even now, they are not few," [Daoyuan] said. [Dongshan] asked, "Why are they right under your feet? The Master replied, "Right before one's face, it is missed.
Daoyuan said, "The Master is lush without weeding, and straight without leaning. One day, he took his leave; Daoyuan saw him off at the gate.
He patted the Master’s back and said, “The treasure is near; this city is not real. The Master nodded in agreement. He then traveled to Yuzhang to visit Dian-niu.

On the way, he passed through Yunju, where wind and snow blocked his path for forty-two days. At noon on the forty-second day, as the sound of the wooden board signaling the meal rang out clearly, he attained a sudden and great awakening.
Upon arriving at the gate, Dian-niu pointed at him alone and asked, “Where have you seen gods and ghosts?”
[The Master] came. The Master said, "When I heard the sound of the board at Yunju, I came. Dian-niu asked, "What is it? The Master said, "It shatters empty space;
it has no handle or grip at all. Dian-niu said, "The matter beyond the upward path is not yet here. The Master said, "The neighbor to the east sits in the dark;
the neighbor to the west scolds one another. Dian-niu said, "Rising far above Buddhas and patriarchs—one such unicorn is enough for you to establish yourself in the future."
The Layman Fan Chong, Vice President of the Secretariat (Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuan Tong Min).

The Layman Fan Chong, courtesy name Zhixu, while serving as a member of the Han Garden (the Imperial Secretariat), was governing Yuzhang. Passing by Yuan Tong, he went to pay his respects to Chan Master Min.

After the tea had been served, [Min] said: "I am soon to grow old; I have fallen into the ranks of those wearing the purple and gold [official robes], and have drifted somewhat away from this matter."
"Far away. Yuantong called out, "Director of the Imperial Library! The Master responded with an acknowledgment. Yuantong said, "How can there be anything far?
The Master leaped up in realization and said, "I beg the Master to grant me further instruction. Yuantong said, "From here to Hongdu, it is four stages' journey.
The Master paused in thought. Yuantong said, "If you see it, you see it immediately; if you deliberate upon it, you have already missed it. Thereupon, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
The Layman Wu Juhou, Grand Councilor (Dharma heir of Chan Master Yuan Tong Min):

When the Layman Wu Juhou, Grand Councilor, returned to Zhongling while holding his official insignia, he visited Chan Master Yuan Tong Min and said, "Some time ago, when I was traveling to the provincial capital for the examinations, I passed through here and crossed Zhaozhou’s Barrier.
I therefore asked the former abbot, Elder Ne, about the matter of penetrating the barrier."
“How is it? Nan said. “I went off to serve in office, and now more than fifty years have passed unnoticed.

Min asked, “Have you ever clearly realized the matter of passing through the barrier? Nan replied, “I have passed through eight times, always maintaining this mindfulness, yet I am still not entirely free and easy.
Min handed him a fan and said, “Please use this fan. Nan immediately waved the fan. Min said, “What is there that is not yet free?”
While at the place where he was sprinkling water, the Master suddenly had an awakening and said, "I request the final word. Miaomin then waved his fan twice.
The Master said, "Intimate! Intimate! Miaomin replied, "The tongue of this barbarian reaches three thousand li."
The Layman Minister of the Interior, Lu Hang (Dharma heir of Yuan Tong Min).
While the Layman Minister Lu Hang was warming himself by the hearth with Yuan Tong, he asked: "There is no need to laboriously bring up the various ancestral precedents;
I ask that the Master point directly to a single phrase. Yuan Tong pointed at him with a stern voice and said: "Look at the fire! The Minister hurriedly...
He brushed aside his robe and suddenly attained great enlightenment. He expressed his gratitude, saying, "It is clear that the Buddha-dharma is not so very much.
Yuan-tong shouted, "Put it down! The Master responded, "Yes, yes."
The Layman Du Xiang of the Left Ministry (a successor of Master Yuan Tong Min) asked Yuan Tong:
"This Dharma cannot be understood through thought or discrimination; how should one approach it? Yuan Tong said:
"Enter the mass of fire with your whole body. The Layman asked: "Ultimately, what is it like?"
Xiao understood. Yuantong said, "Go straight ahead. The Master hesitated. Yuantong said, "Would you like some more tea?
The Master replied, "There is no need. Yuantong asked, "Why do you not understand it in this way? The Master realized the meaning and said, "I see now that it was all along too near.
Yuantong said, "Eighty thousand miles! The Master then composed a verse: "Inconceivable! This is a great mass of fire. Just so..."
"How can one go? One does not depart from this very place. Yuantong said, "Eh! There is still this [notion] remaining. The Master said, "I beg the Teacher to grant me further instruction.
Yuantong said, "Go right like this. The cauldron is cast of iron. The Master bowed his head in gratitude.
Chan Master Daochuan of Yefu (a dharma heir of Jingyin Cheng).
Chan Master Daochuan of Zhiji at Yefu in Wuyi Commandery was the son of the Di family of Kunshan.

Initially serving as an archer-official (*gongji*) of the county, he heard that the Head Seat Qian of Dongzhai was expounding the Dharma for both monastics and laypeople, so he went to follow him. He practiced seated meditation without weariness.
One day, having been punished with a flogging for negligence in his duties, he suddenly attained great enlightenment beneath the staff.
He subsequently resigned his post and relied upon Chan Master Jiaoxiong Miguang (the twelfth generation descendant of Linji;
the sixteenth generation descendant of Nanyue), who was himself a dharma heir of Chan Master Dahui Zonggao of Mount Jing.
Chan Master Miaoguang Jiaozhong Huai’an of Quanzhou was the son of the Li clan of Min. He crossed the mountain ridges to pay his respects to Chan Master Yuanwu at Yunju.
Subsequently, he studied under Huangbo Xiang and Ga’ān Wu; their exchanges of mind and words were all in accord.

Due to the outbreak of bandits in the Huai and Chu regions, he returned to pay his respects to Foxin. It happened that Dahui was residing in Guangzhou, so he went there to follow him. Dahui said to him: "You..."
To provide one or two examples of what was attained at Focin (Focin-chu): The Master [Zhaozhou] cited the public case of Puhua while ascending the hall, saying:
"Focin would not have it this way. If you do not come in such a manner, how will you proceed?
He then struck him across the spine, saying, "Let him manifest his body throughout the entire world. Dahui asked, "What is your opinion? The Master replied, "I do not approve of him."
Later, he added a footnote [to this]. Daoyi said, "This is precisely taking the illness as the Dharma. The Master remained resolute and did not find it convincing.

Daoyi said, "You should simply try to grasp its meaning through reflection. The Master ultimately still thought it was not so. After ten days had passed, he recalled the words of Chan Master Haiyin Xin, who had remarked:
"The thunder is great, yet there are no raindrops at all. Only then did he become free from obstruction and hasten toward [the realization].
He said to Mahāmati: "Mahāmati, you cited the words of Langye who saw the Way, as well as the saying that Xuansha had not yet reached the ultimate, to question me.
After the Master [Langye] had responded, Mahāmati laughed and said: 'Although he has advanced one step, it is merely that he does not settle in any location.
It is like a person cutting down a tree: if one strikes a single blow at the root, the life-force is severed. You, however, have been striking at the branches; how could that sever the life-force?'"
"It is rooted there. Today, those everywhere who speak of Chan in such vast numbers—seeing things all in this manner—what benefit does it bring to the matter?
Of the true lineage of Yangqi, there are only three or four people. The Master departed in indignation. The following day, Dahui asked him, "Do you still have doubts?
The Master replied, "There is nothing to be doubted. Dahui said, "Just as when the ancients met, before they had even opened their mouths..."
At that time, having already discerned the reality of the matter, or having heard his words, he immediately recognized their depth or shallowness. "How is this principle? [he asked].

The Master was struck with awe and broke into a sweat, not knowing where to turn. Dahui ordered him to investigate the "phrase of existence" and the "phrase of non-existence. Dahui then went to Yunmen’s hermitage.
The Master was walking with him as an attendant when one day he asked, "I have reached this point, yet I cannot attain thorough penetration. Where does my sickness lie?
Dahui said, "Your sickness is most chronic; even the world's physicians fold their hands in helplessness. Why?
Because others die and cannot live again, whereas you are now alive and have never died. If you wish to reach the ground of great peace and happiness, you must first undergo a death."
The Master’s state of doubt grew ever deeper. Later, he entered the room. Dàhuì asked, “The gruel has been eaten; the bowls have been washed; the medicinal taboos have been removed.
Now, bring forth a single phrase! The Master replied, “Torn asunder. Dàhuì let out a thunderous shout and said, “And you speak of Chan again?
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment. Dàhuì struck the drum and addressed the assembly, saying, “To grasp at tortoise hair is laughable.”
Hehe! One blow and ten thousand heavy gates and locks open. What joy and fulfillment in this very day of my life!
Who would say that a thousand miles have deceived me here? The Master also presented a verse, saying: A single pressure, and the opportune moment roars like thunder;
Startling up Mount Sumeru, the Northern Dipper is hidden. Vast waves surge, flooding the heavens; I grasp the nostrils, yet I lose my mouth.
Chan Master Donglin Daoyan (Dharma Heir of Jingshan Dahui Zonggao):
Chan Master Wan’an Daoyan of Donglin in Jiangzhou was a native of Tongchuan. Having studied under Yuanwu for a long time, he attained a slight degree of awakening.
When Yuanwu returned to Sichuan, he instructed Daoyan to rely upon Miaoxi, and sent a letter to Miaoxi which read: "Daoyan is like a piece of brocade."
The painting was completed, with only the eyes yet to be dotted. It is impossible to measure the future of those who shall succeed him.
While Miaoxi resided at Yunmen and Yangyu, the Master was present at both; there, they questioned one another morning and evening until he attained great enlightenment.
Chan Master Dingxu of Xichan (Dharma heir of Jingshan Gaofeng).
Chan Master Lanna Dingxu of Xichan in Fuzhou was the son of the Lin family of that prefecture. As a youth, he gained renown as a candidate for the Jinshi examination.
At the age of twenty-five, while reading the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra*, he suddenly exclaimed, "How nearly have I been misled by this scholar’s cap! He then desired to leave the household life.

His mother found this difficult to accept, as his marriage was scheduled for that very year. The Master then cut her off, saying: "The peach and apricot trees entrust their blossoms all at once to the spring breeze;
the green bamboo and yellow flowers shall henceforth be my companions forever. He eventually followed Chan Master Baoshou Yue to become a bhikṣu.

Carrying his single staff, he traveled through Lake and Xiang, visiting renowned masters everywhere. Finding no difference in the flavor of the Dharma, he returned to his hometown and built a hermitage at...
At the summit of Qiang Peak, he did not descend from the mountain for three years. Chan Master Foxincai invited him out to lead the assembly at Dachen.
Once, when the master was discussing with his students the karmic conditions regarding the saying "the very mind is Buddha," Miguang—a friend of the master—wrote to him, saying:
"The abbot of Miaoxi Hermitage on Yangyu Island has a style of practice distinct from that of other quarters; you should come there for a short visit."
"How is it? The Master did not answer. Miguang used a stratagem to invite the Master for a meal; the Master went to attend.

It happened that Miaoxi was conducting a "room-entering" (入室) session for his disciples. The Master followed along to join in the appreciation. Miaoxi raised a case: "A monk asked Mazu, 'What is the Buddha?
Mazu said, 'The very mind is the Buddha. What do you say to this? The Master offered a response. Miaoxi rebuked him, saying, "Your understanding is like..."

"How could I dare to presume to be a teacher to others? He struck the drum for a public discourse, exposing all that he had cherished and mastered throughout his life and dismissing it as erroneous understanding.
The Master’s tears flowed down his cheeks; he did not dare look up at him and thought silently to himself:

"If what I have attained has already been dismissed, how can the essential meaning transmitted from the West have ended with this alone? Thereupon, he returned his heart to the ranks of the disciples.
One day Miaoxi asked, "When there is no releasing from within and no entering from without—just at such a time, what is it like?
As the Master was about to open his mouth, Miaoxi took up his bamboo staff and struck him three times across the spine. At this, the Master attained great enlightenment.
He spoke in a stern voice, "The Master has already had too much. Miaoxi struck him once more. The Master prostrated.
Miaoxi laughed and said, "Today you finally know that I did not deceive you. He then sealed this with a verse: "The eye of Mahesvara stands upright upon the crown of the head;
A life-stealing talisman hangs askew from the elbow. Blind the eyes and cast off the talisman— At the eastern wall of Zhaozhou."
The "Hanging Gourd" [episode] thus caused his reputation to resound throughout the monastic community.
Chan Master Daoyuan of Kaishan (a dharma heir of Jingshan Dahui):
Chan Master Daoyuan of Kaishan in Jianning Prefecture was a native of that region. He first went to the capital and relied upon Yuanwu. [He remained there for] no...
Upon his departure, he followed Miaoxi to a hermitage in Quannan. When Miaoxi took charge of Mount Jing, the Master also accompanied him.
Before long, Miaoxi sent the Master to Changsha to deliver a letter to Layman Zhang of Ziyuan.
The Master thought to himself, "I have practiced Chan for twenty years without reaching a point of entry; if I go on this journey, my practice will surely fall into ruin. He intended to decline.
As they were traveling, a friend of his named Zongyuan scolded him, saying, "It is not permissible to practice Chan while on the road;

you must stop! Let us go together. The Master had no choice but to continue on his way. While traveling, he spoke weeping to Zongyuan, saying, "In my entire life of practicing Chan, I have found nothing at all that brings me strength.
Now, moreover, I am rushing along this road; how can I achieve realization? Zongyuan—
He told him, "As for everything you have studied in various quarters, everything you have realized, and everything that Yuanwu or Miaoxi has explained for you—do not concern yourself with any of it.
Regarding matters on the road that can be substituted, I shall substitute for you entirely.
There are only five things for which I cannot substitute; these you must attend to yourself. The Master asked, "What are these five things?"
"I wish to hear the essentials of this," he said. Zongyuan replied, "Dressed in clothes, eating food, defecating and urinating, you carry a corpse along the road.
At these words, the Master grasped the essential meaning; unconsciously, he began to dance with his hands and feet.
Zongyuan said, "Now you may send a letter. You should proceed forward; I shall return first. Zongyuan immediately returned to Jingshan, while the Master remained for half a year.
Just as he was about to return, Miaoxi saw him and said with joy, "Son of Jianzhou, you will not be leaving this time.
This refers to Chan Master Foguo Deguang of Yuyang Monastery in Qingyuan Prefecture (a dharma heir of Jingshan Dahui Zonggao).
Master Deguang was a native of the Peng family of Linjiang Commandery. From his youth, he was dedicated to the study of learning.
At the age of twenty, he received the tonsure at Ji Chan Master’s Dongshan Guanghua Temple in his native district.

One day, he entered the master’s room, where Ji asked, "It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing—what is it? The Master was at a loss and became filled with doubt. He did not sleep all night.
The following day, he went to the abbot’s quarters to request further instruction, saying, "Yesterday, I was honored by the Master’s question. Since it is neither mind..."
"It is neither Buddha, nor is it an object. Ultimately, what is it? I hope the Venerable Master will compassionately point this out.
Ji Zhenwei let out a shout and said, "You little śrāmaṇera, do you want me to provide a commentary for you?
He then took up his staff and struck him across the back, driving him away. At that, the Master attained realization. Later, he visited Yue’an Gao, Ying’an Hua, and Baizhang Zhen.
He could never bring himself to accept [the teaching]. Later, when Dahui took charge of the Yuyang Monastery, the finest talents from across the four seas gathered there like scales of fish;

the Master was among them. In Dahui’s room, Dahui asked the Master: "If you call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of contact; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you commit the fault of turning your back.

You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. As the Master prepared to respond, Dahui struck him with his staff. At that moment, the Master attained sudden and great enlightenment. From then on...
What was previously attained disintegrated like crumbling walls or melting ice.
Chan Master Tanyi of Yuyuan (a dharma successor of Jingshan Dahui):
Chan Master Tanyi of Yuyuan in Fuzhou had long relied upon Yuanwu, considering himself free from doubt. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he went forth.
While residing at Xinghua Xiangyun, his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dahui entered Min, he realized that the Master’s realization was not yet definitive;
he sent a letter inviting him to come. The Master delayed, so Dahui held a small-scale sermon (xiaocan) and severely rebuked him, subsequently posting a public notice for the fourfold assembly.
Having no choice, the Master broke the summer retreat to go and visit Dahui. Dahui interrogated him regarding his realization, and after a while said: "Such is your understanding."
"How dare I succeed the Elder Yuanwu? The Master withdrew from the monastery to attend upon him.
One day, while in the inner room, Dahui asked, "I want someone who does not practice Chan to be a National Teacher. The Master replied, "I am fit to be a National Teacher. Dahui shouted him out.
Not long after, Dahui said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening was not at the point where the bamboo was struck; Juzhi attained it..."
"It is not on the tip of the finger. At these words, the Master attained immediate enlightenment.
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu (a dharma successor of Jingshan Daoyuan):
Chan Master Wuben of Jianfu in Raoyou was a native of Jiangzhou. Having come from Yunmen in Jiangxi, he attended and served [Master] Miaoxin.
Xiyu arrived at Xiaoxi in Quannan. At that time, many men of talent and refinement had gathered there, and those who received his certification of realization were numerous.
The Master privately remarked that they were all abandoning him and intended to depart. Miaoxi, knowing this, said to him: "You need only focus your mind on investigation.
If you have any realization, I shall recognize it even before you open your mouth. Shortly thereafter, he heard that the Master had entered the room [for formal instruction].
Therefore, he said to the Master, "I have been attending you for many years practicing Zen, yet day after day I can only say, 'I do not understand.
" The Master scolded him, saying, "You little devil! Before you were even born, I already had your teeth knocked out three times at the Huoshan Temple.
Let me teach you something! From this point on, his resolve became even more keen; he took up the koan of the dog having no Buddha-nature.

He was contemplating the "No-Character" (Wuzi) kōan. One night, as the third watch approached, while he was leaning against a pillar in the hall and drifting into a drowsy sleep, he did not realize that the words "No-Character" had escaped his lips.
Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment. Three days later, Miaoxi returned from the provincial city; the Master hurried to his quarters.
No sooner had his feet crossed the threshold than he had not yet uttered a word when Miaoxi said, "Old Barbarian, this time you have finally reached the very head.
This refers to Chan Master Zunpu (a dharma successor of Jingshan Daoyuan).
Chan Master Wuyuan Zunpao of Yuba Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture was a native of Fuzhou. In his youth, he studied the Way alongside Yuquan Yi under Yuanwu.
After several years, he returned to his hometown and assisted Yi at Xiangyun in Putian.

In the *jiayin* year of the Shaoxing era, when Dahui resided at Yangyu, the Master went there to inquire after him. During their session in the inner quarters, Dahui asked, "Sansheng and Xinghua emerged from..."
He came forth, yet he did not speak for the sake of others. You say: "Do these two old fellows have a way of manifesting themselves or not?
The Master struck Daie once on the knee. Daie said, "Was this single blow of yours to avenge Sanxing, or was it to avenge Xinghua?
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! As the Master hesitated, Daie struck him again. Furthermore—
He said, "You must not, under any circumstances, forget this one blow.
Later, while in his quarters, Dahui asked a monk, "When Deshan saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately strike; when Linji saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately shout;
when Xuefeng saw a monk enter the gate, he would say, 'What is this? When Muzhou saw a monk, he would say, 'A ready-made case—let you go.'"
"Thirty blows! You say: 'Do these four old fellows have any way of benefiting others? The monk said, 'They do. Dahui said, 'Noted (zha).
As the monk hesitated, Dahui gave a shout. Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly grasped the subtle meaning;
Dahui joyfully granted him approval."
Chan Master Nengren Zuoyuan (Dharma heir of Jingshan Daokao):
