Elder Foji visited the Master. The Master asked, "I have heard that you, Elder, have been uniquely transforming a single region. For what reason have you come to travel to this mountain peak?"
Furi said, "The bright moon hangs in the sky; the ice and frost do not freeze of their own accord. The Master asked, "Is this not the family style of an elder?
Furi said, "A steep, towering barrier of ten thousand layers, within which the precious moon is contained. The Master said, "This is still merely literary expression.
What is the family style of an elder? Furi said, "Today I am fortunate to have met Furi."

He then asked: "When 'the hidden and secret preserves the ultimate truth,' people know there is a Way, yet they cannot attain it; when 'the vast simplicity leaves no room for blame,' people know there is a Way, yet they can attain it.
Within these two paths, they remain merely at the point where people ascend or descend. I do not yet know what the Master’s own Way is."

[The monk] asked, "How do you speak of the Way? The Master said, "In my house, where the Way is practiced, there is nothing to be spoken of. Furi said, "On the path of the Tathāgata, there is no partiality or crookedness;
please, let us harmonize a single performance of the profound sound. The Master said, "Let the two wheels shine upon one another as they please."
The emerald pool beyond the clouds has no connection [to this world]. Furi said, "Tell the countless white-haired guests: this time, young ones, do not return to your hometowns.
The Master said, "Old and young share the same wheel, without front or back; on the mysterious path of my house, let there be no divergence."
Fojiu said, "A single word settles the world; for whom were these four lines proclaimed? The Master said, "You say there are three or four;
I say that within them, even one does not exist."
Chan Master Shenyi of Dingshan (Dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou).
Chan Master Shenyi of Dingshan in Chuzhou once questioned Master Xingjue while traveling on pilgrimage. [Xingjue] asked: "It does not fall into numerical categories;
please, Master, speak. The Master held up his prayer beads and said, "Are these falling or not? Xingjue replied, "Perfect spheres."
"Three apertures—everyone of this age knows they exist. I ask you, Master, to complete the previous dialogue. The Master struck him. Xingfan shook his sleeves and departed.
The Master said, "Thirty years from now, he will go away beating his breast and weeping bitterly.

After Xingfan established his own monastery, he addressed the assembly, saying, "Thirty years ago, when I was at Mount Ding, I was thoroughly deceived by him; it was no small matter. (Xuedou Xian says: As for Mount Ding’s application...)
How can one avoid falling into the trap? Though the *pí* tree may be known, one has not yet attained the eye that discerns the Dharma. Try to examine this!
Chan Master Fadu of Yanqing (Dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou).
Chan Master Fadu of Yanqing Mountain in Xiangzhou. A monk asked: "When an earthworm is cut in two, both ends..."
Movement. "The Buddha-nature is at the 'which' end. The Master spreads his two hands (Dongshan Shou separately says: "The one who asks is at the 'which' end").
Chan Master Cihui of Jiufeng (dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou):
Chan Master Cihui of Jiufeng in Fuzhou. Initially at Mount Gui, Guishan ascended the hall and said: "All of you..."

This man possessed only the great capacity (*mahā-vega*), but not the great function (*mahā-prayoga*). The Master [Baizhang] then withdrew and departed. Guishan called out to him, but the Master did not look back.
Guishan said, "This son is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma. (Baofo Zhan said: "It was like a melody; he lost the beginning and forgot the end.
One day, he took his leave of Guishan, saying, "I, your disciple, bid farewell to the Master. Though I shall be a thousand li away, I shall never be apart from you. Guishan...
Shan Dongrong said, "Excellent.
Regarding the Venerable Mi of Jingzhao Prefecture (the Dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou):
after the Venerable Mi of Jingzhao Prefecture—also known as the Seventh Master—had completed his period of study, he returned to his home monastery. There, an elder asked him about the moon.
[He] broke the well-rope; people of the time called it a "snake. I do not know what the Seven Masters called it when they saw the Buddha.
The Master said, "If there were a seeing of the Buddha, that would be the same as [the view of] sentient beings. An old practitioner said, "A peach pit from a thousand years ago...
The Master ordered a monk to go ask Yangshan, "In these times, is awakening still necessary? Yangshan said, "Awakening is not non-existent; however, how..."
Naluo fell into the second head. The Master deeply approved of this. (Letan Qing said: "Mihu’s establishment of the gate was deeply approved by Yangshan as being the 'second head.

As for entering into the profound discourse on principle, which is the 'first head,' he had not yet awakened. Tiantong Hua said: "Mihu wielded the hammer of the fundamental share; Yangshan displayed the business of the sword's edge.

Within the school of teaching, these two elders are surely worthy of honor. But in the lineage of the patch-robed monks, they are both men who deserve a beating. He then instructed a monk to ask Dongshan: "What is that ultimate state? Dongshan—

Mount [Shan] said, "You must question him first before you can understand. The Master also approved of this. A monk asked, "Since ancient times, have the most eminent sages attained the true and ultimate principle?
The Master said, "They have. The monk asked, "As for that true and ultimate principle, how do they attain it?
The Master said, "At that time, Huo Guang sold a counterfeit silver city to the Xiongnu. Who wrote the contract? The monk asked, "Who was it?"
"Such-and-such a person has simply reached a state where his mouth is closed and he cannot speak. The Master said, "On level ground, one teaches a person to act as a guarantor.

(Jingshan Daowu cited these words, and upon reaching the phrase "Who wrote this contract?", he said: "If Jingshan had been that monk at that time, he would have uttered a turning word to stuff this old fellow's mouth shut. But tell me, what word would he have uttered? After a long silence, he said: 'If it were easy to obtain, one would simply look upon it as something trivial.'")
The Monk of Mount Huo in Jinzhou (Dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou).
When a monk from Yangshan arrived, he announced himself as "a great Zen Buddha under Mount Jiyun who has received four blows of the staff; I have come for an audience.
The Master then called for the *vinaya-dhara* to strike the bell. The "Great Zen Buddha" strode forward with rapid steps.

And he departed. (Xuedou Xian said: "Although this fellow changed with the occasion, alas, he has a head but no tail. Zhaojue Qin said: "This fellow carries the 'winter melon seal' of Yangshan upon his back and flaunts it before others.

Had it not been for Huoshan, he would have nearly been deceived. Nevertheless, it is a pity that his command was carried out only halfway. At that time, instead of calling the *karmadāna*, he should have seized him and given him four more strokes of the rattan. Let us listen to this fellow’s doubts for thirty years!)"
Master Yuankang (the dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou).
While Master Yuankang was visiting Shilou, as soon as Shilou saw him, he drew up his legs and sat down.
The Master said, "How perfectly complete your dignified demeanor is! Shilou asked, "What did you just see? The Master replied, "I have been needlessly..."
The man led him away. Shilou said, "It must be like this before it can be called true seeing.
The Master said, "How tragic! How many people have been deceived! Shilou then rose to his feet. The Master said, "He has seen, but he does not move.

Shilou said, "Even with all one's strength, one cannot escape being settled [in this state]. The Master clapped his hands three times. (Nanquan Yuan said, "If the people of the world could decide between these two right and wrongs...")
[He] attained it. (If one attains through severance, they participate in the same realization as others).
The Attendant Wang Jingchu (a dharma heir of Guishan Lingyou):
While the Attendant Wang Jingchu of Xiangzhou was attending to his official duties, Master Mi arrived. The Attendant then raised his brush and showed it to him.
Baizhang said, "Can you still discern the void? The Master threw down his brush, entered his residence, and did not come out again. Baizhang became suspicious.
The following day, he commissioned the Master of Offerings from Gushan to enter and probe his intentions. Baizhang also followed him there, hiding behind a screen to observe.
As soon as the Master of Offerings sat down, he asked, "What words did Master Baizhang have yesterday?"
They did not see each other again. The Official said, "The lion bites the man; the donkey from Han chases the clod. Upon hearing these words, Huimi understood his previous error.
He immediately came forward and laughed heartily, saying, "I understand! I understand! The Official said, "Understanding is certainly not lacking, but try to explain it to me.
Huimi said, "Please, Attendant, bring it forth. The Official then held up a single chopstick. Huimi said, "This wild..."

A fox spirit. The Duke said, "This fellow has seen through [it]. (Daguai Zhe said: "Although Mishu was like this, he could only manage a single peg. Changshi said, 'This fellow has seen through it,' which is very much like watching from a tower and then knocking down the tower.
Daguai is not so; although Changshi was a worldly man, he held the power of life and death in his brush. Mishu was a virtuous teacher of a region, yet he simply could not escape his trap.
At that time, had he waited for him to throw down the brush, he should have simply said: 'I have always suspected this fellow.'"")
Chan Master Guangyong of Nanta, the Fifth Generation of the Southern Lineage of Mount Heng (Dharma Heir of Yangshan Ji).
Chan Master Guangyong of Nanta on Mount Yang at Yuanzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Fengcheng in Yuzhang. He relied upon Yangshan...
He received the tonsure and traveled north to pay his respects to Linji. Returning once more, he attended upon Yangshan. Yangshan asked, "What have you come for?
The Master replied, "To pay my respects to the Master. Yangshan asked, "Have you seen the Master? The Master replied, "I have. Yangshan said:
"Master, how are you like a donkey? The Master said, "When I see the Master, I am not like a Buddha either. Yangshan said, "If you are not like a Buddha, what are you like?
The Master said, "If there were anything to be like, how would that differ from being a donkey? Yangshan was greatly startled and said, "Ordinary and sage are both forgotten;
emotion is exhausted and the essence is revealed. For twenty years I have tested people with this, yet no one has reached a definitive conclusion."
As for "one who has realized," Yangshan took him under his protection. Every time Yangshan pointed to him and said to others, "This boy is a Buddha in flesh.
Chan Master Jingtong of Mount Huo (a dharma heir of Yangshan Jie):
Chan Master Jingtong of Mount Huo in Jinzhou first visited Yangshan. At that time, Yangshan was sitting with his eyes closed. The Master then raised [his hand]...
Raising his right foot, he said, "It is so, it is so. The twenty-eight patriarchs of India were likewise so; the six patriarchs of China were likewise so;
the Master was likewise so; and Jingtong was likewise so. Yangshan rose up and struck him with four willow switches.
Because of this, the Master called himself "The Great Chan Master of the Four Willow Switches beneath Mount Jiyun" (Guizong).
Below [the seat] there was also a Great Chan Master named Zhitong. After he had resided there for some time, a practitioner asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

The Master then performed a prostration. The practitioner said, "Why does the Master prostrate to a layman? The Master replied, "Do you not see it is said: 'The one who bows is the Buddha; the one who receives the bow is also the Buddha'?"
The Venerable Disciple. The Master asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk held up his sitting mat.
The Master said, "A dragon's head, a snake's tail. He asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master struck him. The monk also struck him. The Master said, "You strike me!"
"There is reason; I shall strike you. "There is no reason; the Sangha says nothing. The Master struck him again and drove him out.
When the Master’s fundraising tour was nearing its end, he first prepared firewood in the wilds beyond the city and took leave of his patrons everywhere.

After finishing his meal, he went to the site of the wood and said to his disciples, "Come to report to me at noon. When noon arrived, the Master himself took a torch, climbed onto the stacked wood, and used his alms-bowl lid...
After placing [the image] upon his head, he manifested the form of a halo; holding a staff in his hand, he made the gesture of the *vajra* for subduing Māra and stood amidst red flames.
This was Chan Master Wuzhuo Wenxi (the dharma heir of Yangshan Huiji).
Chan Master Wuzhu Wenxi of Hangzhou was a native of Yuxi in Jiahe.
He traveled to Huayan Temple on Mount Wutai and arrived at the Vajra Cave to pay his respects. There he encountered an old man leading an ox who invited the Master into the temple.
The old man called out, "Juntí! and a boy appeared in response to greet him. The old man released the ox and led the Master up into the hall; the entire structure of the hall was...

He was radiant with a golden hue. The old man sat upon his couch, pointed to an embroidered seat, and bade him sit. The old man asked, "Where have you recently come from? The Master replied, "From the South.
The old man asked, "How is the Buddha-dharma maintained in the South? The Master replied, "In this age of the Dharma's decline, the bhikṣus rarely observe the precepts and regulations.

The old man asked, "How many followers do they have? The Master replied, "Sometimes three hundred, sometimes five hundred. The Master then asked in turn, "As for the Buddha-dharma here in this place..."

"How is the Dharma maintained? The Old Man said, "Dragons and snakes are intermingled; ordinary people and sages dwell together. The Master asked, "How many followers are there? The Old Man said, "Three times three before, and three times three after.

(Fenyang Zhao spoke on behalf [of Xuefeng]: "If you can recognize this, it is like Xuefeng inquiring after Lingyun. An ancient said, "Three times three before, and three times three after. What is the meaning of this? Lingyun said, "Fish in the water; birds on the mountain.

Xuefeng asked, "How do you understand this meaning? Lingyun said, "High enough to shoot with an arrow; deep enough to hook with a line. Jingshan Daokai said: "Had I seen him at that time, I would have simply..."

He said to him, "For a master to maintain the Dharma in such a manner is truly not easy. Tiantong Jie said: "Let us set aside for a moment whether the assembly consists of three hundred or five hundred; consider only this: when Mañjuśrī said, 'Three by three before, three by three after,' how do you explain it?

After a long silence, he said: "The bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet the dust does not stir; the moon pierces the bottom of the pond, yet the water leaves no trace. Chushi Qi said: "Ultimately, as for 'three by three before, three by three after,' how many are there?

Some say: 'As for "three by three before, three by three after," I am not your equal; you yourself understand it well. Weng called to his attendant to serve tea and offer *sukara* (butter-milk), and the Master partook of their flavors.
His mind was suddenly enlightened. The old man picked up a glass goblet and asked, "Is there such a thing as this in the South?

The Master said, "No. The old man said, "What do you usually use to drink tea? The Master had no reply. (Dongshan Jia spoke on his behalf, opening both hands and saying, "Setting aside the question of existence or non-existence for a moment...")

"Borrow this to look at; would it be possible? Caoshan Ji (Ji of Caoshan) spoke on his behalf: "For a long time I have received the Great Being’s brandishing of the sword; why then do you dwell within a single speck of dust? Changqing Ling (Ling of Changqing) spoke on his behalf:

"If it were so, it would be like a foolish guest advising his host. Langye Jue (Jue of Langye) said: "If it is indeed so, one may say he snatches food from the tiger's mouth. If it is not so, it is like moving a boat to become familiar with the currents and raising the oars to navigate the waves.

Fenyang Zhao (Zhao of Fenyang) said: "Thank you for your inquiry. The Master, seeing that the sun was already late, asked the old man: "May I stay for one night? The old man replied: "Do you have a mind of attachment?"
He was there, but he was not permitted to stay overnight. The Master said, "I have no mind of attachment. The Old Man asked, "Have you ever received the precepts?

The Master replied, "I have received them long ago. The Old Man said, "If you have no mind of attachment, what use is it to receive the precepts? The Master took his leave. The Old Man ordered a youth to see him out.
The Master asked the youth, "Three by three before, three by three after—how many is that? The youth called out to him.
"Venerable Sir," the teacher replied, "Yes. The boy asked, "How much is it? (Dongshan Jia said: "If you wish to observe the father, first observe the son.

Fenyang Zhao, at the point where [the teacher] said he would receive the precepts, remarked: "He regrets his previous words. At the point where [the teacher] asked the boy how much it was, he remarked:

"He recognizes you. The teacher again asked, "What place is this? The boy replied, "This is the Vajra Cave Prajñā Temple. The teacher was moved with sorrow and realized that the old man was none other than Mañjuśrī.
[He said: "I shall not see you again. He then prostrated before the youth and requested a word as a parting gift.
The youth spoke this verse: "No anger on the face is the offering; No anger in the mouth emits the wondrous fragrance;
No anger in the heart is the true treasure— Stainless and untainted, it is the eternal reality. Having finished speaking, Junti and the temple vanished together. Thereupon, the Master remained there.

He traveled to Mount Wutai. In the third year of the Xiántóng era, he went to Guānyīn in Hóngzhōu and visited Yǎngshān, where his mind was suddenly awakened and his realization accorded with the master’s.
Yǎngshān appointed him as the steward (*diǎnzuo*). Once, Mañjuśrī appeared atop the rice-pot;
the Master struck it with his rice-stirring paddle and said, "Mañjuśrī is Mañjuśrī, and Wénxǐ is Wénxǐ. Thereupon Mañjuśrī spoke this verse: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip."
When the sweet melon reaches the stem, it is sweet. Having practiced for three great kalpas, you were nevertheless disparaged by this old monk.
One day, a strange monk came to seek alms-food. The Master set aside his own portion and gave it to him. Yangshan, having foreknowledge of this, asked:
"Just now a person of the fruit-stage arrived; did you give him food? The Master replied: "I set aside my own share to bestow it upon him. Yangshan said: "You have brought about great benefit."
The Monk of Miling in Hongzhou (a dharma heir of Jingshan Yi).
The Monk of Miling in Hongzhou often said: "There is nothing beyond this. A monk asked: "I do not yet understand what that is."
"There is nothing beyond this. The Master said, "It does not go outside of this. Later, a monk asked Changqing, "Why is it that it does not go outside of this?
Changqing said, "What do you intend to call it?"
Chan Master Gu of Shuangfeng (Dharma heir of Shuangfeng).
Chan Master Gu of Shuangfeng in Fuzhou was originally a lecturer on the sutras. He went to visit the former Chan Master Shuangfeng, who asked him, "Virtuous One, where do you reside?
He replied, "In the city. Shuangfeng said, "Do you ever think of me, the old monk? He replied, "I always do."

He thought of Master Shishuang Qingzhu, but had no means to pay his respects. Shuangfeng said, "This very one who is thinking is you, Venerable Sir. The Master understood this intent from that moment on;
he immediately ceased his lecture series and attended upon him for several years. Later, he went to Shishuang, where he simply followed along with the assembly.
He no longer requested further instruction. The assembly remarked, "The former attendant once received the seal of transmission from Shuangfeng; this has often been heard by Shishuang.
Shishuang wished to interrogate him regarding his realization but had not yet found the opportunity.
When the Master took his leave, Shishuang followed him out the gate with a whisk and called out, "Former Attendant! The Master turned his head, and Shishuang said, "If you try to grasp it..."
"Off! This attachment is immediately deviant. Not to intend it is not [the truth]. Nor should you form a conceptual understanding.

Only one who 'knows there is' can know it; no one else can. Go well, go well. The Master responded, "Yes, yes," and immediately departed. Shortly thereafter, Shuangfeng passed away, and the Master succeeded him as abbot.
A monk asked, "When the Master took his leave of Shishuang at that time, what was the meaning of Shishuang’s words?"
"How is it? The Master said, "He simply told me not to cling to right and wrong. (Baoci then said: "Now tell me, did he understand Shishuang’s meaning or not?")
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao (Dharma Heir of Nanta Yong), the Sixth Generation under Mount Nanyue.
Chan Master Huiqing of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou was a native of the kingdom of Silla. Once, while ascending the hall, he took up his staff and showed it to the assembly.
The assembly said: "If you have a staff, I will give you a staff; if you have no staff, I will take yours away.
[He] leaned on the staff and descended from the seat. ○ The Master said to the assembly: "I am twenty-eight years old."
Arriving at Yangshan, he went to visit Nanta. Seeing him ascend the hall, Nanta said, "All you people here:
if you were a true man, as soon as you emerged from your mother’s womb, you would let out a lion’s roar—would that not be so? At these words, my body and mind came to rest.
He remained there for five years.
Regarding Chan Master Quanfu of Qinghua in Yuezhou:
Chan Master Quanfu of Qinghua in Yuezhou was a native of Kunshan in Wu Commandery. He first visited Nanta, where Nanta...
The questioner asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From Ezhou. Nan-ta asked, "What is the name of the Magistrate of Ezhou?
The Master said, "I do not dare to offend him while under his jurisdiction. Nan-ta said, "In this way, you do not fear him.
The Master said, "A man of great character—why must you test me? Nan-ta laughed heartily and subsequently granted him certification.
The Seventh Generation under Nanyue:
Chan Master Jiche of Yingzhou (Dharma Heir of Bajiao Qing).
Chan Master Jiche of Bajiao Mountain in Yingzhou first visited Fengxue, who asked him, "What is the Correct [Path]?"
Fayan. The Master said, "A lump of clay. Fengxue marveled at this. Next, he visited the former master Bajiao.

When Bajiao ascended the hall, he cited Yangshan’s saying, "Two mouths, neither has a tongue; this is my school's fundamental principle. At these words, the Master attained a sudden and complete realization.
*Jiaowai biezhuan*, Volume Eleven and Volume Twelve (Yunmen School),
Sixth Generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Yunmen Wenyan (Dharma heir of Xuefeng Cun).
Chan Master Wenyan of Guangfeng Monastery on Mount Yunmen in Shaoyou was a native of Jiaxing. He possessed a keen nature and innate wisdom from birth.
His wisdom and eloquence were divinely bestowed. Upon reaching adulthood, he shaved his head and received full ordination at the altar in Piling.
He attended Master Zhicheng for several years, thoroughly investigating the Vinaya-piṭaka. Because he felt his own realization was not yet clear, he went to consult with Master Muzhou.
As soon as Muzhou saw him approaching, he closed the door. The Master knocked on the door, and Muzhou asked, "Who is it? The Master replied, "It is I. Muzhou asked, "What are you doing? The Master...
The Master said, "My own matter is not yet clear; I beg the Teacher for instruction. Muzhou opened the door, and upon seeing him, he closed it again.
The Master did this, knocking on the door for three consecutive days. On the third day, Muzhou opened the door, and the Master pushed his way inside.
Muzhou immediately seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! As the Master hesitated, Muzhou pushed him out and said, "A wheel-rut from the time of Qin!"
He then closed the door, injuring the Master’s foot. From this, the Master attained realization. Muzhou directed him to visit Xuefeng.
Upon arriving at Xuefeng’s manor, the Master saw a monk and asked, "Elder, are you going up the mountain today? The monk replied, "Yes.
The Master said, "Please deliver a kōan to the Abbot for me, but you must not say it was my words."
The monk replied, “I have. The Master said, “When you reach the mountain, see the Abbot ascend the hall.
As soon as the assembly has gathered, go out, clasp his neck with your hands, stand there, and say: ‘Old man, why do you not cast off this iron cangue from your neck?
The monk followed the Master’s instructions exactly. When Xuefeng saw the monk speak in this manner, he descended from his seat, seized him by the chest, and said, “Speak quickly!”
"Quickly, Master! The monk had no reply. Xuefeng pushed him away and said, "That was not your words.
The monk said, "It was my words. Xuefeng said, "Attendant, bring the rope and staff! The monk said, "It was not my words;
it was an elder from Zhejiang on the manor who instructed me to come and speak thus. Xuefeng said, "Everyone, go to the manor to welcome five hundred [monks]."
A good spiritual friend arrived. On the following day, the Master went to Xuefeng. As soon as Xuefeng saw him, he said, "Why have you reached such a state?
The Master then bowed his head. From that point on, they were in accord. Having studied and refined their understanding for many years, Xuefeng secretly transmitted the seal of the school to him.

The Master left the mountain range and traveled everywhere to visit various masters, investigating and exhausting their diverse approaches; his sharp eloquence was formidable and peerless. His reputation spread throughout the world.
What he heard was recorded. Later, he arrived at Lingshu Temple. In a mysterious way, this accorded with the prediction that Master Zhisheng would receive him as his head seat (*śrāmaṇera*).
Initially, when Zhisheng resided at Lingshu for twenty years, he did not formally appoint a head seat. He would often say: "My head seat is here;
my head seat is tending the oxen; my head seat is traveling on pilgrimage. One day, he ordered the bell to be struck to welcome the head seat outside the main gate.

The assembly went out to welcome him. When the Master arrived, they invited him directly into the Head Seat’s Quarters (*shouzuo liao*) to unpack his belongings (as seen in the *Renyantianmu*, Chapter on Lingshu).

Later, the Lord of Guangzhou commanded the Master to take up residence at Lingshu. On the day he opened the hall for formal preaching, the Lord of Guangzhou came in person and said, "I, your disciple, request your instruction.

The Master replied, "Before one's eyes, there is no other path" (Fayan Yi’s alternative reading says: "It must not fail to benefit others"). [The Master] then cited the passage concerning the World-Honored One’s first birth.
He pointed one finger toward heaven and one finger toward the earth, walked seven steps, and looked around in the four directions, saying:

"In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am honored. The Master said: "Had I seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, for the sake of peace throughout the world.
Later, while the Master was attending a vegetarian feast in the Wende Hall, there was Attendant Ju.
Question: "Is the fruit on the numinous tree ripe yet? The Master said: "In what year did you come to believe that the Way is born? [Case] Xuefeng said:
"The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great Dharma Wheel upon the flames. The Master said: "The flames preach the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods;
the Buddhas of the three periods stand upon the ground and listen. (Huanglong Xin said: "Xuefeng and Yunmen vie with one another in brilliance. When the firewood is exhausted... [text ends])

The fire is extinguished. Where do the Buddhas of the three periods of time go to listen? Do not linger sitting in the depths of the white clouds; take care that cold ashes do not burn you to death. Tiantong Huahua said: "The Buddhas of the three periods of time and the flames preach the Dharma together;

the flames burn the Buddhas of the three periods of time to death. Yuansou Duan said: "If you can realize it upon hearing Xuefeng’s words, you will make onlookers laugh. If you can realize it upon hearing Yunmen’s words, you will not even be able to save yourself. If you can realize it upon hearing Ying’an’s words..."
"The eyebrows and whiskers of all people throughout the great earth will fall out. A monk asked Lingshu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Lingshu remained silent.

After he passed away, his disciples were drafting an inscription for his memorial stele and wished to include this exchange. They asked the Master, "How should we record the Master's silence on the stele?
The Master replied, "The Master ascended the hall [and said]: 'The Buddha-dharma is indeed very much present; it is simply...'"

[The Master] said, "Your tongue is short. After a long silence, he said, "It is long. Once, while performing communal labor carrying firewood, the Master picked up a piece of wood, tossed it down, and said, "The entire Tripitaka speaks only of this.
Seeing a monk measuring rice, he asked, "How many Bodhidharma’s eyes are there in that rice basket?
The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf, saying, "A peck-measure cannot exhaust them. The Master was once—
One day, [Dayu] thrust his hand into the mouth of a wooden lion and cried out, "Bite me! Bite me! [Nanquan] shouted, "Help! Help! (Rouzong Ruo offered a substitute saying:

The Master said, "How many patriarchs did you mow down? He replied, "Three hundred. The Master said, "In the morning they strike three thousand; in the evening they strike eight hundred. "East..."

"The handle of the ladle in my house is long; the handle of the ladle in the western house is short. Again, what about this? The *zhisui* (steward) remained silent. The Master then struck him. Yunmen Zhe said:

"The *zhisui* remained silent—there are three hundred patriarchs who can testify to this. Although Yunmen’s command was carried out, the staff nonetheless lacked an eye. Do not go to the yamen with your topknot still tied. In the space of a single thought, he struck the meditation seat (*zuoju*). The monk then rubbed his forehead and made the gesture of gazing at the moon. The Master said, "If you continue like this, you will lose your eyesight in the future. The monk... [passed away].

Chan Master Qingbing of Dongshan was a native of the Li clan of Quanzhou. He studied under Yunmen, who asked him, "Where did you depart from today?
He replied, "Huilin. Yunmen raised his staff and said, "Master Huilin goes in this manner."
"Do you see? Yunmen asked. The master replied, "I deeply appreciate this question. Yunmen looked to his left and right and simply smiled.
From that time on, the master entered the inner room [for formal training] and attained realization. (Liang Shouzhang, Dharma heir of Yunmen Wenyan.)
The Venerable Lang of Mount Yunmen in Shaoyou had studied at lecture halls since childhood. He once heard a monk ask Yunmen, "What is the phrase that penetrates the Dharmakāya?
Yunmen replied, "Hide one's body within the Big Dipper. The Master could not fathom its subtle meaning, so he went to visit Yunmen.
As soon as Yunmen saw him, he seized him and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master hesitated; Yunmen pushed him away.
He then presented a verse, saying: "Yunmen towers high, the white clouds hang low; the current is swift, and the fish dare not dwell.

Since you have entered the gate, his understanding is already known; why trouble yourself again to tread through the mud? Thereupon, the Master attained great enlightenment and immediately prostrated himself.
From then on, he served Yunmen as his head seat (upādhyāya).
The Eighth Generation under Nanyue:
Master Dali of Shaoyang (Dharma Heir of Baiyun Xiang).
When Master Dali of Shaoyang first visited Baiyun, Baiyun raised his fist and said, "Lately, I have not been like this."
"Ma-ye. The Master received this instruction and prostrated. From then on, he entered the inner quarters.
Regarding the Venerable Baohua of Lianzhou (a dharma heir of Baiyun Xiang):
A monk once asked the Venerable Baohua of Lianzhou about Dayong, who had said: "After receiving the six-zhu robe bestowed by Heaven and putting it on..."
"How shall I repay the imperial grace? Dayong replied, "Upon coming, I donned the three-fold patched robe; upon returning, I hung my six-zhu garment.

When the Master heard this, he said, "This old frozen leper speaks such words! Upon hearing this, Dayong sent someone to deliver a message, saying, "How is it that your karmic ties as a slave have not yet been severed?
The Master said, "I threw a brick only because I hoped to draw out a jade. ○ The Master.
On another occasion, he wore a crown and said to the assembly, "If you say this is a layperson, yet his body is draped in the *kāṣāya* robe;
if you say this is a monk, yet his head wears a crown. The assembly was speechless.
Chan Master Yue of Mount Yue (Dharma heir of Baiyun Xiang).
Chan Master Yue of Mount Yue in Shaoyou City first visited Baiyun. Baiyun asked, "What practice do you engage in?
He replied, "I recite the *Peacock Sūtra*. Baiyun said, "A fine young man from a good family, yet following after birds and beasts. When the Master heard this, he [attained realization].
He was struck with wonder by these words and subsequently attached himself [to the master] for a long time, until he finally attained realization of the essential meaning.
Regarding Ledu Lingcheng San-sheng (a successor of Baling Jian):
Master Ledu Lingcheng San-sheng was once asked by Chan Master Zhimen Kuan, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From the water."
When Qingyue appeared, Zhimen said, "Go ask him well. The Master said, "My short jacket has not been dyed black. Zhimen said, "Go drink tea.
The Master had a verse regarding the meaning of the Westward Journey, which says: "A monk asked me about the meaning of the Westward Journey;
I spoke of my dwelling in the mountains for seven or eight years. My straw sandals have only three holes; My hempen robe has been patched twice at the shoulders. East..."
Whenever I see West Hermitage Snow, The long-flowing stream descends while the spring source ascends.
After the white clouds have dispersed at midnight, A single orb of bright moon arrives before my bed.
Chan Master Liangya of Fuyan (the first Dharma heir of Dongshan).
Chan Master Liangya of Fuyan in Tanzhou served as the First Seat at Mount Dong. During a period of formal inquiry, a monk stepped forward and asked, "What is the Buddha?
Dongshan replied, "Three pounds of flax. After the session ended, Dongshan went to the master’s quarters and said to him:
[The Master] said, "Would I have been able to answer this monk's question today? [Dongshan] said, "It happened to coincide with my shaving my head.
Dongshan said, "So you were making such a show of it! He then shook out his sleeves and departed. The Master said, "This old fellow thought he had seen through me;
he could not handle this koan. Thereupon, he composed a verse and presented it, saying: "A cow's head painted in five colors, With a forehead marked in gold."
On a clear spring day in the second month, all the farmers took this as their standard. On the Cold Food Festival, they celebrated the New Year with three or five hundred pieces of iron currency.
Dongshan saw this and deeply approved.
Chan Master Muzhou of Qianming (the first dharma heir of Dongshan).
Chan Master Muzhou of Qianming in Yuezhou asked Dongshan, "What is it like when the mechanism is halted and the reward is withdrawn? Dongshan said:
"Playing puppets at the bottom of the water. The Master asked, "Who is it that watches and enjoys this? Dongshan said, "Those who have stilled their mechanisms and ceased their appreciation.
The Master said, "If that is so, then those who know the music do not harmonize with one another. Dongshan asked, "As for the matter of those who know the music, how is it?"
The Master said, "The great month has thirty days. Dongshan said, "Not yet; speak further.
The Master said, "I deserve to receive the heavy staff from the Master's hand. Dongshan then desisted.
Chan Master Yunhuo of Xifeng (Dharma Heir of Qingliang Ming).
Chan Master Yunhuo of Xifeng in Jizhou was the son of the Zeng family of that prefecture. In his youth, he visited various masters;

later, he went to see Qingliang and asked, "How was it before the Buddha appeared in the world? Qingliang replied, "Clouds obscure the trees at the gate of the sea. [Yunhuo] said, "After he appeared in the world..."
"What then? Qingliang said, "I shall split open Mount Cakravāḍa. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. Qingliang certified his realization.
This was the ninth generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong (Dharma heir of Wenshu Zhen).
Chan Master Dongshan Xiaocong of Ruizhou was at Yunju while traveling; serving as the head of the lamp-hall, he saw a monk and said:
"The Great Sage of Sizhou is nearby, appearing in Yangzhou. Someone asked, "Since he is the Great Sage of Sizhou, why does he appear in Yangzhou?
The Master said, "A gentleman loves wealth, but he takes it by the right way.
Later, a monk reported this to the Hermit Xiang of Lotus Peak. The Hermit was greatly amazed and said, "The descendants of Yunmen still exist!"
At midnight, he gazed toward Yunju and paid his respects. Once, while the Master was carrying firewood up the mountain, he encountered a monk on the path who asked, "There is wood upon the mountain;
why are you carrying it down? The Master set the wood down on the ground and said, "Do you understand?

The monk replied, "I do not. The Master said, "I need this to burn. *Shilin Gong’s Verse says:* *Firewood and embers, laboring as they are borne upon the body;* *Meeting on a narrow path, there is no room for debate.* *Faint smoke and setting sun beyond the green mountains,* *A ground filled with fallen leaves.*
Difficult to erase the marks of axe and hatchet. ○ The Master personally planted ten thousand pines on the Eastern Ridge and constantly recited the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
Consequently, the people of the mountain named that ridge "Vajra. While he was planting the pines, Chan Master Bao arrived. At that time, Bao had come personally from the Fifth Patriarch.
The Master asked, "How do you speak the phrase for ascending the ridge? Bao replied, "It would kill me with its urgency."

The Master leaned on his hoe and scolded him, saying, "Where did you get this? Are you interpreting it according to the words? Seeing that [the monk] had asked about climbing the ridge, the Master immediately said, "I am short of breath;
the Buddha-dharma has instead become widely disseminated. Bao requested to speak in his stead. The Master said, "This gasping for breath will kill a man! One day, the Master felt unwell.
He ascended the hall to take leave of the assembly and recited a verse on the Dharmakāya, saying: "In practicing Chan and studying the Way, do not be vague."
"Mang! You have thoroughly penetrated the Dharma-body of the Northern Dipper’s Treasury. Now that I am old, decrepit, and extremely frail, I lack the strength to deliberate with others.
Only my spade understands my intent; when planting pine trees, it ascends once more to the Diamond Realm. Having finished speaking, he passed away in stillness.
Chan Master Chongxian of Xuedou (Dharma Heir of Zhimen Zu).

Chan Master Chongxian of Xuedou in Mingzhou was a native of the Li clan from Suining Prefecture. He had studied the sutras at lecture halls, investigating principles and exhausting the profound mysteries.

His interrogations were as swift as charging hooves, and his wit and eloquence were unrivaled; all recognized him as a vessel of the Dharma, and everyone pointed him toward a pilgrimage to the South. He first visited...
Zhimen then extended his inquiry, saying, "If you do not give rise to a single thought, how can there be any fault? Zhimen called for the Master to come forward;
as soon as the Master drew near, Zhimen struck him across the mouth with his whisk. As the Master was about to open his mouth, Zhimen struck him again.
The Master attained sudden enlightenment. Zen Master Dongshan Chong would always ask newly arrived monks, "What is the meaning of the 'Water-Ox' of Mount Huangbo?
Most who answered failed to accord with Dongshan’s intent. When the Master arrived, he was questioned by him as before.
The Master said, "This will serve as a banner for future generations. Dongshan was about to speak when the Master took his sitting mat, gave it a single sweep, and departed.
Dongshan called out, "Wait a moment, Venerable! The Master replied, "I have not yet entered the hall. Later, the Master served as the guest prefect at Dalong.
One day he asked: "The one who speaks and the one who remains silent are not it; that which is neither speech nor silence is also not it. All together, they are entirely not it.
When the Great Function is set aside and manifests before you, people know it exists. I wonder, Great Dragon, how is it? Great Dragon said:
The Master said, "This old fellow has crumbled like ice dissolving. Da Long said, "I grant you thirty blows.
The Master bowed and returned to the assembly. Da Long then called for the monk who had just been questioning him.
As the Master stepped out, Da Long asked, "Why did I crumble like ice dissolving? The Master replied, "It is only now that I see my own failure."
Dàlóng changed his expression and said, "I cannot bear it, I cannot bear it! Master, you should stop. Later, he recounted this to National Teacher Yǎ of Nányuè.
Yǎ said, "Dàlóng, why did you not give him his proper fodder? The Master said, "The National Teacher must continue his travels.
Bǎohuā, the attendant, came to visit the Master. The Master asked, "Bǎohuā, how many people are in your assembly? The attendant replied, "It is unnecessary for the Master [to ask]."
It was still like this. The Master said, "I am asking you properly; why are you jumping about? The attendant said, "You must not let him off.
The Master said, "A true lion cub. After they had finished drinking tea, the Master grabbed him and said, "Just now you were so discourteous.
The attendant hesitated, and the Master gave him a slap, saying, "Go back and report this clearly to Baohua."

When the Head Seat Zong arrived, the Master was about to exchange formal greetings. The Master called him back, saying, "Since you already know how to believe, you must now surrender with folded hands.
Zong said, "Today I have failed. The Master said, "Before the blade has even been applied, the thief's body has already been exposed.
Zong said, "This is killing me with indignation! The Master said, "A defeated general is not executed. Zong said, "That is so. The Master said, "Prostrate yourself."
[Zong] said, "Thirty years from now, there will be someone who brings this up. The Master said, "I have already let you pass.
The Court Editor, Layman Zenghui, was serving as the Governor of Chizhou during the Tianxi era. One day, they met at Jingde Temple.

He cited the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue* to investigate [the teachings], using the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* to cross-examine the Master regarding the sayings of the Chan school. The Master said, "This [teaching] does not even accord with..."
Regarding the teachings of the vehicles, [Master] Zeng compared them to the *Zhongyong* and the *Daxue*. A scholar of heterodox learning sought a direct and swift way to comprehend this matter;

snapping his fingers once, he said, "Just realize it in this way. Under these words, he attained the essential meaning. At the beginning of the Tiānshèng era, when Zeng was governing Sìmíng, he sent letters and gifts to welcome the Master.
Once the Master had been appointed to Xuědòu and arrived there, Zeng said, "Recently, I [discussed] this with Elder Qīng..."
They were discussing the story of Zhaozhou testing the old woman. "I do not know for certain," they said, "whether there was actually a point where he saw her through.
The Master asked, "What did Elder Qing say? They replied, "He said, 'Once again, you have gone this way. The Master said, "Elder Qing, let that pass for now.
You scholars should know that throughout the world, no patch-robed monk can escape from the trap set by this old woman."
Ceng said, "There is another way to speak of this matter here. Had Zhaozhou not exposed her, the old woman would have suffered a lifetime of injustice.
The Master said, "She has been exposed. Ceng laughed loudly.
Chan Master Jipeng of Yungai (Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zhimen Zu).
Chan Master Jipeng of Yungai in Tanzhou first visited Chan Master Shuangquan Ya. Ya instructed him to serve as attendant to Attendant Ke.
Yaya showed him the koan of the *bānyang* (plantain) staff. For a long time, he failed to gain any realization. One day, while Yaya was warming himself by the fire, the Master stood in attendance.
Yaya suddenly asked, "Regarding the koan of the staff—try bringing it up so we may deliberate upon it together.
As the Master was about to speak, Yaya took up the fire tongs and struck him with them. At that moment, the Master attained a sudden and great awakening.
Chan Master Zhixian of Beichen (Dharma heir of Fuyan Ya).

On the evening of the New Year’s Eve, Chan Master Zhixian of Beichen in Tanzhou gave a small-scale sermon, saying: "The year has ended and the age has reached its limit; there is nothing more to give."
"The various people divide the year’s harvest; this old monk cooks it. With one white ox roaming in the open field, he steams millet rice and boils wild vegetable soup over a fire of split logs.
After everyone has eaten, they perform the village dance (*muratari*). Why? To avoid depending on others’ doorways or leaning against their walls.
When called 'Sir' by the people of the age, he simply descends from his seat and returns to the abbot’s quarters. It is deep night."
The rector entered the abbot’s quarters and inquired after his well-being, saying, "There are officials from the county who have arrived to summon the Master. The Master asked, "What for, rector?
The rector replied, "They say the Master slaughters oxen and does not pay for the hides and horns. The Master then pulled off his head-cloth.
He threw it onto the ground, and the *vinaya-dhara* (ritual master) picked it up. The Master leaped down from his meditation seat, grabbed him by the chest, and shouted, "Thief! Thief!
The *vinaya-dhara* took his hat and placed it over the Master's head, saying, "The weather is cold; please take this back, Master. The Master laughed heartily.
The *vinaya-dhara* then went out. At that time, Fachang was serving as the attendant. The Master looked at Fachang and said, "This fellow..."
"Consider this: how is it? Fachang said, "Paper is expensive in Tanzhou; one document shall suffice to cover it all.
Chan Master Shixian of Kaixian (a dharma heir of Deshan Yuan) was from Linjiang Prefecture.
He went to visit Chan Master Deshan, who was then at Mount [Deshan]. Upon seeing Deshan...
In the hall, he looked around at the assembly and said, "The lion yawns; the elephant king turns his head back. Suddenly, the Master attained realization.
He entered the room to present his understanding, to which Deshan asked, "How do you understand this? The Master turned his head back and said, "A donkey in the back garden is eating grass."
Deshan approved of this. Later, he arrived at Xuedou. When Xuedou spoke with him, he was delighted by his transcendence over Yixian and remarked, "The Way-farer Yixian roams freely across the sea."
Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun of the Tenth Generation under Nanyue (Dharma Heir of Dongshan Cong).
Chan Master Yunju Xiaoshun of Nankang Commandery was a native of Ruizhou. He studied under Dongshan. One day, as he was traveling to Wu...
Chang went out to beg for alms. His first call was upon Layman Liu. At that time, the Master was young and, unaware of the Layman’s extensive training, treated him with some degree of casualness.
The Layman said, "I have a question for you, old man. If our views accord, I shall open my scrolls; if they do not, I ask that you return to the mountain.
He then asked, "How is it when an ancient mirror has not yet been polished? The Master replied, "Black as lacquer. The Layman said, "After it has been polished..."

"How is it? the Master asked. The layman replied, "It illuminates heaven and earth. The layman then gave a long bow and said, "Please, let the Master return to the mountain," whereupon he brushed out his sleeves and entered his residence.
The Master felt dejected and immediately returned to Dongshan. When Dongshan asked for the reason, the Master recounted the events in detail.
Dongshan said, "Ask me, and I will answer you. The Master posed the preceding question. Dongshan said, "It is not far from here to Hanyang.
The Master then offered the latter part of the verse. Dongshan said, "Before Huanghelou is Yingwuzhou. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. [He] ascended the hall [and said]:
"In various quarters there are those who play with the heads of snakes, stroke the tails of tigers, leap across the great ocean, and walk upon the edge of a sword."
Hiding his body within. At Yunju here, one washes one’s feet with hot water on a cold day; at night, one takes off one’s sandals and sleeps;
in the early morning, one immediately fashions straw sandals. When the wind blows down the fence, one calls for laborers to split rattan and bind it back up.
Cuiyan Zhen pointed to his chest and constantly scolded his teacher for preaching "unconcerned Chan" (wushi chan). Master Shishuang Yong sent someone to deliver a message, saying: "Shun..."
Regarding Dongshan’s realization of the "ancient mirror" kōan: how could this possibly be called "teaching the Zen of non-action"?

You, by criticizing him, have lost one of your own eyes yourself. Upon hearing this, the Master (Yunju) composed a verse: Yunju does not understand Zen; He washes his feet and goes up to bed to sleep.
The winter melon is straight and blunt; The bottle gourd is curved and bent. Master Yong also composed a verse: Shishuang does not understand...
Chan. Washing his feet, he went up to bed to sleep. His pillow fell to the ground, smashing the monastery’s brick.
Chan Master Chishō of Furi (Dharma heir of Dongshan Cóng), Chan Master Chishō of Furi in Hangzhou:
a native of the Li family of Tanjin in Tengzhou. At nineteen, he began his travels to seek teachers. Throughout...
He visited Zhishi and received the Dharma from Dongshan. At night, the Master would carry an image of Avalokiteśvara upon his head and recite its name;

he would not sleep until he had completed one hundred thousand recitations. He composed the *Yuanjiao lun* (Treatise on the Origin of the Teachings) in over one hundred thousand words. Later, he resided at the Yongan Aranya.

He presented the *Chánmén dìngzǔ tú* (Diagram of the Patriarchs of the Chan Gate), the *Chuánfǎ zhèngzōng jì* (Record of the True Lineage of the Transmission of the Dharma), and the *Fǔjiào biān* (Compendium for Aiding the Teaching) to the Emperor.

Upon reading them, Emperor Rénzōng sighed with admiration and ordered the Court of the Transmission of the Law (*Chuánfǎ Yuàn*) to compile them for inclusion in the Tripitaka. An imperial edict was issued to honor him, and he was granted the title Mingjiao (Illuminating Teaching).
Prime Minister Hàn Qí and Grand Councilor Ōuyáng Xiū both invited him for audiences and treated him with the highest respect. When he returned eastward in the fourth year of the Xīníng era...
On the fourth day of the sixth month, he rose at dawn and wrote a verse, saying: "The moon is bright in the late night; today I joyfully walk alone.
I shall not follow the old man of Daimai, greedily pursuing the cries of the flying squirrel. At midnight, he passed away.
Xu Shi, the Prefectural Governor of Hongzhou (a dharma heir of Dongshan Ceng).
Having attended upon Dongshan, he attained the Eye of the True Dharma. One day, while sitting with Letai Cheng and Shanglan Pu, Cheng asked:
"I have heard the Langzhong say: 'Sitting through the night on the Cloud-Linked Rock; planting spring pines amidst the rain.'"
"What did you say to Dongshan at that time? The Master said, "The office has been dismissed early today.
Cheng said, "I heard you replied, 'The Great Sage of Sizhou appears in Yangzhou'—is that so? The Master said, "Serve another cup of tea. Cheng said, "His reputation is not in vain.
The Master said, "When will you, Reverend, return to the mountain? Cheng said, "Today I was seen through by Shanglan."
"Pu! [Fuhui] gave a shout. Cheng said, "It must be you who can do it. Gong said, "When the boat cannot be saved, one breaks the bailer.
Master Huailian of Yuyang (a dharma heir of Leduan Cheng), Chan Master Huailian Dajue of Mount Yuyang in Mingzhou, was a native of the Chen family of Longxi in Zhangzhou. One day—

While washing his face, he splashed water upon the ground; a slight awakening arose within him, and he immediately set out in search of a teacher. He traveled far to the Dharma seat at Letan, where he attained realization and received formal certification.
He served as a disciple for over ten years. During the Renshou era, Emperor Renzong summoned him to the Huacheng Hall for an audience and inquired about the essential meaning of the Buddha-dharma.
The Emperor bestowed upon him the title Chan Master Dajue. Later, the Emperor dispatched an imperial messenger to ask him: "Just as you have departed..."
When the attendant holding the fly-whisk stood up to pose a difficult question, the Master replied with a verse: "Having joints, yet not bamboo; The three stars and the crescent moon palace.

One person dwells beneath the sun, Not the same as the common crowd. The Emperor read this and was greatly pleased. Shortly thereafter, he dispatched a messenger to bestow upon the Master a camphor bowl.
After the Master had expressed his gratitude, he held up the bowl and said: "In our Dharma, we wear dyed robes and use earthenware [bowls]."
Tiěshí deemed this bowl unlawful and subsequently burned it. When the imperial messenger returned and reported this, the Emperor sighed in admiration without end.
He then ordered the Head Seat Lítāo (a dharma heir of Lètán Chéng) to address the matter.
Having long studied under Lètán, Lètán had once asked him: "The Patriarch came from the West to transmit the mind-seal alone."
"Directly pointing at the human mind, seeing one's nature and becoming a Buddha—how do you understand this? The Master said, "I do not understand.
Letan said, "Before you left the household life, what did you do? The Master said, "I herded oxen. Letan said, "How did you herd them?
The Master said, "In the early morning I rode out; in the evening I rode back. Letan said, "That is truly excellent."
"No. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and immediately composed this verse: "Letting go of the cow-ropes, I have left the home-life;
Shaving off beard and hair, I don the kashaya robe. When someone asks me about the meaning of my coming from the West, I hold my staff across my shoulder and shout: 'La-li-la!'"
Chan Master Chenghao of Yüquan (Dharma Heir of Beita Guangfa).
Chan Master Chenghao of Yüquan in Jingmen Commandery was a native of Danling in Meizhou. While traveling to study under various masters, he visited Beita.
He revealed the essential points of the enlightened mind and attained the Samādhi of Great Sovereignty.

He wrote the names of the patriarchs of successive generations upon a "calf-thighed loincloth" (a cloth worn between the legs), saying: "Only Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra are slightly superior. He then tied this onto his sash;

thus, the monastic community referred to it as the "White Cloth Loincloth. A local monk also attempted to imitate him, but when the Master saw him, he rebuked him, saying: "What kind of Way do you possess?"
How could one dare to treat this principle as a mere joke? To do so would be beyond remedy, leading only to spitting up blood. Soon after, at Lumen (Deer Gate), he passed away just as he had said.
Zhang Wujin, while serving as an envoy to the Jingxi Nanlu circuit, went to pay his respects to him.

He subsequently established the Dharma at Dayang in Yingzhou. At that time, the abbot of Guyin was privately pleased by this. When the Master accepted the invitation and ascended the seat, he said: "I was at Guyin..."
In the tenth year of the Yìn era, I have never drunk a single drop of water from Gǔyǐn, nor chewed a single grain of rice from Gǔyǐn.
If you do not understand this, come to Dàyáng and I shall break it open for you. Carrying his staff, the Master descended from the seat and departed with an air of pride.
The Master presented a verse on the Dharmakāya: One night the rain poured down in torrents, Toppling the grape arbor. The administrators, the heads of departments, and the practitioners—
Human effort: that which supports and props up. Proping and propping, supporting and buttressing, until daybreak—still, as before, a pitiful sight.
Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai (Dharma heir of Xuedou Xian).
Chan Master Tianyi Yihuai of Yuezhou was a native of the Chen family of Leqing, Yongjia. During the Tiānshèng era, he took the [monastic] examination...
Having received his transmission, he went to pay his respects to Jinluan Shanye; both the prefecture and the province granted him their seal of approval.
He then traveled from Luoyang to Longmen and returned once more to the capital. There, he suddenly encountered Yan Fahua, who patted the Master’s back and said, “Yunmen and Linji have departed.
Upon arriving in Gusu, he paid homage to Mingjue at Cuifeng. Mingjue asked, “What is your name? He replied, “Yihuai. Mingjue—
[The monk] said, "Why not name me 'Hua-yi' (Embracing Righteousness)? Mingjue said, "You attained it at that time. [Mingjue] asked, "Who gave you this name?
[The monk] said, "It has been ten years since I received the precepts. Mingjue said, "How many pairs of straw sandals have you worn out on your travels?
[The monk] said, "Master, do not deceive people. Mingjue said, "I have no measure of transgression; you also have no measure of transgression."
"What do you say? The Master was speechless. Mingjue struck him, saying, "You hollow talker and deceiver! Get out!
Later, while entering the room for instruction, Mingjue said, "It is not so, nor is it otherwise; neither 'so' nor 'otherwise'—none of these are acceptable.
As the Master hesitated, Mingjue struck him again. This occurred several times. Subsequently, he served as the water steward.
While drawing water, he broke his carrying pole. Suddenly awakened, he uttered this spontaneous verse: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven.
Standing alone on the peak ten thousand fathoms high, I snatch the bright pearl from the jaws of the black dragon. With a single word, I have scrutinized and seen through Vimalakīrti."
Mingjue heard this, struck the armrest, and praised it as excellent. Subsequently, he sat at the site of enlightenment seven times, and his transformative teachings spread throughout the land;

those who inherited his Dharma were very numerous. [He] ascended the hall and said: "A wild goose passes through the vast sky, its reflection sinks into the cold water. The goose has no intention of leaving a trace; the water has no mind to retain the reflection.
If one can be thus, only then will one understand how to act among the heterodox classes. There is no need for continuity; even if a wild duck is cut [in half],..."
The cranes and wild tribes fill the peaks and valleys. When let go, there are a hundred uglinesses and a thousand clumsinesses; when gathered in, they are cramped and hunched.
If used, one dares to compete in wealth with the Eight Great Dragon Kings; if not used, it is not worth half a penny.
In the meditation hall, he asked: "A man without hands can perform boxing; a man without a tongue can speak words. Suddenly—"
"A hand-man beats [him]. A tongueless man, a tongueless man—what could he say? He also said: "The soul of Shu cries out through the night;
the quail and the owl wail all night long. The Gate of Perfect Penetration stands wide open; for what reason is there a separation between cloud and mud?"
Huijin, the Steward of Shuiyue Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture (a dharma successor of Xuedou Xian).
Huijin, the steward of Shuiyue Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture, relied upon Mingjue at Xuedou. Upon hearing the master cite the story of Mount Sumeru, he attained silent resonance with it.

Mao said, "Huìjīn. Míngjué asked, "Who gave you gold? Mao said, "I intend to go to the abbot’s quarters shortly to express my thanks.

Chan Master Liaoyuan of Yunju (Dharma heir of Kaixian Xian):
Chan Master Liaoyuan Foyin of Mount Yunju in Nankang Commandery was a native of the Lin family of Fuliang in Raoyou.

Having attained awakening through his past conditioning, he immediately traveled extensively to consult various masters. Eventually, he found his spiritual resonance at the Dharma seat of Kaixian and emerged as a patriarchal master. He presided over the monastic seat nine times.

At the Dharma Hall, while the fourfold assembly was leaning toward [the Master], one day, after the Master had entered the room with his disciples, the Layman东坡 (Dongpo) happened to arrive before him.
The Master said, "There is no seat here; why have you come here, Layman? The Layman replied:
“Borrowing the Buddha’s seal for a moment, I take the four elements as my sitting mat. The Master said, “I, this mountain monk, have a question.
If you, Layman, can answer it, then please sit and speak the Way. If you cannot, you shall forfeit the jade belt at your waist. The Layman joyfully replied, “Please, go ahead.
The Master said, “Just now you said, ‘I borrow the mountain monk’s four elements as a sitting mat. But what about the mountain itself?”
"The four great elements of the Sangha are fundamentally empty; the five aggregates are not existent. Layman, where do you sit?
The layman was unable to answer, so he presented his jade belt to the Master. The Master, in turn, bestowed upon him a *yunshan* (cloud-mountain) patched robe.

The layman then composed a verse, saying: "A hundred thousand lamps form a single lamp-light; All are the wondrous Dharma Kings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. Therefore, Dongpo does not dare to be sparing."
I borrow your four elements to serve as a meditation bed; my sickly bones can hardly endure the girdle of jade. My dull faculties still fall short of the "arrow-point" pivot of the mind.

Chan Master Damei Faying (dharma heir of Jiufeng Shaofa), the eleventh generation under Nanyue.
Chan Master Zu Jing Faying of Damei in Mingzhou was the son of the Zhang family of that prefecture. He visited Jiufeng, who recognized his potential;
when they conversed, it was as if he had long been in a monastic assembly, so Jiufeng probed him with rigorous scrutiny. The Master grasped the essential meaning.

At the beginning of the Xuanhua era, an imperial decree ordered all monks and nuns to become "virtuous scholars" (*de shi*). The Master took up his brush and wrote a commentary on the *Laozi*, which he submitted to the throne. Upon reviewing it, the Emperor said:

An attendant said, "The *Commentary on the Scripture of the Sublime Dharma* (*Faying daode jing jie*) is concise in expression yet profound in principle; it is unprecedented in antiquity. It should be granted entry into the Daoist Canon (*Daozang*) for circulation.

The following autumn, an imperial edict was issued to restore the monastic community of monks and nuns throughout the empire. However, the Master alone remained steadfast in his resolve not to change.
At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he rose at dawn wearing a birch-bark crown, a crane-feather cloak, holding a ceremonial ivory tablet, and wearing vermilion shoes. He then had a drum beaten.
He assembled the congregation and ascended the seat. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The orchid blooms in the spring valley, and the chrysanthemum flourishes by the autumn fence;

things must inevitably flourish and wither, each having its own time. In the past, monks and nuns were disparaged and the Way was exclusively served; later, the Way and its flatteries were leveled, and monks and nuns were restored.

But tell me, what are the physical forms of monks and nuns like? He then took up a crown and showed it to the assembly, saying: "The crown upon my head has always been like the full moon; though it is crowned..."
His hair did not become immortal; this morning he cast it down without obstruction, emitting a divine light that pierced the azure heavens.
He threw it upon the ground, then changed into monastic robes. Holding up a crane-feather cloak (*hegang*), he said: "In the past, the Tathāgata traded for a fur robe;
for years I have felt ashamed wearing this crane-feather cloak. Return to me the garments of a manly Tamer of Men; you should know that this object is unsuitable. He then cast it away.
He picked up the ivory tally and said: "I suspected the meditation board was too groundless; who would have thought it would be deceived by this ivory tally? Why did you suddenly let go today?
An old immortal official, retired from service throughout the heavens! He threw it down. Picking up his vermilion sandals, he said:
"Dharmatrāta took one pair back with him; from then on, his descendants walked barefoot. Borrowing these vermilion sandals to replace the hemp shoes."
