The Venerable Faming (a dharma heir of Baoben Lan).

The Venerable Faming of Kaiyuan Monastery in Jingzhou followed Baoben; not long after, he attained profound realization of the Dharma-patience (*dharmakṣānti*). Later, he returned to his native village.

His conduct was dissolute and he was fond of wine; whenever he played *lu* dice, he would invariably become heavily intoxicated. It had become his habit to sing several stanzas of Liu Yuxi’s lyrics every day.

The local villagers mocked him, refusing to invite him to vegetarian feasts but complying when invited to drink. This continued for over ten years, until everyone referred to him as the "Drunken Monk.
One day, he said to the assembly at the temple, "I shall depart tomorrow morning; do not go elsewhere."

The assembly laughed at him in secret. At dawn the next day, he adjusted his robes, took his seat, and called out loudly, "I am departing! Listen to one verse from me! When the assembly heard this, they rushed to look.
The Master then said, "Throughout my life I have been intoxicated; in intoxication I have stumbled and fallen. Yet, there was still discernment.

Now tonight, when the wine has sobered, where is the willow bank? Only the morning breeze and the waning moon. Having finished speaking, he became silent. They shook him, but he had already passed away.
He has shed his mortal coil.
Layman Liu Jingchen, Chief Administrative Officer (dharma heir of Yizhai Yi):
Layman Liu Jingchen, styled Xingchao, entered official service at a young age due to his exceptional talent. He later applied himself to the Buddha-dharma.
He did not yet believe it. At the age of thirty-two, he encountered Chan Master Donglin Zhaojue Zong, who instructed and enlightened him;
he then became reverently devoted. Consequently, he set his heart upon the Way of the Patriarchs. Subsequently, he traveled to the capital and visited Chan Master Huelin Chong.
When a monk asked, "What is the source of all Buddhas? Snow Ridge (Xuedou) replied, "The cold colors of a thousand peaks. Below these words—

He served as a provincial official for over a year at the Luochuan commandery. He then went to attend upon Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanxiao of Mount Shao. As he was about to leave his post, he took his leave of Master Shao, who instructed him, saying:
"With such dedication as you apply yourself, why should you worry about not attaining enlightenment? Hereafter, should there arise extraordinary states of experience," [he should remain undisturbed].
"Your immeasurable joy is such that you should quickly gather [your belongings]. If you can gather them and depart, you will become a vessel for the Dharma;
if you cannot gather them, you will suffer the affliction of unrest and incur the calamity of losing your mind. Not long after, he returned once more to the capital.
He went to visit Master Yi Chan of Zhengjue at Zhihai. He inquired about the causes and conditions [of enlightenment]. Zhihai said, "An ancient said, 'The ordinary mind is the Way.
Throughout the twelve periods of the day, you emit light and shake the earth, yet you do not realize it yourself. You seek it outwardly, becoming increasingly estranged and distant.
Gong was further filled with doubt and could not resolve it. One night, he entered the room, and Zhihai cited from the *Chuan Deng Lu* (The Record of the Transmission of the Lamp).
When Carangxi arrived, the King asked Venerable Prajñātāra, "What is the Buddha? The Venerable replied, "To see one's own nature is to see the Buddha.
When the Duke was questioned about this, he could not respond; his doubts were profound. He then returned home and went to bed, where he slept soundly until the fifth watch.

Upon waking, as he was reflecting on the matter, he suddenly beheld various extraordinary signs. His inner and outer being became transparently clear, and his six sense faculties were shaken with realization.
Heaven and earth revolved; it was like the moon appearing as the clouds parted. Overjoyed beyond measure, he suddenly recalled the words with which Shao Shan had charged him before their parting.

He suppressed his emotions for a time and, at dawn, went to Zhihai. He reported everything he had attained to Zhihai to serve as proof, saying, "Furthermore, you must be able to put this into practice before you have truly mastered it.
Zhihai asked, "Do you not need to undergo actual cultivation? Zhihai spoke in a stern voice.

He said, "What kind of matter is this? Yet you speak of 'practicing' it. Gong attained silent realization and subsequently composed eight verses on "Illuminating the Ground of Mind" (Famingsin-di song) as well as the treatise "Clarifying the Way and Admonishing the Confucians" (Mingdao yuru pian) to warn the world.
The Layman Master Qingxian Zhao Bian (Jiangshan Quan’s Dharma Heir), the Twelfth Generation Descendant of Nanyue. Layman Master Zhao Bian, surnamed Qingxian,
whose courtesy name was Yue Dao, cast aside sensory pleasures and sounds at the age of over forty, fixing his mind [on the Way].
Regarding religion: Fohui came and resided at Nanchan Monastery in Quzhou. The Master (Gong) visited him daily, yet Fohui never permitted him to utter a single word.

Later, while serving as the administrator of Qingzhou, he would often sit in meditation during his leisure from official affairs. Suddenly, a great thunderclap struck; startled by it, he attained immediate enlightenment and composed a verse, saying:
"Sitting silently in the hall, leaning back on a vacant rest, The source of the mind is unmoving, as still as water. One.
With a clap of thunder, the crown of his head opened; he called forth that which was his own from of old. Fohui heard this and said with a laugh, "Zhao Yuedao has simply struck lucky.
At seventy-two years of age, the Duke retired from office as Grand Master of the Imperial Household (Taizi Shaobao) and returned home to build a lofty studio for his own enjoyment.
He inscribed a verse to express his intent, saying: "The golden belt at my waist has already been laid aside; within this, [I find]..."
"Ordinary and commonplace. If people of the world wish to know the Old Man of Gaozhai, he is simply Zhao Sili of Ke Village.
He spoke again, saying, "Be careful not to mistake him;
he belongs to the thirteenth generation under Nanyue."
Chan Master Guochang Baolin (Fayun was his Dharma heir):
Chan Master Guochang Baolin Baojue of Wuzhou. He was the son of the Shi family of Anzhou.

While the Master and the Censor-in-Chief Yang Cigong were entering the mountains together on a tour, Yang picked up the "Stone for the Bodhisattva’s Meal" and asked, "Since this is a stone for a meal..."
"Why is it that you cannot bite through it? The Master said, "Precisely because it is too hard. Yang said, "That still involves redundant words. The Master said, "I do not understand;
what do you say, Provincial Commissioner? Yang said, "Hard. The Master said, "That too is the second moon.
Yang wrote the plaque for the Hall of the Seven Buddhas and asked, "What is it like when the Seven Buddhas appear in the world again? The Master said, "To meet them once."
Once again, a new record:
Lecturer Congjian of Upper Tianzhu, Lin’an Prefecture (the Dharma-heir of Fayan Wenyi).
Lecturer Congjian Ciben of Upper Tianzhu, Lin’an Prefecture, was a native of Songyang in Chuzhou. Regarding his residence...
His contemplation reached a profound resonance with the truth. Once, he sought instruction from Dàtōng by means of his spiritual power. One day, Dàtōng wrote a letter and sent it to him.
When the Master opened the seal, he beheld two circular symbols, one black and one white; upon seeing them, he attained awakening.
Master Ruan of Tiantai (dharma heir of Benjue Yi).
Master Ruan of Ruan Hermitage at Tiantai in Taizhou had long relied upon Fayan Wenji. While contemplating Yunmen’s saying, “Walking on water atop Eastern Mountain,” he realized his own insight.
He returned to live in seclusion on his former mountain, keeping company only with monkeys and deer. When the regional governor heard of his reputation, he dispatched an envoy.
He was forced to take up the position of abbot. The Master composed a verse, saying: "For thirty years I have dwelt upon this mountain; For what reason has the county edict arrived in these woods?
Cease using the trivial affairs of the dusty world To exchange for my lifelong leisure and further leisure. Thereupon, he set fire to his hermitage.
In the end, he did not know where he would stop.

The Layman Prime Minister Fu Bi (Dharma heir of Touzi Yong), the Layman Prime Minister Fu Bi, styled Yanguo, followed the exhortations of Lord Qingxian; thereafter, he did not cease his efforts by day...

At night, he proceeded with vigor along this path. He heard that Chan Master Yuan of Touzi presided over the Dharma seat, preeminent throughout the Huaidian region, and went there to resolve his doubts.
It happened that Yuan was ascending the seat for the assembly; seeing him look around like an elephant king turning in a circle, the Master attained a slight realization.

Adhering to the ritual of a disciple, he hurried to the master’s quarters and requested that his attendant invite him into the inner chamber. As soon as Yong saw him, he said, "The Excellency has already come in;
Fu Bi is still outside. Upon hearing this, Gong broke into a sweat that drenched his back, and he attained great enlightenment immediately.
Chan Master Huishen of HuiLin (Dharma Heir of Xinfang of Changlu).
Chan Master Cishou Huishen of HuiLin, Dongjing, was the son of the Xia family of Shouchun Prefecture. He traveled abroad to seek the Way.
Jingzhao relied upon Jiahe Zisheng. Jingzhao recounted the karmic conditions concerning Liangsui’s meeting with Magu, asking:

"What was the place where Liangsui attained realization? The Master immediately understood it thoroughly. He left [his teacher] and resided at Zifu, where his sandals filled the space outside his door.
When Chan Master Fojian Qin of Jiangshan arrived there while traveling for alms, the Master led him on a tour of the quarters until they reached the section for the thousand-monk community.
Xuefeng Qin asked, "Since you were once a street-walker among a thousand people, why is there now only one? The Master said, "Better one reality than many falsehoods.
Qin said, "Is that so? The Master looked abashed. Later, when the imperial court converted Zifu Temple into a Shenxiao Palace, the Master left for Jiangshan Mountain and stayed at Xianan.
Chen went there to seek further instruction. Qin said, "Zifu knows this sort of thing."

[The monk] then stopped. The Master said, "I am truly not yet at ease. I hope you will not withhold it from me; please diligently raise the story of the 'Soul Departing from the Maid,' and examine it thoroughly until it is turned over again and again.
[The monk] did so, and his doubts and obstructions were greatly cleared away. He presented a verse, saying: "It is just the place where I have always walked;
Yet when casually mentioned, it becomes a riddle. Last night a sudden gale arose, Blowing down the peach blossoms—how many must there be? Qin.
Striking the armrest, he said: "Is this not the living intent of the Patriarch?
Chan Master Ruguī of Wanshou (a successor of Xìn of Chánglú), the Chan Master Ruguī of Wanshou in Píngjiāng Prefecture, would invariably ask any monk he met: 'How have you been lately?'"
As a monk was about to respond, [the Master] patted his back and said, "Inconceivable. When he was about to pass into nirvana, the assembly gathered;
he spoke again, "Inconceivable," and then passed away with palms joined.
Chan Master Wuishang of Guangfu Monastery in Lin’an Prefecture (a successor of Baoning Ying).
When Chan Master Wuishang first visited Jueyin, he asked, "Regarding Nanquan’s beheading of the cat, what was his underlying meaning?
Jueyin replied, "It must have been Nanquan himself who could do it. Jueyin then challenged him with the previous words.

The Master was unable to respond. Upon reaching the Sangha Hall, he suddenly attained great enlightenment and said, "The ancients said, 'From this day forward, I shall no longer doubt the tongues of the old monks of the world.
I truly believe this now. He then composed a verse and presented it to Jueyin, saying:
"It must be the foremost pivot of Nanquan; Unknowingly and unawares, the awl strikes the head. If one did not have the 'blue and white eyes' facing them directly,"
"It is just like a [kan-nyo] bird guarding an empty pond. Before he had finished speaking, Jueyin raised his fist and said, "At this very moment, what is to be done?
The Master overturned the meditation seat. Jueyin then let out a shout. The Master said, "Drawing the bow after the thief has fled," and then departed.
Worthy Wang of Wei Prefecture (a dharma successor of Yuanfeng).
The name of Worthy Wang of Wei Prefecture has been lost. Having lost his wife, he grew weary of worldly phenomena and subsequently attended upon Yuanfeng.
Under Yuanfeng’s words, he realized his place of return. One day, Yuanfeng said to him, "You are the Lu Xuan of our time. The worthy immediately covered his ears.
Soon thereafter, he returned to the south of Mount Tan and lived there, dwelling in a thatched hut for three years. Once, he spontaneously sang: "Within the mountains of Tan, how long the days are!
On the ridges of green pines, the realm of white clouds. Chanting birds and crying monkeys serve as my place of practice.
With hair unbound, I gather ferns and sing, and laugh again. Let people call me a madman, a man of the wild."
*Chiao-wai pieh-chuan*,
Scroll 12 and Scroll 13 (Fayan School),
Eighth Generation below Nanyue.
Chan Master Wen-yi of Qingliang (Dharma heir of Luohan Chen).
Chan Master Wen-yi of Qingliang Monastery in Jinling was the son of the Ru family of Yuhang. He traveled to Fuzhou to study under Changqing.
He did not yet have great realization. Later, together with Shaoxian, Fajin, and another person, he wished to cross the mountain pass.
Passing through Dizang Monastery, they were delayed by snow and rested for a short while. As they sat by the brazier, Dizang asked, "Where are you going on this journey?
The Master replied, "I am going on a pilgrimage. Dizang said, "What is the matter of pilgrimage? The Master said, "I do not know. Dizang said, "Not knowing is most intimate."
Furthermore, while the three men were discussing the *Treatise by Zhaolun*, they reached the passage: "Heaven and earth share the same root as I.
Dizang asked, "Are the mountains, rivers, and the great earth the same as, or different from, your own self, Venerable Sir? The Master replied, "They are different. Dizang held up two fingers.
The Master said, “It is the same. Jizang then held up two fingers and immediately departed.
When Xueji was about to leave, Jizang saw him off at the gate and asked, “Upādhyāya, you usually say that the three realms are mind-only and all phenomena are consciousness-only.
Now, look at this stone in the courtyard: tell me, is it within the mind or outside the mind? The Master replied, “It is within the mind. Jizang—
Dizang said, "What is the purpose of a wandering monk coming here? You have placed a mere stone upon your heart.

The Master was at a loss for a reply and immediately set down his pack, seeking definitive instruction beneath Dizang’s seat. For nearly a month, he presented his insights and explained his understanding of the principles.
Dizang told him, "The Buddha-dharma is not like this. The Master said, "I am now exhausted of words and cut off of principle."
Dizang said, "If one speaks of the Buddha-dharma, everything is already manifest. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Upon the arrival of Zifang Shouzhang from Changqing, the Master raised the verse of Changqing and asked, "What is the body revealed alone amidst the myriad phenomena?
Zifang held up his whisk. The Master said, "How can you understand it in such a way? Zifang replied, "Master..."
"What do you think, Venerable Sir? The Master said, "What do you call 'the myriad phenomena'? [The student] replied, "The ancients did not negate the myriad phenomena.
The Master said, "'Amidst the myriad phenomena, the body alone is revealed. What is there to say about negating or not negating? At these words, the student suddenly attained awakening.
He recited a verse to offer his sincere devotion. From that time on, those from various quarters who possessed understanding and realization flocked to him in great numbers.

At first, they followed their own habitual practices; the Master subtly provoked them with exhortations, and they gradually came to accept his teachings. The assembly, like fish gathering in the sea, never numbered fewer than a thousand.
The Master asked Chief Xu: "A hair’s breadth of difference results in worlds apart. Elder brother, compose [a verse]."
"How do you understand this? Xiu replied, "A hair's breadth of difference, and heaven and earth are set apart.
The Master said, "How can you understand it in such a way? Xiu asked, "How about you, Preceptor? The Master said, "A hair's breadth of difference, and heaven and earth are set apart.

Xiu then bowed. (Dongchan Qi said: "The Abbot responded in this way; why did he not accept it? When Xiu requested further instruction, Fayan also spoke in just this manner and [Xiu] was able to go forth. But tell me, where does the point of doubt and error lie? If you look at it...)

They have attained penetration. The Venerable Daoshang has a source; this was brought forth by Wuzu Jie. Fayan struck him across the back with his staff. Baoning Yong said, "At that time, Master Xiu should also have said to Fayan: 'How can such an understanding suffice?

Jingshan Gao said, "Fayan and Master Xiu were like drawing thread from silk—continuous and dense. They upheld the tradition of Dizang’s school; it can truly be said that light filled their eyes. But as for those under my own gate, Jingshan, you must buy more straw sandals and travel on foot before you will do.

Why? Because a hair’s breadth of error leaves heaven and earth between you and the truth. From where did they get this news? Chushi Qi said, "Those two old fellows did not understand the 'turning phrase. If Tianning were suddenly asked today, 'A hair's breadth of error,' what would he say?"

"How can one act when heaven and earth are so vastly separated? He said to him: "Yesterday someone asked this; thirty blows of the staff and he was sent out of the monastery. The Master was warming himself by the fire with Master Wukong.
Picking up the incense ladle, the Master asked, "You must not call it an incense ladle;

what would you call it, brother? Wukong replied, "An incense ladle. The Master did not approve. It was only twenty-odd days later that Wukong finally understood these words. A monk came for an audience.

Next, the Master pointed toward the curtain. At that time, two monks went together to roll it up. The Master said, "One gains, one loses. (Dongchan Qi asked: "How do you understand this, Senior Monk? One replied:

"It is because he does not understand the essential meaning that he goes to roll up the curtain. Another said: "He who was pointed at understood; he who went without being pointed at lost. Is such an understanding acceptable or not? Since such an understanding is not permitted—)

Furthermore, let us ask the Elder: which one gains, and which one loses? Huanglong Qing said: "Fayan held the Mohe Moye sword in his hand; killing or giving life was at his discretion. Since both monks rolled up the curtain together, tell me, which one gained and which one lost?"

Do you understand? "Matters of the world are settled by the standard of justice; the human heart is difficult to align with the full moon. [The Master] asked Elder Baizi, "An ancient said, 'Mountains and rivers have no obstruction;
light penetrates everywhere. Now, what is this light that penetrates everywhere?

Baizi replied, "The sound of the pestle on the east side. (Niuju Rou offered a different version: "The Master intends to create an obstruction. The Master pointed to some bamboo and asked a monk, "Do you see it?"
[The monk] said, "I see it. The Master said, "The bamboo comes into the eye; the eye goes to the edge of the bamboo. [The monk] said, "It is not like that at all. (Fadeng Qin said:

"At that time, you should have just wrenched open your eyes toward the Master. Guizong Rou offered an alternative: "The Master simply does not trust me. There was a layman who presented a painted screen.
After the Master looked at it, he asked, "Is your skill in your hands or in your mind? He replied, "In my mind. The Master said, "Which one is your mind?"
The layman had no reply. (Gui-zong Rou spoke on his behalf, saying: "Today, I have instead made it easy. Ascending the hall, [the Master] said:
"Throughout the entire world, all is bright and clear; there is not a single thread of hair. If there were a single thread of hair, that would be a single thread of hair. (Fa-deng Qin said:

"If there were a single thread of hair, it would not be a single thread of hair. The Master pointed to a stool and said: "If you recognize this stool, you will have more than enough room around it. (Yun-men said: "Recognize the stool...")

"Son! Heaven and earth are vastly different. Xuedou Xian said, "The marsh is so vast it hides mountains; the principle is able to subdue the leopard. Yunfeng Yue said, "In official business, even a needle cannot pass;

in private, carts and horses may go through. Jianfu Huai said, "If you recognize this bench, you will know it is made of nanmu wood. Wuzu Yan said, "These two fellows: one crosses the boat, the other wades the water. If you can examine this thoroughly, I grant that you possess the True Dharma Eye. Yuantong Xiu, having finished citing the words of Fayen, Yunmen, and Tianyi, said:

"I, this mountain monk, say: 'Recognize the bench; its four legs rest on the ground. Within this assembly, there is emerging and submerging, half-closing and half-opening, gain and loss, intimacy and distance. You practitioners with eyes—examine this for yourselves as you please!"

Letan Qing cited the words of Fayan, Yunmen, Xuedou, and Xuedou’s successor, and said: "These three fellows all rely on others for their understanding; they are divided between clarity and obscurity, never escaping the realm of seeing and hearing—they are like the moon reflected in water.

Huanglong was not like this: 'It fills the space beyond heaven and earth; it unfolds before the sun and moon. Jingshan Guangzhao said: "If you recognize the bench, it is easy to shave your head and wash your feet. Although this is so, many misunderstand it. Tiantong Huiming said:

"To understand at a point where there is abundance all around is to fall into partiality regarding principle. To understand at a point where heaven and earth are vastly different is to fall into partiality regarding phenomena. But tell me, in what state does Guizong act for the sake of others? The rhinoceros develops patterns on its horn from gazing at the moon; the elephant has flowers enter its tusks because it is startled by thunder. Chushi Zhiqian.

It is said: "Do not mistake idle talk for idle talk; often matters arise from idle talk. Shuzhong Yun said: "The pine is straight and the thorn is crooked; the crane is white and the crow is black. Because he opened a well, it was filled with sand.
[The Master] blocked the spring’s source. The Master said, "When the spring’s source is not open, it is obstructed by sand;
when the Way-eye is not open, what obstructs it? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf: "It is obstructed by the eye. He asked a monk, "Where have you come from?

The monk replied, "I have come from Sizhou to pay respects to the Great Sage. The Master said, "Does the Great Sage emerge from the stupa this year? The monk replied, "He does. The Master then asked a bystander.

He said: "You say that he reached Sizhou but did not reach [the Great Sage]. (Fushan Yuan said: 'This monk did indeed reach him; it was simply that Sizhou did not see the Great Sage. Daochang Quan said:)"
"This monk sees as soon as he sees him. The Great Sage never failed to recognize Fayen. Dongchan Guan said: "This monk has indeed arrived; he saw the one at Sizhou and he recognized the Great Sage.
As for Fayen, he was merely searching for his own head and could not see it. The Master said to a young boy: "Because you recognize your father through this child, what is your father's name?
The boy had no reply. (Fadeng Qin spoke on his behalf: "Just cover your face with your sleeve. The Master then asked the monk: "If you were a filial son, how would you respond?"
A turning phrase. Tell me, what words should be spoken here? The monk had no reply. The Master spoke on his behalf: "He is a filial son.
The Master asked a lecturer of the *Śata-dharma-śāstra*: "The hundred dharmas present both essence and function;
the gate of illumination brings together subject and object. You, the lecturer, are the subject and the Dharma-seat is the object. How do you explain their being 'simultaneously presented'?"

An elder once said on his behalf: "I would call this a Dharma-seat. Nanzong Rou said, "There is no need for the Master to trouble yourself in such a way. Once, while the Master was suffering from an ailment in his leg, a monk came to inquire after him.
The Master said, "When non-humans come, I cannot move; when humans come, I cannot move. Tell me, what words can be spoken within the Buddha-dharma in such a situation?

The monk replied, "The Master may well rejoice that you have recovered. The Master did not approve. He spoke another verse himself: "A wooden man sits upon a stone bench; A stone woman stands before a bronze mirror. If you wish to know the Buddha-dharma, Look at the face of the old woman."
"Today the Master seems diminished by one day. One day, while discussing the Way with King Li, they went together to view peony flowers.
The King requested that the Master compose a verse, and the Master immediately composed it, saying: Clad in coarse wool, facing a fragrant thicket, our inclinations have always been different.
My hair has turned white from this very day; the flowers were red as they were last year. Their exquisite beauty follows the morning dew; their sweet fragrance pursues the evening breeze. How...
"One must wait for them to wither and fall before one finally knows they are empty. The King suddenly realized its meaning.
This was the National Teacher De Shao of Tiantai (the Dharma heir of Qingliang Yi), the ninth generation descendant of Nanyue.
National Teacher Deshao of Mount Tiantai was the son of the Chen family of Longquan in Chuzhou.

During the Tongguang era of the Later Tang dynasty, he traveled to seek instruction, first visiting Master Tong at Touzi, and subsequently paying his respects to Longya, to whom he asked: "The majestic and honored one..."
"Why can one not approach it? Longya said, "It is like fire meeting fire. The Master asked, "What if water should suddenly come upon it?
Longya said, "Go away; you do not understand my words. The Master asked again, "Heaven does not cover it, and earth does not support it—what is the principle of this?
Longya said, "A seeker of the Way should be thus. The Master asked this seventeen times.
Longya answered in exactly this way. The Master still did not understand the meaning and requested further instruction. Longya said, "Dharma brother, you will understand it yourself in the future.
Later, while bathing at Tongxuan Peak, the Master suddenly realized the significance of the previous conversation.
He immediately assumed a solemn demeanor, burned incense, and prostrated toward Longya from afar, saying, "Had he spoken thus to me at that time, today..."
[The Master] said, "I am certainly scolding you. He then asked Shushan, "What kind of person’s realm is this 'a hundred circuits and a thousand layers'?

Shushan replied, "Twisting straw rope on the left to bind the little ghosts. The Master said, "It does not fall within the past or present; please tell me, Master. Shushan said, "I will not say. The Master asked, "Why will you not say?
Shushan replied, "Within this, there is no discrimination between existence and non-existence. The Master said, "Master, you have spoken well. Shushan... [the text ends here].
Shan was startled by this. Thus he visited fifty-four spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) in succession, yet in all cases his karmic affinity for the Dharma had not yet been realized.
Finally, he went to Linchuan to pay his respects to Fayan. Upon seeing him at first glance, Fayan held him in high esteem. One day, Fayan ascended the hall to address the assembly.
A monk asked, "What is one drop of water from the Cao source? Fayan replied, "It is one drop of water from the Cao source.
The monk withdrew in bewilderment. At the side of his seat, the Master attained sudden enlightenment; all the stagnation of his life was dissolved like melting ice.
He then reported his realization to Fayan. Fayan said, "In the future, you shall become a teacher to the king, causing the ancestral Way to flourish; I am not your equal.
He subsequently returned to his home province and traveled to Mount Tiantai, where he beheld the traces left by the Chan Master Zhiyi (Zhizhe), which appeared as if they were his former residence.
Since the Master shared the same surname as Zhiyi, he was then called the "Later [Zhiyi]."
...the Master’s person. Initially, he resided at White Sand (Bai Sha). At that time, King Zhongyi was still a prince serving as the Governor of Taizhou;
having heard the Master’s reputation, he invited him to inquire about the Way. The Master said to him, "In the future, you shall become a preeminent leader; do not forget the Buddha's grace.

In the first year of the Qianyou era of the Han dynasty, the year Wushen, the King succeeded to the throne and dispatched an envoy to welcome the Master, performing the rites due to a disciple. There is a *Chuantian*... [text fragment].

Wisejik (also known as Luoxi), a disciple of the Tiantai master Zhiyi, repeatedly said to his teacher: "The teachings of the Master Zhiyi have been transmitted for many years and I fear they have become scattered and lost.
Now, in the kingdom of Silla, the original texts are fully preserved; were it not for the compassionate power of the Venerable Master..."

"Who, then, is capable of bringing it here? The Master thereupon reported this to the King. The King dispatched an envoy, who, carrying the Master’s letter, went to that country, copied the work in its entirety, and returned.
To this day, it remains widely circulated in the world. The Master composed a verse, which says:
"At the summit of Tongxuan Peak, it is not of this human world. Outside the mind there is no dharma; before one's eyes are green mountains.

Fayan heard this and said, "By means of this very verse, you may establish my school" (Jingshan Daokai said: "The extinction of the Fayan school was precisely due to this one verse"). Because of this, the Master [Fayan] flourished.
Master Ming asked: "Kāśyapa holds Śākyamuni’s robe, which measures sixteen feet, at Mount Kukkuṭapāda, awaiting Maitreya’s descent into the world.
When he takes this sixteen-foot robe and puts it on his body of one thousand feet, it fits perfectly.
Now, since Śākyamuni’s body is sixteen feet tall and Maitreya’s body is one thousand feet tall, is it that the body itself has become shorter, or is it the robe?"
Jie Changxie said, "You understand it, Master. Ming shook his sleeves and went out. The Master said, "If I, this mountain monk, had answered you, you would not be wrong;
there would have been cause and effect. If you were not wrong, I would have seen it. Seven days later, Ming spat up blood.
Master Fuguang urged him, saying, "Go quickly to repent. Ming then went there, and only then did the Master [respond].

Zhaozhou wept bitterly and said, "I pray that the Master will show me compassion and grant me permission to repent. The Master said, "It is like a person who falls to the ground and rises by means of that very ground;
I have never taught you how to rise from a fall. Zhaozhou spoke again, saying, "If you grant me permission to repent, I shall serve you for the rest of my life.
The Master uttered these words for him: "The Way of Buddha after Buddha is equal, yet there appears to be high and low; Śākyamuni and Maitreya are [one]."
Seal upon seal.
Chan Master Taiqin of Qingliang (the dharma heir of Qingliang Yi):
Chan Master Taiqin Fadeng of Qingliang in Jinling. During his time among the assembly, his character was bold and unrestrained; he did not attend to worldly affairs. The assembly...
They changed the topic. Fayan alone was in accord with him. One day, Fayan asked the assembly, "Who can untie the golden bell from the tiger's neck?
No one in the assembly could answer. The Master (Xuedou) arrived just then; Fayan repeated his previous question to him. The Master said, "The one who tied it can untie it."
Fayan said, "You fellows must not underestimate him. [He] ascended the hall and said: "I originally intended to dwell in the mountains to hide my ineptitude and nurse my illness;
however, as time passes, I am constrained by the fact that my late teacher has a kōan that remains unresolved. I have come forth to settle it for him."
At that time, a monk asked, "What is the unresolved case of the former master? The Master struck him and said, "The patriarch failed to settle it;
the calamity reaches his descendants. The monk asked, "Where does the fault lie? The Master said, "The fault lies with me; the calamity reaches you."
When the Prince of Jiangnan was still the Duke of Zheng, he received the mind-seal (citta-dharma) from the school of Fayan.
After Fayan entered parinirvāṇa, the Prince once asked the Master, "What unfinished case did my former teacher have? The Master replied, "I am currently analyzing it. [Cuiyan Zhi said:

"To exert oneself for the sake of the assembly brings disaster to one's own door. [Tiantong Jue said: "If this monk had been a true man, he would have come forth and overturned the meditation seat. Not only would he have found his own way out..."]

"This is the path of the body. It also spares one’s ancestors from failing to achieve liberation, lest their calamity descend upon their descendants. Zhaojue Qinju said: "The humble aspirations of this mountain monk are originally just like this. Today I have come forth solely for the sake of the Fifth Patriarch, our late teacher, who had a ready-made public case (gong'an).

To proclaim it before the assembly, let those who do not spare their own lives step forward and investigate it. If there is no such person, I shall have no choice but to pick up and play with it myself. (He gave a shout, struck the meditation seat with his whisk, and descended.)
Chan Master Qingsong of Lingyin (Dharma Heir of Qingliang Yi).
Chan Master Qingsong of Lingyin in Hangzhou was a native of Fuzhou. Initially, he visited Fayen, who pointed to the rain and said to him, "Every drop falls into the eyes of the Venerable.
At first, the Master did not understand the meaning. Later, while reading the Avatamsaka Sutra...
Yan was deeply moved and attained realization. He received the seal of approval from Fayan.
Regarding Chan Master Daoheng of Baizhang in Hongzhou (a dharma successor of Qingliang Yi):
Chan Master Daoheng of Baizhang in Hongzhou went to study under Fayan. He subsequently requested further instruction on the following matter: "When a non-Buddhist asked the Buddha, he did not ask..."
There was one who said, "If you do not ask, there is no speaking. Before he had finished his sentence, Fayuan said, "Stop, stop! Where do you intend to find the World-Honored One?
You have been searching for him for a long time! From this, the Master attained awakening and entered [the Way].
Chan Master Daoyan of Yongming (Dharma Heir of Qingliang Yi).
Chan Master Daoyan of Yongming Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Wu family from Hexing Prefecture.
Initially, he visited Fayan, who asked him, "Aside from your formal inquiries and requests for instruction, what sutra are you studying? The Master replied, "The Avatamsaka Sutra. Fayan said:

“Are the categories of totality and particularity, identity and difference, and formation and disintegration subsumed under which gate? The Master replied, “The text is found within the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra*.
According to principle, however, all phenomena—both mundane and supramundane—possess these six characteristics. Fayan asked, “Does emptiness itself possess these six characteristics or not?
The Master was bewildered and had no reply. Fayan said, “You ask me; I shall direct it back to you.”
The Master then asked, "Does emptiness also possess the six characteristics? Fayen replied, "Emptiness. At this, the Master attained enlightenment;
he leaped for joy and prostrated himself in thanks. Fayen asked, "How do you understand this? The Master replied, "Emptiness. Fayen approved of this.
On another day, as a great assembly of men and women entered the monastery, Fayen asked the Master, "The Vinaya states that one can hear a hairpin through a wall..."
"The sound of bracelets is itself called breaking the precepts. To see gold and silver intermingled, or to behold crimson and purple robes crowding together—is this breaking the precepts or not?
The Master said, "What an excellent point of entry! Fayen said, "In the future, you will have five hundred disciples."
He was highly esteemed by kings and nobles.
Chan Master Huiming of Ba’en (a dharma successor of Qingliang Yi):
Chan Master Huiming of Ba’en in Hangzhou was surnamed Jiang. He traveled south through the regions of Min and Yue, visiting various Chan [monasteries].
[He] understood. Yet he did not yet accord with his original mind. Later, he went to Linchuan and visited Fayan; teacher and disciple reached a spiritual accord.
One day, a newly arrived monk came to pay his respects. The Master asked, "Where have you recently departed from? He replied, "The capital.

The Master said, "Venerable sir, since you have left the capital to come to this mountain, the capital is diminished, while you are increased here. Since you are increased, there is a lack of dharmas outside the mind."
Thus, the mind-dharma is not fully explained. If one attains the principle, one remains; if one does not realize it, one departs. The assembly has no response. (Jingshan Gaofeng spoke on his behalf:

"Venerable Sir, you cannot deceive me, nor can I deceive you. He further said: "Right now, is there anyone who can speak a phrase that deceives one another? If you can speak such a thing, I will grant that you have leaped through the Diamond Ring and swallowed the Thorny Jujube.
The Master subsequently moved to the White Sand Hermitage on Mount Tiantai. There was a senior monk named Pengyan, who was widely learned.

[The Master] possessed a powerful memory. When Yan came to visit him to debate the principles of the *zongcheng* (the vehicle of the school), the Master said, "Excessive words distance one further from the Way.
Now, I have a matter I wish to ask you about: as for all the sages of antiquity and the former worthies, was there anyone among them who did not attain enlightenment?
Yan replied, "If they were sages and former worthies, how could there be anyone among them who had not attained enlightenment? The Master said, "When one person awakens and returns to the Truth..."
"Yuan, the empty space of the ten directions would all be utterly extinguished. Yet Mount Tiantai stands towering today; how could it ever be extinguished? Yan had no reply.
During the Qianguyu era of the Han dynasty, King Zhongyi invited the Master into his palace to inquire about the Dharma. He ordered him to reside at Zichong Monastery.
The Master spoke extensively on the profound teachings of Xuansha, Dizang, and Fayen, reaching the ultimate pinnacle of their essential principles. Consequently, the King commanded him...
Cuiyan Lingcan and other eminent Chan masters, as well as renowned officials from the capital, were appointed to determine the victor.
Tiantong Chanshi asked, "All Buddhas and all Buddha-dharmas emerge from this sutra; I wonder from where this sutra emerges?
The Master said, "What are you saying? As Tiantong was about to offer a reply, the Master said, "Too late. Ziyuan.
The Elder asked, "What is the samādhi of presence before one? The Master said, "Do you hear? Ziyang replied, "I am not afflicted by deafness.
The Master said, "Indeed, you are afflicted by deafness. The Master then cited the epitaph for Xuefeng and questioned the elder monks.
That which exists by virtue of conditions undergoes formation and destruction from beginning to end; that which does not exist by virtue of conditions remains eternally firm throughout the kalpas.

Setting aside for a moment this matter of permanence and destruction, Xuefeng—where is he right now? (Fayan Yi offered a different reading: "Right now, is this formation or destruction? The elder monk had no reply.
Even if there were one who could have replied, they would not have been able to withstand such an incisive interrogation. At that time, the assembly of eminent scholars was silenced.
I prostrate. The King was greatly delighted.
Chan Master Qingxi of Yunju (a dharma successor of Qingliang Yi):
Chan Master Qingxi of Yunju Mountain in Nankang Commandery was a native of Quanzhou. There was an Imperial Messenger named Liao who entered the monastery.
When Zhen saw Master Fayuan, he asked, "What kind of fruit was that you were offering me just now?
The Master replied, "It was artificial fruit. The messenger said, "If it was artificial fruit, why did you offer it to me? The Master said:
It simply requires that the heavenly messenger recognize the false.
Regarding Chan Master Zhiyi of Luohan [Temple] (a dharma successor of Qingliang Yi):
Chan Master Xuanfa of Luohan [Temple] in Zhangzhou was eating *bingdan* (steamed cakes) with Elder Yandu. Yandu said:
"A hundred kinds, a thousand varieties—their essence is non-dual. The Master asked, "What is this non-dual essence? Yuanzhao picked up a steamed bun and held it up.
The Master said, "You are merely clinging to the hundred kinds and thousand varieties. Yuanzhao said, "That too is just your own way of seeing, Master. The Master said, [I know].
"You are also like Layman Gongyong combing his hair. When the Master was about to pass into extinction, he said to the assembly:
"Tonight my four elements are not in harmony. Clouds rise and birds fly; winds move and dust stirs. It is vast and boundless. Is there anyone who can cure this?
If one could cure it, we would never recognize each other again for eternal kalpas. If one cannot cure it, one will see me at all times. Having spoken, he passed away.
Baoci Wensui Chan Master (Dharma Heir of Qingliang Yi).
Chan Master Baoci Wensui of Jinling was the son of the Lu family of Hangzhou. He once investigated the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra* and attained a profound realization of its essential meaning.
The dependent origination of truth and falsehood is profound and extensive in its beginning and end. Consequently, he composed a commentary with topical divisions and cross-referenced annotations.
Once his work was completed, he presented it to Fayan to describe his own achievements; it deeply accorded with the intent of the sutra.

Fayan said, "Does the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* not contain the principle of the 'eight returns'? The Master replied, "It does. Fayan asked, "To what does clarity return? The Master replied, "Clarity returns to the sun."
He asked, "What does 'the sun returns' mean? The Master was bewildered and had no reply. Fayen commanded that the commentary he had written be burned.
From then on, the Master took him to heart as his teacher, seeking further instruction until he finally forgot all intellectual understanding.
Chan Master Xuantze of Ba’en Temple (Dharma Heir of Qingliang Yi).
Chan Master Xuantze of Ba’en Temple in Jinling was a native of Weinan in Huazhou.
Initially, he asked Qingfeng, “What is the student’s own self? Qingfeng replied, “The child of the fire element comes seeking fire. Later, he visited Fayan.
Fayan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master said, "From Qingfeng. Fayan asked, "What words or phrases did Qingfeng say? The Master recounted the previous conversation.
Fayan asked, "How do you understand this, Senior Monk? The Master said, "'The direction Bingding belongs to fire,' yet he further seeks fire;
it is like using oneself to seek oneself. Fayan said, "Even if you understand it thus, how can that suffice? The Master said, [silently].
"Such-and-such a person is exactly like this; I do not yet know how you, the Master, would respond. Fayan said, "Ask me, and I will tell you.
The Master asked, "What is the student’s own self? Fayan said, "The child Bingding comes seeking fire."
The Master attained sudden enlightenment upon these words. On the day of the opening of the hall, King Li and Fayan were both present.
A monk asked, "When the dragon roars, mist rises; when the tiger howls, wind arises. I know this to be a matter concerning the transcendence of the world, yet why is it that I do not understand it?
The Master said, "Try to understand it well. The monk looked up, and the Master looked as well. Fayan then withdrew his body.
When he entered the assembly, Fayan and King Li both turned pale with alarm. Fayan returned to his quarters and ordered an attendant to summon the monk for a formal dialogue.
When the monk arrived, Fayan said, "Venerable, regarding that question you asked just now before this assembly of gods and men who possess the eye of Dharma—why did you not prostrate yourself?
You have merely covered over me. He then struck him once with his sitting cloth (*zuoju*). Three days later, the monk...
He passed away emitting light.
Chan Master Ce-zhen of Gui-zong (a successor of Qing-liang Yi):
Chan Master Fa-shi Ce-zhen of Gui-zong on Mount Lu was the son of the Wei family of Wei County in Caozhou. His original name was Hui-chao.
He went to visit Fayan and asked, "Huishao consults the Master: what is the Buddha? Fayan said, "You are Huishao.

From this, the Master attained awakening. (Zhaojue Qin said: Some say that Huishao is himself the Buddha, which is why Fayan answered in such a way. Others say it is very much like riding a cow while searching for the cow.)

Regarding the statement, "There is," the question itself is precisely what "is. If you understand the interaction in such a manner, not only will you betray yourself, but you will also deeply wrong the ancients. Xuedou Xian’s verse says: "The spring breeze of the river lands cannot stir it."
The partridge cries out amidst the deep flowers. When the three-tiered waves rise high, the fish transforms into a dragon;
yet the foolish person still scoops water from the night pond.
Master Jin of Guxian (the Dharma heir of Qingliang Yi) was Master Jin of Guxian Monastery in Zezhou. While attending Fayan, Fayan asked a monk: "From [self]..."
"Leaving this place, where have you come from? he asked. The monk replied, "I have come up from the mountain ridges. Fayan said, "Not easy.
The monk said, "In vain I have traversed so many mountains and rivers. Fayan said, "So many mountains and rivers are not bad either.
At these words, the monk was speechless. The Master attained realization at this point.
Chan Master Yongming Yanshou (Dharma heir of Tiantai Shaokang), the tenth generation descendant of Nanyue.
Chan Master Yongming Yanshou of Hangzhou was a native of the Wang family of Yuhang. He went to Mount Tiantzhu on Mount Tiantai.
For ninety days he practiced meditative concentration. Upon visiting National Teacher Shao, the Master was deeply esteemed by him at first sight;

the Teacher secretly transmitted the profound essence of the Dharma to him and further said to him, "You have a karmic affinity with the Marshal; in the future, you shall greatly promote the Buddhist cause. King Zhongyi invited him to open the mountain for the new Lingyin Monastery.
The following year, he moved to the Great Practice Site of Yongming, where the assembly numbered over two thousand monks. A monk asked:
"What is the wondrous principle of Yongming? The Master said, "Add more incense. The monk said, "Thank you for your instruction.

The Master said, "I am glad there is no connection [between us]. The monk bowed; the Master said, "Listen to this verse: 'If you wish to know the principle of Yongming, there is a lake before the gate.
When the sun shines, radiance arises; when the wind comes, waves stir. [Question: "What is the Great [Way]?"
The Master of the Round Mirror said: "Breaking the Sand Pot.

This refers to Chan Master Shouwei Zongyi of Guangping Monastery in Fuzhou (a dharma successor of National Teacher Tiantai Shaor). He was a native of that province and studied under National Teacher Tiantai.
Having received the imperial decree, he then transmitted the robe and the Dharma. At that time, a monk asked, "At the summit of Mount Dayu, it could not be lifted;
how is it that today you transmit it to the Master? The Master lifted it up and said, "Is there anyone who dares say that Tiantai obtained it?"
Chan Master Zhifeng of Wuyun (Dharma Heir of Tiantai Shaokang):
Chan Master Zhifeng of Huayan Monastery on Wuyun Mountain in Hangzhou was a native of Yuhang. He was thoroughly versed in the three studies [of scripture, discipline, and meditation].
Having thoroughly realized the nature and characteristics [of phenomena], he once dreamed that he ascended Mount Sumeru and beheld three Buddhas seated in a row. First was Śākyamuni, next Maitreya;
he prostrated at the feet of both, yet he did not recognize the third Honored One, regarding him only with an upward gaze.
Śākyamuni said to him, "This is the Lion-Moon Buddha (Siṃhacandra), who shall succeed Maitreya. Only then did he prostrate. After waking, he consequently read the *Mahā*... [text fragment].
The Tripitaka [collection] thus corresponded to his dream. During the Tianfu era, he traveled abroad and arrived at Yunju on Mount Tiantai, where he visited the National Teacher.

Through their master-disciple connection, the profound mysteries were suddenly revealed. One day, while sitting in meditative absorption within the Samantabhadra Hall, a divine being suddenly knelt before him.
The Master asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am a deity who protects the precepts. The Master said, "I suffer from..."

"You have past transgressions that have not yet been extinguished; do you know of them? He replied, "What offense has the Master committed? It was merely a minor lapse. The Master asked, "What was it?
He said, "Whenever one washes a bowl, the water is also the property of a donor. Yet the Master always pours it away; this is improper."
Having finished speaking, he vanished. From then on, the Master would drink all the water used for washing his alms bowl.

After doing so for a long time, he consequently developed a spleen ailment, which was only cured after ten years. (Whenever one discards food, drink, saliva, mucus, or excrement, one should snap the fingers and silently recite the mantra, casting it away with a mind of renunciation.)
Chan Master Quanken of Zhiye Monastery in Wuzhou (Dharma heir of Tiantai Shao).
When Chan Master Quanken of Zhiye Monastery first visited National Teacher [Huizhong], the National Teacher asked him, "What is your name?"
The Master said, "I fully agree. The National Teacher asked, "What is it that you agree with? At these words, the Master attained realization and prostrated himself.
Chan Master Yu'an of Shangfang at Rui鹿 Temple (a dharma heir of Shao of Tiantai).
Chan Master Yu'an of Shangfang at Rui鹿 Temple in Wenzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He received the Dharma from Tiantai.
Furthermore, he was constantly reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*. Upon reaching the passage, "When knowledge and vision establish knowledge, this is the root of ignorance;
when knowledge and vision are without seeing, this is nirvana," the Master read it by breaking the phrasing: "Knowledge and vision establish / Knowledge, which is the root of ignorance;
/ Knowledge and vision are without / Seeing, which is nirvana. At this, he attained a realization. Someone said to the Master, "You have broken the phrasing [of the text]."
"I have understood. The Master said, "This is my place of awakening; I shall not change it for the rest of my life. At that time, he was called An Lengyan (An of the Śūraṅgama).
Chan Master Benxian of Rui鹿 (Rui-lu), a successor of Tiantai Shao:
Chan Master Benxian of Rui-lu Temple in Wenzhou was the son of the Zheng family of that prefecture. He studied under National Teacher Tiantai. [The Master] guided him...

Upon hearing the words, "It is not the wind or the banner that moves; it is your mind, O worthy one, that moves them," the Master immediately attained realization. Thereafter, he instructed his disciples, saying:

"When I first studied the Tiantai Dharma-gate, I attained understanding at the mere mention of its words. Nevertheless, for a thousand days thereafter, throughout the four modes of deportment, [I maintained this awareness]."

It was like something obstructing his chest, as if he were sharing a dwelling with an enemy. One day, he suddenly attained a fierce awakening, like washing one's face and touching the bridge of one’s own nose.
This was Master Hongshou of Xingjiao (a dharma heir of Tiantai Shaofu).

Chan Master Hongshou of Xingjiao Temple in Hangzhou was once engaged in communal labor with the National Teacher. Upon hearing a piece of firewood fall, he attained realization and composed this verse:
"Where it falls, it is not another thing; In its various positions, it is no mere dust. Mountains, rivers, and the great earth— The entire body of the Dharma King is revealed."
Chan Master Daoci of Yunju (Dharma heir of Qingliang Qin).
Chan Master Daoci of Yunju in Hongzhou was the son of the Jin family of that same prefecture. He traveled extensively through various Chan assemblies, yet his desire for study did not cease.
Later, while serving as the librarian at Shanglan Monastery, Faden one day said to the Master: "If someone asks me—"
[The Master asked: "What is the meaning of the Westward Journey? He replied, "Neither east nor west. The Librarian asked, "How do you understand this?
The Master responded, "Neither east nor west. Faldeng said, "If you understand it thus, how can it be right?
[The Master] said, "Daoqi is simply like this; I do not know what your honorable intention is, Master. Faldeng said, "He has his own descendants. Thereupon, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Clarifying His Essential Teaching:
Chan Master Kuangxing of Qianguang Temple in Hangzhou (Dharma Heir of Yongming Qian).
Chan Master Kuangxing of Qianguangwang Temple in Hangzhou was the son of the Zheng family of Wenzhou. He entered the monastic order in his youth and applied himself with diligence.
He thoroughly investigated the Vinaya section and listened to the *Tiantai Wenzhu* (Textual Commentary). He settled his mind in the Perfect and Sudden *Zhi Guan* (Calming and Contemplation).

Later, upon reading the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he found its literary style and principles so vast and profound that he could not yet fully comprehend them. One night, after reciting the sutra for a long time, he dozed off at his desk.
In a dream, he saw a solar disc descend from the sky and opened his mouth to swallow it. From that moment, he suddenly attained awakening regarding the various categories of meaning.
He was suddenly liberated and free from all obstructions. Later, he attended Master Yongming, who merely confirmed his previous understanding and offered no further instructions or metaphors.
This concludes the account of Chan Master Yihai of Ruiyan (d.u.), the eleventh generation descendant of Nanyue (a successor of Yunju Qi).
Chan Master Yihai of Ruiyan in Mingzhou was a native of Xichuan. He went to the Dharma seat of Yunju, where Yunju asked him, "What kind of thing comes like this?
At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse, which says:
"Yunju’s 'What kind of thing?'— When questioned, my head grows dazed. To accept it directly as it is— Even that is still buried in birth."
Chan Master Weizheng of Jingtu Monastery in Hangzhou (a dharma heir of Chan Master Sufu of Jingtu).
He was the son of the Huang family of Huating in Xiuzhou. He took up his staff and traveled eastward.

He studied the Three Contemplations (*sanguan*) at Tiantai and subsequently returned to Mount Jing. There, he consulted the veteran master Wuisu regarding the principle of the single transmission (*danchuan*).
Wuisu was presiding over the Jingtu Monastery on Mount Gongchen in Lin’an, and the Master assisted him there; after a long time, he succeeded him upon the seat.
When Ye Qingchen, the Palace Secretary, was governing Jinling, he invited the Master to discuss the Way. One day, Ye said, "Tomorrow, at the Prefectural..."
There was a banquet and drinking party. The Master, being strictly observant of the precepts, replied, "Could you please stay for one more day to enjoy some pure conversation?
The Master consented. The following day, a messenger was sent to invite him; the Master left behind a single verse and departed, saying: "Yesterday I took it as today; Today I take it as tomorrow."
Leaving the gate, leaning on his staff, he reflected again: "As a monk, it would be more fitting to dwell among the crags and valleys;

this is quite unsuitable for the midst of a banquet for the state's elite. The guests sitting there all admired his refined bearing. The Master was naturally fond of riding a yellow calf when going out or coming in;

he would hang his *kamaṇḍalu*, headcloth, and alms bowl upon its horns, and the people in the market would vie with one another to gaze at him. Once, the Governor of Hangzhou, Vice Minister Jiang, was dining with the Master.

The "Friend Beyond the World" (Fangwai You) would frequently go to visit him. Upon arriving at the courtyard of the commandery, he would unyoke his oxen and spend the entire day in conversation and laughter before departing.
Jiang composed a poem that says: "The Zen guest regularly enters the old capital; A water jar hangs from the horn of a yellow ox. Sometimes he goes through clouds and across snow;
It would be well to paint him together with the clouds. The Master once composed a verse while in the mountains, which begins: "On the mountain above the bridge..."
Ten thousand layers. Beneath the bridge, the water flows for a thousand li. Only the white herons know that I come here constantly.
*Chiao-wai pieh-chuan*, Scroll 13;
*Chiao-wai pieh-chuan*, Scroll 14.
Chan Master Xingsi of Qingyuan, Dharma heir of the Sixth Patriarch, Chan Master Dajian:
Chan Master Xingsi was a native of the Liu clan of Ancheng in his home province of Jizhou. From childhood...
He left home at the age of twenty-six. Whenever he sat in a group to discuss the Way, his teacher remained silent. Upon hearing of the Dharma seat at Caoxi, he went there to pay his respects.
He asked, "What should I devote myself to, so that I do not fall into stages? The Patriarch replied, "What have you been doing until now?"

The Master said, “I do not even practice the Noble Truths. The Patriarch asked, “In what rank do you fall? The Master replied, “Since I do not even practice the Noble Truths, what rank could there be?
The Patriarch held him in high esteem. (Jingshan Daoyuan said: Do not treat idle talk as mere idle talk; often matters arise from idle talk. Chushih Zongqi said:
For one who plays with lumps of mud, what limit is there? Although the disciples under his guidance were numerous, the Master stood at their head, just as the Second Patriarch did.

It is said that at Shaolin, [Huike] was told he had attained the marrow. One day, the Patriarch said to the Master (Bodhidharma): "Since the beginning, the robe and the Dharma have been transmitted together;

from master to disciple they have been handed down in succession. The robe serves as a token of faith, while the Dharma is the seal upon the mind. Now that I have found the right person, what need is there to worry about a lack of faith?"
"Since I received this robe, I have encountered many hardships. How much more so will those who come in future generations, for whom contention will surely be frequent?

Let the robe remain here to guard the mountain gate. You, however, should propagate the teaching in one region so that it does not become extinct. Once the Master had received the Dharma, he returned to reside at Qingyuan.
(6) When the Sixth Patriarch was about to pass away, the śrāmaṇera Xiqian (who was later known as Master Shitou) asked him, "Master, [you have lived] for a hundred..."
Three years later, Xiqian asked, "I do not yet know whom I should rely upon. The Patriarch said, "Go and seek it out.

When the Patriarch passed away, Xiqian would often sit upright in a quiet place, as still and silent as if he had forgotten his very birth. The Head Seat asked him, "Your teacher has already passed away."
"What are you doing sitting here in vain? Xuanzang said, "I am following my late master’s final instructions, which is why I am searching for him.
Daozuo said, "You have an elder brother, Master Si, who currently resides in Jizhou. Your karmic connection lies there; your teacher’s words were very direct, yet you have simply lost your way."
Upon hearing these words, Xuanqian bowed and took his leave of the patriarch’s shrine, proceeding directly to visit Master Jingju.
The Master asked, "From where have you come? Xuanqian replied, "From Caoxi. The Master asked, "What have you brought back? He said, "Even before reaching Caoxi, there was nothing lost.
The Master said, "If that is so, what was the use of going to Caoxi? He replied, "If I had not gone to Caoxi, how would I have known it was not lost?"
Shi said, "The Great Master of Caoxi, do you still recognize the Abbot? The Master asked, "Do you recognize me now?
Shi replied, "I recognize him; yet how could one possibly recognize him? The Master said, "Though there may be many horns, a single qilin is enough. Xuanzhen asked again.
"Since you, Preceptor, left Caoxi, when did you arrive here? The Master said, "I actually know the time and occasion of your departure from Caoxi.
[Xiqian] said, "Xiqian did not come from Caoxi. The Master said, "I also know where you have gone."
The Master said, "Venerable One, you are fortunately a great man; do not act rashly. On another day, the Master again asked Xian, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Caoxi.
The Master then raised his whisk and said, "Is there such a thing as this at Caoxi?
He replied, "Not only at Caoxi, but even in the Western Heavens there is none. The Master said, "Have you perhaps been to the Western Heavens? He replied, "If I had gone, then there would be."
The Master said, "Not yet; speak further. [Mazu] said, "Master, you too must say at least half of it; do not rely entirely on this student.
The Master said, "I do not refuse to tell you, but I fear that in the future there will be no one to take it up.
The Master then ordered Qian to deliver a letter to National Teacher Huairang of Mount Nanyue, saying: "Once you have delivered the letter, return quickly. I have a small adze."

Dongshan Shouquan lived with you on the mountain; when he moved to that other place, before even presenting his letter, he asked: "When one does not admire the various sages and does not prize one's own spiritual nature, what then?
Nanyue said, "Your question is far too high, my son. Why not ask about things below?

Dongshan said, "I would rather suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eternal kalpas than seek liberation by following the various sages. Thereupon, Nanyue ceased speaking. (Xuansha Shibei said: "How great was Stonehead!")

He was toppled by Nanyue, and even until now he has not been able to rise. Xuedou Xian said, "Shitou ended up carrying a wooden board across his back. He also said, "How great, how great is Dayi! He did not know how to enforce the mandate.
