His words were not complete, and thus he was criticized by others. At that time, when he waited for Danxia to speak, [Danxia] said, "You have misjudged many people of the various quarters. [Dongshan] merely clapped his hands and laughed, saying, "This old fellow is much like one who confesses before he is beaten.
If this is so, then even the venerable Old Danxia could not avoid being made suspicious.
Chan Master Dadian Baotong (Dharma Heir of Shitou Xiqian).
Chan Master Dadian Baotong of Ling Shan in Chaozhou first visited Shitou. Shitou asked, "Which one is your mind?
The Master replied, "The one that perceives these words. Shitou then shouted at him and sent him out. After ten days had passed, the Master asked again.
The Master said, "The former is not it. Apart from this, what is the mind? Shitou said, "Set aside the raising of eyebrows and blinking of eyes;
bring forth the mind. The Master said, "There is no mind that can be brought forth. Shitou said, "Originally there is a mind; why do you say there is no mind?
To say there is no mind is to slander it entirely. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment. (Jingshan Daokai said: "Tell me, what did Dadian realize? )
On another day, while standing in attendance, Shitou asked, "Are you a monk who practices Zen, or are you a monk who merely tramples upon the districts and prefectures?
The Master replied, "I am a monk who practices Zen. Shitou asked, "What is Zen? The Master said, "Raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye.
Shitou said, "Setting aside raising an eyebrow and blinking an eye, present me with your original face. The Master said, "Please [accept it], Reverend."
Xiang removed the external mirrors of raising eyebrows and blinking eyes. Shitou said, "I have already removed them. Xiang said, "I have presented them to you.
Shitou said, "Since you have presented them to me, what is my mind like? Xiang said, "It is no different from the Master's.
Shitou said, "That does not concern you. Xiang said, "Fundamentally there is nothing. Shitou said, "You, too, are without anything. Xiang said, "Since..."
"No thing is itself the true thing. Shitou said, "The true thing cannot be obtained; the meaning of your mind’s perception and measurement is such as this.
You must protect and maintain it with great care. One day, Han Yu, the Duke of Wen, visited him and asked, "How old are you, Master?"
The Master held up his prayer beads and asked, "Do you understand? The official said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "One hundred and eight times, day and night.
The official did not comprehend this and returned home. On the following day, he came again; upon reaching the gate, he saw the Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) repeating the previous conversation.
He asked him, "What was the meaning of that? The Head Seat clicked his teeth three times. When he saw the Master repeat the same question, the Master likewise clicked his teeth three times.
The Duke said, "It turns out that the Buddha-dharma is not of two kinds. The Master asked, "What is the principle behind this?

The Duke replied, "Just now, when I questioned the Head Seat, he answered in exactly the same way. The Master then summoned the Head Seat and asked, "Was it you who answered thus? The Head Seat replied, "Yes."

The Master then struck him and drove him out of the monastery. (Baofu Zhan said: "The Head Seat knows the beginning but not the end; Dayuan’s command was not issued in isolation. Jingshan Xìn said: "Master Dayuan was like drawing a bow after the thief had fled;
he buried the layman alive. Even so, he could only save half of him. He then offered this verse: "At night, the thief was bitten by a dog; the hole in the wall was hurriedly patched up well.

Had it been patched poorly, how many in Chang'an would have known the dawn? On another day, Master Wen addressed the Teacher, saying: "My duties as the Prefectural Governor are numerous; I pray for the essential points of the Buddha-dharma."
[Daoyuan] said, "I request a word from the Master. The Master remained silent for a long while. Daoyuan was at a loss. At that time, Sanping was serving as the attendant;
he struck the meditation seat three times. The Master asked, "What is this? Sanping replied, "First move with concentration, then extract with wisdom.
Daoyuan then said, "The Master’s teaching style is lofty and steep; I have found a point of entry through the attendant. (Wuzu Jie spoke on behalf of Dadian.)

Xiyuan Bao said: "Although the attendant was a skilled assistant, this was still 'striking the upright because of the crooked. Master Wen obtained a point of entry and ultimately remained a mere subject and son. Jie’s act of striking the attendant on behalf of Dadian was not as good as letting the matter pass.
Then, after a long silence, he said: 'Do you understand? Sincere hearts are few who recognize; when faced directly, the deluded are many.'"
Chan Master Changzi Kuang (Dharma Heir of Shitou Xiqian).
Chan Master Changzi Kuang of Tanzhou went to pay homage at the ancestral stupa at Caoxi; upon his return, he visited Shitou.
Shitou asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Lingnan. Shitou said, "The merit shop at the head of Mount Dayu has been completed."
"Not yet," said the Master. "He has been accomplished for a long time; he simply lacks the 'dotting of the eyes' (*kaṭākṣa*).
Shitou asked, "Do you wish for the dotting of the eyes? The Master replied, "I request it at once. Shitou then lowered one foot. The Master prostrated himself.
Shitou asked, "What principle did you perceive that you prostrate yourself? The Master replied, "According to what I have perceived, it is like [a spark] upon a red-hot furnace."

Dianxue (Baoci) then said: "Tell me, does Changzi respond with eyes, or does he respond without eyes? If he has eyes, why does he ask for his eyes to be opened? If he has no eyes, it is also said that [his realization] has been accomplished for a long time.
How do you resolve this? Qingliang Qin spoke on his behalf: "The Master may be said to have clouded vision. Xuedou Xian said: "If there are no eyes, what is there to open?

Yunju Yuan said: "A pity to labor in vain. Jingshan Gao said: "There has been much deliberation among the assembly. Some say: 'If there are no eyes, what is there to open? Others say: 'Does he not want his eyes opened? Wait until he says, "Please," and then strike him across the back. If one acts thus, it is not yet sufficient."

[The monk] wished to avoid defiling this merit. Yunmen, however, was not like that; he waited for this old fellow to lower one foot and simply said, "Rise, Master. Chushi Qi said: "Long-beard [Wuzhuo] came personally from Dayu Ridge, yet he was pointlessly deceived by Shitou.

What did he see that he asked, 'Is this set of merit-images finished yet? It is like driving a stake into empty space. Furthermore, Long-beard could not hold his ground and said, 'It has been finished for a long time; it only lacks the dotting of the eyes.'"

"One blind man leading a crowd of blind men. Stonehead lowered one foot; would he still have been able to open their eyes? "If one person is not yet awake, two are even more bewildered. It is like a single speck of snow on a red-hot furnace—truly so. Everyone must take care not to catch the echo or rely on the void;
it is but empty talk and false speech. When Layman Pang arrived, the Master ascended the seat.

Once the assembly had gathered, the Layman stepped forward and said, "Each of you should examine yourselves," and then stood to the right of the meditation platform. At that time, a monk asked: "Without touching the master of the house, please..."
The Master answered the question. The Master said, “Do you recognize Master Pang? [Pang] replied, “I do not.
The layman then grabbed the monk and said, “Alas, alas! The monk had no reply. The layman then let him go. A short while later, the Master asked, “Did that monk just now receive a blow of the staff?
The layman said, “I will wait until he is willing before I do so. The Master said, “The layman sees only the sharpness of the tip of the awl.”
[The Master said: "I do not see the square head of the chisel. The layman said, "If you speak in such a way, it is fine for me;
however, if outsiders hear this, it will surely not be good. The Master asked, "In what way would it not be good? The layman said, "You, Master, see only the sharp point of the awl;
you do not see the keen edge of the chisel. Li Xingpo came. The Master then asked her, "Do you remember when we were in Jangzhou?"

"What is the matter? the old woman asked. "It is not that you, Master, do not understand," the Master replied. "There is much falsehood and little truth in it," she said. "What is there to hide? he asked.
"I am mindful that you are a woman, so I let you go with your staff," she said.
"I have never seen any fault in the Venerable One," she continued. "Where does the old monk’s fault lie? he asked. "The Teacher has no fault; how could I [have one]? she replied.
"Transgression. The Master said, "What about one who has committed no transgression? The old woman then held up her fist and said, "In this way, everything becomes inverted.
The Master said, "Truly, there is nowhere to hide."
Chan Master Shili of Jingzhao (Dharma heir of Shitou Xiqian).
Chan Master Shili of Jingzhao Prefecture asked Shitou, "What is the student’s fundamental matter? Shitou said, "Why do you seek it from me?
[The master] said, "I do not seek it from the teacher. [Shitou asked,] "How then can it be attained? Shitou said, "Do you still..."
"Have you ever lost anything? The Master then realized its essential meaning.
Chan Master Huilang of Zhaoti Monastery (a Dharma heir of Shitou Xiqian):
Chan Master Huilang of Zhaoti Monastery in Tanzhou was a native of Qujiang in Shixing. He first went to visit Mazu. Mazu...
The Master asked, "What do you seek by coming here? He replied, "I seek the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. The Patriarch said, "The Buddha has no knowledge or vision;

knowledge and vision are merely demons. From where have you come? He replied, "I have come from Mount Nanyue. The Patriarch said, "Since you have come from Mount Nanyue, you have not yet recognized the essential heart of Caoxi.
You should return there quickly; it is not fitting for you to go elsewhere. The Master returned to Shitou and immediately asked, "What is the Buddha?"
Shitou said, "You have no Buddha-nature. The Master asked, "What then of all sentient beings who move and stir?
Shitou replied, "All sentient beings who move and stir indeed possess Buddha-nature. The Master asked, "Why then does Huirang lack it? Shitou said, "It is because you are unwilling to accept it.
At these words, the Master attained faith and entry. Later, whenever students arrived, he would simply say to them, "Go."
"Go! You have no Buddha-nature" (at that time he was called Dàlǎng).
Chan Master Zhènlǎng of Xìngguó Temple in Chángshā (Dharma heir of Shítóu Qiān):
Chan Master Zhènlǎng of Xìngguó Temple in Chángshā first visited Shítóu and immediately asked, "What is the Patriarch?"
Regarding the meaning of the Westward Transmission, Shitou said, "Go ask the pillar. [Zhenglang] said, "I do not understand. Shitou said, "I, too, do not understand.
At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Chan Master Fotuo of Famen Monastery in Fengxiang Prefecture (dharma heir of Shitou Xiqian).
He habitually held a string of prayer beads and recited three names:
first, Śākyamuni; second, Yuanhe; third, Fotuo. As for everything else, what is it but a "wan-die-qiu" (a broken bowl)?
He then passed through a single pearl, ending and beginning again; his deeds were extraordinary, and people of the time could not fathom them.
As for Chan Master Ji of Datong in Dingshui (the Dharma heir of Shitou Xiqian):
when Mihu arrived leading a multitude and was just about to meet him, the Master suddenly pulled him back.
He sat facing the wall on his meditation seat. After Mi Hu had stood behind him for a short while, he returned to the guest area. The Master said, "It is indeed so;

however, if you do not test and break through this [delusion], you will later suffer at the hands of those who disparage and strip you of your dignity. He then ordered an attendant to invite Mi Hu to come back.
[The Master] pulled the meditation bench over and sat upon it. The Master then circumambulated the bench once and returned to his quarters.
Mihu, however, pulled the meditation bench over and led the assembly out. The Master visited Layman Pang. The Layman said, "When I was in my mother’s womb, there was a saying;
let me present it to you, Master. You must not attempt to explain it through intellectual reasoning. The Master—
[The Master] said, "This is still a matter of being separated by lifetimes. The Layman said, "I told you before that one must not construct rationalizations.
The Master said, "That is a startling statement; how could one not be afraid? The Layman said, "According to your understanding, it may indeed be called startling.

The Master said, "By not constructing rationalizations, you have instead constructed a rationalization. The Layman said, "It is not merely a separation of one or two lifetimes. The Master said, [silently].
"A monk who subsists on gruel and rice may be scrutinized as he pleases. The Layman snapped his fingers three times.
One day, when Master [Zhaozhou] saw Layman Pang approaching, he immediately shut the door and said, "An old man of many knowledges—do not meet with me.
The Layman said, "Sitting alone and speaking to oneself—who is at fault? The Master then opened the door; as soon as he stepped out, he was seized by the Layman, who said, "Master!"

"I am very knowledgeable; I am very knowledgeable," [the layman] said. The Master replied, "Let us set aside your great knowledge for a moment. When a door is closed and when it is opened, when it is rolled up and when it is spread out—how much difference is there between them?
The layman said, "Just this one question would have sufficed to kill me with its intensity. The Master remained silent. The layman said:
Seeking cleverness and ending up with clumsiness.
The Third Generation under Qingyuan:
Chan Master Zongzhi of Daowu (Dharma heir of Yaoshan Yan).
Chan Master Zongzhi of Daowu Mountain in Tanzhou was the son of the Zhang family of Haihun in Yuzhang.

He joined the dharma assembly of Yaoshan and attained a secret realization of the mind-seal. One day, Yaoshan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from wandering the mountains."
Yaoshan said, "Without leaving this room, quickly bring it forth. The Master said, "The crow on the mountain peak has a head like snow;
the fish swimming in the bottom of the stream are never at rest. After the Master left Yaoshan, he visited Nanquan.
Nanquan asked, "What is your name, *śrāmaṇera*? The Master replied, "Zongzhi. Nanquan said, "Where wisdom does not reach, how do you establish your school? The Master said:
"By all means, do not speak of it. Nanquan said, "If you speak of it, horns will surely grow. Three days later, the Master and Yunyan were at the rear rack mending needles.
Nanquan saw them and asked, "The Dharma-teacher Zhi said the other day, 'Where wisdom does not reach, by all means do not speak of it;
if you speak of it, horns will grow. How, then, should one practice? The Master then—
Withdrawing his hand, he entered the Sangha hall. Nanquan then returned to the abbot’s quarters. The Master came again to hold the needle.
Yunyan said, "Disciple, why did you not respond to the Master just now? The Master replied, "You are quite clever.
Yunyan did not grasp the meaning, so he asked Nanquan, "Why did that Zen monk (Zhidoutuo) not respond to the Master just now? I..."
[The assembly] gathered. They requested the Master to provide instruction. Nanquan said, "He indeed walks among the heterodox species.
Yunyan asked, "What is it to walk among the heterodox species? Nanquan said, "Have you not heard it said: 'Where wisdom does not reach, one must strictly avoid speaking'?
If you speak, horns will grow. You must directly walk among the heterodox species. Yunyan also did not understand. The Master knew that Yunyan...
Yunyan did not present him [to Mazu]. He then said, "This person's karmic conditions do not lie here; let us return together to Yaoshan.

Upon their return, Yaoshan asked, "Why have you returned so quickly? Yunyan replied, "It was simply because our karmic conditions were not in accord. Yaoshan asked, "What were those karmic conditions?"
Yunyan brought up the previous conversation. Yaoshan said, "How do you understand why he returned at that very moment?
Yunyan had no reply. Yaoshan then laughed heartily. Yunyan then asked, "What is it to walk among those of different species?"
Yaoshan said, “I am weary today; wait until another time to come. Yunyan said, “I have returned specifically for this matter.
Yaoshan said, “Go now. Yunyan then departed. Standing outside the abbot’s quarters, the Master heard that Yunyan had not attained realization;
unconsciously, he bit his finger until it bled. The Master then came down and asked Yunyan, “Elder brother, did you understand?”
[The monk] went to ask the Abbot about that causal condition: "What was it? Yunyan said, "The Abbot did not tell me. The Master then bowed his head. [A monk asked Yunju:

"One must avoid saying anything—what does this mean? Yunju said, "These words are most poisonous. [The monk asked: "What are the most poisonous words? Yunju said, "A single blow of the staff kills both dragon and snake.
When Yunyan was about to pass away, he left a letter to take leave of the Master. After the Master had finished reading the letter, he said to Dongsan Mi:
The Master (Shibai) said, "Yunyan did not know 'there is. I regret not having said it to him at that time.

Nevertheless, even so, he did not fail to be a true son of Yaoshan. (Baoci then said, "When the ancients spoke thus, did they still know 'there is' or not? Furthermore, Yunyan did not understand at that time; tell me,")

"Where is it that he does not understand? Cuiyan Zhi said: "Daowu said, 'Yunyan did not know there was [something more]. He regretted not having told him back then. But as for saying this—did Daowu actually know there was [something more] or not?
Yaoshan ascended the hall and said: "I have a single phrase that I have never yet spoken to anyone. A monk stepped forward and said: "It has followed me here. A monk asked Yaoshan:
"How do you speak this one phrase? Yaoshan said: "It is not something spoken. The Master (Shishuang Qingzhu) said: "..."
[This] was already explained long ago. One day, the Master took up his rain hat and went out. Yunyan pointed to the hat and asked, "What will you do with this?
The Master said, "It has its uses. Yunyan said, "What if a black wind and a violent rain should come upon you?
The Master said, "I will cover myself with it. Yunyan said, "Will it still accept being covered? The Master said, "Even so..."
It is so. Furthermore, there is no leakage. ○ Miaoshan asked Yunyan, "What serves as the seat for Bodhi?
Yunyan replied, "The unconditioned (wuwei) serves as its seat. Yunyan then asked Miaoshan, to which Miaoshan replied, "The emptiness of all phenomena (dharmas) serves as its seat."
He asked the Master, "What is it like? The Master said, "If he sits, let him sit; if he lies down, let him lie down.
But there is one person who neither sits nor lies down—speak quickly, speak quickly! Guishan then desisted. Guishan asked the Master, "Where have you come from?
The Master said, "I have come to visit the sick. Guishan said, "How many people are ill? The Master said, "There are those who are ill, and there are those who are not."
“Not being ill,” Baizhang said. Guishan asked, “Is this not Master Zhidoutuo? Baizhang replied, “Being ill and not being ill—neither concerns him at all.
Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Guishan said, “Even if one could speak it, it would have nothing to do with him.
Yunyan asked, “How is the style of your house, my younger brother, these days? Baizhang said, “I ask my elder brother to point it out for me.”
"What can he do? Yunyan said, "He has not come for this; how much time has passed? The Master said, "The roots of his teeth still retain a trace of rawness.
A donor offered a pair of trousers. Yaoshan held them up and showed them to the assembly, saying, "Does the Dharma-body still possess the four great elements?
If anyone can say so, I will give him a pair of trousers. The Master said, "The nature-ground is not empty."
"Emptiness is not the earth-element; this is the earth-element. The same applies to the other three great elements. Yaoshan said, "I give you a waist-cloth.
Yunyan was unwell, so the Master said to him, "Apart from this leaking shell, where shall we meet?"
Yunyan said, “We meet at the place of neither arising nor ceasing. The Master said, “Why not say that we do not meet even at the place of neither arising nor ceasing?
(Xuedou Xian said, “Attendant, take note of this question for me. Zhaojue Qin said, “Where would one not encounter him?
While Yunyan was mending his shoes, the Master asked, “What are you doing? Yunyan said, “I am mending what is worn out with what is worn out. The Master said, “...”
"Why do you not say that it is both ruined and not ruined? The Master heard a monk reciting the *Vimalakīrti Sūtra*, which says:
"Eight thousand bodhisattvas and five hundred śrāvakas all wished to follow Mañjuśrī. The Master asked, "Where are they going? The monk had no reply, so the Master struck him.
(Later, a monk asked Heshan Yin about this; Heshan said, "Only when one serves as an attendant will it be appropriate. The Master arrived at Wufeng.
Wu-feng asked, "Do you still recognize the old master Yaoshan? The Master said, "I do not recognize him. Wu-feng said, "Why do you not recognize him?
The Master said, "I do not recognize him. Shi-shuang asked, "The Master’s single piece of bone rings like bronze when struck."
"Where have you been going? The Master called to his attendant. The attendant responded, "Yes. The Master said, "When will you ever get there?
It will be like the year of the donkey! Chan Master Tansheng of Yunyan (Dharma heir of Yaoshan Weiyan).
Chan Master Tansheng of Yunyan was a native of the Wang family in Jianchang, Zhongling. He studied under Chan Master Baizhang Huaihai.

The Master [Huangbo] spent twenty years [at Baizhang], but the karmic conditions were not yet harmonized. Later, he went to Yeshan. Yeshan asked, "Where have you come from? He replied, "From Baizhang.
Yeshan said, "What words or phrases did Baizhang use to instruct his disciples? The Master said, "He usually says: 'I have a single phrase that possesses all one hundred flavors.
Yeshan said, "'If it is salty, it has the flavor of salt; if it is bland, it has the flavor of blandness. It is not salty...'"
"Not bland; this is the flavor of the eternal. "How is it that the phrase 'endowed with a hundred flavors' is realized? The Master had no reply.
Yaoshan said, "What can you do about birth and death right before your eyes? The Master said, "There is no birth and death before my eyes.
Yaoshan asked, "How long have you been at Baizhang? The Master said, "Twenty years. Yaoshan said, "Having spent twenty years at Baizhang, you still have the air of a layman."
Nor did he remove it. On another day, while standing in attendance, Yaoshan asked again, “What further Dharma did Baizhang teach?

The Master replied, “At times he said: ‘Beyond the three phrases, one must let go; within the six phrases, one must realize. Yaoshan said, “Three thousand miles away, I am glad you have no connection [to that].
Yaoshan asked again, “What further Dharma did he teach? The Master replied, “At times he would ascend...”

Chan Master Chuanzhi Decheng (Dharma Heir of Yaoshan Yan).
Chan Master Chuanzhi Decheng of Huating in Xiuzhou was of lofty integrity and possessed a measure that was beyond the common.
Having had his mind certified by Yaoshan, he maintained a bond of spiritual fellowship with Daowu and Yunyan. Upon leaving Yaoshan, he said to the two of them:
The fellow practitioners said, "You gentlemen should each take charge of a region and establish the school of Yaoshan. As for me, my nature is rustic and wild;
I only delight in mountains and waters, seeking to dispel my emotions through such pleasures, and I possess no other ability.

In the future, should you learn where I reside, if you encounter a sharp and talented presiding master (zuozhu), send one person here. If they prove capable of being refined, I shall transmit to them that which I have practiced throughout my life."

He succeeded in repaying the kindness of his former master. Thereupon, they parted ways and traveled to Huating in Xiuzhou, where he floated upon a small boat, passing his days according to circumstances to receive those coming and going from all quarters.
At that time, no one knew of his lofty conduct, so he was known as the Boatman Monk (*Chuanzi Heshang*).
One day, while mooring his boat by the bank and sitting idly, an official asked him, "What is the meaning of the 'Harmony' (*He')?"

While they were engaged in their daily activities, the Master held up an oar and asked, "Do you understand? The official said, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The oar sweeps through the clear waves;
a golden-scaled fish is rarely encountered. Later, Daowu arrived at Jingkou and encountered Jiaoshan while he was presiding over the assembly.

Mount said, "In what way am I at fault? I hope you will explain it to me. Daowu said, "I shall certainly not say anything.
I ask that you, Master, instead go to Chuanzi at Huating. Jia Shan asked, "What kind of person is he?
Daowu said, "This man has not a single tile above him and not a needle’s point of ground below. If you, Master, go there, you must go in disguise."

There are four kinds of people. The first person has surpassed the Buddhas and patriarchs in their speech, yet cannot take even a single step in practice.

In the moment of action, there is no yielding; face-to-face, they vie for precedence. With their interlocking points and crisscrossing patterns, they mutually preserve and mutually seize. Everywhere it is said that this is 'a master hand displaying its skill among master hands. Is this truly so, or not? From the perspective of Huirui’s insight, if Zunbuna can be careful at the beginning and guard against the end, and wait for Shaoshan to point out the path, he will take a swift stride and ascend directly into the inner sanctum.

You may rest assured that he will be accommodated beneath the bright window. This not only cuts off the entanglements of conceptual proliferation, but also avoids being caught on others' hooks and lines. Why? Because where a single move has not yet reached its limit, the entire board remains empty and ready for use."

Chan Master Gantun of Touzi (a fellow dharma-heir of Touzi).
While Chan Master Gantun of Touzi was traveling in the mountains, he saw a cicada’s exuviae. An attendant asked, "The shell is right here;
where has the cicada gone? The Master picked up the shell, shook it three or five times by his ear, and made the sound of a cicada. The attendant—
At this, he attained awakening.
Regarding Chan Master Yanzhun of Guanyin Monastery in Dongjing (a Dharma heir of Touzi):
Chan Master Yanzhun of Guanyin Monastery in Dongjing was the son of the Lin family of Xingtai. He went to visit Touzi. Touzi—
Question: "Where did you stay last night? The Master said: "In the Immovable Site of Enlightenment (*acalabodhimaṇḍa*). Touzi said: "If you say it is immovable, how did you come here?
The Master said: "Having arrived here—how could that be movement? Touzi said: "So, you originally stayed in a place of non-attachment."
Touzi silently consented to this. He subsequently resided at Guanyin Temple, where his community regularly numbered several hundred.

During the reigns of Emperors Gaozu and Shizong of the Zhou dynasty, when the two emperors were living in seclusion, they would invariably pay him homage whenever he ascended to the abbot’s quarters. Upon their accession to the throne, they specially bestowed upon him purple robes and appointed him as the Great Master of Pure Precepts (Jingjie Dashi).
Chan Master Wuyin of Heishan (Dharma heir of Jiufeng Qian), sixth generation below Qingyuan.
Chan Master Wuyin of Heishan was a native of the Wu clan of Fuzhou. At the age of seven, he left home to become a monk under Xuefeng.
Having received full ordination according to his age, he went to visit Jiufeng. Jiufeng asked, "You have come from afar; you follow the assembly with a dazed look.
What kind of realm is this in which you practice cultivation? By what path can you achieve liberation? The Master replied, "The deep darkness has been cleared away, yet the blind remain blind.
Jiufeng then permitted him to enter the room. Later, he resided at Heshan during the reign of Li [Yong] of Jiangnan.
The Lord summoned him and asked, "Where have you come from, Master? The Master replied, "From Heishan. The Lord asked, "Where is that mountain?
The Master said, "People come to pay court at the Phoenix Palace; the mountains and peaks never move. The Lord held him in high esteem.

Regarding "Clearing the Slash-and-Burn Fields," Yongquan asked, "After the fire has burned out, what is the matter? The Master replied, "An iron snake cannot penetrate it.
Chuanchu of Qingfeng (Dharma successor of Luopu An).
Chuanchu of Qingfeng Monastery in Fengxiang Prefecture was a native of Jingzhou. One day, Luopu asked him: "The monastery..."
"Master, where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from sweeping the snow. Luopo asked, "How deep is the snow? The Master said, "It covers everything on the trees.
Luopo said, "That may be so, but hereafter you will surely dwell in a snow cave. Later, he visited Baihui.
Baihui asked, "I have heard it said that Luopo has a path of vital energy (*shengji*). Is this true? The Master replied, "Yes."
Baishui said, "Block off the path of the living and come toward the path of the dead. The Master said, "On the path of the living, there are countless dead people;
on the path of the dead, no living man finds a place. Baishui said, "This is the way of Luopu; what about yours?
The Master said, "Not only Luopu, even Jiashan could do nothing about it. Baishui asked, "Why was it that Jiashan..."
"How can one do anything about it? The Master said, "Have you not heard that there is a path of the living mechanism?

The monk had no reply. Lopu said, "I give you ten days. If you can provide a suitable phrase, I will let you go.
The monk practiced walking meditation and searched in the darkness; by chance, he entered the garden. The Master asked him, "Venerable sir, since you were about to depart, why are you here now?
The monk explained his situation in detail and earnestly requested that the Master provide the words for him. The Master said, "How could dense bamboo hinder the flow of water? The mountain..."

Under Rize’s seat there were five hundred people; later, while residing at Yong’an, his assembly numbered over five hundred.
Thus, it truly accorded with Lopu’s prediction. Dongxi Jiding Chan Master (the dharma heir of Lopu An).
Chan Master Jieding of Dongxi in Jiazhou first questioned Luopu: "The moon-tree has no branches, yet it provides long-lasting shade;
I pray that the Master will directly point out the wondrous, profound mystery. Luopu said: "In the place where the myriad phenomena flourish, things do not rely upon one another;
with a thousand waves in the clear water, the solitary peak stands apart. Thereupon, the Master attained the essential meaning.
Chan Master Mudeng Shandao (Dharma heir of Wen Panlong).
Chan Master Mudeng Shandao of Mount Mudeng in Yuanzhou first visited Luopo and asked: "Before the single bubble has even arisen..."
"How does one discern the course of the water? Luopu said, "Shift the boat to learn the water's pulse; raise the oar to distinguish the waves.
The Master did not attain realization and went to consult Panlong. He asked the same question as before. Panlong said, "Shift the boat and you do not recognize the water;

raise the oar and you immediately lose the source. From this, the Master attained awakening. (Yunfeng Yue said: "If Muping had understood under Luopu's words, he would still have had some margin for improvement. It is a pity that he turned toward Panlong.")

Chan Master Wuben Liangjie of Mount Dong in Ruizhou. He was the son of the Yu family of Kuaiji. In his youth, he followed a teacher and practiced recitation.

why does the sūtra say they do not exist? The teacher was startled and marveled at him.
He replied, "I am not your teacher. At the age of twenty-one, he received full ordination at Mount Song and began his travels.

Later, as the Master was crossing a stream with Dongshan, Dongshan asked, “How deep is the water?”
"About how much? The Master said, "Not wet. Dongshan said, "A coarse person. The Master said, "Please, Master, say something. Dongshan said, "Not dry. (Wuzu Yan said:

[The Master] called out, “Dongshan! When Dongshan was thus questioned, his meditation seat shook violently.

He then said, “Master Ying, when I was at Yunyan, I once asked the Old Man [Yunyan], and my meditation seat shook violently. Today, having been questioned by you, my entire body breaks into a sweat. Dayang Huan said:

“The earth shakes. This does not mean that these three old fellows do not exist. If you wish to see Nanquan, you must wait until Maitreya descends to be born. Suddenly, if a man were to come forth and say, “There is no Maitreya above in heaven, and there is no Maitreya below on earth,” then who would be made to descend to be born?

How would you answer this? Simply tell him, “It is the old monk’s own fault. Chushi Qi said: “To cry until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one’s mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring. Later, the Master settled in a hermitage at Sanfeng.
After ten days had passed without him attending the hall, Dongshan asked, “Why have you not been to the hall lately?”

it seems you still hold such a view. "Come back this evening," he added. When the Master returned in the evening, Dongshan called out, "Attendant En! The Master responded.
Dongshan asked, "When you are neither thinking of good nor thinking of evil, what is this? The Master then returned to his hut.
He sat in silent meditation. From that point on, the celestial deity could no longer find him at all. This continued for three days until it ceased. Dongshan asked the Master, "What are you doing?
The Master replied, "I am making sauce. Dongshan asked, "How much salt do you use? The Master replied, "I add it as I go along.
Dongshan asked, "What flavor does it have? The Master replied, "It is perfect. Dongshan asked, "What about a person who is a great icchantika?"

"Regarding the five heinous crimes, where is filial piety and support? The Master said: 'Only then is filial piety and support truly accomplished. From that time on, Dongshan permitted him to be the leader within the meditation hall.

"When will you find the way to turn yourself around? He replied, "The waters are warm and the flowers bloom; spring spreads wide as the swing falls amidst the willow shadows. Official Liu Yu asked, "From where does the rain come?

"This is the teacher of all Buddhas. The Master shouted, "You field rat! The monk bowed. The Master said, "How do you understand this? The monk shouted, "This old monk!

To recognize the opportune moment, to distinguish between fortune and misfortune, and to possess the eye that can turn the pivot through mutual accommodation—such a person is hard to find even among a thousand or ten hundred men.]

"What has become of this beggar who goes around the platform with a begging bowl? It is like loving one's child so much that one fails to notice their ugliness. One can only laugh at the beggar who goes around the platform with a begging bowl—it is like facing south and looking for the Big Dipper. The Master once ordered an attendant to deliver a pair of trousers to a practitioner living in a hermitage.
The practitioner said, "I already have trousers from my mother's birth," and refused them altogether. The Master again ordered the attendant to ask: "Before your mother gave birth to you..."
"What are you attached to? The practitioner was speechless. Later, after he passed away, there were *śarīra* relics.

While the Master was performing manual labor at Dongshan, he accidentally killed a worm with his hoe. Dongshan asked, "What about this one? The Master replied, "It will not die."

Later, a monk asked, "Regarding the story of the Master at Dongshan cutting down earthworms, was it not the case that you had nothing to say? The Master said, "At that time there were words;

"Saint," [he replied]. "Yes, yes"—this was his assent to his own numinous spirit. Xiangyan said, "If you, my junior master, speak thus, you will vomit blood for thirty years from now on.

"Arriving at this point, it is difficult indeed; it is like a lotus flower in the month of December.

"How could one attain it by speaking thus? If it concerns this sick monk, it is not so. Gushan asked, "What is the teacher of Vipaśyin Buddha?

The Monk Xiange of Jingzhao (Dharma Heir of Dongshan Jia).

Having received the seal of mind from Dongshan, he lived among the common people in Minchuan. He did not maintain ritual implements nor did he follow the monastic codes. In winter...
In summer, he wore only a single robe. Day after day, he followed the riverbank to gather shrimp and clams to fill his belly.
At dusk, he would sleep among the paper offerings at the White Horse Temple on Mount Dong. The local residents called him the "Shrimp-Gathering Monk.

Zhuzhu asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? The Master immediately replied, "The wine stand and tray before the deity.

"Qianfeng washed his face and touched his nose; Yunmen ate his meal and bit on grit. When the two met suddenly, it turned out they were old enemies. Even so, I grant that the Old Barbarian (Bodhidharma) may know it, but I do not grant that he may understand it.

He further said: "Both are airing their family’s shame; fortunately, there is no bystander to witness it. One move passed; he has fallen into the second. Suddenly, someone comes forth and strikes him across the spine. Why? To shatter the skull so that all news is exhausted; let the great earth remain dark and vast. Tianqi said: "Even if a single cloud looks upon the moon..."

Within, its radiance illuminates heaven and earth; thus it is no exaggeration to say that for those with clear eyes, there is darkness three feet before them. Do not boast of thunderclaps crashing through the void; in the end, not even a hair’s breadth is revealed. This too is like a pheasant hiding in the mountains—burrowing its head while neglecting its tail.

The Master drew a line with his staff and said: "It is right here. (Later, the monk requested further instruction.)

Yunmen Wenyan held up a fan and said, "The fan leaps and bounds up to the Thirty-three Heavens, striking the nose of Śakra. A single blow to the carp of the Eastern Sea causes rain to pour down like an overturned basin. Do you understand? Xuedou Xian, acting on behalf of the monk, let out a shout.

Furthermore, a monk requested instruction from Changqing, who said, "Go ask the second seat in the hall. Xuedou, acting on behalf of the monk, said, "Wrong. Later, a monk asked Xuedou about this, and Xuedou said, "Falling into a pit, tumbling into a ditch. And again, he said of himself—

The ancients said: "The heart of a thief is naturally timid. Huanglong Nan said: "Qianfeng’s single occasion of pointing the way was a concession to beginners; Yunmen then further transformed it, so that later generations would not grow weary. Daopei Xiu said:

"Ancient and modern alike have all said that Qianfeng settled this monk in the Hall of the Patriarchs and opened a path for future generations. Little do they realize that when this old fellow Qianfeng was questioned by this monk, he was left utterly flustered and at a loss. My worthies, tell me: where does the confusion lie?"

After a long silence, he said: "It is not in the water, nor is it in the mountains; it lies only within the shifting movements of the human mind. Nanhua Bing remarked: "Qianfeng exhausted his compassion to guide the student at the critical moment; Yunmen skillfully opened up expedient means to trigger realization face-to-face."

Directly, it is like withered wood sprouting flowers and cold ashes sending up flames. But tell me: when the carp of the Eastern Sea is struck once, the rain pours down like an overturned basin—what matter on the boundary does this clarify? It is like using the wind to fan a fire; not much effort is required. Wuqian Tai said:

"Holding fast the eye that governs heaven and earth, it is continuous without leaking so much as a hair’s breadth. Playing amidst the various realms of dust, its wondrous function is fully manifested. In the place of stability and secrecy, the three realms are revealed; in the place of solitude and peril, all eight directions are level and smooth.

Chan Master Wensui of Qishan (Dharma heir of Dongshan Jia).
Chan Master Wensui of Qishan was a native of Fuzhou. In his youth, he relied upon Chan Master Huanchong of Mount Daci in Hangzhou to receive his monastic training.
At that time, Yantou and Xuefeng were among the assembly; observing the Master’s discourse, they recognized him as a vessel for the Dharma.
They traveled together to various regions. Each of the two great masters received the seal of transmission from Deshan.
Although the Master frequently challenged and inspired them, they remained ultimately stuck in stagnation. One day, he asked Deshan, "Tianwang spoke thus;
Longtan spoke thus. I wonder, how would you, Reverend, speak? Deshan said, "Try reciting what Tianwang and Longtan said."
[Qingyuan] looked at him. As the Master was about to offer a word in reply, Deshan struck him. Having been struck, the Master returned to the Yanshou Hall and said, "It is so, it is so;
yet he strikes me far too hard. Yantou said, "If you speak like this, you must not say later that you have seen Deshan.

(Fayan Yi commented: "It is so, it is so; yet he strikes me wrongly. Xuedou Xian said, "Virtuous ones, Qinshan established a point of inquiry that is truly extraordinary. Yet, alas, his head is a dragon's while his tail is a snake's. You all try to cite the case of Tianwang Long..."

he did not know how to beat Qinshan back to life. Weishan Zhe said: "Under Deshan’s gate, the grass falls and the wind blows. Daguang Moshan was not like this: when asked, 'I wonder, Master, what will you say? he would strike him across the spine. Now tell me, who is right—Deshan or Moshan?"

"Do you understand? Transversely grasping the Mo-ye sword, he maintains the full and correct command; in this realm of Great Peace, he beheads the deluded and the stubborn. Do you see Deshan? He suddenly picked up his staff, struck it once on the ground, and said: "The thief is the petty person. Later, [Xuedou] attained awakening under Dongshan and became his successor. He was twenty years old [at the time].
7. While staying at Qinsan, he reflected upon his own faults before the great assembly. He recounted the occasion when he was with Dongshan.

At these words, the Master was suddenly enlightened; he prostrated in thanks.
Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen (Dharma Heir of Qinglin Qian).
Chan Master Xianyun of Shimen in Xiangzhou was a native of Jingzhao. Initially, he asked Qinglin, "How should one apply the mind to become equal to all the sages?
Qinglin looked up for a long while and said, "Do you understand? The Master said, "I do not understand. Qinglin said:
"Go. There is no place for a son of the Way to apply his mind. The Master prostrated and attained realization; he did not travel elsewhere again, but instead became a garden head.
One day, while returning to stand in attendance, Qinglin asked, "What have you been doing today, my son? The Master replied, "I have been planting vegetables.
Qinglin said, "The entire world is the Buddha-body; where do you plant them? The Master replied, "The golden hoe does not move."
At Tulei, the spiritual sprouts grow wherever they are planted, and the green forest rejoices. On the following day, Qīnglín entered the garden and called out, “Master Yùn!
The Master responded with an assent. Qīnglín said, “I have planted an extra tree that casts no shadow, to leave for later generations to behold.
The Master said, “If it is a tree that casts no shadow, how could it be planted? Qīnglín said, “Setting aside for a moment its not being planted—have you ever seen its branches and leaves?”
The Master said, “I have never seen it. Qinglin said, “Since you have never seen it, how do you know it does not receive planting?
The Master said, “Precisely because I have never seen it, it does not receive planting. Qinglin said, “So it is, so it is. When Qinglin was about to pass into parinirvāṇa, he summoned the Master.
The Master responded with an assent. Qinglin said, “After the sun has turned behind the western mountains, you must not settle haphazardly.”

The Master said, "Snow fills the golden sandalwood trees; the numinous branches are ever-springing through the ages. Qinglin asked, "If someone were to ask you about the matter of the golden needle and the thread pouch, what would you say?
The Master replied, "If it were something like feathers and wings, I would never dare to speak of it rashly.
At first, he resided at the Lanruo Hermitage on Mount Nanyue. Not long after, he moved to Jiaoshan, traveling there via Tan.
At that time, the Marquis of Chu was coming out of the city to receive him. He immediately asked, "What is the Great Way of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master replied, "Good brother! Your Imperial carriage with its six dragons is a marvel of a thousand ages; the jade-street procession advances forth from the Golden Gate."
The King was greatly pleased. He invited him into the Tianche (Celestial Seal) Palace and provided offerings for several days before they finally reached Jia Shan.

Chan Master Kuangyi of Ziling (a dharma heir of Huayan Jingfa), also known as Chan Master Dingjue of Ziling in Fengxiang Prefecture, first arrived at Panlong. There he saw a monk ask: "The azure abyss..."
"Clear as a mirror—where can a coiling dragon find rest? The Coiling Dragon said, "Sunk in the sand, its bottom is unseen; floating on the waves, it is full of rugged peaks.
The Master did not approve. The Coiling Dragon asked the Master to speak. The Master said, "The golden dragon soars far beyond the azure heavens;
how could it be trapped within the mechanism of the jade wheel in the pool? The Coiling Dragon approved.
Venerable Master Xiangcheng of Jingzhao (Dharma heir of Beiyuan Tong).
Venerable Master Xiangcheng of Jingzhao Prefecture first visited Beiyuan, who asked him: "What is it like when one appears as two?"
Beiyuan said, "One thing has deceived you. At these words, the Master attained realization.
This was Chan Master Qing of Shanglan Yuan, the seventh generation under Qingyuan (he was a dharma successor of Dongshan).
Chan Master Qing of Shanglan Monastery in Ruizhou first traveled to study under Xuefeng. He asked, "What is the very essence of Xuefeng’s meaning?
Xuefeng struck him on the head with his staff. The Master responded, "Yes. Xuefeng laughed heartily.
Later, having received the seal of approval from Dongshan, he opened the Dharma at Shanglan.
Chan Master Huimin of Tongan (Dharma Successor of Dongshan).
Chan Master Huimin of Tongan in Hongzhou first visited Dongshan. He asked, "By what do all the sages take their life?
Dongshan said, "By its non-interruption. The Master asked, "Is there anything further beyond this? Dongshan said, "There is. The Master...
[The Master] asked, "What is the matter that transcends [the ordinary]? Dongshan said, "It does not proceed from interruption.
At these words, the Master attained realization. Chan Master Chilong of Tianchi (dharma heir of Jinfeng Zhifa).
While Chan Master Chilong of Tianchi on Mount Lu was at Jinfeng, during a communal work session of carrying firewood, Jinfeng asked, "Carrying..."
"Does a woodcutter cross over water? The Master said, "There is one person who does not cross over water. [The monk] asked, "If he does not cross over water, does he still carry firewood?
The Master said, "Although he does not carry firewood, you must not disturb him."
Chan Master Huizhong of Guiyang (Dharma heir of Ca’An Yi).
Chan Master Huizhong of Guiyang in Quanzhou was originally a son of the Chen family of that province. He went to visit Ca’An. Ca’An asked, "From where have you come?
The Master replied, "From Mount Liupan. Ca’An asked, "Do you see the six eyes? The Master replied, "I am troubled by my lack of vision."

Tong. Cao’an ignited [the lamp] for him. The Master subsequently returned to his former mountain. It happened that during the reign of Emperor Wuzong of the Tang dynasty, the Buddhist teachings were suppressed;

by imperial decree, the monks were required to adopt the attire of commoners. When Emperor Xuanzong restored the religion, the Master said: "The ancients had a saying: 'A Daoist who ascends does not receive the registers;

a śrāmaṇera who attains Buddhahood does not undergo full ordination. I shall simply remain a layman. I will not eat after midday, and I will practice dhyāna without a fixed dwelling, never venturing beyond my tracks."
Shan (Mountain) was thirty years [in the lineage].
Chan Master Zhi of Tong’an (Dharma heir of Tong’an Pi).
Chan Master Zhi of Tong’an in Hongzhou: Previously, when Tong’an was about to pass away, he ascended the hall and said: "Before the Many-Sons Stupa..."
Zongzi said, "Xiu! What is it like before the Five Old Man Peak? He asked this three times, but no one offered a reply.

Finally, the Master stepped forward and said, "Standing in formation outside the bright-night curtain, ten thousand miles of song and chant proclaim the Great Peace. Tong'an said: [This was the answer].
"It must be this donkey-man indeed.
This refers to Chan Master Dayang Huijian (dharma heir of Lingquan Ren).
Chan Master Dayang Huijian of Yingzhou: initially while at Lingquan, during his entry into the inner chamber, Lingquan asked, "What..."
"Where have you come from? The Master said, "I have come from the Sangha Hall. Lingquan asked, "Why did you not strike the pillar?
At these words, the Master attained realization.
Chan Master Guangde Yi (Dharma Heir of Guangde Yan).
Chan Master Guangde Yi of Xiangzhou went to visit the former Guangde [Yan], paid his respects, and asked, "What is the Master’s secret, hidden place?
Guangde said, "To hide one's body does not necessarily require mountain crags or valleys; in the midst of the bustling marketplace, those who behold it are rare."
The Master said, "If that is so, then one goes on to offer water and flowers. Guangde said, "If suddenly clouds and mist gather, what will you do, Layman?
The Master said, "My drawing of water and gathering of fuel shall not be in vain. Guangde said with joy, "Great assembly, look upon this second-generation Guangde!
The Master subsequently succeeded him as abbot, gathering disciples and opening the Dharma.
Chan Master Ziling Wei (a dharma successor of Ziling Yi).
When Chan Master Ziling Wei first arrived at Jia Shan, Jia Shan asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The Master replied, "From the north."
Jiashan asked, "What lineage do you belong to? The Master replied, "In the past, when the Old Barbarian let out his lion’s roar, the crown of my head split open and remains so to this day;
I am of the eighth generation under Qingyuan."
Chan Master Lian Shan Yuan Guan (Dharma Heir of Tong’an Zhifa).
Chan Master Lian Shan Yuan Guan of Dingzhou. A monk asked, "What is the patriarchal style of the Master? The Master said, "The waters of Yiyang are swift;
fish move with difficulty. The pines of Bailing are tall; birds find it hard to perch. [Another monk] asked, "When the household thief is difficult to guard against..."
"How is it? the Master said. "If you recognize it, it does not become an enemy. The monk asked, "After recognizing it, what then? The Master said, "It is banished to the realm of non-arising.
The monk asked, "Is this not where one establishes one's dwelling and sustains one's life?

The Master said, "Dead water does not harbor dragons. The monk asked, "What is a dragon in living water? The Master said, "It stirs up waves but does not create billows. The monk asked, "What if it suddenly overturns the mountain torrent?"
"How is it when the mountains topple? The Master descended from his seat, seized him, and said, "Do not let it soak the corner of this old monk’s *kāṣāya*.

(Huanglong Qing said: "This old man Liangshan thoroughly understood the pivot of the occasion; he was worthy of being called a master. Yet, alas, by opening the door on a pretext, he led others on until they were caught by the thief. Huanglong would not have done so. Had he seen him ask, 'How is it when the house-thief is difficult to guard?

he would have cut him in two with a single stroke, ensuring he could never again find a place to peek. Nevertheless, if a patch-robed monk were suddenly to come forth and point at the mountain monk, saying, 'Thief! Thief! how would you deal with that? Those with eyes—look!")

This is the clarification of grasping. Huguang Yuan said: "Liangshan only knows how to climb higher step by step; he does not know how to let go from the void. If it were this mountain monk, it would not be so. Suppose someone asked, 'What if you suddenly encounter a situation where the valley floods and the mountains collapse?

I would simply say to him: 'The clouds are at the peak of the ridge, never idle. Tiantong Hua said: "Master Liangshan fought with a thief; sword met sword. With drums beating in a tumultuous clash, although he did not flee abandoning his armor or trailing his weapons, he only knew how to fight the thief—he did not know how to kill the thief.

If someone were to ask me, 'How is it when a thief is difficult to guard against in one's own home? I would strike them across the spine. Why? Have you not heard it said: 'Unify them through ritual'?"
Chan Master Yung-ching Te-fu (Dharma Heir of Huo-kuo Yuan).
Chan Master Yung-ching Te-fu of Hua-an Commandery first visited Huo-kuo and asked: "The direct source of the root is what the Buddhas have certified;
as for picking leaves and seeking branches, I am unable to do so—what then? Huo-kuo said: "Cease grasping at the clouds and trees. Three.
Autumn Fruit: Cease playing with the solitary moon-disc in the azure pool. The Master then suddenly resolved his doubts.
Chan Master Shaoyuan of Shimen (a successor of Shimen Che):
Chan Master Shaoyuan of Shimen in Xiangzhou. Initially, while at Shimen, he was working as a field laborer. Shimen asked him, "How is it?"
"This is the water buffalo at the head of the field. The Master said, "Its horns turn and shake heaven and earth; where there is morning sun, there is spring everywhere.
Later, Shimen asked again, "Is the water buffalo well? The Master said, "It has never lacked grass and water.
[Shimen] asked, "What about the work in the field? The Master said, "Deep plowing and shallow sowing. [Shimen] said, "Are you practicing according to the Dharma? The Master said, "I have not."
Next, regarding Stone Gate (Shimen) Head Seat Jun (a dharma heir of Shimen Che):
Head Seat Jun was a native of Taiyuan. Since arriving at Stone Gate, more than thirty years have passed; the monastic communities have long admired him.
Once, while a monk was invited to drink tea, [the Master] asked, "What is the one stroke by which the Head Seat acts for others?
The Master said, "I still remember it from just now. The monk asked, "And how is it right now? The Master said, "Serve the tea well.
One day, as he entered the garden with a hoe over his shoulder, a monk asked, "Among the three bodies, which one goes to perform manual labor? The Master stood there holding the hoe.
The monk said, "Is it not simply that there is nothing? The Master took up his hoe and walked away.
This was Chan Master Jǐngxuán of Dà'yáng (d.u.), the ninth generation descendant of Qīngyuán [Huìzhāo] and a successor of Liāngshān Guàn.
Chan Master Jingxuan of Dayang Mountain in Yingzhou was a native of the Zhang family of Jiangxia. At nineteen, he became a fully ordained monk (*bhikṣu*).

Having studied the definitive meaning of the *Awakening of Faith in Mahāyāna* (the *Yuanjue jing*), there was no one who could surpass him in his lecture halls. He subsequently traveled to various regions.

Upon first arriving at Liangshan, he asked, "What is the formless site of enlightenment? Liangshan pointed to Guanyin and said, "This is a painting by the scholar Wu. As the Master was about to respond—
He advanced to speak. Liangshan urgently asked, "Which of these has form, and which is formless? The Master then attained realization and prostrated himself.
Liangshan said, "Why do you not utter a single phrase? The Master replied, "I would not decline to speak it, but I fear it would take up too much paper and ink.
Liangshan laughed and said, "This saying shall be carved upon a monument. The Master then offered this verse: "I..."

In the past, beginners studying the Way were deluded; they sought knowledge across ten thousand waters and a thousand mountains. Though they could distinguish the present from the ancient, they ultimately failed to realize it;

when told directly that there is no-mind, their doubts increased further. Having received the Master’s pointing out of the mirror of the Qin dynasty, they see clearly the time before their parents were born.
Now, having attained awakening, what is there to be gained? At night, the black rooster is released and flies with the snow. Lingquan said: "This is the Dongshan [tradition]."
His lineage was worthy of reliance, and at that time his reputation was widespread. After Liangshan passed away, he left the memorial pagoda and went to Dayang, where he visited Chan Master Jian.
Jian yielded his seat to him, appointing him as its master.
Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi (Tenth Generation under Qingyuan; Dharma Heir of Dayang Huiyan).
Chan Master Yiqing of Touzi in Shu Prefecture was the son of the Li family of Qingzhou. He received full ordination after passing the scriptural examinations and studied the *Śata-dharmaka-śāstra*.
The Treatise states: Not long after, he sighed and said, "The path of three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* is so remote; what benefit is there in exhausting myself?

He then entered Luoyang to study the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*, his understanding as clear as a string of pearls. Once, while reading the verses of the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, he reached the passage on "the self-nature of the mind" and had a sudden realization, saying, "The Dharma transcends words;
how can it be expounded? He immediately abandoned his studies at the monastic seat to travel elsewhere. At that time, Chan Master Yuanjian was residing at Huisheng Rock.

One night, he dreamed that he was holding a blue hawk; this was an auspicious omen. When dawn arrived, Master Yuanying came, and Yuanjian received him with formal prostrations and invited him to stay.
He instructed him to contemplate the kōan concerning the outsider’s question to the Buddha: "Did you ask for words or not ask for words?
After three years had passed, one day Yuanjian asked, "Do you remember the point of the phrase? Try to bring it up. As the master was about to respond, Yuanjian covered his mouth. The master—

He attained clear and thorough enlightenment and then prostrated himself. Yuanying said, "Have you wondrously awakened to the profound mechanism? The Master replied, "Even if there were such a thing, it must be spat out.
At that time, Attendant Ziqi was standing by and said, "Qing Huayan, today you have been like a sick man who has broken a sweat."
The Master looked back and said, "Shut your dog’s mouth! If you chatter further, I shall vomit. From then on, another three years passed.
Yuanjian occasionally went out from the cave to show him the fundamental principles of the school; [Yuanjian] was entirely in perfect accord with them.

[The Master] bestowed upon him a pair of leather sandals with a top-knot design from Dayang and instructed him, saying, "Continue my lineage and its spiritual style. Do not linger here for long; you must act skillfully."
Huchih then wrote a verse and sent it, saying: Mount Sumeru stands in the vast void, The sun and moon revolve as its attendants.
The myriad peaks gradually lean upon one another, While the white clouds undergo their transformations. The wind of Shaolin rises from the thickets; The bamboo blinds of Caoxi are rolled up.

A golden phoenix dwells in the dragon’s nest— How could the imperial moss be crushed by a carriage wheel? He was ordered to rely on Chan Master Yuantong Xiu. When the Master arrived there, he had no one to consult.
Question: "He does nothing but indulge in sleep. The attendant reported this to Master Tong, saying, "There is a monk in the hall who sleeps every day;

we must enforce the monastic regulations. Tong asked, "Who is it? The attendant replied, "The Elder Qing. Tong said, "Not yet. Wait until I have investigated the matter. Tong then took up his staff and entered the hall.
Seeing the Master fast asleep, he struck the meditation bench and rebuked him, saying, "In my place, there is no 'free rice' given to you!"
While sitting, he ate and then struck [the master] to put him to sleep. The Master asked, "What does the Master instruct me to do? Tōng said, "Why not go practice Zen?
The Master said, "Fine food is not for a person already full to eat. Tōng said, "But what can be done? There are many who will not accept the Seat-holder's [your] teaching."
The Master said, "Wait until he is willing; what can be done then? Tong asked, "Whom has the Senior Monk seen come? The Master replied, "Fushan.
Tong said, "No wonder he is so stubborn and unruly. Thereupon, they took each other's hands and laughed as they returned to the abbot’s quarters.
From this, his reputation for the Way became exceedingly great.
Chan Master Qingpou of Xingyang (Dharma Heir of Dayang Huiyan).
While Chan Master Qingpou of Xingyang in Yingzhou was serving as the garden head under Dayang, he was planting melons when Dayang asked him:
"When will the melons ripen? The Master said, "They have already ripened and rotted away. [The monk] said, "Pick out the sweet ones and bring them here.
The Master said, "For whom would you eat them? [The monk] said, "For those who do not enter the garden. The Master said, "I wonder, who is it that does not enter the garden?"
"Will you eat it? [The Master] said, "Do you recognize him? The Master said, "Although I do not recognize him, I cannot but give it to him.
Dayang smiled and departed. Minister Zheng Jin asked, "At what time did the Master open the hall for teaching?
The Master said, "Without passing through the kalpas of the *asaṃkhyeya*, before the birth of sun and moon. While the Master was lying ill, Dayang asked, "This body is like..."
"Bubbles and illusions. It is within bubbles and illusions that things are accomplished. If there were no bubbles and illusions, there would be no way to accomplish the Great Matter.
If you wish to accomplish the Great Matter, recognize these bubbles and illusions. "How so? The Master said, "That is still a matter of this side. Dayang said:
"What is the matter with that side? The Master said, "The crimson wheel shines across the earth; no flowers grow beneath the sea. Dayang said, "Are you so very alert?
The Master gave a shout, saying, "I thought I had forgotten! He then finally passed away into stillness.
Chan Master Shencheng of Fuyan (Dharma Heir of Dayang Huiyan).
While Chan Master Shencheng of Fuyan on Mount Nanyue was standing in attendance upon Dayang, Dayang said:
"There is a person whose entire body is raw and festering, lying amidst a thicket of thorns, surrounded on all sides by fire. If one can draw near to this person..."
The marketplace was opened wide. When [Yangshan] could not approach him, he asked, "At such a time, what do you take as your basis?
The Master said, "My six sense organs are incomplete and my seven consciousnesses are not whole. Dayang said, "Tell him to come out; I wish to see him.
The Master said, "Just now there was no one else by my side to respond to the Master. Dayang said, "The official does not permit even a needle. The Master then bowed. (Later, the Master...)

He went to Master Huarong of Huayan and recounted the previous conversation. Huarong said, "Cold as a grain of frost; fine as ice and snow. Prime Minister Li went specifically up the mountain and asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
The Master pointed to the cypress tree in front of the courtyard. The Prime Minister asked this three times, and the Master answered in this way three times.
The Prime Minister was delighted and composed a verse, saying: "Appearing and disappearing amidst idle clouds, filling the great void; It turns out that the true form is right here."
Not a single speck of dust exists. Again and again he inquired about the meaning of the Westward Transmission, yet [the Master] only pointed to a single cypress tree before the courtyard.
Chan Master Xianru of Mount Luofu (a dharma heir of Dayang Huiyan).
Chan Master Xianru of Mount Luofu in Huizhou: when he first arrived at Dayang, Dayang asked him, "Where are you from?"
A man said, "It is Yizhou. Dayang asked, "How many *li* is it from here? He replied, "Five thousand *li*.
Dayang said, "When you came this way, have you ever trodden upon it? He replied, "I have never trodden upon it. Dayang said, "Can you fly through the air?"
He said, "I do not understand how one leaps into the void. Dayang said, "How could you possibly reach this point? He replied, "At every step I am not confused about my direction;
throughout my entire being there is no place of distinction. Dayang said, "Have you attained the samādhi that transcends all quarters? He replied, "The holy mind cannot be grasped."
"How could samādhi ever manifest as a name? Dayang said, "So it is, so it is. You should believe this: the original substance is fully manifested;
principle and phenomena are non-dual. Guard and maintain this well within yourself."
Chan Master Guixi of Baima (Dharma Heir of Dayang Hui).
Chan Master Guixi of Baima in Xiangzhou initially asked Dayang, "This student is ignorant and deluded; I beg you to point out a path of entry. Dayang said, "Attained.
After a long silence, he called to the Master. The Master responded, "Yes? Dayang said, "I give you this path of entry."
At these words, the Master attained realization.
This was Chan Master Fuyong Daokai (d.u.),
the eleventh-generation descendant of Qingyuan (a dharma heir of Touzi Qian).
Chan Master Daokai Fuyong of Tientai in Tokyo was the son of the Cui family from Yizhou. From childhood, he studied the practice of abstaining from grain.

He lived in seclusion on Mount Iyang before traveling to the capital, where he registered his name at Shuitai Temple. Having passed the examination on the *Lotus Sūtra*, he received full ordination. He then visited Touzi at Haihui Monastery and asked:
"The words and phrases of the Buddhas and Patriarchs are like the common tea and rice of daily life; apart from these, what else is there?"

"Is there a place for a person to dwell? he asked. Touzi said, "You speak of the Emperor’s decree within the realm; does it still require Yao, Shun, Yu, or Tang? The Master wished to offer further words, but Touzi struck his mouth with a whisk and said, "From the moment you first conceived this thought, you already deserved thirty blows. The Master was immediately enlightened; he bowed twice and departed. Touzi called out, "Come here for a moment! The Master turned back. Touzi said, "I knew you would come. The Master then bowed again. Touzi said, "Go and see Xuefeng. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. Upon hearing this, the Master attained great enlightenment. He returned to Touzi and related what had happened. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill people; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can give life; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can both kill and give life; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, and grant freedom; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, and bestow the Dharma; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, and even perform miracles; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, perform miracles, and even turn the world upside down; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, perform miracles, turn the world upside down, and even cause the heavens to shake; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, perform miracles, turn the world upside down, cause the heavens to shake, and even make the earth tremble; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, perform miracles, turn the world upside down, cause the heavens to shake, make the earth tremble, and even cause the sun and moon to fall; go and study under him. The Master went to Xuefeng and asked, "What is the meaning of Bodhidharma coming from the West? Xuefeng said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master said, "I have already seen it. Xuefeng said, "If you have already seen it, why do you ask? The Master was greatly enlightened. He returned to Touzi and told him. Touzi said, "Xuefeng has a staff that can kill, give life, grant freedom, bestow the Dharma, perform miracles, turn the world upside down, cause the heavens to shake, make the earth tremble, cause the sun and moon to fall, and even cause the four oceans to dry up; go and study under him. During the serving of tea, the Master held up his bag and asked, "Does the Great King understand? The King replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The Human King and the Dharma King each illuminate one another.
He remained for ten days, after which he declined on account of illness. On the second day of the twelfth month, he bathed, ascended the hall, addressed the assembly, and passed away.
The Monk Baozhang of Thousand Years’ Age.

The Monk Baozhang of Thousand Years’ Age was a native of Central India. In the twelfth year of the Weili reign era of Emperor Wei (the *dingmao* year), he descended as a spirit and received his physical form;
he held his left hand in a fist at birth, which only opened when he was seven years old upon his tonsure, hence his name Baozhang. During the Wei and Jin periods...
He traveled east to this land, entered Shu to pay homage to Samantabhadra, and remained at Daci Monastery where he never ate.
Each day he recited more than a thousand scrolls of the *Prajñāpāramitā* and other sutras. One who praised him said: "His weary jade teeth are cold, like a rushing mountain spring;
sometimes sitting in the dead of night, the gods and ghosts weep before his steps. One day he said to the assembly: "I have a vow: to remain in this world for a thousand..."
This year marks his six hundred and twenty-sixth year; thus he is called the "Thousand-Year One.

He subsequently traveled to Mount Wutai, then moved his residence to Huayan on Mount Zhurong, Shuangfeng in Huangmei, and Donglin on Mount Lu. Eventually arriving in Jianye, he encountered Bodhidharma’s arrival in the Liang dynasty.
The Master approached him to inquire about the essential meaning of the Dharma and attained awakening. Emperor Wu, holding the Master’s years of practice and realization in high esteem, invited him—
He entered the inner court. Not long after, he traveled to Wu, where he composed a verse: "In the city of Liang I met the Teacher; through Zen practice I realized the mind-ground.

Drifting and wandering, I have traveled through the two Zhe regions, exhausting all their finest mountains and waters. Following the current downstream, he passed through Qianqing and arrived at Tiantong (Tianzhu).
He traveled to Mount Mao, ascended Mount Taibai, and passed through Yandang. He stayed for an extended period at the seventy-two hermitages of Mount Cuifeng.
Returning to Mount Chicheng, he rested at Yunmen, Fahua, Zhujia, Yupu, Chifu, Dayan, and other locations. Upon returning to Feilai Peak, he took up residence in Shidou Cave.
There is a verse by him that reads: "Having traveled the four hundred prefectures of China, I find that everywhere here is called a place where men of the Way roam."
This was the fifteenth year of the Zhenguan era. Later, he resided at Baoyan Monastery in Pujiang, where he maintained a close friendship with Chan Master Lang.
Whenever he sent a messenger to inquire after him, a white dog would gallop there; Lang likewise employed a green monkey as his messenger.

Thus, he inscribed upon Lang’s wall: "The white dog brings the letter; the green monkey returns with the bowl washed. On the first day of the New Year in the second year of the Xianqing era, he fashioned a [statue] by hand.
The image was completed on the ninth day. He asked his disciple Huiyun, "To whom does this resemble? Yun replied, "It is no different from you, Master.
Thereupon, he bathed, changed his robes, and sat in the lotus position. Addressing Yun, he said, "I have remained in this world for one thousand seven hundred and twenty-two years;
now I shall depart from the world. Listen to my verse: "Originally there is neither birth nor death; Now I likewise manifest birth and death."
"I shall go to dwell in the mind; after my next birth, I will return here. He then made this entrustment:
"Sixty years after my passing, there will be a monk who comes to take my bones; do not refuse him. Having finished speaking, he passed away.

Fifty-four years after his parinirvāṇa, the Elder Sthavira Simha came from Yunmen to the site of the stupa. He prostrated and said, "I hope the stupa will open wide. After a short while, the door of the stupa indeed opened.
Qī: Its bones were linked together like refined gold. Floating [upon the water], it was taken to Mount Qinwàng, where a stūpa was constructed to enshrine them.

Calculating from the Dīngmǎo year of the reign of King Wīlè of the Zhōu dynasty to the Dīngyí year of the Xuǎnqìng era of Emperor Gāozōng of the Táng dynasty, there are exactly one thousand seven hundred and twenty-two years.
Since arriving in this land, more than four hundred years have passed.
Master Fashun, Master Fashun, was surnamed Du.

It was traditionally said that he was an incarnation of Mañjuśrī. He descended as a spirit in Wannian County of Yongzhou, where his divine traces were so brilliant and manifest that they could not be fully recorded.
He once composed a verse on the Dharma-body (*dharmakāya*), which says: "The ox of Huai Prefecture eats..."

the preciousness of the Cintāmaṇi is not the ultimate preciousness. Looking from the left and right, the wind cannot enter; looking from the front and back, the rain cannot wet it. Therefore, the Lotus Sūtra says: 'Profound, firm, deep, and far-reaching; no one can reach it.'")
The details regarding the Dharma heirs of Master Shixing are unknown. Once,
