The Chan Master Yushan of Taling.
This Chan Master Yushan of Taling had never traveled on pilgrimage. Once, when a transformation-monk from Mount Lu arrived, they discussed matters concerning the Gate of the Patriarchs (Zongmen).
[The monk] instructed him to contemplate the question: "When a monk asked Fandeng, 'How does one advance further atop a hundred-foot pole? Fandeng said:"
"Ugh! For three years [he practiced]. One day, while crossing a bridge on a donkey, he stepped upon a plank and fell.
Suddenly, he attained great enlightenment. He then composed a verse, saying: 'I possess a divine pearl; for long it has been locked away by the dust of worldly toil.

Today the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, piercing through the myriad peaks of mountains and rivers. Because of this, he no longer traveled to seek teachers elsewhere. This was the Master Baizhang’s verse, which Baiyun Yuan subsequently harmonized with.

Yet he was still able to cross over his teacher. Zuan wrote in praise: "Having already advanced from atop a hundred-foot pole, one step upon the mountain stream bridge causes mountains and rivers to vanish.
From this point on, he never leaves the banks of Tea Creek; every song and chant is nothing but 'Ra-li-ra'."
Dharma Master Sengzhao encountered the persecution of the Qin King. As he was about to undergo execution, he spoke this verse: "The four elements originally have no master;

Chan Master Xian Jingzhao asked Grand Master Lengyan:

Fenyang Shanzhao (in his commentary) said: "Both are already old.
Master Gongqi, Master Gongqi, once went to Luohan Monastery. On the way, he encountered a young gentleman riding an ox. The Master asked him, "Which is the road to Luohan?"
"Where are you going? The official patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master shouted, "This beast!
The official said, "As for the path of the Arhats, where does it go? The Master then patted the ox and said, "Speak! Speak! The official said, "Even if it were so..."
There were still some hooves and horns remaining. The Master struck him, whereupon the official slapped the ox and ran away.
Regarding Chan Master Tang Chaoyin of the Tang Dynasty:
during his humble days, while once wielding a mallet to strike at the earth, he saw a large clod of dirt and playfully struck it violently with the mallet.

If one strikes it, it should shatter into pieces. Huo attained great enlightenment [later there was an elder who heard it said: "The entirety of the mountains, rivers, and the great earth has been reduced to a hundredfold fragments by Master Yin"].
Chan Master Fahai Li of Chuzhou.
Because the imperial court issued an edict to convert his monastery into a Shenxiao Palace, the Master ascended the seat and addressed the assembly, saying:
"It is precisely because one has not yet attained thorough penetration that one speaks of right and wrong; it is simply due to a lack of true realization."
Thus, this is divided from that; even my own body does not exist, so what need is there to speak of anything outside the body? Viewed through the correct eye, it is all a source of laughter.
Now, however, the Sage Ruler has issued an edict to convert a monastery into a Shenxiao temple.
To add a crown to the Buddha’s head—when one calculates it, what could be wrong with that? Today, this mountain monk cannot help but shoulder his staff across his shoulder.
Hanging his alms-bag high, he establishes his dwelling within the seamless stupa; beneath the rootless tree, he whistles to the moon and chants to the wind.

In years to come, when he attains the Way and ascends on a white cloud during the day, he will be able to repay the unrequitable debt of gratitude and assist in the Unconditioned (wuwei).

Regarding the Dharma Master Shenzhao Benru:
he once requested instruction on the *Sūtra King* from the Venerable Siming. The Venerable one raised his voice in a thunderous roar.
He said, "Your name is Benru. At these words, the Master immediately attained realization and composed a verse, saying: "Everywhere I encounter the path home; At every turn, I reach my native land.
The reality is already manifest from the beginning; Why wait for deliberation?"
The Dharma Master Zhengwu of Shangzhu in Lin’an Prefecture:
The Dharma Master Yuanzhi Zhengwu of Shangzhu in Lin’an Prefecture was the son of the Lin family of Taizhou.

He relied upon the Dharma Master Xian of Bailian to inquire about the Way of the Total Transformation. Xian pointed to a walking lamp and said, "A lamp such as this is devoid of intrinsic nature and transcends all negation."

Fundamentally empty and quiescent, the principle is complete therein. Yet, as for the six classes of ordinary beings and the four types of noble ones, their perceptions differ; thus, transformation is present within it.

When the Master did not yet accord with this realization, he later encountered a passage while sweeping the floor and reciting the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*: "Knowing that all phenomena are eternally without self-nature, the seeds of Buddhahood arise from conditions.

The Nun Xuánjī of Jìngjū.
During the Jǐngyún era of the Táng dynasty, she received the full precepts. She frequently practiced meditative concentration within a stone grotto on Mount Dàrì.

One day, she suddenly thought to herself: "The nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is profoundly still; fundamentally, there is neither going nor staying. To loathe clamor and hasten toward stillness [is a delusion]."
Was he truly enlightened? He then went to visit Xuefeng. Xuefeng asked, "Where have you come from?

The Elder Master Wuming (Twenty-six Cases):
Once there was an elder master who, throughout an entire summer retreat, did not speak a single word to his assembly of monks. A monk sighed and said, "I have spent this entire summer in vain.
I did not dare hope that the Master would preach the Buddha-dharma, yet I could at least have heard two words of the True Cause."
He attained [realization]. Upon hearing this, an elder remarked, "Dharma brother, do not speak so hastily. If we speak of the true cause, there is not even a single character.
Having finished speaking, he struck his teeth together and said, "Just now, I was groundless; it was improper to speak in such a manner.

An elder in the neighboring wall heard this and said, "What a fine pot of soup, ruined by a single mouse dropping! (Baoci then raised the point for inquiry, saying: "Tell me, was this a word of praise, or a word of disapproval? If it was praise... )

[The monk] sighed. "It has been defiled by rat droppings; how can it be called a superior path? If he were unwilling, what fault would there be? Can this be verified? Xuedou Xian said: "In whose household are there not one or two grains [of rice] in the cauldron? Huanglong Qing said:

"Those two elders saw only the sharpness of the awl's point, but did not see the squareness of the chisel's head. As for this monk saying, 'I do not dare hope for the Master to speak of the Buddha-dharma; I would be content to hear even the two characters of the True Cause (zhengyin)'—is this understanding or not? Those who study the profound essentials must possess the eye that penetrates all directions; you must discern the ancient and the modern within words."
Once there was a monk who stayed within the sutra hall but did not read the scriptures; every day he sat in meditation. The Librarian asked, "Why do you not read the scriptures?
The monk replied, "I am illiterate. The Librarian said, "Why do you not ask others?
The monk stepped forward, joined his palms, bowed, and asked, "What character is this? The Librarian was speechless. (The Dàtōng edition reads: "Or again, he said, 'I do not know it. )

Once there was an elderly master who lived in a hermitage. He wrote the character for "mind" (心) above his door, he wrote the character for "mind" on his window, and he wrote the character for "mind" on his wall.

Fayan Yi said: "Above the door, one should simply write the character for 'door' (門); on the window, one should simply write the character for 'window' (牕); on the wall, one should simply write the character for 'wall' (壁). Baoci Shui said: "One need not write the character for 'door' above the door;
one need not write the character for 'window' on the window; one need not write the character for 'wall' on the wall. Why? Because the meaning of these characters is already manifest."

In the past, there were two hermitage masters living in separate huts. They did not see one another for ten days, and when they suddenly met, the master of the upper hut asked the master of the lower hut, "I have not seen you for a long time; where have you been?
The master of the lower hut replied, "I have been in my hut building a seamless stupa. The master of the upper hut said, "I also wish to build one. May I borrow your stupa from you?"
[The Master] made a gesture. The abbot below said, "Why did you not say so sooner? It has just been borrowed by someone else. (Fayan Yi said:
"Now tell me, was it his model that was borrowed, or was it not his model?")
Once there was a hermitage master who, seeing a monk approach, held up his fire-tube and asked, "Do you understand? The monk said, "I do not.
The master said, "This is something that has been used for thirty years without being exhausted. The monk then asked, "What did you use before those thirty years?
The master had no reply. (Gui-zong Rou offered this in his stead: "One must also know.")
Once there was an elder who, when questioned by the Prince of Jiangnan, said: "I have a water buffalo that has traveled ten thousand *li* without a single blade of grass.
I do not know where to let it graze. The elder had no reply. (Gui-zong Rou spoke on his behalf, saying: "Let it graze in a good place.")
Once there was an elder who asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "I have come from Niu-tou Mountain to pay homage to the Patriarch.
The elder asked, "Did you see the Patriarch? The monk had no reply. (Gui-zong Rou offered this on his behalf: "It seems as though he does not believe you.")
Once there was an old master who spoke in verse: "A single void atop the mountain of the five aggregates; Though entering and exiting through the same gate, we do not meet.
For immeasurable kalpas we have lived in rented quarters; In the end, we do not know the true host. [Another old master said: "Since you do not know him,"]
[This refers to] who it was that he originally asked for the lease.
A monk asked an old master, "What is it like to be one within the secret chamber? The old master said, "When there is a guest, I do not answer.
Xuansha Zhiyuan commented, "How could it ever have been secret? Nianzong Ruo addressed the old master differently, saying, "Why did you allow him to see [the truth]?"
Once there was an elder monk. A monk asked him: "The soul returns from afar; eat the mulberries of my home garden.
What are the mulberries of the home garden? (Baoci [Fayan Wenyi] then spoke on his behalf: "Even these cannot be eaten. Faldeng Qin said: "They would defile your mouth.")
Long ago, there was an elder who said: "The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years in order to seek one who understands him.
If you understand it in this way, the day will come when you will eat iron rods. Another elder said: "The Patriarch sat facing the wall for nine years; how could he not feel ashamed?
If you understand it in this way, you must buy straw sandals and travel for another thirty years. (Langye Huijue said: "Since it is not so, then... )

"Way. What was the meaning behind the Patriarch’s wall-facing? After a long silence, he said: "If you wish not to incur the karma of the Avīci Hell, do not slander the Tathāgata’s True Wheel of Dharma. Tiantong Jie, having finished citing Langye’s words, said:

"The two elders were merely knocking on bricks and beating tiles; Master Langye painted a tiger and ended up with a cat. Do you all wish to see the intent behind the Patriarch’s wall-facing? It is like a bottomless pit that is difficult to fill."
Once there was an elder master. When a monk asked him, "A lion uses its full strength when seizing a rabbit, and it uses its full strength when seizing an elephant.
I wonder, what kind of strength is it that it fully employs? The elder replied, "The strength of non-deception" (Fayan Wenyi commented elsewhere: "I do not understand the words of the ancients").
Once there was an elder who said: "This plot of land has been entrusted to you for a long time now.

I stand here waiting for you to grasp it. (Fayan Yi said: "I, this mountain monk, am sitting here now, waiting for you to grasp it. Is there any principle in this? Which is close and which is distant? Try to judge for me.")

In the past, there was an elderly master who kept a young attendant, yet neither of them knew the proper rules of conduct. One day, a traveling monk arrived and instructed the boy in the rituals of etiquette.
That evening, seeing the elderly master returning from outside, the boy went forward to offer his greetings. The master was astonished and suspicious.
He then asked the boy, "Who taught you? The boy replied, "A certain senior monk (shangzuo) in the hall. The old master summoned that monk and questioned him:
"Senior monk, you have been traveling among other houses; what kind of mental conduct is this?
This boy has been raised here for two or three years and is naturally quite lovely. Who taught you to corrupt him? Pack your things quickly and leave at once!"

At twilight, drenched by the rain, he was driven out. (Fayan Yi said: "The ancients were so forthright in their manifestation; how strange is this little bit of family style! But tell me, what was the intent? )
Long ago, there was a monk who arrived at Caoxi. At that time, the monk in charge of the robes and bowl held up the robe and said, "This is what could not be lifted at the head of Dayu Ridge.
The [visiting] monk asked, "Why is it in your hands, Venerable? The monk had no reply. (Yunmen Wenyan said: "..."
They did not understand one another. It is also said: "I thought you were a lion cub.

Long ago, there was an elder who asked a presiding master (zuozhu): "Regarding the commentaries and sub-commentaries (*shu* and *chao*), how do their explanations of the meaning differ in breadth or brevity?
The presiding master replied: "The *chao* explains the *shu*, and the *shu* explains the sutra. The elder asked: "What does the sutra explain? The presiding master was speechless.
Formerly, people from the kingdom of Goryeo came to Qiantang to carve a sacred image of Avalokiteśvara. When they attempted to carry it onto their ship, it would not budge.

Consequently, they invited it to Kaiyuan Temple in Mingzhou to be enshrined there for offerings. Later, someone posed this question: "The scripture says that there is no land where he does not manifest his body;

why then did the sacred image not go to Goryeo? (Changqing Ling said: "Though the manifestation of the body is universal, the perception of its form is partial. (Fayan Yi also said: "Have you recognized Avalokiteśvara yet?")
Before the pagoda at Sizhou, a monk was prostrating. Someone asked him, "Venerable sir, you prostrate every day; do you actually see the Great Sage?
(Fayan Yi spoke on his behalf, saying: "Tell me, what is the meaning of your prostration?")
The attendant of the Si-zhou Pagoda locked the door at the appointed time. Someone asked, "Since you are the Great Master of the Three Realms, why are you being locked up by your disciple?
The attendant had no reply. (Fayan Yi spoke on his behalf, saying: "The disciple locks; the Great Master locks. Fandeng Qin spoke on his behalf, saying: "Give me back my key!
An old master also spoke on his behalf, saying: "Jizhou locks; Qianzhou locks.")
There was an image of a holy monk that was being dripped upon by leaks from the roof. Someone asked the monk, "Since you are a holy monk, why do you have leaks?
The monk had no reply. (National Teacher Shao spoke on his behalf, saying: "Being leakless is not being a holy monk.")
Someone asked a monk, "What kind of lamp do you light? The monk replied, "A perpetually burning lamp. [The man] asked, "When was it lit? [The monk] said, "It was lit last year.

[The man] asked, "Where is the perpetual burning? The monk was speechless. (Changqing Ling, speaking on his behalf, said: "Had he not done so, you would have known that you were being deceived by him.
Fayan Yi offered a different response: "This moves the gentleman.")
There was a presiding master (zuozhu) who was reciting the name of Amitābha. A junior monk called out, "Preceptor!
When the preceptor looked back, the junior monk did not respond. This happened three or four times. The preceptor scolded him, saying, "I have called you three or four times;

what is the matter? The junior monk replied, "How long has it been since you last called him? As soon as I call him, he immediately gives rise to karmic obstruction" (Fadeng Qin remarked: "A curse!").
There was a monk who, having finished reciting the sutras with a young boy, told him to place the sutra inside a case.
The boy said, "That which I have recited—where shall it be placed? (Fadeng Qin spoke on his behalf, saying: "What sutra did you recite?")
There was a monk who entered the underworld and saw Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva. Kṣitigarbha asked him, "What practice have you cultivated throughout your life?

The monk replied, "I recite the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*. [Kṣitigarbha] said, "'Cease, cease! There is no need to speak; my Dharma is subtle and difficult to conceive. Is this speaking or not speaking? The monk had no reply.
(Gui-zong Rou offered this verse on his behalf: "Returning from here, I dare to circulate it.")
Under the assembly of the Abbot of Yan’guan, there was a monk serving as an administrator who suddenly saw a ghost messenger come to pursue him.

The monk said to the messenger, "I am currently serving as an administrator and have not yet had the leisure to practice; may I request seven days' grace? The messenger replied, "I shall wait to report this to the King.
If he grants permission, you may return in seven days; otherwise, I will arrive in an instant. Having spoken, the messenger vanished. When the seventh day arrived—
Later, he returned again to search for that monk, but was unable to find him at all. Afterwards, someone raised this question to another monk:
"If you are discovered by him, how would you deal with him? (Dongshan Jia spoke on his behalf: "He has already found me.")
A monk from Liutong Monastery in Taizhou wished to cross the river by boat. Someone asked him, "Since you possess the six supernatural powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), why do you rely on a boat?
The monk was unable to answer. (National Teacher Shao of Tiantai spoke on his behalf, saying: "I did not wish to startle the assembly.")
The Anonymous High Official (Seven Cases):
One day, the monk of Dajian Temple requested that the Second Seat be invited to open the hall for the Prefect of Hongzhou, Lord Song.
The Lord asked, "Why not invite the First Seat? The assembly was speechless. (Fayan Wenyi spoke on their behalf: "There is no need to do so.")
The Chancellor of Jiangnan, Feng Yanshi, was traveling with several monks to Mount Zhong. Upon reaching the "One-Man Spring," he asked, "The spring is for one person;
how can so many people share it? A monk replied, "We do not allow it to be deficient. Feng Yanshi did not accept this answer, so he offered another:
"Who is it that is deficient? (Fayan Yi offered a different version, saying: "Who is it that is insufficient?")
The official asked, "What is your name, monk? He replied, "No selection. The official said, "If someone were suddenly to offer you a bowl of sand, what then?
He replied, "I thank the official for his offering" (Fayan Wenyi commented elsewhere: "This is still a matter of selection").

There was a monk living in a hermitage in Guangnan. When the ruler of the country went out hunting, his attendants informed the master of the hermitage, "The Great King is coming; please rise to welcome him.
The master said, "Not only would I not rise for the Great King, I would not rise even if the Buddha himself were to come.

The king asked, "Is the Buddha not your teacher? The master replied, "He is. The king said, "If so, why do you not rise when seeing your teacher? (Fayan Yi spoke on his behalf, saying: "This is still insufficient to repay his kindness.")
On Hongtang Bridge in Fuzhou, there were monks seated in a row. An official asked, "Is there a Buddha here?
The monks had no reply. (Fayan Yi spoke on their behalf, saying: "Who are you?")
Long ago, there was an official who entered the Tianwang Temple in Zhenzhou and beheld the divine image.

He asked the temple master, "What meritorious work is this? The master replied, "It is the Guardian King of the State. The official asked, "Does he protect only this country, or does he protect all other countries as well?

The master replied, "When he is in Qin, he protects Qin; when he is in Chu, he protects Chu. The official said, "On the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month, break down the city walls of Zhenzhou! At that, the heavens—
"Where has the King gone? The head monk had no reply.

Formerly, there was an official who composed a "Treatise on the Non-existence of Ghosts. One night, while he was wielding his brush in the middle of the night, he suddenly saw a ghost appear and say, "You claim there are no ghosts;
what about me? (Wuzu Yan said: "If I, this old monk, had seen him at that time, I would have simply made a 'magpie beak' with my hand and said to him, 'Gu-gua! [a sound of crying]).
Five Cases of the Nameless Practitioner:
Once there was a practitioner of the Way who sat with his back turned toward the Buddha in front of the Buddha Hall. A monk said, "Practitioner of the Way, do not sit with your back to the Buddha.
The practitioner replied, "In the fundamental teaching of the Great Virtuous One, it is said that 'the Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm. So, where would one be sitting?"
[The Master] said, "I have attained it. [The monk] made no reply. (Fayan Yi’s commentary says: "I recognize you.
There was a practitioner who entered the Buddha hall with the Dharma Master. The practitioner spat toward the Buddha.
The Master said, "This practitioner lacks propriety; why do you spit at the Buddha? The practitioner replied, "I came from a place where there is no Buddha, so I am spitting at you, Sir. The Master—

"Non-opposition. (Miaoshan Yu said: "The benevolent person becomes non-benevolent; the non-benevolent person becomes benevolent. Yangshan Ji, acting for the Dharma Master, said: "Just spit at the practitioner. He also said:
"If the practitioner has something to say, tell him: 'Bring me back the place where there is no practitioner.'")
A dead fish was floating on the surface of the water. Someone asked a monk, "Is it not the case that fish take water as their life? The monk replied, "Yes.
[The man] asked, "Why then have you died in the water? The monk had no reply. (Master Ji of Tiantong in Hangzhou spoke on his behalf, saying:
"That is so; why did he not go to die on the bank?")
A hawk pursues a pigeon, which flies onto the railing of the Buddha Hall and trembles.
Someone asks a monk, "All sentient beings dwell in constant peace and joy within the shadow of the Buddha. Why does the pigeon tremble upon seeing the Buddha?
The monk has no reply. (Fadeng Qin spoke on his behalf: "He is afraid of the Buddha.")
Once there was a monk traveling toward Fushan who encountered an old man selling salt along the way. The monk asked, "In which direction does the road to Fushan lead?
The old man remained silent for a long while. When the monk asked again, the old man said, "Are you deaf?
The monk replied, "What did you say to me? The old man said, "I told you the road to Fushan. The monk asked, "Do you understand Zen? The old man said, [silently].
"Do not say you understand Chan; even the Buddha-dharma will eventually be exhausted. The monk said, "Try to explain it to me. The old man lifted up his salt basket. The monk said, "Difficult.
The old man asked, "What do you call this? The monk said, "Salt. The old man said, "What connection does that have [to the Dharma]?
The monk asked, "What do you call it? The old man replied, "I cannot tell you again that it is salt."
The Nun Wuming (Five Cases):
Long ago, there was a nun who supported a hermit for twenty years, constantly employing a young girl aged eighteen to serve him.
He sent a woman to serve him meals. One day, he had the woman hold him firmly and asked, "At this very moment, what is it?

The abbot replied, "A withered tree leans against a cold cliff; for three winters there is no warmth. When the woman reported this to the old lady (the patroness), she said, "For twenty years, I have been supporting nothing but a worldly fellow.
She then dismissed him and ordered his hermitage to be burned down. (Jingshan Xing remarked: "Looking at this from a cool distance, this old lady... )
This son is no slouch! Why wait until he has been sent away and the monks have been barred before setting fire to it? Tell me, where does Shuangji’s meaning lie? Those with eyes, discern and see!
Long ago, there was a monk who went to visit Mihu. On the road, he encountered an old woman living in a hermitage. The monk asked, "Old woman, do you have any kinsmen?
She replied, "I do. The monk asked, "Where are they? She said, "The mountains, rivers, and the great earth; whether grass or trees—all these are my kinsmen.
The monk said, "Are you not perhaps a nun? She asked, "How do you see me? The monk said—
The laywoman said, "You cannot be a monk. The monk said, "Old woman, do not confuse and defile the Buddha-dharma.
The laywoman said, "I am not confusing or defiling the Buddha-dharma. The monk said, "If you act like this, is that not confusing and defiling the Buddha-dharma? The laywoman said:
"You are a man; I am a woman. How could we ever be confused?

Laywoman Pang entered Lukmen Temple to offer a vegetarian feast. When the *vina* (chant leader) requested her intention for the dedication of merit, the laywoman took up a comb, stuck it behind her hair-knot, and said, "The dedication has been made. She then departed.

The laywoman Chen Dao from Wenzhou once traveled extensively to seek instruction from renowned masters throughout the various regions. Later, she attained enlightenment under the guidance of Master Jing at Changlao Mountain.
She composed a verse which says: Upon the level summit of the high hill, There are but woodcutters everywhere.
Everyone harbors the intent of an axe or a knife, Yet they do not see the mountain flowers reflecting red upon the water.
In the past, there was a female lay patron who entered the monastery to distribute money to the assembly of monks according to their seniority. A monk said, "Place one portion before the Holy Monks.
The woman asked, "How old are the Holy Monks? The monk had no reply. (Fayan Yi, speaking on his behalf, said: "When the mind is clear, one knows at once.")
During the Song Dynasty,
Emperor Taizong of Song once visited Xiangguo Temple. Seeing a monk reading a sutra, he asked, "What is this?"
The Emperor asked, “Which sutra? The monk replied, “The *Renwang Jing* (Benevolent Kings Sutra). The Emperor said, “Since this is my own sutra, why is it in your hands?
The monk was speechless. (Xuedou Xian’s substitute reply: “Heaven has no partiality; it aids only virtue. [Another instance: While opening the precious pagoda, the Emperor asked a monk, “Who are you?
He replied, “I am the master of the pagoda. The Emperor said, “This is my pagoda; why do you act as its master? The monk was speechless. (Xuedou...)
Xuedou Xian’s substitute says: "The entire nation knows. One day, while a monk was in audience, the Emperor asked, "Where have you come from?
The monk replied, "From Sleeping Clouds Hermitage on Mount Lu. The Emperor said, "I have heard that where the clouds sleep deeply, one does not face the court.

Why have you come here? The monk had no reply. Xuedou Xian’s substitute says: "It is difficult to escape the ultimate transformation. When another monk entered for an audience, he reported, "Does Your Majesty still remember? The Emperor—
The Emperor asked, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "Since our parting at Vulture Peak, it has been until this very day.

The Emperor asked, "What proof do you have? The monk was speechless. (Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf: "I, this poor monk, have come specifically for this purpose. When the imperial temples were consumed by fire and the Tripitaka scriptures were reduced to ashes, a monk wished to petition for their restoration through imperial decree.
The Emperor summoned him and asked, "In the past, Kāśyapa Matanga was not burned; why is it that they are now being burned?"
[The Emperor] tried to burn it, but the monk had no reply. (Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf: "Your Majesty has not forgotten the entrustment.

Once, the Emperor dreamed of a divine being who said to him, "I request that Your Majesty give rise to the Bodhicitta. Consequently, during the morning audience, he questioned those in attendance and the officials of the streets:

"How does one give rise to the Bodhicitta? No one had an answer. (Xuedou Xian spoke on his behalf: "Truly, this is rarely heard in all antiquity. Master Zhiji presented a diagram of the Three Realms to the Emperor. The Emperor...
Question: "In which realm am I? My wisdom is tranquil and without peer. (Baoning Yong’s commentary says: "Your Majesty, where do you not hold the title of Honored One?
One day, after the morning audience had concluded, the Emperor held up his alms bowl and asked Prime Minister Wang Sui: "Since it cannot be lifted at the head of Mount Dayu..."
"Why is it, then, in Your Majesty's hands?
[The Emperor] had no reply.
In the third year of the Zhenghe era of Emperor Huizong, the Patrol Officer of Jiazhou submitted a memorial stating that by the roadside of his jurisdiction, there was a large... [text fragment].
There was an ancient tree that had been broken by the wind; inside it sat a monk in meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), his hair and beard covering his body and his fingernails encircling his frame.

The Emperor issued an edict ordering him to be carried on a palanquin to the capital. He commanded the Tripitaka Master Dharmatāla from the Western Heaven to bring him out of his trance using a golden gong.
Upon emerging, the monk was asked which era he belonged to. He replied, "I am Huichí, the younger brother of Dharma Master Huiyuán of Donglin. Because...

He traveled to Mount Emei and entered meditative absorption beneath a tree. [The Emperor asked,] "Is Dharma Master Huiyuan well? The Tripiṭaka Master replied, "Dharma Master Huiyuan was a man of the Jin dynasty;
seven hundred years have passed since his passing. Daochi did not speak further. The Tripiṭaka Master asked, "Since you have arrived here, Master, where do you wish to return?
Daochi said, "To Chenliu County. He then entered meditative absorption once more. The Emperor composed three verses and ordered that an image of him be painted and distributed.

The verse says: For seven hundred years, this ancient sage has remained in meditative absorption; to whom can he reveal his news? How could he compare to one who returned to the West with but a single shoe?

What need is there to labor over life and death as if they were wood and bark? To hide a mountain in a marsh is also to hide the self; when the world is without anything to hide, the Way becomes accessible.
I send word to Zhuang Zhou: do not engage in speculative deliberation; within the tree, there is no person carrying a burden. Sentient beings.

The body is not insentient; it is the body within samādhi for every person, both you and I. If you can realize that the Bodhi tree is fundamentally non-existent, there is no need for arduous toil to question Huineng.
Emperor Xiaozong questioned Chan Master Fozhao Guang of Lingyin, saying: "When Śākyamuni Buddha entered the mountains to cultivate the Way, he achieved his goal after six years.
What was it that he accomplished? I request the Master to explain this clearly. The Master replied: "I had thought Your Majesty..."
Forgetfulness.
*Jiaowai biezhuan* (Teachings Outside the Scriptures), Scroll 16 (End).
